summary: P-adic differential equations, rigid cohomology and p-adic weights, stages RD.0-RD.7, in 304 nodes. RD.0-RD.1 plan the structure theory of the Robba rings (units, Bezout property, finite separable extensions, the extended Robba ring), Frobenius lifts on Robba rings and on dagger algebras with their homotopy, differential modules with generic radii, breaks and Swan conductors, and sigma-modules with degrees, Harder-Narasimhan slopes and Dieudonne-Manin over the extended Robba ring; the Laurent-series rings themselves and the dagger algebras are imported from P7 and F1. RD.2 plans Kedlaya's slope filtration theorem and the p-adic local monodromy theorem with its finite etale and logarithmic forms and the form Berger's proof consumes. RD.3 plans frames, tubes, strict neighbourhoods and j-dagger, overconvergent (F-)isocrystals, independence of the frame, the Monsky-Washnitzer description and full faithfulness of restriction to convergent isocrystals. RD.4-RD.5 plan rigid cohomology with and without compact support, Frobenius and its independence of the lift, excision, Gysin and the Monsky-Washnitzer comparison, then Kedlaya's finiteness, Poincare duality and Kunneth along the architecture of his proof. RD.6-RD.7 plan the Lefschetz trace formula, the p-adic Fourier transform and Kedlaya's rigid Weil II with smooth-proper purity, then the rigid-crystalline comparison and the export of each Weil factor to WeilConjectures WC.6.

nodes.title: Frobenius lifts on the integral, bounded and full Robba rings
nodes.statement: Fix K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with ring of integers O_K, uniformiser π, residue field k of characteristic p, and a Frobenius lift σ_K on K (a continuous ring endomorphism with σ_K(O_K) ⊆ O_K reducing to x ↦ x^q on k, q = p^a). Let O_E be the ring of Laurent series Σ_{i∈Z} a_i t^i with a_i ∈ O_K and a_i → 0 as i → −∞ (the integral Amice ring; E = O_E[1/π]), let R^int ⊆ O_E be the series converging on some annulus r < |t| < 1 (all coefficients integral), R^bd = R^int[1/π], and R the Robba ring (all three imported from PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations). A Frobenius lift is a ring endomorphism σ of O_E that is σ_K-semilinear on O_K, continuous for the weak (levelwise) topology, and satisfies σ(t) ∈ R^int and σ(t) − t^q ∈ π·R^int. Such σ is determined by u = σ(t) through σ(Σ a_i t^i) = Σ σ_K(a_i) u^i; conversely every u ∈ R^int with u ≡ t^q mod π defines one. It preserves R^int and extends uniquely to continuous ring endomorphisms of R^bd, E and R, carrying the functions on r < |t| < 1 into the functions on r^{1/q} < |t| < 1 for r close to 1.
hypotheses: K is discretely valued; π is a uniformiser; q = p^a and σ_K induces the q-power map on k. When k is perfect and K = W(k)[1/p], σ_K may be taken to be (a power of) the Witt vector Frobenius.
The condition σ(t) ∈ R^int is Kedlaya's overconvergence condition lim inf_{i→−∞} w(a_i)/(−i) > 0 on the coefficients of σ(t) (slope filtrations revisited, Convention 2.3.1).
A Frobenius lift need not be a power of a p-power Frobenius lift (slope filtrations revisited, Remark 2.2.5); the older monodromy paper requires a composition power of a lift of the p-power map.
No ring of functions on a fixed annulus r < |t| < 1 carries a Frobenius lift: σ moves the inner radius from r to r^{1/q}.
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness from u: O_E is the π-adic completion of O_K[t, t^{-1}] and O_K[t, t^{-1}] is dense for the levelwise topology (monodromy paper, Section 2.3), so a levelwise-continuous σ is determined by σ(t) and σ_K; u is a unit of O_E because its reduction t^q is a unit of k((t)), so Σ σ_K(a_i) u^i converges levelwise.

Preservation of R^int: by the comparison of naive and true partial valuations (slope filtrations revisited, Lemmas 2.3.3 and 2.3.5), if u/t^q is a unit of the ring of bounded functions on |π|^r ≤ |t| < 1 then the sup norms satisfy |σ(f)|_{ρ^{1/q}} = |f|_ρ for |π|^{qr} ≤ ρ < 1; hence σ maps bounded functions on an annulus near the boundary to bounded functions on a thinner annulus.

Extension to R^bd = R^int[1/π] and E = O_E[1/π] is by inverting π (σ(π) = σ_K(π) is π times a unit). Extension to R: R is the union of the Fréchet completions of R^bd on annuli (slope filtrations revisited, Definition 2.4.2), and the norm identity of the previous step makes σ continuous from the ρ-norms to the ρ^{1/q}-norms, so σ extends uniquely by continuity.
acceptance: Standard lift σ(t) = t^q: σ(Σ a_i t^i) = Σ σ_K(a_i) t^{qi}.
Cyclotomic lift for K = Q_p, q = p: σ(t) = (1+t)^p − 1 lies in R^int and is congruent to t^p modulo p; log(1+t) ∈ R satisfies σ(log(1+t)) = p·log(1+t) (slope filtrations revisited, Remark 3.3.6).
Transport to a finite separable extension L of k((t)): the lift extends uniquely to R^int_L (see the finite-separable-extension node); a standard lift is in general not standard on R^int_L.

nodes.title: Partial valuations v_n, w_r on Witt vectors and the overconvergent Witt vectors W_con
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be a perfect field of characteristic p with a (possibly trivial) valuation v_ℓ, complete, let k_0 ⊆ ℓ be a perfect subfield on which v_ℓ is trivial, and let O be a finite totally ramified extension of W(k_0) with uniformiser π, equipped with an extension of σ; put W(ℓ, O) = W(ℓ) ⊗_{W(k_0)} O. Every x ∈ W(ℓ, O)[π^{-1}] has a unique Teichmüller expansion x = Σ_{i∈Z} [z_i] π^i (z_i ∈ ℓ, zero for i ≪ 0). For n ∈ Z put v_n(x) = min_{i ≤ n} v_ℓ(z_i); for r > 0 put v_{n,r}(x) = r·v_n(x) + n, let W_r(ℓ, O) be the set of x ∈ W(ℓ, O) with v_{n,r}(x) → ∞ as n → ∞, and w_r(x) = min_n v_{n,r}(x); w = w_0 is the π-adic valuation normalised by w(π) = 1. Put W_con(ℓ, O) = ∪_{r>0} W_r(ℓ, O).
hypotheses: ℓ perfect and complete for v_ℓ; the valuation may be trivial, in which case W_r = W and W_con = W(ℓ, O).
Normalisation w(π) = 1 (Kedlaya, slope filtrations revisited, Remark 2.1.11), not w(p) = 1; results do not depend on it.
σ on W(ℓ, O) is the log_p(q)-th power of the Witt vector Frobenius σ_0, tensored with the given σ on O; then v_n(x^σ) = q·v_n(x) and w_r(x) = w_{r/q}(x^σ).
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness of Teichmüller expansions: each x ∈ W(ℓ, O) is uniquely Σ_{i≥0} [z_i] π^i (slope filtrations revisited, Definition 2.1.4); inverting π allows finitely many negative i.

The inequalities v_n(x + y) ≥ min(v_n(x), v_n(y)), v_n(xy) ≥ min_m (v_m(x) + v_{n−m}(y)) with equality when the minimum is attained once, v_n(x^σ) = q v_n(x) and v_n([z]) = v_ℓ(z) for n ≥ 0 follow from the Witt vector addition and multiplication formulas (Definition 2.1.5).
σ sends W_{qr} onto W_r (Definition 2.1.5); W_r is a subring by the inequalities.
acceptance: For ℓ with trivial valuation W_r(ℓ, O) = W(ℓ, O) for every r.
For z ∈ ℓ with v_ℓ(z) > 0 the Teichmüller lift [z] lies in every W_r and is a unit in W_r if z ≠ 0 (Remark 2.2.11(a)).
If v_ℓ(y) < 0, then Σ_{i≥0} [y^{q^i}] π^i lies in W(ℓ, O) but in no W_r(ℓ, O).

sources.excerpt: note that each x ∈ W(K, O) can be written uniquely as Σ_{i=0}^∞ [z_i]π^i for some z_0, z_1, · · · ∈ K

nodes.title: w_r is a valuation on W_r(ℓ, O)[π^{-1}] (Newton-polygon additivity)
nodes.statement: For x, y ∈ W_r(ℓ, O)[π^{-1}] nonzero, let i, j be the smallest and largest n achieving min_n v_{n,r}(x), and k, l those for y. Then i + k and j + l are the smallest and largest n achieving min_n v_{n,r}(xy), and w_r(xy) = w_r(x) + w_r(y). In particular w_r is a valuation on W_r(ℓ, O)[π^{-1}] and w_r(x) = w_{r/q}(x^σ).
hypotheses: ℓ perfect, complete for v_ℓ; notation of the partial-valuation node.
proofSteps: Apply v_{m,r}(xy) ≥ min_n (v_{n,r}(x) + v_{m−n,r}(y)) with equality when the minimum is attained once.
For m = i + k and m = j + l the value v_{i,r}(x) + v_{k,r}(y) is attained exactly once; for m < i + k or m > j + l it is never attained; this gives the claim.
acceptance: Rank one check: w_r([z]π^m) = r v_ℓ(z) + m and the product rule holds on monomials.

sources.excerpt: Then i+k and j+l are the smallest and largest integers n achieving min_n{v_{n,r}(xy)}, and this minimum equals min_n{v_{n,r}(x)} + min_n{v_{n,r}(y)}.

nodes.title: W_con(ℓ, O) is a henselian discrete valuation ring
nodes.statement: W_con(ℓ, O) is a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal (π) and residue field ℓ; it is henselian, and it is not π-adically complete when v_ℓ is nontrivial.
hypotheses: ℓ perfect and complete for v_ℓ.
proofSteps: DVR: every nonzero x ∈ W_con is π^m times an element with nonzero reduction; an element of W_r with nonzero reduction u_0 is a unit in some W_s (Remark 2.1.10: u is a unit of W_r iff v_{n,r}(u) > v_{0,r}(u) for n > 0, which holds after shrinking r).

Henselian: given a polynomial P over W_con and y with P(y) ≡ 0 and P'(y) ≢ 0 mod π, choose r with w_r(P(y)/P'(y)) > 0; Newton iteration converges both for w and for w_r, so the root lies in W_r (Lemma 2.1.12).
Non-completeness: see the non-example of the partial-valuation node.
acceptance: The residue map W_con → ℓ is surjective (Teichmüller lifts) with kernel πW_con.
Hensel test: for p odd and ℓ ∋ y with y^2 = c, the polynomial X^2 − [c] has a root in W_con lifting y.

sources.excerpt: The (noncomplete) discrete valuation ring W_con(K, O) is henselian.
the usual Newton iteration gives a series converging under w to a root z of P in W(K, O) with z ≡ y (mod π). However, the iteration also converges under w_r

nodes.title: Kedlaya's analytic rings Γ^ℓ_I, Γ^ℓ_an,r and Γ^ℓ_an,con
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be a field of characteristic p complete for a (possibly trivial) valuation v_ℓ, k_0 ⊆ ℓ a subfield on which v_ℓ is trivial, O finite totally ramified over the Cohen ring C_{k_0} with uniformiser π, Γ = Γ^ℓ = C_ℓ ⊗_{C_{k_0}} O, and σ a Frobenius lift on Γ (lifting the q-power map of ℓ) carrying O into itself. Via the completed direct limit of Γ →σ Γ →σ ⋯ ≅ W(ℓ^perf, O^perf) the functions v_n, v_{n,r}, w_r restrict to Γ; put Γ_r = Γ ∩ W_r(ℓ^perf, O). Say Γ has enough r_0-units if every nonzero element of ℓ lifts to a unit of Γ_{r_0}, and assume this. For I ⊆ [0, r_0) bounded away from r_0, Γ_I is the Fréchet completion of Γ_{r_0}[π^{-1}] for the valuations w_s, s ∈ I; Γ_an,r = Γ_{(0,r]}, Γ_an,con = ∪_{r<r_0} Γ_an,r, Γ_con = ∪ Γ_r (a henselian DVR). σ induces Γ_I → Γ_{q^{-1}I}; for I ⊆ J the restriction Γ_J → Γ_I is injective with dense image. The Newton polygon of x ∈ Γ_I is the lower convex hull of the points (v_n(x), n) with the segments of slope −s, s ∉ I, removed; its slopes (with multiplicities) are the slopes of x.
hypotheses: ℓ complete; 'enough r_0-units' holds for ℓ perfect (Teichmüller lifts) and for ℓ = k((t)) by the comparison of naive and true valuations (see the Robba ring comparison node) and it passes to finite separable extensions.
When v_ℓ is trivial, Γ_an,con = Γ_con[π^{-1}] = Γ[π^{-1}] is a complete discretely valued field.
Kedlaya's K is written ℓ here, to keep K for the characteristic-0 coefficient field.
proofSteps: Definitions 2.2.1-2.2.13 of slope filtrations revisited: Cohen ring, Frobenius lift, embedding into W(ℓ^perf, O^perf), Γ_r, enough units, Γ_con.
Definition 2.4.2: Fréchet completion Γ_I; the functions v_n, v_{n,s}, w_s extend by continuity; σ: Γ_I → Γ_{q^{-1}I}; restriction maps injective with dense image (density of Γ_{r_0}[π^{-1}]).
Definition 2.4.4 (Newton polygon of elements) and Definition 2.4.8 (Γ_an,con).
Γ_con is a henselian DVR with residue field ℓ: Definition 2.2.13 with Lemma 2.1.12 applied inside W_con(ℓ^perf, O).
acceptance: For ℓ with trivial valuation: Γ_I = Γ[π^{-1}] for every I and Γ_an,con = Γ[π^{-1}].
For ℓ = k((t)): Γ_an,con is the Robba ring (comparison node).

sources.excerpt: we may identify the completed direct limit of (2.2.4) with W(K^perf, O^perf); we may thus use the induced embedding Γ_K ↪ W(K^perf, O^perf) to define v_n, v_{n,r}, w_r, w on Γ.
We say Γ has enough r-units if every nonzero element of K can be lifted to a unit of Γ_r.
Let Γ_I be the Fréchet completion of Γ_{r_0}[π^{−1}] for the valuations w_s for s ∈ I
Let Γ^K_an,con be the union of the Γ^K_an,r over all r ∈ (0, r_0); this ring is an integral domain by Lemma 2.4.7.

nodes.title: Slopes of a product are the sums of the slopes; Γ_I is a domain
nodes.statement: For x, y ∈ Γ_I nonzero and s ∈ I, the multiplicity of s as a slope of xy is the sum of its multiplicities as a slope of x and of y. In particular Γ_I and Γ_an,con are integral domains. For a closed interval [r', r] ⊆ [0, r_0) the total multiplicity of x ∈ Γ_{[r',r]} is finite and equals i − j, where i is the largest n achieving min_n v_{n,r}(x) and j the smallest n achieving min_n v_{n,r'}(x).
hypotheses: Notation of the analytic-ring construction.
proofSteps: For x, y ∈ Γ_r[π^{-1}] this is the multiplicativity lemma for w_r applied at each s ∈ I.
In general approximate x, y in Γ_I by elements of Γ_r[π^{-1}] closely enough that the extremal indices are unchanged (Lemma 2.4.7).
Finiteness of total multiplicity: Remark 2.4.6.
acceptance: For elements of O[π^{-1}]^× there are no slopes; a product of two elements each with one slope s of multiplicity 1 has slope s with multiplicity 2.

sources.excerpt: For x, y ∈ Γ_I nonzero, the multiplicity of each s ∈ I as a slope of xy is the sum of the multiplicities of s as a slope of x and of y. In particular, Γ_I is an integral domain.
for any closed subinterval I = [r', r] of [0, r_0), the total multiplicity of any x ∈ Γ_I is finite.

nodes.title: Semiunit presentations of elements of Γ_I
nodes.statement: Call a semiunit an element of Γ_{r_0} that is zero or a unit. For I ⊆ [0, r_0) bounded away from r_0, every x ∈ Γ_I admits a semiunit presentation x = Σ_{i∈Z} u_i π^i (u_i semiunits, the sum converging in Γ_I). For any semiunits u_i and r ∈ (0, r_0), w_r(u_i π^i) ≥ min_{n≤i} v_{n,r}(Σ_{j≤i} u_j π^j).
hypotheses: Γ has enough r_0-units (this is what makes each residue class liftable to a semiunit).
proofSteps: Lemma 2.5.3(a),(b): estimates for partial sums of semiunit series, by induction on i.
Lemma 2.5.4: a semiunit presentation over Γ_{[r,r]} of an element with v_{n,s}(x) → ∞ for s ∈ I converges in Γ_I.

Proposition 2.5.5: first for x ∈ Γ_r by successive π-adic approximation with semiunits; then for I = [r,r] by approximating x by elements x_l ∈ Γ_r[π^{-1}] and correcting finitely many terms at each stage; the corrections for a fixed i form a series converging in Γ_{r_0} whose limit is a semiunit; the general I follows from Lemma 2.5.4.
acceptance: If ℓ is perfect, the Teichmüller presentation Σ [f_n(x)] π^n is a semiunit presentation.

sources.excerpt: For I a subinterval of [0, r_0) bounded away from r_0, every x ∈ Γ_I admits a semiunit presentation.
Define a semiunit to be an element of Γ_{r_0} which is either zero or a unit.

nodes.title: Numerical membership criterion, intersections and Mayer-Vietoris splitting for Γ_I
nodes.statement: (a) For r ∈ (0, r_0) and x ∈ Γ_{[r,r]}: x ∈ Γ_r iff v_n(x) = ∞ for all n < 0. (b) For I ⊆ J bounded away from r_0 and x ∈ Γ_I with v_{n,s}(x) → ∞ as n → ±∞ for every s ∈ J: x ∈ Γ_J. (c) For ℓ ⊆ ℓ' complete, Γ^ℓ and Γ^{ℓ'} having enough r_0-units, and I ⊆ J ⊆ [0, r_0) bounded away from r_0: Γ^ℓ_I ∩ Γ^{ℓ'}_J = Γ^ℓ_J inside Γ^{ℓ'}_I; in particular Γ^ℓ[π^{-1}] ∩ Γ^{ℓ'}_con[π^{-1}] = Γ^ℓ_con[π^{-1}]. nodes.title: Units of Γ_I are the elements without slopes; units of Γ_an,r lie in Γ_r[π^{-1}]
nodes.statement: A nonzero x ∈ Γ_I is a unit of Γ_I iff it has no slopes (in I). If I = (0, r], this holds iff x is a unit of Γ_r[π^{-1}]. Consequently the units of Γ_an,con are exactly the units of Γ_con[π^{-1}], i.e. the nonzero elements of the field Γ_con[π^{-1}].
hypotheses: Enough r_0-units.
Γ_con is a DVR, so Γ_con[π^{-1}] is its fraction field.
proofSteps: Units have no slopes by slope additivity.

Conversely if x has no slopes, one index m minimises v_{m,s}(x) for all s ∈ I; normalise m = 0; the truncation lemma (e) gives y ∈ Γ_r close to x, and enough units gives a unit z of Γ_r with w(y − z) > 0; then w_s(1 − x z^{-1}) > 0 on I and Σ (1 − x z^{-1})^i converges to (x z^{-1})^{-1}.
For I = (0, r]: no slopes forces v_n(x) = ∞ for n < m, so x ∈ Γ_r[π^{-1}] by the membership criterion, and likewise x^{-1}.
acceptance: π and the units of O are units; for ℓ = k((t)) the element Π_{i≥1}(1 − t^{p^i}/p^i) of R has infinitely many slopes and is not a unit (monodromy paper, Section 2.3).

nodes.title: Γ_r and Γ_I for closed I are principal ideal domains (Lazard)
nodes.statement: For r ∈ (0, r_0), Γ_r is a principal ideal domain, and for every closed interval I ⊆ [0, r_0), Γ_I is a principal ideal domain. For ℓ = k((t)) these are the rings of bounded functions on |π|^r ≤ |t| < 1 and of analytic functions on the closed annulus {log_{|π|}|t| ∈ I}, and the statement specialises to Lazard's theorem.
hypotheses: ℓ discretely valued or trivially valued (the division algorithm uses discreteness of v_ℓ); enough r_0-units.
proofSteps: Positioning (Lemma 2.6.1): for x ∈ Γ_{[r,r]} nonzero there are a unit u of Γ_{r_0} and i with uπ^i x normalised (w_r = 0, v_0(· − 1) > 0, v_{n,r} > 0 for n < 0).
Division algorithm (Lemma 2.6.3): define the height of x ∈ Γ_r; for x ≠ 0 and y there is z of smaller height with y − z ∈ xΓ_r and w_r(z) ≥ w_r(y); the iteration converges because v_ℓ is discrete.
Γ_r is a PID (Proposition 2.6.5): an element of minimal height generates any nonzero ideal.
Factorisation (Lemma 2.6.7): for I = [r', r] and x ∈ Γ_I there is a unit u of Γ_I with ux ∈ Γ_r having all slopes in I.

Γ_I is a PID (Proposition 2.6.8): the ideal of Γ_r generated by the ux, x ∈ J, is principal by Proposition 2.6.5 (the printed proof cites 2.6.8 itself; see sourceIssues) and its generator generates J.
acceptance: Γ_{[0,0]} = Γ[π^{-1}] is a field (a PID trivially).
For ℓ = k((t)) and I = [s,s] a single circle, every ideal of the ring of analytic functions on the circle is generated by a polynomial (Lazard; overview Proposition 3.2.3).

nodes.title: Approximation of invertible matrices and factorisation over overlapping intervals
nodes.statement: (a) For I closed ⊆ [0, r], r < r_0, and M ∈ GL_n(Γ_I) there is U ∈ GL_n(Γ_r[π^{-1}]) with w_s(MU − I_n) > 0 for s ∈ I; if w_s(det M − 1) > 0 on I one can take det U = 1. (b) For I = [a,b], J = [c,d] with a ≤ c ≤ b ≤ d and M an n×n matrix over Γ_{I∩J} with w_s(M − I_n) > 0 on I∩J, there are U ∈ GL_n(Γ_I), V ∈ GL_n(Γ_J) with M = UV.

proofSteps: (a) Lemma 2.7.1: induction on n; choose the last row of a determinant-one matrix A over the PID Γ_r[π^{-1}] approximating the cofactor relation, using that β_n' + c for c ∈ O of large valuation are pairwise coprime; then approximate Gaussian elimination and back-substitution over Γ_I, and approximate the elementary factors over Γ_r.

(b) Lemma 2.7.2: iterate M_l = U_l^{-1} M V_l^{-1}, splitting M_l − I_n = Y_l + Z_l by the Mayer-Vietoris splitting (intersections node (d)); the products converge and the estimates put the limits in GL_n(Γ_I) and GL_n(Γ_J).

nodes.title: Vector bundles over Γ_an,r are free; closed submodules and closed ideals
nodes.statement: For I bounded away from r_0 and S a collection of closed subintervals of I closed under finite intersections and covering I, an S-vector bundle over Γ_I is a family of finite free Γ_J-modules M_J (J ∈ S) with compatible isomorphisms M_{J_1} ⊗ Γ_{J_2} ≅ M_{J_2} for J_2 ⊆ J_1. The category does not depend on S (Kiehl-Tate type gluing). For r ∈ (0, r_0) the functor from finite free Γ_an,r-modules to vector bundles over Γ_an,r = Γ_{(0,r]} is an equivalence. Consequently every closed submodule of a finite free Γ_an,r-module is free and every closed ideal of Γ_an,r is principal. For ℓ = k((t)): every finite free ∇-module or vector bundle on a half-open annulus |π|^r ≤ |t| < 1 over a discretely valued K is given by a free module over the ring of functions (compare overview Theorem 3.4.3, stated there for spherically complete K).
hypotheses: Enough r_0-units; discreteness of v_ℓ.
proofSteps: Gluing (Lemma 2.8.2): for J ⊆ J_1 ∪ J_2 with J_1 ∩ J_2 ≠ ∅, factor the transition matrix A = UV (factorisation lemma) and use Γ_{J_1} ∩ Γ_{J_2} = Γ_{J_1∪J_2}.

Theorem 2.8.4: choose closed J_1 ⊆ J_2 ⊆ ⋯ exhausting (0, r]; inductively change bases by U_i over Γ_r (approximation lemma) and by (I_n + V_i)^{-1} (truncation lemma) so that w_s(W_i − I_n) > s/r_i − 1 → ∞; the product W_1W_2⋯ converges in GL_n(Γ_an,r) and gives a global basis.
Corollary 2.8.5: a closed submodule gives a sub-vector bundle.
acceptance: Rank-one case: a line bundle on the half-open annulus over discretely valued K is trivial (Lazard).

nodes.title: Γ_an,r and Γ_an,con (in particular the Robba ring) are Bézout domains
nodes.statement: For r ∈ (0, r_0) and an ideal J of Γ_an,r, the conditions (a) J is closed, (b) J is finitely generated, (c) J is principal, are equivalent. Hence Γ_an,r and Γ_an,con are Bézout domains; for ℓ = k((t)) the Robba ring R is a Bézout domain (Lazard's theorem for annuli).
hypotheses: Enough r_0-units; v_ℓ discrete (Remark 2.9.7: the implication closed ⇒ principal would need spherical completeness of ℓ otherwise).
proofSteps: (c) ⇒ (a),(b) is clear; (a) ⇒ (c) is the closed-ideal corollary of the vector bundle theorem.

(b) ⇒ (a): reduce to J = (x, y) with 1 in the closure. Lemma 2.9.1 (refined factorisation: g ∈ Γ_r[π^{-1}] with slopes in [s,r] generating the same ideal as f on Γ_[s,r]), Lemma 2.9.2 (approximation modulo x with prescribed decay) and Lemma 2.9.3 (principal parts: compatible residues modulo f on an exhausting chain of closed intervals come from a global g) give b ∈ Γ_an,r with by − 1 divisible by x on each Γ_{I_i}, hence in Γ_an,r by the membership criterion.
Γ_an,con is the union of the Γ_an,r, so finitely generated ideals come from some Γ_an,r.

nodes.title: Finite modules over Bézout domains: unimodular rows, saturated spans, freeness, Galois descent of saturated submodules
nodes.statement: Let R be a Bézout domain. (a) If x_1, …, x_n generate the unit ideal there is A ∈ SL_n(R) with first row (x_1, …, x_n). (b) For a finite free R-module M and any subset S ⊆ M, the saturated span SatSpan(S) = M ∩ Frac(R)·S is free and a direct summand of M; every finite torsion-free R-module is free. (c) Every finite locally free (equivalently finite projective) R-module is free. (d) If R_1/R_2 is an extension of Bézout domains, G a group of automorphisms of R_1 over R_2 with fixed ring R_2 such that every G-stable finitely generated ideal of R_1 meets R_2 − {0} (automatic for G finite), M_2 finite free over R_2 and N_1 ⊆ M_2 ⊗ R_1 a saturated G-stable submodule, then N_1 = N_2 ⊗ R_1 for a unique saturated N_2 ⊆ M_2. (e) An R-module is flat iff torsion-free (Mathlib).
hypotheses: R a Bézout domain (for example the Robba ring, Γ_an,con, Γ_con[π^{-1}], a DVR).
proofSteps: (a) Monodromy paper Lemma 2.3: induction on n via the generator d of (x_1, …, x_{n−1}).
(b) Lemma 2.4: induction on rank using (a) to split off a primitive vector.
(c) Proposition 2.5: F → M surjective, N = SatSpan(ker), F/N free of the right rank, and M → F/N is locally a surjection of free modules of equal rank.
(d) Lemma 2.6: induction on rank, descending one vector y using G-invariance.
(e) is Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout.
acceptance: Over a DVR (a PID) (b)-(c) reduce to the structure theorem; for the Robba ring they give that σ-modules and ∇-modules may be taken free.

Then N_1 is equal to N_2 ⊗_{R_2} R_1 for a saturated submodule (necessarily unique) N_2 of M_2.

nodes.title: Finite separable extensions: Γ^L_con finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con and Γ^L_an,con = Γ^ℓ_an,con ⊗ Γ^L_con
nodes.statement: Let L/ℓ be finite separable. Then Γ^L is a finite unramified extension of Γ^ℓ, σ extends uniquely to Γ^L (and Gal(L/ℓ) acts when L/ℓ is Galois), Γ^L has enough units if Γ^ℓ does, Γ^L_con is finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con with Γ^L_con ≅ Γ^ℓ_con[x]/(P(x)) for any x ∈ Γ^L_con whose reduction generates L over ℓ (P the minimal polynomial), and the multiplication map Γ^ℓ_an,con ⊗_{Γ^ℓ_con} Γ^L_con → Γ^L_an,con is an isomorphism, Γ^L_an,con ≅ Γ^ℓ_an,con[x]/(P(x)). If L/ℓ is Galois with group G, the G-invariants of Frac Γ^L_an,con are Frac Γ^ℓ_an,con. For ℓ = k((t)) this gives, for every finite separable extension L of k((t)), the rings R^int_L, R^bd_L, R_L; the pair (R^int, m_R) is henselian, so finite étale covers of the boundary annulus correspond to finite separable extensions of k((t)) (formally étale covers).
hypotheses: Enough units for Γ^ℓ; pseudo-finite separable extensions L = M^{q^{-n}} are handled by Frobenius twisting (Definition 2.2.8).
proofSteps: Unramified extension and extension of σ: Definition 2.2.8 (Γ^L is the unique unramified lift; σ extends uniquely by henselian lifting of the q-power map).
Enough units: Lemma 2.2.12 (primitive element x lifted by henselianity, equivalence of norms on L over ℓ, estimate of v_{n,s} of lifts).
Γ^L_con = Γ^ℓ_con[x]/(P): Proposition 2.2.15; Γ^L_s ≅ Γ^ℓ_s[x]/(P) for small s by Lemma 2.1.12, hence Proposition 2.4.10.
Galois invariants of fraction fields: Corollary 2.4.11 (norm trick).
Henselian pair (R^int, m_R): overview Proposition 3.5.5 (Newton iteration with control on |·|_r), giving Definition 3.5.6 of formally étale covers.
acceptance: For L = k'((t)) with k'/k finite separable, Γ^L_an,con is the Robba ring over the unramified extension K' of K.
Artin-Schreier: L = k((t))[u]/(u^p − u − t^{-1}) gives R_L = R[u']/((1+πu')^p − (1 + pπ t^{-1})) with π^{p−1} = −p (overview Lemma 5.3.3).

Then the fixed subring of Frac Γ^L_an,con under the action of G = Gal(L/K) is equal to Frac Γ^K_an,con.

nodes.title: The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree
nodes.statement: Let R = R_K be the Robba ring over K (germs of Laurent series Σ_{i∈Z} c_i t^i, c_i ∈ K, converging on some annulus r < |t| < 1; imported from PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations with its Gauss norms |·|_ρ, Fréchet topology on each annulus ring and limit-of-Fréchet (LF) topology on R), R^int, R^bd = R^int[1/π], O_E and E = O_E[1/π] as in the Frobenius-lift node. Let σ be a Frobenius lift with u = σ(t), and let ℓ = k((t)), Γ = O_E, so that the analytic-ring construction applies. Choose r > 0 with u/t^q a unit of the ring of bounded functions on |π|^r ≤ |t| < 1. Then for s ∈ (0, qr] and all n: min_{j≤n} v_{j,s} = min_{j≤n} v^naive_{j,s}, where v^naive_n(Σ c_i t^i) = min{i : w(c_i) ≤ n}; consequently Γ_s = bounded functions on |π|^s ≤ |t| < 1 with integral coefficients, w_s(f) = −log_{|π|} |f|_{|π|^s} (sup norm on the circle |t| = |π|^s), Γ has enough qr-units, and Γ_con = R^int, Γ_con[π^{-1}] = R^bd, Γ[π^{-1}] = E, Γ_{(0,s]} = functions on |π|^s ≤ |t| < 1, Γ_an,con = R. The identification is independent of σ as topological rings; only the auxiliary partial valuations v_n, and the embedding into W(k((t))^perf, O^perf), depend on σ.
hypotheses: K discretely valued with uniformiser π; O = O_K is finite totally ramified over a Cohen ring of k.
Radius convention: Kedlaya's parameter s corresponds to the radius ρ = |π|^s; an interval I ⊆ (0, r_0) corresponds to the annulus {|π|^{max I} ≤ |t| ≤ |π|^{min I}} and (0, r] to |π|^r ≤ |t| < 1.
The Frobenius lift is used only to transport Kedlaya's machinery; statements about the underlying topological ring (Bézout property, units, free vector bundles) hold for any choice (Remark 2.3.9).
proofSteps: Lemma 2.3.3: for s ∈ (0, qr], min_{j≤n} v^naive_{j,s}(x) = min_{j≤n} v^naive_{j,s/q}(x^σ), checked on monomials u^i and then termwise with a unique minimising index.

Lemma 2.3.5: write x via Teichmüller coordinates, raise to a large q-power by σ and compare with naive valuations of lifts of the coordinates; with Lemma 2.3.3 this gives equality of the true and naive partial valuations.
Corollary 2.3.7: Γ has enough qr-units and Γ_con = Γ_con^naive = R^int.

Remark 2.3.8 and Example 2.4.9: Γ^naive_r[π^{-1}] is the ring of bounded analytic functions on |π|^r ≤ |t| < 1, w^naive_s is the sup norm on |t| = |π|^s, and Γ_an,con consists of the Laurent series over O[π^{-1}] with lim inf_{n→−∞} w(c_n)/(−n) > 0 and lim inf_{n→∞} w(c_n)/n ≥ 0, which is P7's Robba ring.
Independence of σ as topological rings: both sides are described by coefficient conditions that do not mention σ (Remark 2.3.9).
acceptance: The Laurent polynomial t − p (K = Q_p, standard lift) has v^naive_0 = 1 and v^naive_n = 0 for n ≥ 1, one slope 1, and its zero is on |t| = p^{-1} = |π|^1.
For the cyclotomic lift σ(t) = (1+t)^p − 1 the naive and true valuations agree on Γ_s for s ≤ pr with r chosen as in the statement.

nodes.title: The bounded Robba ring R^bd is a henselian discretely valued field with residue field k((t)); R^bd = R ∩ E
nodes.statement: (a) R^int is a local ring with maximal ideal m_R = {Σ c_i t^i : all c_i ∈ m_K} and residue field k((t)); since K is discretely valued, R^int is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π and valuation w(Σ c_i t^i) = min_i w(c_i); it is henselian and not π-adically complete, its π-adic completion being O_E. (b) R^bd = R^int[1/π] is the fraction field of R^int, hence a henselian discretely valued field, with residue field k((t)) and completion E. (c) Inside the space of coefficient families Z → K: R^bd = R ∩ E = {f ∈ R : sup_i |c_i| < ∞} (the functions analytic and bounded on some annulus r < |t| < 1) and R^int = R ∩ O_E. (d) R^bd is dense in R for the LF topology and in E for the π-adic topology. No perfectness of k is needed.
hypotheses: K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0; k arbitrary of characteristic p.
If K is not discretely valued, R^int is local but not a valuation ring in this way (overview Remark 3.5.3); this layer assumes K discretely valued.
proofSteps: (a) Local with residue field k((t)): for x ∈ m_R, |x|_ρ < 1 for ρ close to 1, so 1 + x is invertible in R^int (overview Lemma 3.5.2). DVR: R^int = Γ_con by the Robba-ring comparison, and Γ_con is a henselian DVR (analytic-ring construction, from Lemma 2.1.12). π-adic completion O_E: monodromy paper Section 2.3.
(b) A DVR localised at its uniformiser is its fraction field; henselianity is a property of the valuation ring.

(c) A Laurent series converging on r < |t| < 1 satisfies |c_i|ρ^i → 0 as i → −∞ for some ρ < 1, hence c_i → 0 as i → −∞; if moreover sup_i |c_i| < ∞ it is bounded on r' ≤ |t| < 1 for r' ∈ (r,1), and conversely boundedness on an annulus forces sup_i |c_i| ≤ sup of the function by letting ρ → 1. Scaling by a power of π lands in R^int.
(d) Laurent polynomials are dense in each annulus ring and in O_E.
acceptance: t is a unit of R^int; π is not a unit of R^int but is a unit of R^bd; t − p = t(1 − p t^{-1}) is a unit of R^int because p t^{-1} ∈ m_R.
Σ_{n≥0} p^n t^{-p^n} lies in O_E but not in R^int (completion versus overconvergence node).
The residue field of R^int is k((t)), not k: the reduction of Σ c_i t^i is Σ c̄_i t^i.

nodes.title: Units of the Robba ring are exactly the nonzero elements of R^bd (Lazard, Kedlaya)
nodes.statement: R^× = R^bd − {0}. nodes.title: Flatness, faithful flatness and base change for R^bd → R, R^bd → E and finite separable extensions
nodes.statement: (a) R and E are free, hence faithfully flat, modules over the field R^bd; for a map f of finite R^bd-modules, f is injective (surjective, bijective) iff f ⊗ R is, iff f ⊗ E is. (b) For L/k((t)) finite separable of degree d: R^int_L is finite étale of rank d over R^int, R^bd_L = R^bd ⊗_{R^int} R^int_L, R_L = R ⊗_{R^bd} R^bd_L and E_L = E ⊗_{R^bd} R^bd_L are finite free of rank d, hence faithfully flat; if L/k((t)) is Galois with group G then (R_L)^G = R, (R^bd_L)^G = R^bd, (E_L)^G = E. (c) Every torsion-free module over R (for example R^alg, R_L, or any domain containing R) is flat over R; every finitely generated submodule of a finite free R-module is free. (d) For a finite free R^bd-module M: M = (M ⊗ E) ∩ (M ⊗ R^alg_con[π^{-1}]) inside M ⊗ W(ℓ^alg, O)[π^{-1}], via Γ[π^{-1}] ∩ Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] = Γ_con[π^{-1}].

nodes.title: The extended Robba ring R^alg = Γ^alg_an,con over the completed algebraic closure of k((t))
nodes.statement: Let ℓ^alg be the completion of an algebraic closure of k((t)) with v(t) = 1 (a perfect, algebraically closed, complete valued field), Γ^alg = W(ℓ^alg, O) with the Witt vector Frobenius σ (bijective), and let Γ^alg_r, Γ^alg_con, Γ^alg_I, Γ^alg_an,r and R^alg := Γ^alg_an,con be the analytic rings of the analytic-ring construction for ℓ^alg (with enough r-units for every r, Teichmüller lifts being units). R^alg is a Bézout domain; its units are the nonzero elements of the field Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}]; the residue field of the henselian DVR Γ^alg_con is ℓ^alg (algebraically closed); for every closed interval I the ring Γ^alg_I is a PID; the union of the Γ^L_I over pseudo-finite separable extensions L of k((t)) is dense in Γ^alg_I when 0 ∉ I. A Frobenius lift σ on R^int determines a σ-equivariant embedding R ↪ R^alg (next node). Also Γ^alg[π^{-1}] = W(ℓ^alg, O)[π^{-1}] is a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field (the ring over which generic slopes are read).
hypotheses: ℓ^alg is complete (Kedlaya's convention 2.2.16; the monodromy paper uses the uncompleted algebraic closure, which gives the same Γ^alg_an,con, Remark 2.4.13).
O is fixed; Kedlaya assumes π fixed by σ when working over R^alg (Convention 4.0.1), which is harmless after enlarging O.
proofSteps: Instantiate the analytic-ring construction with ℓ = ℓ^alg (perfect, so Γ^ℓ = W(ℓ, O) and Definition 2.1.5 applies directly).

Bézout, units and PID: the corresponding theorems for analytic rings (enough units holds by Remark 2.2.11(a); v on ℓ^alg is not discrete, but its value group is Q; Kedlaya's Chapter 2 hypotheses are met because the valuation used for w_r is the π-adic one, which is discrete).
Density: Lemma 2.4.12.
acceptance: For the trivially valued perfect field ℓ = k^alg one gets W(k^alg, O)[π^{-1}], the base of classical Dieudonné-Manin theory.
H^0 of the rank-one σ-module R^alg(−1) is in bijection with the maximal ideal of ℓ^alg (Lemma 4.3.1): nonzero Frobenius eigenvectors of negative slope exist over R^alg but not over O[π^{-1}].

nodes.title: The derivation d/dt on annulus rings, R, R^bd, R^int, O_E and E, its norm bounds and Ω^1 = R dt
nodes.statement: d = d/dt, Σ c_i t^i ↦ Σ i c_i t^{i−1}, is a K-linear derivation of the ring of functions on each annulus A(I) and of R, R^bd, E (O_K-linear on R^int and O_E). For every ρ in the relevant interval, |df/dt|_ρ ≤ ρ^{-1}|f|_ρ, with equality for f = t^i and p ∤ i; the operator norm of d/dt on (functions on A(I), |·|_ρ) is ρ^{-1} and its spectral norm is p^{-1/(p−1)}ρ^{-1}. d commutes with the restriction maps between annuli of different radii and is continuous for the Fréchet topology of each annulus ring and the LF topology of R. The module of continuous differentials of R over K (resp. of R^int over O_K) is free of rank one on dt, with df = (df/dt) dt; connections on modules over these rings are automatically integrable. ker(d/dt on R) = K and R/(d/dt)R = K·t^{-1}. For a Frobenius lift σ: d(σ(f))/dt = (dσ(t)/dt)·σ(df/dt), and dσ(t)/dt ∈ π R^int (so dσ ≡ 0 modulo π).
hypotheses: Characteristic 0 is used for ker d = K and for the cokernel computation; the norm bounds use only |i| ≤ 1 for integers i.
proofSteps: Termwise differentiation preserves each convergence condition since |i c_i| ρ^{i−1} ≤ ρ^{-1}|c_i|ρ^i; equality at t^i with p ∤ i gives the operator norm; |(d/dt)^s f|_ρ ≤ |s!| ρ^{-s}|f|_ρ with equality at f = t^s (the coefficients s!·C(i,s) have C(i,s) ∈ Z), and lim_s (|s!| ρ^{-s})^{1/s} = p^{-1/(p−1)}ρ^{-1} (overview Definitions 5.1.1-5.1.2).
Compatibility with restriction and continuity follow from the uniform bound on each circle.
Continuous differentials: slope filtrations revisited Example 7.1.3 and the monodromy paper Section 2.5 (Ω^1_R free on du with d(Σ x_i u^i) = Σ i x_i u^{i−1} du).

Kernel and cokernel: a Laurent series with Σ i c_i t^{i−1} = 0 has c_i = 0 for i ≠ 0; Σ_{i ≠ −1} c_i t^i has the primitive Σ c_i t^{i+1}/(i+1), which converges on the same annulus because |1/(i+1)| ≤ |i+1| grows at most linearly in |i| while |c_i|ρ^i decays geometrically on every closed sub-annulus (overview Example 4.1.11).

nodes.title: Two Frobenius lifts differ by a convergent Taylor series; dependence on the coordinate
nodes.statement: Let σ_1, σ_2 be Frobenius lifts on R^int with the same σ_K. Then δ = σ_2(t) − σ_1(t) ∈ π R^int and for every f ∈ R: σ_2(f) = Σ_{n≥0} δ^n · σ_1((1/n!) d^n f/dt^n), the series converging in R (in R^int, R^bd, E for f in these rings). More generally, for t' ∈ R^int with t' − t ∈ π R^int, the substitution t ↦ t' is given by the convergent Taylor series f ↦ Σ_n (t' − t)^n (1/n!) d^n f/dt^n. Hence the standard lift for the coordinate t' (t' ↦ t'^q) and the standard lift for t (t ↦ t^q) are related by this formula; ring-level Frobenius invariants such as H^0 of the rank-one σ-module R(n) for n < 0 depend on the choice of σ when k((t)) is imperfect.
hypotheses: σ_1 and σ_2 agree on K; the coordinate change is required to reduce to t modulo (π, t^2).
proofSteps: δ ∈ π R^int because σ_i(t) ≡ t^q mod π.

Convergence: |(1/n!) d^n f/dt^n|_ρ ≤ ρ^{-n}|f|_ρ (binomial coefficients are integers), σ_1 rescales Gauss norms by ρ ↦ ρ^{1/q} near the boundary, and |δ|_ρ ≤ |π| near the boundary; so the n-th term is bounded by (|π|ρ^{-1})^n |f| on a thin annulus.

Both sides are continuous σ_K-semilinear ring endomorphisms (the right side is multiplicative by the Leibniz rule for divided derivatives) agreeing on K and on t, hence equal by the uniqueness part of the Frobenius-lift node.

The same argument with σ_1 replaced by the identity gives the coordinate-change formula; this is the ring case of the Taylor map of Kedlaya's Swan conductors I, Definition 2.6.2, and of the Taylor isomorphism of the overview, Remark 4.1.9.

Dependence of H^0(R(n)) on σ: slope filtrations revisited Remark 3.3.6 (for O = Z_p and q = p the standard lift gives H^0(R(−1)) = 0, while the cyclotomic lift gives log(1+t) ∈ H^0(R(−1)), since σ(log(1+t)) = p·log(1+t)).

nodes.title: Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth O_K-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)
nodes.statement: Let O_K be a complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic 0 with uniformiser π and residue field k containing F_q, and σ_K a Frobenius lift on K (continuous, σ_K(O_K) ⊆ O_K, reducing to x ↦ x^q). Let S be a smooth finitely generated O_K-algebra and S† its weak completion (Monsky-Washnitzer; AdicSpacesPartII:F1), so that S†/πS† = S/πS =: S̄ is smooth over k. Then there is a ring endomorphism φ of S†, σ_K-semilinear over O_K, with φ(x) − x^q ∈ πS† for all x ∈ S†. It extends to a K-(semi)linear endomorphism of S† ⊗ K preserving S†, and it is finite flat. When k = F_q and σ_K = id (for instance K finite over Q_p with residue field F_q), φ is an O_K-algebra endomorphism with φ(x) − x^q ∈ πS†, i.e. AlgHom.IsArithFrobAt φ (πS†) holds. Lifts are not unique; two of them are homotopic (next node).
hypotheses: S smooth and of finite type over O_K; S† is the Monsky-Washnitzer weak completion (the subring of the π-adic completion of elements Σ_j p_j(x_1, …, x_n) with p_j ∈ π^j O_K[X] of degree ≤ λ(j+1)).
k need not be finite; for k ⊋ F_q the lift is σ_K-semilinear (a K-linear map S†^{σ_K} → S† lifting the relative Frobenius).
proofSteps: S† is a very smooth lift of S̄ in the category of weakly complete O_K-algebras: for every surjection B → C of weakly complete O_K-algebras, every map S† → C lifts to S† → B (Arabia, Theorem 3.3.2(b), deduced from his Theorem 2.1.2(b); no Artin approximation is needed).

The q-power map on S̄ is a morphism of k-algebras S̄ ⊗_{k,σ} k → S̄ (for k = F_q, an F_q-algebra endomorphism of S̄). Base-changing S† along σ_K gives a very smooth weakly complete algebra S†^{σ_K} with reduction S̄ ⊗_{k,σ} k.

Arabia, Theorem 3.3.4(a): a morphism of reductions out of a very smooth algebra lifts; applied with target B = S† and C = S̄ this gives φ. (Alternatively van der Put, Theorem 2.4.4(ii), via the Artin approximation property of O_K⟨t⟩†.)
Finite flatness: the q-power map on the smooth k-scheme Spec S̄ is finite flat, and flatness lifts (Kedlaya, finiteness paper, Remark 3.2.4 and Lemma 2.2.3).
Explicit examples: S = O_K[x] with φ(x) = x^q; for a hyperelliptic curve y^2 = Q(x) with the points y = 0 and ∞ removed, Kedlaya's formula y^σ = y^p (1 + (Q(x)^σ − Q(x)^p)/Q(x)^p)^{1/2}.
acceptance: S = O_K[x, x^{-1}]: φ(x) = x^q defines a lift, and φ(x) = x^q(1 + πx) does too; they differ.

Coleman's use: for a good-reduction pair (X, D) over O_K with residue field F_q, the dagger algebra of the complement of D admits an O_K-linear lift of the q-power Frobenius (ColemanIntegration L1/frobenius-lift).
The completion O_K⟨x⟩ also has Frobenius lifts, but its de Rham cohomology is wrong (completion-versus-overconvergence node); the theorem is about the weak completion.

nodes.title: Two lifts with the same reduction are homotopic and induce chain-homotopic maps of overconvergent de Rham complexes
nodes.statement: Let S† be the weak completion of a smooth finitely generated O_K-algebra, B† a weakly complete finitely generated O_K-algebra, and φ_0, φ_1: S† → B† two O_K-algebra maps with φ_0 ≡ φ_1 modulo π (for example two Frobenius lifts of S̄ when k = F_q, with B† = S†). Then (a) there is an O_K-algebra map h: S† → B†⟨T⟩† (the weak completion of B†[T]) with p_0∘h = φ_0 and p_1∘h = φ_1, where p_i: B†⟨T⟩† → B† sends T to i; (b) the induced maps φ_{0*}, φ_{1*}: Ω^•_{S†} ⊗ K → Ω^•_{B†} ⊗ K of overconvergent de Rham complexes are chain homotopic, a homotopy being δ = integration ∫_0^1 dT on the summand B†⟨T⟩† dT ∧ Ω^{•−1}_{B†} (and 0 on B†⟨T⟩† ⊗ Ω^•_{B†}), composed with h_*; (c) hence φ_{0*} = φ_{1*} on H^i(Ω^•_{S†} ⊗ K) for all i. In particular the Frobenius endomorphism of Monsky-Washnitzer cohomology H^i_MW(S̄/K) induced by a Frobenius lift does not depend on the lift, and H^i_MW(S̄/K) is functorial in S̄.
hypotheses: Same setting as the existence node; semilinear lifts are handled by base change along σ_K.
proofSteps: (a) Arabia, Théorème 3.3.4(b): morphisms out of a very smooth algebra whose reductions are homotopic (here equal) are homotopic in the category of weakly complete algebras, via B†⟨T⟩†. (Van der Put, Theorem 2.4.4(iii), constructs h by Artin approximation from h̄(a) = φ_0(a) + (φ_1(a) − φ_0(a))S/π with S = πT.)

(b) Van der Put, proof of Theorem 2.4.4(iii): Ω^q(B†⟨T⟩†) ⊗ K is the direct sum of B†⟨T⟩† ⊗ Ω^q(B†) ⊗ K and B†⟨T⟩† dT ∧ Ω^{q−1}(B†) ⊗ K; with δ as stated, p_1^* − p_0^* = dδ + δd. Integration ∫_0^1 of an overconvergent series Σ b_n T^n is Σ b_n/(n+1), convergent because |1/(n+1)| grows polynomially.
(c) Chain-homotopic maps agree on cohomology; functoriality: van der Put Corollary 2.4.5.
acceptance: For S = O_K[x] with φ_0(x) = x^q and φ_1(x) = x^q + π: h(x) = x^q + πT; on H^1(O_K⟨x⟩† ⊗ K) = 0 there is nothing to check, and on the Gm example S = O_K[x, x^{-1}] with φ_0(x) = x^q, φ_1(x) = x^q(1 + πx): both induce multiplication by q on H^1 = K·dx/x.
ColemanIntegration L1/frobenius-lift-independence (a) consumes (c).

nodes.title: Differential (∇-)modules over annuli, the Robba ring and differential fields
nodes.statement: Let (A, ∂) be one of: the ring of functions on an annulus A(I) = {|t| ∈ I} over K, the Robba ring R, R^bd or E, with ∂ = d/dt (the RD.0 derivation); R^int or O_E with ∂ = d/dt (O_K-linear); or a differential field (F, ∂) of characteristic 0 (for example F_ρ, the completion of K(t) for the ρ-Gauss norm). A ∇-module (differential module) over A is a finite free A-module M with a connection ∇: M → M ⊗_A Ω^1_A = M·dt, i.e. an additive map D = ∇_{d/dt}: M → M with D(fv) = f·D(v) + ∂(f)·v; D is K-linear (O_K-linear) and integrability is automatic since Ω^2 = 0. Morphisms are A-linear maps commuting with D. Constructions: M ⊕ N; M ⊗ N with D(v ⊗ w) = Dv ⊗ w + v ⊗ Dw; the dual M^∨ with (Dλ)(v) = ∂(λ(v)) − λ(Dv); internal Hom; H^0(M) = ker D, H^1(M) = coker D; Ext^i(M, N) = H^i(M^∨ ⊗ N) for i = 0, 1 (Yoneda). On the boundary: the category M_K of ∇-modules on A[r, 1) for some r, with morphisms defined on some smaller A[r', 1) (direct limit over r → 1), is equivalent to the category of ∇-modules over R. Over R (a Bézout domain) finite projective modules are free, and sub-∇-modules are saturated.
hypotheses: K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 (for the equivalence with modules over R and the freeness on half-open annuli).
Over a differential field, 'finite free' means finite dimensional.
Over a higher-dimensional base integrability would be an extra condition; here there is one derivation.
proofSteps: Definition as in the overview, Definition 4.1.1 (coherent locally free sheaves with connection on A[r, 1)) and Remark 4.1.4 (it suffices to give the action of d/dt).

Equivalence with finite free R-modules: vector bundles on half-open annuli |π|^s ≤ |t| < 1 are free over the ring of functions (RD.0 vector-bundle theorem), and a direct limit of such is a finite free module over R = ∪ (functions on annuli).
Saturation of sub-∇-modules: overview Remark 4.1.5 (a ∇-submodule is a locally free subsheaf).
Tensor, dual, Hom and the Yoneda identification Ext^i = H^i(M^∨ ⊗ N): overview Definition 4.1.10.
acceptance: Trivial module (R, d/dt): H^0 = K·1 and H^1 = K·dt/t.
Rank one with D(e) = (a/t)e, a ∈ Z: isomorphic to the trivial module via e ↦ t^{-a}e.
The unipotent module with basis e_1, e_2, D(e_1) = 0, D(e_2) = e_1/t is a nonsplit extension of the trivial module by itself.

nodes.title: Twisted polynomials F{T} and cyclic vectors
nodes.statement: For a differential ring (F, ∂), F{T} is the noncommutative ring of polynomials Σ_{i≥0} a_i T^i (a_i ∈ F) with multiplication determined by T·a = a·T + ∂(a). A differential module V over F is the same as a left F{T}-module structure extending the F-module structure (T acting by D). A cyclic vector of V (rank n) is v ∈ V with v, Dv, …, D^{n−1}v a basis of V; it gives an isomorphism V ≅ F{T}/F{T}P for a unique monic P ∈ F{T} of degree n (D^n v = −Σ_{i<n} a_i D^i v). For F with a nonarchimedean norm, the Newton polygon of P = Σ a_i T^i is the lower convex hull of {(−i, v(a_i))} (v = −log|·|); it is additive under products only for slopes less than −log|∂|_F. The opposite ring of F{T} is the twisted polynomial ring for −∂ and corresponds to duals.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0 whenever cyclic vectors are used; the norm, when present, is nonarchimedean with |∂|_F < ∞.
proofSteps: Construction: F{T} is an Ore extension; associativity is checked on generators.
Cyclic vector ⇒ presentation: the map F{T} → V, Q ↦ Q·v, is surjective with kernel the left ideal generated by the monic minimal relation P.
Newton polygon additivity range: Swan conductors I, Definition 1.1.8, citing the Kedlaya book and Robba; Kedlaya-Xiao Definition 1.3.1.
acceptance: F{T}/F{T}(T − f) is the rank-one module with D(e) = f e.

nodes.title: Cyclic vector lemma for differential modules over a differential field of characteristic 0 with nonzero derivation
nodes.statement: Let (F, ∂) be a differential field of characteristic 0 whose derivation is not identically zero. Then every finite-dimensional differential module V over F has a cyclic vector; hence V ≅ F{T}/F{T}P with P monic of degree dim V. The hypothesis ∂ ≠ 0 is necessary: if ∂ = 0 on F and V = F^2 with D = 0, then Dv = 0 for every v, so V has no cyclic vector. This applies to F_ρ (completion of K(t) for |·|_ρ, ∂ = d/dt) and to Frac of the ring of functions on an annulus.
hypotheses: char F = 0 and ∂ ≠ 0 (equivalently F ≠ its field of constants C).
No completeness or norm is needed.
proofSteps: Case of algebraically closed constants: Magid, Corollary 1 (via the Picard-Vessiot closure: v is cyclic iff v̂: Hom_diff(V, R) → R is injective, and such injections exist when C ≠ F).

Reduction of the general case: the constant field C of F is algebraically closed in F (an element algebraic over C has derivative 0), so F' = F ⊗_C C^alg is a field with constants C^alg; choose a cyclic vector v' = Σ c'_j ⊗ w_j (w_j ∈ V, c'_j ∈ C^alg) of V ⊗_F F'. The determinant of (v, Dv, …, D^{n−1}v) for v = Σ c_j w_j with c_j ∈ C is a polynomial in the c_j with coefficients in F, nonzero because it is nonzero at (c'_j); as C ⊇ Q is infinite it is nonzero at some point of C^m, giving a cyclic vector of V.

Alternative elementary route: Katz's explicit formula (a cyclic vector among the vectors c(a) = Σ_j ((t − a)^j/j!) Σ_k (−1)^k C(j,k) D^k(e_{j−k}) for all but finitely many constants a, where ∂t = 1); Katz's paper was not read (gap).
acceptance: Over F_ρ with ∂ = d/dt the unipotent rank-two module D(e_1) = 0, D(e_2) = e_1/t has cyclic vector e_2: e_2, De_2 = e_1/t is a basis.
Non-example: F with ∂ = 0 and V = F^2 with D = 0 has no cyclic vector (the printed statements in Swan conductors I, Lemma 1.1.5 and Kedlaya-Xiao, Lemma 1.2.4 omit ∂ ≠ 0; see sourceIssues).

nodes.title: Spectral norm of ∂ on a differential module over a complete nonarchimedean differential field
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0 complete for a nonarchimedean norm, with a derivation ∂ of finite operator norm |∂|_F, and let V be a nonzero differential module over F. The spectral norm |∂|_{V,sp} = lim_{s→∞} |D^s|_V^{1/s} for any F-compatible norm |·|_V on V; it does not depend on the norm. If D^s acts on a basis via the matrix D_s (D_0 = I, D_{s+1} = ∂(D_s) + D_s·G, G = D_1), then max{|∂|_{F,sp}, |∂|_{V,sp}} = max{|∂|_{F,sp}, lim sup_s |D_s|^{1/s}} (sup norm on entries), and |∂|_{V,sp} ≥ |∂|_{F,sp}. For an isometric embedding F → F' of complete differential fields, |∂|_{V⊗F', sp} = max{|∂|_{F',sp}, |∂|_{V,sp}}.
hypotheses: F complete nonarchimedean of characteristic 0; |∂|_F < ∞.
Norms on the finite-dimensional V are all equivalent (Schneider, Proposition 4.13, as cited).
proofSteps: Independence of the norm: equivalence of norms on finite-dimensional spaces over a complete field (Swan conductors I, Definition 1.1.7).
Matrix formula: Christol-Dwork Proposition 1.3 (independence of the basis) with the Leibniz formula (4) for D^s(H x); Swan conductors I, (1.1.7.1).
Scalar extension: Kedlaya-Xiao Remark 1.2.7.
acceptance: F = F_ρ, ∂ = d/dt: |∂|_F = ρ^{-1} (operator norm) and |∂|_{F,sp} = p^{-1/(p−1)}ρ^{-1}.

nodes.title: Christol-Dwork: the spectral norm from the Newton polygon of a cyclic presentation
nodes.statement: Let F be a complete nonarchimedean differential field of characteristic 0 and V ≅ F{T}/F{T}P a differential module with a cyclic presentation. Let s be the lesser of −log|∂|_F and the least slope of the Newton polygon of P. Then max{|∂|_F, |∂|_{V,sp}} = e^{−s}. In particular, if the least slope r of P is < −log|∂|_F then |∂|_{V,sp} = e^{−r}.
hypotheses: Same as the spectral-norm node; the Newton polygon uses v = −log|·|.
proofSteps: Christol-Dwork, Théorème 1.5 (attributed to Dwork, Katz, Turrittin), or Kedlaya's book Theorem 6.5.3 (not public) as cited by Kedlaya-Xiao: compare the recursion D^{s} on the cyclic basis with the Newton polygon of P using the operator-norm bound (6) of Christol-Dwork.
acceptance: Rank one P = T − f: the least slope is v(f), so max(|∂|_F, |∂|_{V,sp}) = max(|∂|_F, |f|).
Dwork exponential at ρ < p^{-1/(p−1)}: P = T + πt^{-2} on F_ρ gives |∂|_{V,sp} = |π|ρ^{-2}.

nodes.title: Robba's factorisation of twisted polynomials and the decomposition by subsidiary radii
nodes.statement: Let F be complete. (a) Every monic twisted polynomial P ∈ F{T} factors uniquely as P = P_+ P_m ⋯ P_1 with P_i monic of the single slope r_i, r_1 < ⋯ < r_m < −log|∂|_F, and P_+ monic with all slopes ≥ −log|∂|_F. (b) Put r_0 = ω|∂|_F^{-1}. Every differential module V decomposes uniquely as V = V_+ ⊕ ⊕_{r<r_0} V_r where V_r has pure radii r (all Jordan-Hölder constituents have generic radius r) and V_+ has all subsidiary radii ≥ r_0. (c) If V ≅ F{T}/F{T}P, the multiplicity of s < −log|∂|_F as a slope of P equals the multiplicity of ωe^s among the subsidiary radii of V.
hypotheses: F complete nonarchimedean of characteristic 0; ω = p^{-1/(p−1)}.
proofSteps: (a) Hensel's lemma for twisted polynomials (Robba), Swan conductors I Proposition 1.1.10.
(b) Choose a cyclic vector (cyclic-vector lemma), apply (a) in F{T} and in the opposite ring, and split V accordingly (Kedlaya-Xiao Proposition 1.3.4).
(c) Combine (a) with Christol-Dwork (Kedlaya-Xiao Remark 1.3.5).
acceptance: For V = V_1 ⊕ V_2 with V_i rank one of different radii, the decomposition recovers the V_i.
The trivial module has V = V_+.

sources.excerpt: Then any monic twisted polynomial P ∈ F{T} admits a unique factorization P = P_+ P_m · · · P_1
Then there is a unique decomposition V = V_+ ⊕ ⊕_{r<r_0} V_r of differential modules, such that V_r has pure ∂-radii r, and the subsidiary radii of V_+ are all at least r_0.
the multiplicity of any s < − log |∂|_K as a slope of the Newton polygon of P coincides with the multiplicity of ωe^s in R_∂(V).

nodes.title: Generic radius of convergence R(E, ρ), intrinsic radius T(E, ρ) and subsidiary radii
nodes.statement: Let E be a ∇-module on an annulus A(I) over K (or over R, on A[r,1) for r close to 1) and ρ ∈ I. Let F_ρ be the completion of K(t) for the ρ-Gauss norm, with ∂ = d/dt, and E_ρ = Γ(A(J), E) ⊗ F_ρ for any closed J ∋ ρ in I (independent of J). The generic radius of convergence is R(E, ρ) = ω·|∂|_{E_ρ,sp}^{-1} with ω = p^{-1/(p−1)}; equivalently, for a basis of E over the ring of functions on J with D^s acting via D_s, R(E, ρ) = min{ρ, lim inf_{s→∞} |D_s/s!|_ρ^{−1/s}}. It satisfies 0 < R(E, ρ) ≤ ρ. The intrinsic (toric) generic radius is T(E, ρ) = R(E, ρ)/ρ ∈ (0, 1] (Kedlaya's normalisation in Swan conductors I; the reciprocal of the scale |∂|_{E_ρ,sp}/|∂|_{F_ρ,sp}). The subsidiary radii S(E, ρ) form the multiset of the generic radii of the Jordan-Hölder constituents of E_ρ, counted with their dimensions; the smallest is R(E, ρ).
hypotheses: K complete of characteristic 0 with residue characteristic p, |p| = p^{-1}; ρ may be any real number in I (use Berkovich points or aligned intervals).
Christol-Dwork normalisation R(E, ρ) ≤ ρ; Kedlaya's toric T = R/ρ ≤ 1. Both are recorded; the highest break is defined with T.
proofSteps: Definition: overview Definitions 5.1.3-5.1.4 (with the misprinted 'min' in the ρ-spectral norm read as 'max', sourceIssues) and Christol-Dwork Section 2.2, where R(M, r) = ω‖δ‖_sp^{-1} = min(lim inf ‖G_s/s!‖^{-1/s}, r).
Independence of J and of the basis: spectral-norm node.
Subsidiary radii: Kedlaya-Xiao Definition 1.2.8 (radius multiset), Swan conductors I Definition 2.4.6.
acceptance: Trivial module: R(O, ρ) = ρ, T = 1.

Dwork exponential module E_π (D(w) = −π t^{-2} w, π^{p−1} = −p): D^s w = (−1)^s Σ_k L(s,k) π^k t^{−s−k} w with L(s,k) = C(s−1,k−1) s!/k! (Lah numbers); |D_s|_ρ^{1/s} → |π|ρ^{-2}, so R(E_π, ρ) = ρ^2 and T(E_π, ρ) = ρ for all ρ ∈ (0, 1). PARI/GP: the Lah closed form was verified symbolically against the recursion D_{s+1} = D_s' + D_s f for s ≤ 40, and (1/s)(−log_p |D_s|_ρ) − (1/(p−1) − 2a) at ρ = p^{-a} equals −0.012, −0.002, −0.001, −0.0002 at s = 50, 200, 800, 3200 for p = 3, a = 1/10 and is 0 for p = 5 and a ∈ {1/10, 3/10, 1/2, 9/10}.

nodes.title: Basic properties of generic radii: exact sequences, duals, tensor products, log-concavity, continuity, invariance
nodes.statement: Let E, E_1, E_2 be ∇-modules on A(I). (a) For 0 → E_1 → E → E_2 → 0 exact: R(E, ρ) = min{R(E_1, ρ), R(E_2, ρ)} and S(E, ρ) = S(E_1, ρ) ∪ S(E_2, ρ). (b) R(E^∨, ρ) = R(E, ρ) and S(E^∨, ρ) = S(E, ρ). (c) R(E_1 ⊗ E_2, ρ) ≥ min{R(E_1, ρ), R(E_2, ρ)}, with equality if R(E_1, ρ) ≠ R(E_2, ρ). (d) The function u ↦ log R(E, e^{u}) is concave on log(I) (Christol-Dwork, Proposition 2.3), hence continuous on the interior; it is continuous on every closed subinterval of I (Christol-Dwork, Théorème 2.5). (e) If φ is an automorphism of the open unit disc, there is ρ_0 < 1 with R(E, ρ) = R(φ^*E, ρ) for ρ ∈ [ρ_0, 1). (f) R(E, ρ) is unchanged by extending scalars from K to a complete extension K'.
hypotheses: E free over the rings of functions on closed subannuli (automatic for discretely valued K).
proofSteps: (a)-(c): Kedlaya-Xiao Lemma 1.2.9 (proofs cited from Kedlaya's book, Lemma 6.2.8 and Corollary 6.2.9, not public); for (a) the sub and quotient bases give a block-triangular D_s, so the lim sup of |D_s|^{1/s} is the maximum of those of the blocks (Christol-Dwork formula); (b) the dual basis has matrices −D^T-type recursion with the same growth; (c) D_s on the tensor basis is Σ C(s,i) D_i ⊗ D_{s−i}.

(d) Christol-Dwork Proposition 2.3: log |G_s|_{e^u} is convex in u (Hadamard three circles, overview Lemma 3.2.2(b)), and a lim sup of convex functions is convex; continuity at the endpoints is Théorème 2.5 (uses a cyclic basis).
(e) Overview Corollary 5.2.4 (misprint [ρ,1) for [ρ_0, 1) corrected), from the transfer theorem: φ preserves A[ρ_0, 1) and generic discs.
(f) Kedlaya-Xiao Remark 1.2.7: the spectral norm of d/dt on F_ρ and the matrices D_s are unchanged.
acceptance: For E = E_π ⊕ O: R = min(ρ^2, ρ) = ρ^2 and S = {ρ^2, ρ}.
For the Dwork exponential module, u ↦ log R(E_π, e^u) = 2u is linear (hence concave).

nodes.title: The generic radius is the radius of convergence of horizontal sections at a generic point (Dwork transfer)
nodes.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed complete extension of K with residue field transcendental over that of K, and for ρ ∈ I (in the value group) let t_ρ ∈ C be a generic point of radius ρ: |t_ρ − x| = ρ for all x ∈ K^alg with |x| ≤ ρ. Then (i) for every Laurent series x converging on A(I), |x|_ρ = |x(t_ρ)|; (ii) for r ≤ ρ the following are equivalent: R(E, ρ) ≥ r; for every z ∈ C with |z| = ρ, E admits a basis of horizontal sections on the disc |t − z| < r; E admits a basis of horizontal sections on the disc |t − t_ρ| < r. The horizontal sections are the Taylor series Σ_s ((t − z)^s/s!) D^s(v). Equivalently (Kedlaya-Xiao): pulling E back along the Taylor map x ↦ Σ ∂^s(x)T^s/s! to the disc |T| < R_∂(F_ρ), E becomes trivial on |T| < r iff R(E, ρ) ≥ r.
hypotheses: The generic point exists in a suitable extension C (spherically complete with large residue field).
proofSteps: (i) Overview Lemma 5.2.2: reduce to polynomials, factor over K^alg, and use |t_ρ − z_j| = max(ρ, |z_j|) = |t − z_j|_ρ.
(ii) Overview Proposition 5.2.3: if R(E, ρ) ≥ r the Taylor series of a basis converge on |t − z| < r; conversely convergence at the generic point gives the growth bound on D_s/s! through (i).
Kedlaya-Xiao Proposition 1.2.14 restates this as Dwork's transfer theorem.
acceptance: Trivial module: horizontal sections are constants, converging on every disc; R = ρ (the disc |t − t_ρ| < ρ is the largest disc around t_ρ avoiding 0).
Dwork exponential: the horizontal section exp(−π(t^{-1} − t_ρ^{-1}))·w converges exactly on |t − t_ρ| < ρ^2 (overview proof of Lemma 5.4.7 with n = 1 and b = 1).

sources.excerpt: For any x = Σ c_i t^i ∈ R_I and any generic point t_ρ ∈ C of radius ρ, |x|_ρ = |Σ c_i t_ρ^i|.
(c) E admits a basis of horizontal sections in the disc |t − t_ρ| < r.

nodes.title: ∇-modules solvable at the boundary (overconvergent, 'soluble en 1')
nodes.statement: A ∇-module E on A(ε, 1) is solvable at 1 if lim_{ρ→1^-} T(E, ρ) = 1, i.e. lim_{ρ→1} R(E, ρ)/ρ = 1. Equivalently (Kedlaya's 'overconvergent'), for every η ∈ (0, 1) there is r < 1 such that for every closed subinterval I ⊆ [r, 1) and v ∈ Γ(A(I), E) the sequence ((1/j!) D^j v)_j is η-null (coefficients times η^j tend to 0). Solvable modules form an abelian subcategory M^conv of M_K closed under subquotients, extensions, tensor products and duals. Solvability is invariant under automorphisms of the disc and under finite étale pullback.
hypotheses: K complete of characteristic 0.
proofSteps: The two definitions agree by the transfer theorem (overview Remark 5.1.6).
Closure properties from the generic-radius properties: subquotients and extensions by (a), duals by (b), tensor products by (c).
Invariance: generic-radius properties (e), and Swan conductors I Proposition 2.6.3 for changes of parameter.
acceptance: Trivial and unipotent modules are solvable (T = 1).
The Dwork exponential module is solvable: T(E_π, ρ) = ρ → 1.
D(e) = a e with |a| > ω is not solvable: T(E, ρ) = ω/(ρ|a|) → ω/|a| < 1.

sources.excerpt: We say E is solvable at 1 if lim_{ρ→1^−} T(E, ρ) = 1.
Let M^conv = M^conv_K be the subcategory of M consisting of overconvergent objects; this category is an abelian subcategory of M.
the condition that E be overconvergent in our sense is precisely that lim_{ρ→1} R(E, ρ)ρ^{−1} = 1

nodes.title: Christol-Dwork Frobenius antecedent theorem
nodes.statement: Fix a Frobenius lift σ_K of order 1 on K and the standard extension σ(Σ c_i t^i) = Σ σ_K(c_i) t^{pi} (or the K-linear substitution t ↦ t^p). If E is a ∇-module on A[ρ_0, 1) with R(E, ρ) > p^{-1/(p−1)}ρ for all ρ ∈ [ρ_0, 1), there is a unique ∇-module F on A[ρ_0^p, 1) with E ≅ φ^*F (pullback along t ↦ t^p) and R(F, ρ^p) = R(E, ρ)^p for ρ ∈ [ρ_0, 1). Equivalently, a differential module over F_ρ of scale < p^{1/(p−1)} has a Frobenius antecedent whose scale multiset is the p-th power of that of V.
hypotheses: K may be enlarged by a primitive p-th root of unity by uniqueness (Galois descent).
proofSteps: Christol-Dwork Théorème 5.4 (via cyclic bases and locally good bases, Sections 3-5).

Overview Theorem 6.3.2: with ζ adjoined, the maps h_i: g_i^*E → E given by the Taylor series of t ↦ ζ^i t converge by the radius hypothesis and define a (Z/p)-action; F is the invariant submodule (Galois descent), and the radius statement follows from the disc lemma for z ↦ z^p (overview Lemma 5.3.2, with the misprint corrected as in Swan conductors I, proof of Proposition 2.3.2).
Swan conductors I, Definition 2.3.1 and Proposition 2.3.2: the same construction at the level of F_ρ with scale multiset S^p.
acceptance: For E = φ^*F with F trivial, the antecedent is trivial.
For E_π at ρ close to 1: R(E_π, ρ) = ρ^2 > ωρ iff ρ > ω, so E_π has an antecedent on A[ρ_0, 1) for ρ_0 > ω, with R(F, ρ^p) = ρ^{2p}.

nodes.title: The radius function of a solvable module is concave, piecewise linear with slopes in (1/(rank E)!)Z, and linear near the boundary
nodes.statement: Let E be a ∇-module on A(ε, 1) solvable at 1. Then f(r) = log T(E, e^{−r}) on (0, −log ε) is concave, nonpositive and nonincreasing, piecewise linear with slopes in (1/(rank E)!)Z, and linear on a neighbourhood of 0. Consequently there are b ∈ Q_{≥0} and ε' ∈ [ε, 1) with T(E, ρ) = ρ^b for all ρ ∈ (ε', 1) (the printed Corollary 2.5.5 omits the shrinking to (ε', 1); see sourceIssues).
hypotheses: E solvable at 1; K discretely valued or spherically complete (for free global sections on closed subannuli).
proofSteps: Concavity: Swan conductors I Lemma 2.5.3 (log-concavity of the spectral norms, as in the generic-radius properties (d)); concave, ≤ 0 and → 0 at 0 imply nonincreasing.

Piecewise linearity away from 0: on (r_{h+1}, r_h), where ρ_h = e^{−r_h} is defined by T(E, ρ_h) = |p|^{1/(p^{h−1}(p−1))}, take an h-fold Frobenius antecedent, choose a cyclic vector over Frac of the annulus ring, and read T from the Newton polygon of the twisted polynomial (Christol-Dwork); T is piecewise of the form (|a|ρ^{i p^h})^{1/j} with j ≤ rank E.
Near the endpoints the slopes are increasing, bounded and lie in a discrete set, hence stabilise (Swan conductors I Proposition 2.5.4; compare Christol-Dwork Théorème 4.2-1).
acceptance: Trivial module: f ≡ 0, b = 0.
Dwork exponential: f(r) = −r, b = 1.
D(e) = λt^{-2}e with 0 < |λ| < |π|: T(E, ρ) = min(1, |π|ρ/|λ|); f is 0 near r = 0 and has slope −1 beyond r = log(|π|/|λ|); b = 0 on (|λ|/|π|, 1) but T(E, ρ) ≠ ρ^0 for ρ < |λ|/|π|.

sources.excerpt: The function f(r) = log T(E, e^{−r}) on (0, − log ǫ) is piecewise linear, with slopes in (1/(rank E)!)Z. Moreover, f is linear in a neighborhood of 0.
There exists b ∈ Q_{≥0} such that T(E, ρ) = ρ^b for all ρ ∈ (ǫ, 1).

nodes.title: Highest break b(E) of a solvable ∇-module (differential irregularity)
nodes.statement: For E solvable at 1, the highest break b(E) ∈ Q_{≥0} is the number with T(E, ρ) = ρ^{b(E)} (equivalently R(E, ρ) = ρ^{b(E)+1}) for all ρ < 1 sufficiently close to 1. More generally, E has highest break ≤ β (resp. ≥ β) if R(E, ρ) ≥ ρ^{β+1} (resp. ≤ ρ^{β+1}) for ρ close to 1. b(E) measures the irregularity of the connection at the boundary; it is unrelated to Frobenius slopes (RD.1 slope-and-irregularity node).
hypotheses: E solvable at 1 (so that b(E) exists by the piecewise-linearity theorem).
proofSteps: Existence and rationality: radius-function-piecewise-linear.
Stability under automorphisms of the disc: generic-radius properties (e); pullback along t ↦ t^N with p ∤ N multiplies b by N (overview Lemma 5.4.6).
acceptance: b = 0 for unipotent modules (overview Lemma 5.4.4).
b(E_π) = 1 for the Dwork exponential module (overview Lemma 5.4.7 with n = 1).

sources.excerpt: We will refer to the number b in Corollary 2.5.5 as the (differential) highest ramification break of E, denoted b(E).
we say that E has highest break ≤ β (resp. ≥ β) if there exists ρ_0 ∈ (0, 1) such that R(E, ρ) ≥ ρ^{β+1} (resp. R(E, ρ) ≤ ρ^{β+1})
We have avoided the term “slope”, which Christol and Mebkhout use by analogy with the theory of classical differential modules

nodes.title: Break decomposition of a solvable ∇-module near the boundary (Christol-Mebkhout)
nodes.statement: Let E be a ∇-module on A(ε, 1) solvable at 1. There are η ∈ (0, 1) and a unique decomposition E = ⊕_{b∈Q_{≥0}} E_b of ∇-modules on A(η, 1) such that each E_b has uniform break b: for ρ close to 1 the subsidiary radius multiset S(E_b, ρ) consists of the single element ρ^b (toric normalisation) with multiplicity rank E_b.
hypotheses: E solvable at 1; K arbitrary complete of characteristic 0 (the spherically complete case is Christol-Mebkhout's).
proofSteps: Kedlaya-Xiao, Theorem 2.6.1 (which includes Swan conductors I, Theorems 2.7.2 and 2.8.2): for M solvable at 1 on A(η_0, 1), the functions d!·F_i(M, r) (F_i = sum of the i smallest −log of intrinsic subsidiary radii) are continuous, convex and piecewise affine with integer slopes (their Theorem 2.4.4), nonnegative and tending to 0 as r → 0^+, hence linear near r = 0; their decomposition Theorem 2.5.2 then splits M on A(η, 1) according to the distinct slopes, with Σ_i b_i·rank(M_i) ∈ Z.
Historical route: Christol-Mebkhout, Corollaire 2.4-1 of 'Sur le théorème de l'indice des équations différentielles p-adiques III' (not read) for K spherically complete.

Swan conductors I Lemma 2.7.3: for general K, embed K into a spherically complete K', decompose over A_{K'}(η, 1), obtain the projector v on the highest break component, show v is defined over A_K using Robba's factorisation over A_K[ρ, ρ] and Γ(A_K[ρ,ρ], O) ∩ Γ(A_{K'}(J), O) = Γ(A_K(J), O).
acceptance: The Dwork exponential module has uniform break 1; E_π ⊕ O decomposes as E_1 = E_π, E_0 = O.

nodes.title: Break multiset and differential Swan conductor of a solvable ∇-module
nodes.statement: For E solvable at 1 of rank d, the break multiset b(E) = {b_1, …, b_d} is characterised by S(E, ρ) = {ρ^{b_1}, …, ρ^{b_d}} for ρ < 1 close to 1 (it exists by the break decomposition), and the differential Swan conductor is Swan(E) = b_1 + ⋯ + b_d. It is additive in short exact sequences, invariant under duals and automorphisms of the disc, and multiplied by N under pullback along t ↦ t^N with p ∤ N.

nodes.title: Integrality of the differential Swan conductor (p-adic Hasse-Arf)
nodes.statement: For E solvable at 1, Swan(E) is a nonnegative integer. Moreover, if E has a uniform break b then b·rank(E) ∈ Z.
hypotheses: E solvable at 1 over an annulus over K.
proofSteps: Kedlaya-Xiao Theorem 2.6.1 gives Σ_i b_i·rank(M_i) ∈ Z directly from the integrality of the slopes of F_d(M, r) (their Theorem 2.4.4(b)).
Reduce to E indecomposable over A(η, 1) for η close to 1; by the break decomposition E has a uniform break b.

In the proof of piecewise linearity, uniformity of the break forces the Newton polygon of the twisted polynomial attached to a cyclic vector of an h-fold Frobenius antecedent to have a single slope, so j can be taken equal to rank E: the slopes of r ↦ log T(E, e^{−r}) are multiples of 1/rank E, hence b·rank E ∈ Z (Swan conductors I Theorem 2.8.2; for L = K the 'eventually dominant' derivation is d/dt itself).
Alternative: Christol-Mebkhout's local index identifies Swan(E) with an index (Swan conductors I Remark 2.8.4; unread).

nodes.title: Frobenius modules (σ-modules, φ-modules) over R^int, R^bd, R, O_E, E, R^alg and their Witt-vector analogues
nodes.statement: Let A be a domain containing O_K in which π is not a zero divisor, with a ring endomorphism σ extending σ_K (A = R^int, R^bd, R, O_E, E, R_L for L/k((t)) finite separable, with a Frobenius lift; or A = Γ^alg_con, Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}], Γ^alg[π^{-1}], R^alg, W(κ, O)[π^{-1}] with the Witt Frobenius). A σ-module over A is a finite locally free A-module M with an A-linear map F: σ^*M = M ⊗_{A,σ} A → M which becomes an isomorphism after inverting π; equivalently an additive σ-semilinear F: M → M whose matrix on some (equivalently every) basis is invertible over A[π^{-1}]; equivalently a left module over the twisted polynomial ring A{σ} (F·a = σ(a)·F). Morphisms commute with F. The twist M(c) multiplies F by π^c (c ≥ 0 unless π ∈ A^×). When π is invertible: the dual M^∨ = Hom_A(M, A) with (Fλ)(Fv) = σ(λ(v)), tensor products, internal Hom M^∨ ⊗ N. H^0(M) = ker(F − 1) and H^1(M) = coker(F − 1); Ext(M_1, M_2) = H^1(M_1^∨ ⊗ M_2) is the Yoneda Ext^1. Over the Bézout rings used here finite locally free modules are free; the category is not abelian when the valuation of ℓ is nontrivial (no cokernels).
hypotheses: A Frobenius lift σ is fixed (RD.0); σ need not be bijective (it is on R^alg and Witt vector rings of perfect fields).
Slopes are measured with w(π) = 1 (Kedlaya) and refer to σ, a q-power Frobenius lift.
proofSteps: Definition 3.1.1 of slope filtrations revisited (and Section 2.5 of the monodromy paper); freeness from the Bézout property (RD.0).
Dual, tensor, twist: Definition 3.1.5. H^0, H^1 and the Yoneda identification: Definition 3.1.6 (Hartl-Pink's calculation).
Non-abelianness: Remark 3.1.3.
acceptance: Rank one A(n): basis e with F e = π^n e; H^0(A(0)) ⊇ the σ-fixed elements of O_K[π^{-1}].
For A = W(k)[1/p], k perfect, O = W(k), σ the Witt Frobenius and q = p, σ-modules are Mathlib's isocrystals WittVector.Isocrystal p k V and A(m) is StandardOneDimIsocrystal p k m.

nodes.title: Restriction and induction of Frobenius ([a]_*, [a]^*) and Frobenius pullback
nodes.statement: For a positive integer a let [a]: A{σ^a} → A{σ} be the inclusion. The pushforward [a]_* sends a σ-module (M, F) to the σ^a-module (M, F^a) (restriction along [a]); the pullback [a]^* sends a σ^a-module N to A{σ} ⊗_{A{σ^a}} N (rank multiplied by a). They are adjoint (in both directions), [a]^*[a']^* = [aa']^*, [a]_*[a']_* = [aa']_*, [a]_*(M(c)) = ([a]_*M)(ac), and [a]_*[a]^*(A(c)) ≅ A(c)^{⊕a}. If the residue field of O contains an algebraic closure of F_q and L_i denotes the fixed field of O[π^{-1}] under σ^i, then for σ-modules over Γ_an,con: H^0([a]_*M) = H^0(M) ⊗_{L_1} L_a, and M ≅ N iff [a]_*M ≅ [a]_*N. Frobenius pullback: σ^*(M, F) = (M ⊗_{A,σ} A, F ⊗ 1), and F: σ^*M → M is a morphism of σ-modules which is an isomorphism after inverting π; for a ∇-module E over R, σ^*E carries the pulled-back connection, and a Frobenius structure is a horizontal isomorphism σ^*E ≅ E.

nodes.title: Degree, rank and slope μ(M) = deg(M)/rank(M) of a σ-module
nodes.statement: For a rank-one σ-module M over Γ_an,con (any ℓ, in particular R), deg(M) is the integer n with M ⊗ R^alg ≅ R^alg(n); concretely, if F v = x v on a generator, x is a unit of Γ_an,con, hence lies in Γ_con[π^{-1}], and deg(M) = w(x) (π-adic valuation, w(π) = 1). For M of rank n, deg(M) = deg(∧^n M) and μ(M) = deg(M)/rank(M) for M ≠ 0. The same definition applies over Γ_con[π^{-1}] (R^bd) and Γ[π^{-1}] (E), where deg(M) = w(det A) for the matrix A of F on any basis. Degree is additive in short exact sequences, deg([a]_*M) = a·deg M, deg([a]^*N) = deg N, μ([a]_*M) = a·μ(M), μ([a]^*N) = μ(N)/a; if N ⊆ M is a σ-submodule of the same rank then deg N ≥ deg M, with equality iff N = M (and equality is automatic when v_ℓ is trivial).
hypotheses: Sign convention: 'arithmetic' (Katz, Kedlaya): the twist A(1), F = π σ, has slope +1; it is opposite to the vector-bundle convention (Kedlaya Remark 3.4.6).
proofSteps: Definition 3.4.1 using the rank-one classification over R^alg and the units theorem.
Lemma 3.4.2 (reduce to rank one via exterior powers, then H^0 computations), Lemma 3.4.3 (∧^{n_1+n_2}M ≅ ∧^{n_1}M_1 ⊗ ∧^{n_2}M_2), Proposition 3.4.4.
Over Γ_con[π^{-1}] or Γ[π^{-1}]: change of basis replaces det A by det(U)^{-1} det A σ(det U), whose valuation is unchanged.

nodes.title: Semistable and stable σ-modules, HN filtrations, HN polygons and descent of subobjects
nodes.statement: A σ-module M over Γ_an,con is semistable if μ(M) ≤ μ(N) for every nonzero σ-submodule N, and stable if μ(M) < μ(N) for every nonzero proper N (inequalities reversed relative to vector bundles). A semistable filtration is an exhaustive filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ M_l = M by saturated σ-submodules with M_i/M_{i−1} semistable of slope s_i; it is a Harder-Narasimhan (HN) filtration if s_1 < ⋯ < s_l; an HN filtration is unique if it exists (M_1 is the largest σ-submodule of minimal slope). The Newton polygon of a multiset S of n reals is the graph of the piecewise linear function on [0, n] from 0 with slope on [i−1, i] the i-th smallest element; P lies above P' if no vertex of P is below P' and the endpoints agree. The slope multiset of a semistable filtration consists of the μ(M_i/M_{i−1}) with multiplicity rank(M_i/M_{i−1}); for the HN filtration this is the HN polygon. The HN polygon lies above the polygon of any semistable filtration. A^{⊕n}(c) is semistable of slope c, [a]^*(A(c)) is semistable of slope c/a and stable if gcd(a, c) = 1. For an injection R → S of domains with compatible σ, a saturated σ-submodule N_S ⊆ M ⊗ S descends to R if N_S = N ⊗ S for a saturated σ-submodule N ⊆ M; over a Bézout domain R, N_S descends iff ∧^d N_S does (d = rank N_S).
hypotheses: Γ_an,con for any ℓ; for descent R Bézout.
proofSteps: Definitions 3.4.5, 3.5.1-3.5.3; Proposition 3.5.4 (comparison of polygons, via the ranks d_l = rank(M'_l + M_i) − rank(M'_{l−1} + M_i)); Lemmas 3.4.8-3.4.9 (via H^0 of twists over R^alg); Definition 3.6.1 and Lemma 3.6.2 (descent via exterior powers).
acceptance: A(0) ⊕ A(1) is not semistable (A(0) is a submodule of smaller slope); its HN filtration is 0 ⊂ A(0) ⊂ A(0) ⊕ A(1) with polygon slopes 0, 1.
M_{1,2} is stable of slope 1/2 and has HN polygon with slopes 1/2, 1/2.

nodes.statement: For coprime integers c, d with d > 0, M_{c,d} = [d]^*(A(c)) is the σ-module with basis e_1, …, e_d and F e_i = e_{i+1} (i < d), F e_d = π^c e_1 (over A = R^alg, Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}], Γ^alg[π^{-1}], W(κ, O)[π^{-1}] for κ algebraically closed); it is stable of slope c/d. nodes.title: Existence of eigenvectors and of embeddings of twists over R^alg
nodes.statement: Let R^alg be the extended Robba ring (v_ℓ nontrivial). (a) Every nonzero σ-module over R^alg contains an eigenvector: v ≠ 0 with F v = π^c v for some integer c. (b) For a σ-module M of rank n over R^alg there is c_0 such that for every c ≥ c_0 there is an injection R^alg(c)^{⊕n} → M, and c_1 such that for every c ≤ c_1 there is an injection M → R^alg(c)^{⊕n}.
hypotheses: v_ℓ nontrivial with value group dense (true for ℓ^alg); residue field algebraically closed.
proofSteps: (a) Proposition 4.2.2 (after the monodromy paper Proposition 4.8 and Hartl-Pink Theorem 4.1): split x ∈ Γ_{[r,r]} into Teichmüller parts a(x), b(x) of valuation < d and ≥ d for a suitable d in the value group, define f(v) = π^{-m}b(v) − F^{-1}(a(v)), iterate v_{l+1} = v_l + f(F v_l − π^m v_l) from v_0 = π^{-m}[x]e_1 + [x^{1/q}]F^{-1}e_1; the iteration contracts for w_r, the limit is nonzero, and F v = π^m v propagates v to M_{[r/q^i, r]} for all i.
(b) Lemma 4.2.3: induction on rank using (a), rank-one classification, and splitting of 0 → R(m) → N → R(c_0)^{n−1} → 0 by the Ext computation for standard modules; (b) by duality.
acceptance: M_{1,2} over R^alg has the 2-eigenvector e_1 (F^2 e_1 = π e_1) and contains eigenvectors of slope c for every integer c ≥ 1 but none of slope c ≤ 0 (Corollary 4.1.4).

nodes.title: Every σ-module over Γ_an,con has a Harder-Narasimhan filtration
nodes.statement: Let M be a nonzero σ-module over Γ_an,con (for any ℓ; in particular over R and R^alg). The slopes of nonzero σ-submodules of M are bounded below; the minimum is attained, and any σ-submodule of minimal slope is semistable. Consequently M admits a (unique) Harder-Narasimhan filtration.
hypotheses: Γ_an,con as in RD.0; enlarging ℓ to an algebraically closed complete field with nontrivial valuation is allowed in the proof.
proofSteps: Proposition 4.2.4: after base change to R^alg (nontrivial valuation), M injects into R^alg(c)^{⊕n} (eigenvector node (b)); semistability of R^alg(c)^{⊕n} bounds μ(N) ≥ c; slopes have denominators ≤ n, so the minimum is attained; a submodule of minimal slope is semistable.
Proposition 4.2.5: the sum of two submodules of minimal slope s_1 is a quotient of their (semistable) direct sum, so has slope s_1; the maximal such is M_1; repeat with M/M_1.
acceptance: For a semistable M the HN filtration is 0 ⊂ M.

nodes.statement: Over R^alg with v_ℓ nontrivial: (a) y ↦ Σ_{i∈Z}[y^{q^{-i}}]π^i is a bijection from {y ∈ ℓ^alg : v(y) > 0} onto H^0(R^alg(−1)). (b) For m > 0, every nonzero class in H^1(R^alg(m)) has a representative x ∈ Γ^alg_con with v_n(x) = v_{m−1}(x) for n ≥ m and, for each n ≥ 0, v_n(x) = ∞ or v_n(x) < 0. (c) For d > 0 and x ∈ H^1([d]^*(R^alg(d+1))) there is a nonzero y ∈ H^0(R^alg(−1)) pairing with x to zero in H^1([d]^*(R^alg(1))). (d) Every short exact sequence 0 → M_{1,d} → M → M_{−1,1} → 0 of σ-modules over R^alg splits off an eigenvector of slope 0: M contains an eigenvector of slope 0; dually for 0 → M_{1,1} → M → M_{−1,d} → 0, M^∨ contains an eigenvector of slope 0. (e) For c + c' ≤ 2c'' and 0 → M_{c,1} → M → M_{c',1} → 0, M contains an eigenvector of slope c''.
hypotheses: v_ℓ nontrivial; residue field algebraically closed; π fixed by σ.
proofSteps: (a) Lemma 4.3.1: comparison of Teichmüller presentations of y^σ and πy.
(b) Lemma 4.3.2: positioning of H^1 classes by the plus-minus-zero presentation and an explicit correction sequence.

(c) Lemma 4.3.3: reduces to the system a^σ = πa, πb^{σ^n} = b − ax with x a sum of strong semiunits of negative valuation; this is the monodromy paper's Lemma 4.12, proved there by a piecewise-linear analysis of h(m) = min_{i,l} f(i, l, m) (not repeated in slope filtrations revisited).
(d) Proposition 4.3.4: the connecting map H^0(M_{−1,1}) = H^0(R(−1)) → H^1(M_{1,d}) is pairing with the extension class, not injective by (c); Corollary 4.3.5 by duality.
(e) Corollary 4.3.6: twist to c'' = 0, reduce to c' = −c using Hom computations, and induct on c.
