nodes.title: Existence of standard submodules of small slope (the induction (A_n), (B_n))
nodes.statement: Assume v_ℓ nontrivial. For every n ≥ 1: (A_n) for every a ≥ 1 and every σ^a-module M over R^alg with rank M ≤ n and deg M ≤ 0, M contains an eigenvector of slope 0; (B_n) for every a ≥ 1 and every σ^a-module M over R^alg with rank M ≤ n, M contains a saturated σ^a-submodule which is standard of slope ≤ μ(M).
hypotheses: v_ℓ nontrivial; R^alg as in RD.0.
proofSteps: (A_1), (B_1): rank-one classification.

(A_{n−1}) + (B_{n−1}) ⇒ (A_n) (Lemma 4.4.2): assuming no slope-0 eigenvector, an eigenvector gives 0 → M_{c,1} → M → N → 0 with c > 0 minimal; the slope-c'' extension lemma forces c = 1; then (B_{n−1}) applied to N and the dual extension lemma produce a slope-0 eigenvector, a contradiction.

(A_n) + (B_{n−1}) ⇒ (B_n) (Lemma 4.4.3): with b = n/gcd(n, deg M), (A_n) for [b]_*M twisted gives a b-eigenvector of slope deg M/n, hence a map M_{bc/n,b} → M; its saturated image has average slope ≤ μ(M); conclude by (B_{n−1}) or by Lemma 3.4.2 when the image has full rank.

nodes.title: Dieudonné-Manin classification over a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field
nodes.statement: Let κ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, O finite totally ramified over W(k_0) ⊆ W(κ), R = W(κ) ⊗_{W(k_0)} O (a complete DVR with residue field κ), and σ a q-power Frobenius lift on R fixing π (after enlarging O). Every σ-module M over F = R[π^{-1}] is isomorphic to a direct sum of standard σ-modules M_{c,d}; the multiset of slopes c/d (each with multiplicity d) does not depend on the decomposition; there is a unique decomposition M = ⊕_s M_s into isoclinic σ-submodules of pairwise distinct slopes (the slope decomposition), M_s being spanned (after a finite extension of O) by the eigenvectors of slope s; Hom(M_s, M_{s'}) = 0 for s ≠ s'. For κ = F̄_q this is the classification of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block (sign dictionary: VB0's standard block of slope d/h is M_{−d,h}); for O = W(κ) and q = p it extends Mathlib's rank-one classification WittVector.isocrystal_classification to all ranks.
hypotheses: κ algebraically closed (any cardinality, not only F̄_q); the case of a non-closed residue field gives only a canonical slope filtration after base change.
proofSteps: Monodromy paper Section 5 (R unramified over O, complete, algebraically closed residue field): Proposition 5.1 (eigenvectors over a basis of eigenvectors have the slopes of the basis), Proposition 5.2 (slopes independent of the eigenbasis), Proposition 5.3 (a module spanned by eigenvectors of one slope is isogenous to a sum of standard modules), Lemma 5.4 (eigenvectors of slope s in a cyclic module are bounded by the multiplicity of s in the Newton polygon of x^n + a_{n−1}x^{n−1} + ⋯ + a_0, and exist if it is positive; uses the solvability of σ-polynomial equations, the monodromy paper's Proposition 3.17), Proposition 5.5 (basis up to isogeny of eigenvectors after a finite extension O'/O), Theorem 5.6 (Galois descent of the span of eigenvectors of each slope).

Kedlaya's second route (slope filtrations revisited Theorem 4.5.7(a) with v_ℓ trivial, via Hahn-Mal'cev-Neumann series and Lemma 4.5.5) gives the same statement; uniqueness of the slope decomposition is Proposition 5.2.1 there.
Hom vanishing between distinct slopes: Corollary 4.1.4 with v_ℓ trivial (Notes on isocrystals (3.1.1)).
acceptance: F-matrix [[0, 1], [p, u]] with u a unit (the matrix of Kedlaya's generic example, at the level of a residue field): Newton polygon of x^2 − ux − p has slopes 0 and 1, so M ≅ M_{0,1} ⊕ M_{1,1} (PARI/GP: newtonpoly(x^2 − x − 3, 3) = [1, 0]).
Rank one: the classification is Mathlib's WittVector.isocrystal_classification.

nodes.title: Dieudonné-Manin decomposition of σ-modules over the extended Robba ring R^alg (Kedlaya)
nodes.statement: Every σ-module M over R^alg = Γ^alg_an,con (and, when v_ℓ is trivial, over W(ℓ, O)[π^{-1}]) is isomorphic to a finite direct sum ⊕_i M_{c_i,d_i} of standard σ-modules (a Dieudonné-Manin decomposition). Moreover: a σ-module over R^alg is semistable (resp. stable) iff it is ≅ M_{c,d}^{⊕n} (resp. ≅ M_{c,d}); End(M_{c,d}) is a division algebra; if M_1 is the first step of the HN filtration and d = rank M_1, then ∧^d M_1 is the first step of the HN filtration of ∧^d M; and when v_ℓ is nontrivial there is a nonzero map M_{c,d} → M iff c/d ≥ min_i c_i/d_i, and M → M_{c,d} iff c/d ≤ max_i c_i/d_i.
hypotheses: For v_ℓ nontrivial the proof below; for v_ℓ trivial see the classical Dieudonné-Manin node (the same statement over a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field).
proofSteps: Proposition 4.5.3: a semistable M contains a saturated standard submodule of slope μ(M) by (B_n); the quotient is semistable of the same slope; induct and split by the Ext computation (Corollary 4.1.4). In general take the HN filtration and split it by Corollary 4.1.4 (Ext between increasing slopes vanishes over R^alg in this direction).
Corollary 4.5.9, Proposition 4.5.10, Proposition 4.5.12 and Proposition 4.5.14 follow from the decomposition and the Hom/Ext computations.

The trivially valued case (Theorem 4.5.7(a)) is deduced by Kedlaya from the nontrivial case via Hahn-Mal'cev-Neumann series k((t^Q)) (Lemma 4.5.5); here it is imported from the classical node instead.
acceptance: M with F-matrix [[0, 1], [π, 0]] is M_{1,2}; M with F-matrix diag(1, π) is M_{0,1} ⊕ M_{1,1}.

The Dieudonné-Manin decomposition is not canonical when v_ℓ is nontrivial (Remark 4.5.11): Hom(M_{1,1}, M_{0,1}) = H^0(R^alg(−1)) ≠ 0, so the complement of M_{0,1} in M_{0,1} ⊕ M_{1,1} is not unique (e_2 + x e_1 with σ(x) = πx spans another one).

nodes.title: Frobenius slopes and Newton (HN) polygons of σ-modules: generic slopes over E and R^bd, special slopes over R
nodes.statement: Let σ be a Frobenius lift and ι_σ the RD.0 embeddings into Witt-vector rings. (a) For a σ-module M over E = Γ[π^{-1}] (or over R^bd = Γ_con[π^{-1}]), the generic slopes (generic HN polygon, generic Newton polygon) of M are the Dieudonné-Manin slopes, equivalently the HN slopes, of M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{-1}] = M ⊗ W(ℓ^alg, O)[π^{-1}] (a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field). (b) For a σ-module M over R (or over Γ_an,con for any ℓ), the absolute (special) HN slopes and the absolute HN polygon P(M) are the HN slopes and polygon of M ⊗ R^alg, which by Dieudonné-Manin are the slopes of any decomposition of M ⊗ R^alg into standard modules. (c) For M over R^bd, the special slopes are the absolute HN slopes of M ⊗ R. Slopes are rationals with denominators ≤ rank, measured with w(π) = 1 (divide by w(p) for p-adic slopes); the polygon starts at (0, 0) and ends at (rank M, deg M). For isocrystals over W(k)[1/p] (π = p, q = p) the generic slopes are the classical Newton slopes. The Bessel-type example F v_1 = v_2, F v_2 = p v_1 + u v_2 over R^bd has generic slopes 0, 1 and special slopes 1/2, 1/2.
hypotheses: The generic slopes do not depend on the choice of σ-equivariant embedding into W(ℓ^alg, O)[π^{-1}] (they are HN slopes, intrinsic to M ⊗ Γ[π^{-1}] by Galois descent of the HN filtration over Γ[π^{-1}], generic-slope node); the special slopes are intrinsic to M over R by Theorem 6.4.1 (RD.2).
proofSteps: Well-definedness: Dieudonné-Manin over R^alg and over Γ^alg[π^{-1}] plus the HN interpretation (DM slopes are HN slopes).
Endpoint: deg M equals the sum of the slopes (degree node).
The example: slope filtrations revisited Section 7.3 (generic polygon from the cyclic vector v_1 and the polynomial x^2 − ux − p; special polygon via Dwork's trick).
acceptance: PARI/GP: newtonpoly(x^2 − x − 3, 3) = [1, 0] and newtonpoly(x^2 − 5, 5) = [1/2, 1/2], the generic polygons of the σ-modules with F-matrices [[0,1],[3,1]] over W(F̄_3)[1/3] and [[0,1],[5,0]] over W(F̄_5)[1/5].

nodes.title: Pure (isoclinic) and unit-root σ-modules over R, R^bd and E
nodes.statement: A σ-module M over Γ_an,con (e.g. R) is pure or isoclinic of slope s if all its absolute HN slopes equal s; equivalently M ⊗ R^alg is semistable, equivalently M ⊗ R^alg ≅ M_{c,d}^{⊕n} with c/d = s. A σ-module M over Γ_con[π^{-1}] (R^bd) or Γ[π^{-1}] (E) is isoclinic of slope s if M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{-1}] is isoclinic of slope s (all generic slopes equal s); then M ⊗ R^alg is isoclinic of the same slope. Unit-root means isoclinic of slope 0. Isoclinic modules of a fixed slope are closed under subquotients and extensions within that slope, tensor products add slopes, duals negate them; there are no nonzero morphisms from an isoclinic module of slope s to one of slope s' < s over R.
hypotheses: Absolute slopes as in the Frobenius-slopes node; for R^bd the implication 'generically isoclinic ⇒ specially isoclinic' uses the comparison of polygons (Proposition 5.5.1, planned in RD.2 by part B).
proofSteps: Definitions 4.6.1 and 6.3.1; equivalence with semistability over R^alg by Proposition 4.5.10.
Closure and Hom vanishing: calculus of slopes (Propositions 4.6.3, 4.6.4).
acceptance: R(c) is isoclinic of slope c; M_{1,2} ⊗ R is isoclinic of slope 1/2; R(0) ⊕ R(1) is not isoclinic.

sources.excerpt: We say M is pure (or isoclinic) of slope s if the absolute HN-slopes of M are all equal to s. By Proposition 4.5.10, M is isoclinic if and only if M ⊗ R is semistable. We use the adjective unit-root to mean “isoclinic of slope 0”.
We say that M is isoclinic (of slope µ(M)) if M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{−1}] is isoclinic.
We say that E is isoclinic if the slope multisets at all points are equal to a single repeated value; if that value is 0, we also say that E is unit-root or étale.

nodes.title: Calculus of slopes: direct sums, tensor products, exterior powers, restriction of Frobenius, twists, Hom vanishing
nodes.statement: Let M, M' be σ-modules over Γ_an,con with absolute HN slopes c_1, …, c_m and c'_1, …, c'_n. Then the absolute HN slopes of (a) M ⊕ M' are c_1, …, c_m, c'_1, …, c'_n; (b) M ⊗ M' are the c_i + c'_j (1 ≤ i ≤ m, 1 ≤ j ≤ n) (printed as c_i c'_j; see sourceIssues); (c) ∧^d M are the c_{i_1} + ⋯ + c_{i_d}, i_1 < ⋯ < i_d; (d) [a]_*M are a c_1, …, a c_m; (e) M(b) are c_1 + b, …, c_m + b; (f) M^∨ are −c_1, …, −c_m. If every absolute slope of M_1 is less than every absolute slope of M_2 then Hom(M_1, M_2) = 0. The same holds for generic slopes of σ-modules over Γ_con[π^{-1}] and Γ[π^{-1}].
hypotheses: σ-modules over Γ_an,con (absolute slopes) or over Γ_con[π^{-1}], Γ[π^{-1}] (generic slopes).
proofSteps: Proposition 4.6.3: tensor up to R^alg and apply [a]_* to reduce to modules with bases of eigenvectors (Dieudonné-Manin and Remark 4.5.2), where all claims are read off; (f) from M_{c,d}^∨ ≅ M_{−c,d}.
Proposition 4.6.4: tensor up to R^alg and apply the Hom criterion of Proposition 4.5.14.
Generic version: the same argument over Γ^alg[π^{-1}] with the classical Dieudonné-Manin theorem.
acceptance: Slopes of M_{1,2} ⊗ M_{1,3}: 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6 with multiplicity 6 (M_{5,6}).

sources.excerpt: (c) The absolute HN-slopes of ∧^d M are c_{i_1} + · · · + c_{i_d} for all 1 ≤ i_1 < · · · < i_d ≤ m.

nodes.title: Newton polygons of extensions; splitting criteria over R^alg
nodes.statement: For an exact sequence 0 → M_1 → M → M_2 → 0 of σ-modules over Γ_an,con: (a) P(M) ≥ P(M_1) + P(M_2) (P = absolute HN polygon, sum = union of slope multisets); (b) P(M) = P(M_1) + P(M_2) iff the sequence splits over R^alg. Over R^alg: if every slope of M_1 is ≤ every slope of M_2 the sequence splits, and the HN multiset of M is the union; a filtration of M by saturated σ-submodules with isoclinic quotients whose polygon equals the HN polygon splits.
hypotheses: Absolute polygons as in the Frobenius-slopes node.
proofSteps: (a) The HN filtrations of M_1 ⊗ R^alg and M_2 ⊗ R^alg give a semistable filtration of M ⊗ R^alg with polygon P(M_1) + P(M_2); apply Proposition 3.5.4 (Proposition 4.7.2(a)).

(b) Induction on rank over R^alg: for standard M_1, M_2 use the Ext computation and that End(M_2) is a division algebra; in general split off a standard summand of M_1 (or dually of M_2) (Proposition 4.7.2(b)).
Corollaries 4.7.3 and 4.7.4.
acceptance: 0 → R(1) → M → R(0) → 0 over R^alg splits iff P(M) has slopes {0, 1}; the nonsplit extension (class in H^1(R^alg(1)) ≠ 0) has P(M) = {1/2, 1/2}.

sources.excerpt: (b) We have P(M) = P(M_1) + P(M_2) if and only if the exact sequence splits over R.
Suppose that the Newton polygon of the filtration coincides with the HN-polygon of M. Then the filtration splits.

nodes.title: F-stable lattices: nonnegative generic slopes versus integral models
nodes.statement: (a) A σ-module M over Γ_con[π^{-1}] (in particular over R^bd) whose generic slopes are all ≥ 0 contains an F-stable Γ_con-lattice N (R^int-lattice); if all generic slopes are 0, N can be chosen with F: σ^*N → N an isomorphism. (b) Conversely, for a σ-module M over Γ (e.g. O_E, or R^int after completion), the generic HN slopes are all ≥ 0, and they are all 0 iff F: σ^*M → M is an isomorphism. (c) The same holds over a complete DVR with algebraically closed residue field (monodromy paper Proposition 5.8: all slopes ≥ 0 ⇒ isomorphic to a σ-module defined over R).
hypotheses: Γ_con a henselian DVR (RD.0); lattices are Γ_con-submodules N with N ⊗ Γ_con[π^{-1}] = M.
proofSteps: (a) Proposition 5.1.2: over Γ^alg[π^{-1}] write M' as a sum of standard modules with nonnegative slopes; the span of standard bases is an F-stable Γ^alg-lattice; intersect with M.
(b) Proposition 5.1.3: an eigenvector's slope is min w(F v) − min w(v) ≥ 0 when the Frobenius matrix is integral; for slope 0 build an F-stable filtration with isomorphic Frobenius on graded pieces.
(c) Monodromy paper Proposition 5.8 via the cyclic-vector Newton polygon (Proposition 5.7).
acceptance: R^bd(1) has the F-stable lattice R^int·e with F = π (not an isomorphism); R^bd(−1) has no F-stable R^int-lattice (the generic slope is −1).

sources.excerpt: Let M be a σ-module over Γ_con[π^{−1}] with nonnegative generic slopes. Then M contains an F-stable Γ_con-lattice N.
Let M be a σ-module over Γ. Then the generic HN-slopes of M are all nonnegative; moreover, they are all zero if and only if F : σ^∗M → M is an isomorphism.
Let M be a σ-module over R[1/p] with all slopes nonnegative. Then M is isomorphic to a σ-module defined over R.

nodes.title: Generic HN filtration: slope decomposition over Γ^alg[π^{-1}] and descent to E = Γ[π^{-1}]
nodes.statement: (a) Every σ-module M over Γ^alg[π^{-1}] = W(ℓ^alg, O)[π^{-1}] has a unique decomposition M = P_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ P_l into isoclinic σ-submodules of distinct slopes (the slope decomposition). (b) For a σ-module M over Γ[π^{-1}] (e.g. E, or E_L), the HN filtration of M exists and its base change to Γ^alg[π^{-1}] is the HN filtration of M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{-1}]; in particular the generic HN filtration of M over E is defined over E (it need not split over E). (c) For M over Γ_con[π^{-1}] (R^bd), the reverse filtration of M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{-1}] (P_1 ⊂ P_1 ⊕ P_2 ⊂ ⋯ ordered by decreasing slope) descends to Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] (de Jong).
hypotheses: Γ[π^{-1}] = E is a complete discretely valued field with residue field k((t)) (not algebraically closed), so only the filtration, not the decomposition, descends.
proofSteps: (a) Proposition 5.2.1: existence from Dieudonné-Manin (classical), uniqueness from Hom vanishing between distinct slopes.

(b) Proposition 5.3.1: reduce by exterior powers (Lemma 3.6.2 and Proposition 4.5.12) to a rank-one first step of slope 0; with an F-stable Γ-lattice N (Frobenius-stable-lattice node), N' ∩ M'_1 is the set of π-adic limits of sequences F^l v_l, v_l ∈ N', a linear condition which descends to Γ. (Alternatively Galois descent, monodromy paper Proposition 5.10.)
(c) Lemma 5.4.1 (a slope-0 eigenvector over Γ^alg of a module with nonpositive generic slopes over Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] already lies in it) and Proposition 5.4.3.
acceptance: For M over E with F-matrix [[0, 1], [p, u]], u = t: generic HN filtration 0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ M with M_1 of slope 0 defined over E.

sources.excerpt: Then the Harder-Narasimhan filtration of M, tensored up to Γ^alg[π^{−1}], gives the Harder-Narasimhan filtration of M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{−1}].
Then the reverse filtration of M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{−1}] descends to Γ^alg_con[π^{−1}].
For any σ-module M over Γ^alg[π^{−1}], there is a unique decomposition M = P_1 ⊕ · · · ⊕ P_l

nodes.title: Reading the generic polygon from a cyclic vector or from a diagonally dominant Frobenius matrix
nodes.statement: (a) Let M be a σ-module over Γ[π^{-1}] (or over a complete DVR with algebraically closed residue field, inverted) of rank n with a cyclic vector v (v, Fv, …, F^{n−1}v a basis) and F^n v + a_{n−1}F^{n−1}v + ⋯ + a_0 v = 0. Then the generic HN polygon of M is the Newton polygon of the polynomial x^n + a_{n−1}x^{n−1} + ⋯ + a_0 (with respect to w). (b) If M over Γ^alg[π^{-1}] has a basis on which F acts by A with w(AD^{-1} − I_n) > 0 for a diagonal D, then the generic slopes are the w(D_ii), and A = U D σ(U)^{-1}-type conjugation with U ≡ I holds.
hypotheses: For (a) the reading is special to cyclic presentations; for general matrices the Newton polygon of the characteristic polynomial is not the slope polygon.
proofSteps: (a) Slope filtrations Lemma 5.2.4: over Γ^alg[π^{-1}] with integral slopes choose an eigenbasis e_i (F e_i = π^{c_i} e_i) and factor F^n + ⋯ + a_0 = (F − b_{n−1})⋯(F − b_0) with w(b_i) = c_i; the monodromy paper's Proposition 5.7 gives the same via Lemma 5.4.
(b) Lemma 5.2.6 (monodromy paper Proposition 5.9): solve for U by successive approximation.
acceptance: Kedlaya's example: F v_1 = v_2, F v_2 = p v_1 + u v_2: x^2 − ux − p has Newton polygon with slopes 0, 1 (PARI/GP newtonpoly(x^2 − x − 3, 3) = [1, 0] with u ↦ 1 a unit).
F v_1 = v_2, F v_2 = p v_1: x^2 − p has slopes 1/2, 1/2 (PARI/GP newtonpoly(x^2 − 5, 5) = [1/2, 1/2]).

sources.excerpt: Then the generic HN-polygon of M coincides with the Newton polygon of the polynomial x^n + a_{n−1}x^{n−1} + · · · + a_0.
Then the generic slopes of M are equal to the valuations of the diagonal entries of D.
Then the generic Newton polygon of M coincides with the the Newton polygon of the polynomial x^n + a_{n−1}x^{n−1} + · · · + a_0 over R.

nodes.title: (σ,∇)-modules (φ,∇)-modules over R, R^bd, R^int, E and dagger algebras; Frobenius structures
nodes.statement: Let A ∈ {R, R^bd, R^int (O_K-linear), E, O_E, R_L} with a Frobenius lift σ and the derivation d/dt. A (σ,∇)-module over A is a finite free A-module M with a σ-module structure F and a ∇-module structure D = ∇_{d/dt} such that ∇∘F = (F ⊗ dσ)∘∇, i.e. D(F v) = (dσ(t)/dt)·F(D v) for all v ∈ M; equivalently the linearisation σ^*M → M of F is a horizontal isomorphism (after inverting π) for the pulled-back connection σ^*∇. Morphisms respect F and D. For a ∇-module E over R (or on A[r,1)), a Frobenius structure of order a relative to a Frobenius lift σ of order a is a horizontal isomorphism σ^*E ≅ E. The same definition applies over a dagger algebra of MW-type with a Frobenius lift (integrable connection, σ^*M ≅ M horizontal). Tensor products, duals and internal Homs of (σ,∇)-modules are (σ,∇)-modules; H^0(M) = ker D is a σ_K-module (an isocrystal over the σ-fixed field when finite-dimensional).
hypotheses: Integrability is automatic over annulus rings (one variable) but is part of the definition over dagger algebras of higher dimension.
The compatibility uses dσ: Ω^1 → Ω^1, dσ(dt) = d(σ(t)) = (dσ(t)/dt) dt, which vanishes modulo π.
proofSteps: Definitions: monodromy paper Section 2.5; slope filtrations revisited Definition 7.1.5; overview Definitions 6.1.1-6.1.2; Weil II Section 2.3 (dagger algebras).
Reformulation D(Fv) = (dσ(t)/dt) F(Dv): expand ∇(Fv) and (F ⊗ dσ)(∇v) = F(Dv) ⊗ d(σ(t)).
Tensor operations: F and D act by the product rules; compatibility is checked on pure tensors.
acceptance: Trivial (σ,∇)-module R with F = σ and D = d/dt; R(1) with F e = π e, D e = 0 (a nonzero-slope Frobenius module with trivial connection).
The Dwork exponential module E_π (next nodes) with its Frobenius structure θ = exp(π(t^{-p} − t^{-1})) for σ(t) = t^p.

Kedlaya's Example 7.2.6 (with the printed u^σ = qu read as u^σ = u^q, sourceIssues): F e_1 = e_1, F e_2 = q e_2, ∇e_1 = 0, ∇e_2 = e_1 ⊗ du/u is a (σ,∇)-module that is unipotent but not quasi-constant.

nodes.title: Independence of the Frobenius lift: the Taylor isomorphism σ_1^*E ≅ σ_2^*E
nodes.statement: Let σ_1, σ_2 be Frobenius lifts of the same order on R (same σ_K), and let E be a ∇-module over R that is solvable at 1. The Taylor series v ↦ Σ_{n≥0} (σ_2(t) − σ_1(t))^n/n! ⊗ D^n(v) converges and defines a horizontal isomorphism τ_{σ_1,σ_2}: σ_1^*E → σ_2^*E, with τ_{σ,σ} = id and τ_{σ_2,σ_3}∘τ_{σ_1,σ_2} = τ_{σ_1,σ_3}. Hence a Frobenius structure F_1: σ_1^*E ≅ E determines the Frobenius structure F_1∘τ_{σ_1,σ_2}^{-1} relative to σ_2, and the categories of (σ_1,∇)- and (σ_2,∇)-modules over R are equivalent compatibly with the underlying ∇-modules; properties of the underlying ∇-module (unipotence, generic radii, breaks) do not depend on σ. Every ∇-module with a Frobenius structure is solvable at 1, so the hypothesis holds for (σ,∇)-modules.
hypotheses: σ_1(t) ≡ σ_2(t) modulo π R^int (both reduce to t^q), so the Taylor comparison applies.
proofSteps: Overview Remark 4.1.9: for maps f_1, f_2 inducing the same map on R^int/m_R, the Taylor series gives a natural isomorphism f_1^* ≅ f_2^* on M^conv (local analogue of Berthelot's isomorphism for overconvergent isocrystals); convergence uses solvability (η-null Taylor series) and |σ_2(t) − σ_1(t)| < 1.
Compatibility with composition: formal identity of Taylor series (the ring case is the RD.0 Taylor formula).
Transport of Frobenius structures: overview Definition 6.1.2 remark; Weil II Remark 4.2.4 (the category of (σ,∇)-modules on K⟨x⟩† does not depend on σ).
Solvability of modules with Frobenius structure: next node.
acceptance: For the Dwork exponential module (D w = −π t^{-2} w), σ_1(t) = t^p and σ_2(t) = t^p + p t^{p−1}: τ(1 ⊗ w) = exp(π(σ_1(t)^{-1} − σ_2(t)^{-1}))·(1 ⊗ w), and σ_1(t)^{-1} − σ_2(t)^{-1} = p t^{-p-1}(1 + p t^{-1})^{-1} ∈ pR^int, so the factor is a unit of R^int.

sources.excerpt: Then there is a natural isomorphism between the pullback functors f_1^∗ and f_2^∗ on M^conv, given by the Taylor series
It will follow from Lemma 6.1.4 below (and Remark 4.1.9) that the choice of a Frobenius structure for a single σ determines a Frobenius structure for every σ.
giving a nice interpretation of the fact that the category of (σ, ∇)-modules on K⟨x⟩† does not depend on the choice of the Frobenius lift σ.
forming the pullback involves changing Frobenius lifts, which is achieved using the Taylor isomorphism provided by the connection.

nodes.title: A Frobenius structure forces generic radius 1 at the boundary (Dwork; Christol-Mebkhout)
nodes.statement: Let E be a ∇-module on A[r, 1) (or over R) admitting a Frobenius structure relative to some Frobenius lift. Then (a) for every λ ∈ (0, 1) there is ρ_0 < 1 such that every ρ ∈ (ρ_0, 1) lies in a closed subinterval I ⊆ (ρ_0, 1) over which E has a basis on which t d/dt acts by a matrix N with |N|_r < λ for r ∈ I; (b) E is overconvergent (solvable at 1): T(E, ρ) → 1, i.e. R(E, ρ)/ρ → 1 as ρ → 1. In particular the Frobenius slopes of a (σ,∇)-module impose no restriction on solvability, and a (σ,∇)-module over R has a highest break and a Swan conductor.
hypotheses: K complete of characteristic 0; any Frobenius lift of order ≥ 1.

nodes.title: The rank-one exponential connection (Dwork's exponential): radius, highest break 1, Swan conductor 1, unit-root Frobenius structure
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, K ⊇ Q_p(π) with π^{p−1} = −p, σ_K = id on Q_p(π) (e.g. K = Q_p(π)), σ the standard lift σ(t) = t^p on R, and E_π = R·w with D(w) = −π t^{-2} w (its horizontal sections on generic discs are the multiples of exp(−π(t^{-1} − t_ρ^{-1}))·w; this is the pullback of the Dwork isocrystal ∇e = π e ⊗ dx along x = t^{-1}). Then: (a) exp(πx) = Σ π^n x^n/n! has radius of convergence exactly 1 and diverges at every point with |x| = 1 (v_p(π^n/n!) = s_p(n)/(p−1)); (b) R(E_π, ρ) = ρ^2 and T(E_π, ρ) = ρ for all ρ ∈ (0, 1): E_π is solvable at 1 with highest break 1 and Swan conductor 1; (c) θ = exp(π(t^{-p} − t^{-1})) lies in R^int and is a unit there (Dwork: exp(π(x − x^p)) converges on |x| < p^{(p−1)/p^2}); F(w) = θ w is a Frobenius structure: D(F w) = (d t^p/dt)·F(D w); (d) E_π with this F is unit-root (Frobenius slope 0), becomes trivial after pulling back to the Artin-Schreier extension u^p − u = t^{-1} of k((t)), and E_π^{⊗p} is trivial.
hypotheses: p odd, so that −π also satisfies (−π)^{p−1} = −p; σ_K = id on Q_p(π) (Weil II takes k = F_q and σ_K = id).
proofSteps: (a) Legendre: v_p(n!) = (n − s_p(n))/(p−1).

(b) By induction D^s w = (−1)^s Σ_{k=1}^s L(s,k) π^k t^{−s−k} w with L(s,k) = C(s−1, k−1) s!/k!; the k = s term gives |D_s|_ρ ≥ |π|^s ρ^{−2s}, and |L(s,k)π^k| ≤ |π|^s p^{(s_p(s)−s_p(k))/(p−1)}·(integer factor) gives |D_s|_ρ^{1/s} → |π|ρ^{-2} > |π|ρ^{-1} = |∂|_{F_ρ,sp}; hence |∂|_{E_ρ,sp} = |π|ρ^{-2} and R = ωρ^2/|π| = ρ^2. Overview Lemma 5.4.7 (n = 1) obtains the highest break 1 from the Artin-Schreier cover, and the transfer theorem gives convergence of exp(−π(t^{-1} − t_ρ^{-1})) exactly on |t − t_ρ| < ρ^2.

(c) With x = t^{-1}, θ = exp(π(x^p − x)) = exp(π'(x − x^p)) where π' = −π also satisfies π'^{p−1} = −p (p odd). By Dwork's observation (Weil II Remark 4.2.3) Σ c_i x^i = exp(π'(x − x^p)) converges on a disc of radius > 1, with c_0 = 1 and |c_i| < 1 for i ≥ 1 (PARI check (2) below), so θ ∈ R^int and θ ≡ 1 modulo m_R, hence θ is a unit of R^int. Compatibility: θ'/θ = π(t^{-2} − p t^{-p-1}), so D(θw) = θ'w − π t^{-2} θ w = −pπ t^{-p-1} θ w, while (d t^p/dt)·F(D w) = p t^{p−1}·σ(−π t^{-2}) θ w = −pπ t^{-p-1} θ w.
(d) θ is a unit of R^int, so w(det F) = 0; Weil II Section 4.3 and Swan conductors I Example 3.5.10 (Artin-Schreier character, Swan conductor 1).
acceptance: PARI/GP (1): v_p(π^n/n!) = s_p(n)/(p−1) checked for n ≤ 400 and p = 3, 5, 7; at n = p^k the value is 1/(p−1) (no decay on |x| = 1).

PARI/GP (2): coefficients c_n of exp(π(x − x^p)) computed in Q[π]/(π^{p−1} + p): min_n (v_p(c_n) − n(p−1)/p^2) = 5/18 over n ≤ 120 for p = 3 and 9/100 over n ≤ 60 for p = 5 (so v_p(c_n) ≥ n(p−1)/p^2 in this range, radius ≥ p^{(p−1)/p^2}).

PARI/GP (3): Lah closed form of D^s verified symbolically for s ≤ 40; (1/s)(−log_p|D_s|_ρ) converges to 1/(p−1) − 2a at ρ = p^{-a} (differences −0.012, −0.002, −0.001, −0.0002 at s = 50, 200, 800, 3200 for p = 3, a = 1/10; exactly 0 for p = 5 and a ∈ {1/10, 3/10, 1/2, 9/10}).

nodes.title: Frobenius slope and differential irregularity are independent invariants of (σ,∇)-modules
nodes.statement: There are rank-one (σ,∇)-modules over R (σ(t) = t^p, K ⊇ Q_p(π)) realising every combination of 'slope zero / nonzero' and 'break zero / nonzero': (i) the trivial module R: slope 0, T(ρ) = 1, b = 0, Swan 0; (ii) R·e with F e = p e, D e = 0 (the twist by p): nonzero slope (p-adic slope 1), T(ρ) = 1, b = 0; (iii) E_π: slope 0 (unit-root), T(ρ) = ρ, b = 1, Swan 1; (iv) E_π ⊗ (R·e, F e = p e): nonzero slope, b = 1. Consequently neither invariant determines the other: the Frobenius slopes (HN polygon of the σ-module) and the radius/Swan data (of the ∇-module) must be compared by a proof, not by definition. What does hold: a Frobenius structure forces solvability (T → 1) whatever the slopes, and the slope filtration of a (σ,∇)-module is ∇-stable (Kedlaya slope filtrations revisited Proposition 7.1.6, planned in RD.2 by part B).
hypotheses: With O = Z_p[π] (π^{p−1} = −p) Kedlaya's valuation has w(p) = p − 1; the module F e = p e has w-slope p − 1 and p-adic slope 1.
proofSteps: (i)-(iii): generic radius of the trivial module; the twist by p has trivial connection, so its radius is that of R, and its degree is w(p) ≠ 0; E_π from the Dwork exponential node.
(iv): the tensor product has the same underlying ∇-module as E_π (the second factor has trivial connection), so the same radius and breaks, and its degree is 0 + w(p) (calculus of slopes).
acceptance: This realises the stage acceptance test: a trivial connection, a rank-one exponential connection and a nonzero-slope Frobenius module distinguish radius, irregularity and slope conventions.

nodes.title: A finitely presented module with connection over the Robba ring is free
nodes.statement: Let M be a finitely presented R_K-module with a connection ∇ : M → M ⊗ Ω^1_{R_K} (Leibniz rule for d/dt). Then M is free of finite rank. The same holds over R^L = Γ^L_an,con for L/k((t)) finite separable.
hypotheses: K of characteristic 0 (used to divide by the order of vanishing).
proofSteps: By RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains (b) (finite torsion-free modules are free, so M ≅ T ⊕ M/T) it suffices to show that the torsion submodule T is zero; T is ∇-stable.

Over a closed-interval ring Γ_I (a PID by RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid) let (f) be the annihilator of T: from f m = 0 one gets f' m + f∇m = 0 and f²∇(m) = 0, so ∇(m) ∈ T, f∇(m) = 0, f'm = 0, hence f' ∈ (f); since Γ_I contains Q, (f) is the unit ideal (Crew Proposition 6.1).
Pass to R_K via M = lim M ⊗ Γ_I (Crew 4.8(iv)) and the fact that a torsion element is defined on some annulus.
acceptance: R_K/(log(1+t)) admits no connection: it would force (log(1+t))' = 1/(1+t) ∈ (log(1+t)), impossible since log(1+t) has zeros at ζ − 1 for p-power roots of unity ζ.

nodes.title: Coincident generic and special polygons give a common filtration over Γ_con[π^{-1}]
nodes.statement: Let M be a σ-module over Γ_con[π^{-1}] whose generic and special HN polygons coincide. Then the generic HN filtration of M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{-1}] and the special HN filtration of M ⊗ Γ^alg_an,con are both base changes of one exhaustive filtration of M by saturated σ-submodules.
hypotheses: Notation of RD.2/special-polygon-above-generic.
proofSteps: Reduce to a first step of rank one by RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains (b). The generic first step descends to Γ[π^{-1}] (RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent); the reverse filtration splits over Γ^alg_an,con (RD.1/splitting-of-exact-sequences-by-polygons) and hence over Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] (injectivity of H^1(Γ_con[π^{-1}](n)) → H^1(Γ_an,con(n)), RD.1/rank-one-frobenius-modules); so the coordinate ratios lie in Γ[π^{-1}] ∩ Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] = Γ_con[π^{-1}]. The special first step is the maximal submodule of minimal slope and contains, hence equals, the descended generic one (SFR Theorem 5.5.2; arXiv:math/0110124 Proposition 5.16).

nodes.statement: (a) (Matrix lemma) Let Γ = Γ^E have enough r0-units with r0 > qr, D invertible over Γ_[r,r], h = −w_r(D) − w_r(D^{-1}), and A with w_r(AD^{-1} − I) > h/(q − 1). Then there is U invertible over Γ_[r,qr] with U^{-1}AU^σD^{-1} − I having entries in πΓ_r and w_r(U^{-1}AU^σD^{-1} − I) > 0; if A and D are invertible over Γ_an,r then U is invertible over Γ_an,qr. (b) For a σ-module M over Γ^K_an,con (K = k((t))) there is a finite separable extension L/K and a σ-module N over Γ^L_con[π^{-1}] with N ⊗ Γ^L_an,con ≅ M ⊗ Γ^L_an,con and equal generic and special HN polygons.

(b) Apply [a]_* to make slopes integral; by RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring write U^{-1}AU^σ = D over Γ^alg_an,con with D diagonal of powers of π; approximate U over Γ^L_[r,qr] for pseudo-finite separable L (RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings), apply (a), and read the generic slopes from the resulting matrix via RD.1/generic-newton-polygon-from-cyclic-vector (b) (SFR Proposition 6.2.2; arXiv:math/0110124 Propositions 6.8, 6.9).

nodes.title: Isoclinic σ-modules descend uniquely from the Robba ring to the bounded Robba ring
nodes.statement: (a) For a unit-root σ-module M over Γ_con[π^{-1}], H^0(M) = H^0(M ⊗ Γ[π^{-1}]) = H^0(M ⊗ Γ_an,con); if K is algebraically closed M has a basis of eigenvectors. (b) Base change from isoclinic σ-modules of slope s over Γ_con[π^{-1}] to isoclinic σ-modules over Γ[π^{-1}] is fully faithful. (c) Base change from isoclinic σ-modules of slope s over Γ_con[π^{-1}] to isoclinic σ-modules of slope s over Γ_an,con is an EQUIVALENCE of categories. (d) A σ-module M over Γ_an,con is isoclinic of slope c/d iff it admits a Γ_con-lattice N on which π^{-c}F^d maps some (any) basis to a basis.
hypotheses: The functor in (b) is not essentially surjective in general (ramification breaks of the Galois representation grow too fast; SFR Remark 6.3.4).
Isoclinic over Γ_con[π^{-1}] means isoclinic generic slope (RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module), which implies isoclinic special slope.
proofSteps: (a) Reduce to K algebraically closed (Corollary 2.5.8); slope-0 eigenvectors over Γ^alg lie in M (RD.2/slope-zero-eigenvectors-descend-to-overconvergent), so M ≅ M_{0,1}^{⊕n}; compare H^0 by RD.1/rank-one-frobenius-modules (SFR Proposition 6.3.2).

(b),(c) full faithfulness: Hom(M, N) = H^0(M^∨ ⊗ N) with M^∨ ⊗ N unit-root; essential surjectivity: RD.2/good-models-of-sigma-modules gives a model over Γ^L_con[π^{-1}] (L/K Galois), unique by full faithfulness, hence Gal(L/K)-stable, and it descends by Galois descent (SFR Theorem 6.3.3).
(d) Apply RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices to ([d]_*M)(−c) and its model (SFR Proposition 6.3.5).
acceptance: Unit-root example: M = R_K·e with F e = e is the base change of R^bd·e; the rank one σ-module R_K(c) is isoclinic of slope c and descends to R^bd(c).

The special-but-not-generic isoclinic case: SFR §7.3's M is isoclinic of special slope 1/2 over Γ_an,con, so by (c) M ⊗ Γ_an,con has a model over Γ_con[π^{-1}] that is isoclinic of GENERIC slope 1/2 — necessarily different from the given model (generic slopes 0, 1).

nodes.title: Slope filtration theorem for σ-modules over the Robba ring (Kedlaya; Theorem 1.2 / 6.10 of arXiv:math/0110124, Theorem 6.4.1 of SFR)
nodes.statement: Let M be a σ-module over Γ_an,con = Γ^E_an,con with E = k((t)) (i.e. over the Robba ring R_K with a Frobenius lift φ, RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring), or more generally over Γ^E_an,con for E complete with enough units. Then there is a UNIQUE filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ ... ⊂ M_l = M by saturated σ-submodules such that (a) each M_i/M_{i−1} is isoclinic of some slope s_i and (b) s_1 < ... < s_l; it is the HN filtration of M. Moreover: (c) its formation commutes with base change to Γ^{E'}_an,con for any complete extension E' of E with enough units (in particular to Γ^alg_an,con, so absolute HN slopes are the HN slopes); (d) M is semistable iff it is isoclinic; (e) (precise form, arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 6.10) each M_i/M_{i−1} contains a unique F-stable Γ_con[π^{-1}]-submodule N_i of the same rank spanning it over Γ_an,con, all of whose generic slopes equal s_i; conditions (a),(b) determine the filtration uniquely. In the notation of arXiv:math/0110124 (Theorem 1.2): M_i/M_{i−1} ≅ N_i ⊗ Γ_an,con with N_i defined over Γ_con[1/p] and all slopes of N_i equal to s_i.
hypotheses: k any field of characteristic p (not necessarily perfect), O finite totally ramified over a Cohen ring C(k); σ any Frobenius lift in the sense of SFR (an endomorphism lifting the q-power Frobenius, carrying O into itself), which includes Kedlaya's 2004 Frobenius (a composition power of a p-power lift).
σ-modules are finite locally free, hence free over the Bézout ring R_K (RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains), with F an isomorphism after inverting π (automatic over R_K since π is a unit).
Special slopes (over Γ^alg_an,con) and generic slopes (over Γ^alg[π^{-1}], RD.1/frobenius-slopes) differ in general; N_i has generic slopes = special slopes = s_i.
Slopes: SFR normalises w(π) = 1; this statement is normalisation-independent up to the factor e(K).
proofSteps: Uniqueness: isoclinic σ-modules are semistable (RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring with RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring), so any filtration with (a),(b) is an HN filtration, unique by RD.1/semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration.

Existence: the HN filtration of M ⊗ Γ^alg_an,con (RD.1/harder-narasimhan-filtration-exists and RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring) must be descended; by RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains (b) reduce to a rank one first step M'_1.

By RD.2/good-models-of-sigma-modules choose a finite Galois L/K and a model N over Γ^L_con[π^{-1}] with equal polygons; by RD.2/coincident-polygons-common-filtration M'_1 descends to M_1 ⊆ M ⊗ Γ^L_an,con.

With a generator v = Σ a_i e_i of M_1, the ratios a_i/a_j are Gal(L/K)-invariant elements of Frac Γ^L_an,con, hence lie in Frac Γ^K_an,con (RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings (Galois invariants)); clearing denominators gives a nonzero element of M_1 ∩ M, so M_1 descends (SFR Theorem 6.4.1).
(c) The characterisation by (a),(b) is stable under base change (SFR Corollary 6.4.2); (d) SFR Corollary 6.4.3.

(e) Apply RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring (c) to each (twisted, [d]_*-rescaled) graded piece: the unique isoclinic model over Γ_con[π^{-1}] is N_i (compare the original argument of arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 6.10 via Propositions 6.9, 5.16, 4.4, 4.5, 5.11 and Corollary 3.16).
acceptance: Unit-root case (l = 1, s_1 = 0): M ≅ N ⊗ Γ_an,con with N étale over Γ_con[π^{-1}]; this is the input to Tsuzuki's theorem (RD.2/tsuzuki-unit-root-finite-monodromy).

Bessel isocrystal (arXiv:math/0110124 §1.5): l = 1, s_1 = 1/2 (v_p normalisation): N_1 has generic slopes 1/2, 1/2 although the given model over Γ_con has generic slopes 0 and 1; any implementation must distinguish generic from special slopes.

SFR §7.3 example (F v_1 = v_2, F v_2 = p v_1 + u v_2, u^σ = u^p): the slope filtration of M ⊗ R_K is 0 ⊂ M ⊗ R_K (isoclinic of slope 1/2), while the generic slope filtration over Γ[π^{-1}] has two steps.
R(0) ⊕ R(1): M_1 = R(0), s_1 = 0 < s_2 = 1; the filtration is not required to split over R_K and does not in general (RD.1/splitting-of-exact-sequences-by-polygons).

nodes.title: The Frobenius on differentials has positive generic slopes
nodes.statement: View Ω^1_{Γ_con/O} = Γ_con du (derivation d(Σ c_i u^i) = Σ i c_i u^{i−1} du) as a σ-module via dσ : Ω^1 → Ω^1, dσ(f du) = f^σ d(u^σ). Then dσ(ω) ≡ 0 mod π for every ω, so the generic slopes of Ω^1_{Γ_con/O} are all positive, and the special slopes of Ω^1_{Γ_an,con/O} are nonnegative. The same holds for Γ^L_con, Γ^L_an,con with L/k((t)) finite separable.
hypotheses: σ lifts the q-power Frobenius, so u^σ ≡ u^q mod π and d(u^σ)/du ≡ q u^{q−1} ≡ 0 mod π.
proofSteps: dσ(du) = (du^σ/du) du with du^σ/du ∈ πΓ_con; RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (b) gives positive generic slopes (the Frobenius on the lattice Γ_con du is divisible by π), and RD.2/special-polygon-above-generic gives special slopes ≥ 0 (SFR Remark 7.1.4).
acceptance: For the standard lift u^σ = u^q: dσ(du) = q u^{q−1} du, so the rank one σ-module Ω^1 has generic and special slope w(q) = e(K)·a > 0.

sources.excerpt: by Proposition 5.1.3 the generic slopes of Ω1Γcon /O as a σ-module are all positive. By Proposition 5.5.1, the special slopes of Ω1Γan,con /O as a σ-module are also nonnegative.

nodes.title: Each step of the slope filtration of a (σ,∇)-module is ∇-stable
nodes.statement: Let M be a (σ,∇)-module over Γ_an,con (over R_K: a (φ,∇)-module, RD.1/frobenius-differential-module). Then every step M_i of the slope filtration (RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement) is a (σ,∇)-submodule (arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 6.12(d)).
hypotheses: The Frobenius and connection are compatible: ∇ ∘ F = (F ⊗ dσ) ∘ ∇.
proofSteps: It suffices to treat the first step M_1 (isoclinic of slope s_1). The Kodaira-Spencer map M_1 → (M/M_1) ⊗ Ω^1 induced by ∇ is Γ_an,con-linear and F-equivariant (compatibility of F and ∇).
All slopes of (M/M_1) ⊗ Ω^1 are > s_1: slopes of M/M_1 exceed s_1 and those of Ω^1 are ≥ 0 (RD.2/differentials-have-positive-slopes) and slopes add under ⊗ (RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module).

Hom vanishing (RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module, SFR Proposition 4.6.4) forces the map to vanish, so ∇(M_1) ⊆ M_1 ⊗ Ω^1 (SFR Proposition 7.1.6). Kedlaya's original proof solves a matrix σ-equation with Proposition 3.19(c) (arXiv:math/0110124 p. 81).
acceptance: SFR Example 7.2.6 (corrected): M_1 = span(e_1) of slope 0 is ∇-stable (∇e_1 = 0).

nodes.title: Finite étale extensions of R^int and the Robba rings R^L of finite separable extensions of k((t))
nodes.statement: (a) R^int is a henselian discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal πR^int and residue field k((t)) (K discretely valued). Hence for every finite separable extension L of k((t)) there is a finite étale R^int-algebra R^int_L, unique up to unique isomorphism, with R^int_L/π = L; L ↦ R^int_L is an equivalence from finite separable extensions of k((t)) to finite étale local R^int-algebras ('formally étale covers' of a thin annulus). (b) R^L := R_K ⊗_{R^int} R^int_L and R^{bd}_L := R^bd ⊗ R^int_L; they coincide with Kedlaya's Γ^L_an,con and Γ^L_con[π^{-1}]. The Frobenius lift φ and the derivation d/dt extend uniquely to R^int_L, R^{bd}_L, R^L; for L/k((t)) Galois, Gal(L/k((t))) acts on R^L commuting with φ and d, with fixed ring R_K. (c) If the residue field k_L of L is separable over k (always if k is perfect), choosing u ∈ R^int_L lifting a uniformiser of L gives a continuous isomorphism R^L ≅ R_{K'} (Robba ring over K' = the unramified extension of K with residue field k_L, in the variable u); the isomorphism depends on u but the conclusions drawn from it do not. (d) (Nearly separable extensions, needed when k is imperfect) for m ≥ 0 put K^{(m)} = K viewed through σ_K^{-m} with residue field k^{1/p^m}; a nearly finite separable extension of k((t)) is a finite separable extension of k^{1/p^m}((t)), and its Robba ring is formed over R_{K^{(m)}} ⊇ R_K via φ^m.
hypotheses: K is discretely valued (Kedlaya's overview Remark 3.5.3: otherwise R^int is not a valuation ring).

Separable L/k((t)) may have inseparable residue field extension when k is imperfect (arXiv:math/0110124 §2.2, example k((t))[x]/(x^p − x − ct^{-p}) with c ∉ k^p); then (c) needs the nearly separable replacement (d).
proofSteps: (a) R^int is local with residue field k((t)) (overview Lemma 3.5.2) and henselian by Newton iteration convergent on annuli (overview Proposition 3.5.5; arXiv:math/0110124 Lemma 3.9; RD.0/overconvergent-witt-vectors-henselian); a henselian local ring has the stated equivalence of finite étale algebras (EGA IV 18.5.15; lift a monic separable minimal polynomial of a primitive element, SFR Proposition 2.2.15).

(b) is RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings for E = k((t)); φ extends by étaleness (unique lift of the q-power Frobenius of L, SFR Definition 2.2.8) and d/dt extends uniquely to an étale extension (Kähler differentials of an étale algebra).

(c) Cohen structure theorem L ≅ k_L((ū)); lifting ū to u ∈ R^int_L and the unramified K'/K gives R^int_{K',u} → R^int_L, an isomorphism by uniqueness in (a); complete (Kedlaya, Finiteness, proof of Theorem 5.1.2; overview Remark 3.5.7).
(d) arXiv:math/0110124 §2.2 (nearly separable valued fields; Annals: 'nearly finite separable'), Kedlaya, Finiteness, Theorem 5.1.2 (K_0 = K^{σ^{-m}}).
acceptance: Kummer: for p ∤ n, L = k((t))[v]/(v^n − t) gives R^L = R_K[v]/(v^n − t), the Robba ring in v.

Artin-Schreier: L = k((t))[ȳ]/(ȳ^p − ȳ − t^{-1}) (wild, Swan conductor 1) lifts to R^int_L = R^int[y]/(y^p − y − t^{-1}); the Dwork module trivialises over it (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example).

nodes.title: Constant and quasi-constant ∇-modules over the Robba ring
nodes.statement: A ∇-module M over R_K (RD.1/differential-module: finite free with connection ∇ : M → M ⊗ Ω^1) is constant if it is spanned by ker ∇, equivalently isomorphic to a direct sum of copies of the trivial ∇-module (R_K, d). It is quasi-constant (étale) if M ⊗ R^L is constant for some finite separable L/k((t)) (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring; nearly finite separable if k is imperfect). A (σ,∇)-module is (quasi-)constant if its underlying ∇-module is.
hypotheses: The notion does not involve the Frobenius structure (SFR Definition 7.2.2).
proofSteps: Representation-theoretic description: for L/k((t)) finite Galois with R^L ≅ R_{K'}, E ↦ H^0(M ⊗ R^L) is an equivalence from ∇-modules becoming constant over R^L to semilinear representations of Gal(L/k((t))) on finite-dimensional K'-vector spaces (Kedlaya overview Lemma 4.3.2, via Hilbert 90-type semilinear Maschke and Schur lemmas, overview §4.2).
Closure: quasi-constant modules are stable under ⊕, ⊗, duals, subobjects and quotients but not extensions (overview Definition 4.3.1).
acceptance: (R_K, d) is constant; R_K·e with ∇e = (1/2) e ⊗ dt/t (p odd) is quasi-constant (constant over R_K[v]/(v² − t), horizontal section v^{-1}e) but not constant.

nodes.title: Unipotent ∇-modules over the Robba ring
nodes.statement: A ∇-module M over R_K (more generally over R^L) is unipotent if it admits an exhaustive filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ ... ⊂ M_n = M by ∇-submodules whose successive quotients are constant (RD.2/constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module); equivalently (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 5.1.1) M has a unipotent basis v_1, ..., v_n with ∇v_i ∈ (R_K v_1 + ... + R_K v_{i−1}) ⊗ dt/t; equivalently (Crew §6.6) M is a successive extension of copies of the trivial rank one object (R_K, d). A (σ,∇)-module is unipotent if its underlying ∇-module is. A strongly unipotent basis is one with t∇_{d/dt} v_i ∈ K v_1 + ... + K v_{i−1}.
hypotheses: The definition does not refer to the Frobenius structure and is invariant under continuous automorphisms of R_K (change of the series parameter) (Kedlaya, Finiteness, after Definition 5.1.1).
Every ∇-submodule of a ∇-module is saturated (overview Remark 4.1.5), so the filtration is automatically by saturated submodules and the quotients are free.
proofSteps: Equivalence of the three formulations: a filtration with constant quotients refines to one with rank one trivial quotients; choosing lifts of horizontal bases gives a unipotent basis (Ω^1 = R_K dt/t since t is a unit of R_K); conversely the spans of v_1..v_i are ∇-stable with trivial quotients.

Every unipotent M has a strongly unipotent basis and the K-span of any strongly unipotent basis is canonical (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Proposition 5.2.6, Lemma 5.2.4, Corollary 5.2.5), which leads to RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue.
acceptance: SFR Example 7.2.6 (with u^σ = u^q): unipotent, not quasi-constant.

nodes.title: Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules and (σ,∇)-modules
nodes.statement: A ∇-module M over R_K is quasi-unipotent if M ⊗ R^L is unipotent (RD.2/unipotent-differential-module) for some finite separable extension L of k((t)) when k is perfect, and for some nearly finite separable L in general (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (d)). Equivalently, M admits a filtration over R_K by ∇-submodules whose successive quotients are quasi-constant. A (σ,∇)-module over R_K is quasi-unipotent if its underlying ∇-module is; Kedlaya's 2004 definition (after tensoring with a finite extension of Γ_con, a filtration by (σ,∇)-submodules whose successive quotients have bases in ker ∇) is equivalent for (σ,∇)-modules because the filtration can be chosen canonical (first step spanned by the full kernel of ∇), hence F-stable.
hypotheses: The finite extension is an extension of the bounded Robba ring R^int (a finite cover of the thin annulus), not only a coefficient extension of K; if k is perfect it may be required residually separable (arXiv:math/0110124 §1.1).
proofSteps: Equivalence of the two formulations: if M ⊗ R^L has a unipotent filtration, the shortest one (first step = span of ker ∇ over R^L, etc.) is unique, Gal(L/k((t)))-stable and descends by Galois descent (RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains); its descended quotients are quasi-constant (overview Remark 4.6.2). The same canonicity shows the filtration is F-stable for a (σ,∇)-module.
Closure properties: quasi-unipotent modules are closed under ⊕, ⊗, duals, subquotients and extensions (overview Definition 4.6.1).
acceptance: Every unipotent and every quasi-constant module is quasi-unipotent; the exponential module R_K e, ∇e = e dt is not (RD.2/frobenius-hypothesis-is-necessary).

nodes.title: Residues and antiderivatives on the Robba ring
nodes.statement: Let R = R^L ≅ R_{K'} in a variable u (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (c)). (a) For f = Σ_n a_n u^n ∈ R, the series Σ_{n≠−1} a_n u^{n+1}/(n+1) converges on every annulus on which f converges, so f du = a_{−1} du/u + dg with g ∈ R; the residue res(f du) = a_{−1} is well defined and f du is exact in R iff a_{−1} = 0; ker(d : R → R) = K'.
hypotheses: K' of characteristic 0. The estimate |1/(n+1)| ≤ n + 1 (p-adic absolute value of an integer's inverse is at most the integer) keeps the radius of convergence.
proofSteps: (a) For n ≠ −1, |a_n/(n+1)|ρ^{n+1} ≤ |a_n|ρ^n·(|n|+1)ρ, and polynomial factors do not change convergence on open annuli, so the primitive converges where f does; uniqueness up to constants since d(Σ c_n u^n) = 0 forces c_n = 0 for n ≠ 0.
acceptance: res(du/u) = 1, so du/u is not exact in R (its primitive log u lives only in the logarithmic extension, RD.2/log-robba-ring).

Contrast with the closed disc: ω = Σ_{k≥0} p^k x^{p^k−1} dx has coefficients tending to 0, so it lies in K⟨x⟩dx, but its only formal primitives Σ_k x^{p^k} + c do not lie in K⟨x⟩; on the Robba ring, by (a), every f with a_{−1} = 0 has a primitive in R (the closed-disc example is RD.0/completion-versus-overconvergence (b); it is used in RD.3/punctured-curve-boundary-acceptance).

nodes.title: Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue
nodes.statement: The following categories are equivalent: (a) finite-dimensional K-vector spaces V with a nilpotent endomorphism N; (b) log-∇-modules on the open unit disc A[0,1) with nilpotent residue whose restriction to A(0,1) is overconvergent; (c) unipotent ∇-modules over R_K (or over the ring of any aligned open annulus). The functor (a)→(c) sends (V,N) to V ⊗_K R_K with ∇ = d + N ⊗ dt/t; a quasi-inverse is M ↦ (V = ∪_{n≥0} ker D^n, N = D|_V) with D = t∇_{d/dt}. Moreover Hom and Ext^1 between F(V,N), F(V',N') are the kernel and cokernel of the induced nilpotent endomorphism of V^∨ ⊗ V', and H^0(F(V,N)) ≅ ker N, H^1(F(V,N)) ≅ coker N. For the tame base change t = s^e (p ∤ e), the pullback of F(V,N) is F(V, eN) up to isomorphism.
hypotheses: Crew states (a)≃(c) for his Robba ring A (Proposition 6.7); Kedlaya's overview adds (b) (Proposition 4.5.3).
proofSteps: (a)→(c): V ⊗ R_K is a successive extension of trivial modules since N is nilpotent (Crew 6.6.3).

Full faithfulness and essential surjectivity by induction on length, comparing Ext groups: in (c) they are computed by the de Rham complex and Ext^1((R_K,d),(R_K,d)) = H^1(R_K) = K dt/t, the cokernel of t d/dt on R_K being K·1 (overview Example 4.1.11; RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative) (Crew Proposition 6.7).

(b)↔(c): construct horizontal sections on discs by the operators Q_i(D) built from binomial polynomials, using overconvergence to control convergence (overview Proposition 4.5.3); descending from (b) to (c) is restriction.
Tame base change: find g with dg = (residue correction) and set C = exp(gN) (Crew Proposition 6.9).
acceptance: For N = 0, F(V, 0) = V ⊗ (R_K, d) is constant; for V = K² and N = [[0,1],[0,0]], F(V,N) is SFR's Example 7.2.6 (∇e_2 = e_1 dt/t).

nodes.title: Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules are overconvergent
nodes.statement: Every quasi-unipotent ∇-module over R_K is overconvergent (solvable at the boundary).
hypotheses: Overconvergent ∇-modules form an abelian subcategory stable under extensions (overview Definition 4.1.7, and the proof of Proposition 4.5.3).
proofSteps: By RD.2/quasi-unipotent-differential-module, M has a filtration with quasi-constant quotients, so by stability under extensions it suffices to treat M quasi-constant.
A quasi-constant M becoming constant over a formally étale cover f : X → A[r,1) is a direct summand of a sum of copies of f_*O_X (overview Lemma 4.3.2 and proof of Proposition 4.4.3).

The Frobenius lift pulls back to X (overview Definition 6.1.1: 'a Frobenius lift pulls back to a Frobenius lift on any formally étale cover'), so f_*O_X carries a Frobenius structure and is overconvergent by RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability; direct summands of overconvergent modules are overconvergent (overview Remark 4.6.7).
acceptance: Unipotent modules are overconvergent: the trivial module is, and overconvergence is stable under extensions.

sources.excerpt: One can deduce from Theorem 4.6.6 that every quasi-unipotent ∇-module is overconvergent, by checking in the unipotent and quasi-constant cases.

nodes.title: Tsuzuki's theorem: unit-root (σ,∇)-modules have finite local monodromy
nodes.statement: Let M be a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over Γ_con[π^{-1}] = R^bd (isoclinic of slope 0, RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module). Then for some finite separable extension L of k((t)) (k perfect; nearly finite separable in general), M ⊗ R^bd_L admits a basis of horizontal sections; in particular M ⊗ R_K is quasi-constant. Precise form (arXiv:math/0110124, Annals version, Proposition 6.11): for a unit-root (σ,∇)-module M of rank n over Γ_con and any nearly finite extension K'/k((t)) such that M ⊗ Γ^{K'}_con has a basis on which F acts by a matrix A with v_p(A − I) > 1/(p−1), the kernel of ∇ on M ⊗ Γ^{K'}_con has rank n over O and is F-stable; such a K' can be chosen separable (k perfect) or nearly separable (k imperfect).
hypotheses: Unit-root: an étale lattice exists (RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (a)), which is ∇-stable after applying F repeatedly (SFR proof of Proposition 7.2.3).
Equivalently (Katz, Crew, Tsuzuki; Kedlaya's Notes Theorems 3.7, 3.9, Remark 3.10) the p-adic representation of G_{k((t))} attached to the étale lattice has finite image of inertia.
proofSteps: Reduce to M = M_0 ⊗ Γ_con[π^{-1}] with M_0 a ∇-stable étale lattice (RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (a); SFR Proposition 7.2.3).

IMPORTED (gap): for k algebraically closed the statement is Tsuzuki, Amer. J. Math. 120 (1998), Theorem 5.1.1 (= [35, Theorem 4.2.6] in SFR), with further proofs by Christol (corrected by André-di Vizio) and in Kedlaya's thesis; none is in the public source set.

Formal reductions given by Kedlaya (arXiv:math/0110124 Proposition 6.11): from q = p to q = p^f by forming the (σ_0,∇_0)-module M_0 ⊕ ... ⊕ M_{f−1} of Frobenius pullbacks (arXiv v4 only); from k algebraically closed to general k by a compactness argument over the inverse system T_S of truncated solutions; the (nearly) separable choice of K' via the ascending generic filtration (RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent) and Dieudonné-Manin.
acceptance: Unit-root rank one example: M = Γ_con e with F e = e, ∇ = d: trivial already over Γ_con (L = k((t))).

Artin-Schreier: the rank one unit-root module attached to the character of Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) cut out by y^p − y = t^{-1} becomes trivial over L = k((t))(y) (a wild extension), compare RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example.

nodes.title: The logarithmic Robba ring R^L_log = R^L[log u] with Frobenius, derivation and monodromy operator
nodes.statement: Let L/k((t)) be finite separable (nearly finite separable if k is imperfect) and u ∈ R^int_L lift a uniformiser of L. Put R^L_log := R^L[ℓ], a polynomial ring in one variable ℓ = 'log u', with: the derivation d extended by dℓ = du/u; the Frobenius φ extended by φ(ℓ) = q ℓ + log(φ(u)/u^q), where log(φ(u)/u^q) = Σ_{i≥1} (−1)^{i−1}(φ(u)/u^q − 1)^i / i converges in R^L because |φ(u)/u^q − 1|_r < 1 near the boundary; for L/k((t)) Galois, τ ∈ Gal acts by τ(ℓ) = ℓ + log(τ(u)/u) when |τ(u)/u − 1| < 1 (e.g. for the tame part after a Kummer choice); and the monodromy operator N := −d/dℓ, the R^L-linear derivation with N(ℓ) = −1. Canonical form (arXiv:math/0110124 v4 §6.5): R^L_log is generated over R^L by symbols l_z (z ∈ R^int_L not divisible by π) subject to l_{z^n} = n l_z and l_{z(1+x)} = l_z + log(1+x) (v_0(x) > 0), with l_z^σ = l_{z^σ} and dl_z = dz/z; it is a polynomial ring in l_z for any z lifting a uniformiser.
hypotheses: ℓ is transcendental over R^L (the relation N(ℓ) = −1 ≠ 0 while N kills R^L); equivalently du/u is not exact in R^L (its residue is 1, RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative).
Frobenius normalisation: φ(ℓ) = q ℓ + (unit correction) because φ(u) ≡ u^q mod π; arXiv:math/0110125 (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness) prints p in place of q (sourceIssues).
proofSteps: The series log(1 + x) converges in the w_r-norms for |x|_r < 1 and is additive (arXiv:math/0110124 §6.5).
φ and d commute appropriately: d(φ(ℓ)) = q du/u + d log(φ(u)/u^q) = dφ(u)/φ(u) = φ(dℓ), as required for ∇∘F = (F⊗dφ)∘∇.
N commutes with d (both are derivations and [N, d/du] kills R^L and ℓ), and N∘φ = q φ∘N on R^L_log since N(φ(ℓ)) = −q.
Independence of u: changing u to u' = c u (1 + x) with c a unit changes ℓ by an element of R^L (the canonical l_z description), inducing an isomorphism of R^L-algebras compatible with d, φ, N.
acceptance: For u^σ = u^q (standard lift) φ(ℓ) = qℓ exactly.
Berger's B†_log,K = B†_rig,K[log π] with ϕ(log π) = p log π + log(ϕ(π)/π^p) is an instance (q = p, u = π) (Berger §2.6).

nodes.title: Antiderivatives in the logarithmic Robba ring
nodes.statement: Let R = R^L ≅ R_{K'} in a variable u and R_log = R[ℓ] with dℓ = du/u (RD.2/log-robba-ring). Then d/du : R_log → R_log is surjective with kernel K': every element Σ_{m≤M} f_m ℓ^m (f_m ∈ R) has an antiderivative in R_log, of ℓ-degree at most M + 1. The same holds after tensoring with a finite extension O' of O.
hypotheses: K' of characteristic 0.
proofSteps: For l ≠ −1, u^l ℓ^m = d/du(u^{l+1}ℓ^m/(l+1)) − (m/(l+1)) u^{l}ℓ^{m−1}, so by induction on m the terms with l ≠ −1 are integrated; for l = −1, u^{-1}ℓ^m = d/du(ℓ^{m+1}/(m+1)).

Infinite sums: apply RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative (a) to f_m minus its residue term and integrate by parts in m; convergence on the annulus of f is preserved since only polynomial factors in l appear (arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 6.13 proof, 'recall from calculus'; Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, proof of Proposition 3.3).

Kernel: if d/du(Σ g_m ℓ^m) = 0 with top degree M ≥ 1, the ℓ^M-coefficient gives g_M' = 0, so g_M ∈ K', and the ℓ^{M−1}-coefficient gives g'_{M−1} + M g_M/u = 0, impossible by (a) since res(du/u) ≠ 0 unless g_M = 0.
acceptance: d/du(ℓ²/2) = ℓ/u, and d/du(uℓ − u) = ℓ: both ℓ/u and ℓ have antiderivatives in R_log although neither has one in R.

nodes.title: The slope pieces become horizontal after a finite (nearly) separable extension
nodes.statement: Let M be a (σ,∇)-module over Γ_an,con = R_K with slope filtration (M_i) and bounded models N_i (RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement (e)). Then (f) there is a nearly finite separable extension L/k((t)) (separable if k is perfect) such that each N_i is spanned over Γ^L_con[1/p] by the kernel of ∇; (g) if k is algebraically closed, each N_i ⊗ Γ^L_con[1/p] is a direct sum of standard (σ,∇)-modules (bases of horizontal eigenvectors F v_1 = v_2, ..., F v_d = λ v_1). (arXiv:math/0110124, Theorem 6.12(f),(g).)
hypotheses: k arbitrary; the auxiliary finite extension O'/O used to bring the slopes into the value group is removed at the end.
The proof as printed says 'which span M' where N_1 is meant (misprint already recorded by the decomposition's reviewer).
proofSteps: By RD.2/isoclinic-model-inherits-connection each N_i is a (σ,∇)-module over Γ_con[1/p]. After enlarging O to O' and twisting (or applying [d]_*), N_i becomes unit-root and has an étale ∇-stable lattice (RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (a)).

RD.2/tsuzuki-unit-root-finite-monodromy gives L with ker ∇ of full rank on N_i ⊗ Γ^L_con ⊗_O O'; decomposing kernel elements along an O-basis of O' produces horizontal elements over Γ^L_con spanning N_i ⊗ Γ^L_con[1/p] (Annals Theorem 6.12, proof of (f)).

(g): ker ∇ is F-stable, so for k algebraically closed classical Dieudonné-Manin over the (complete) residue-field-algebraically-closed DVR gives standard pieces (Annals Theorem 6.12, proof of (g); arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 5.6, consumed through RD.1/frobenius-slopes).
acceptance: SFR Example 7.2.6: N_1 = span(e_1) (slope 0) and N_2 = image of e_2 (slope w(q)) are horizontal already over Γ_con (L = k((t))).

nodes.title: The p-adic local monodromy theorem (Crew's conjecture): (φ,∇)-modules over the Robba ring are quasi-unipotent
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete DISCRETELY VALUED field of characteristic 0 with residue field k of characteristic p (k arbitrary), R_K the Robba ring over K and φ ANY Frobenius lift on R_K (RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring). Then every (φ,∇)-module M over R_K (RD.1/frobenius-differential-module) is quasi-unipotent (RD.2/quasi-unipotent-differential-module): there is a finite separable extension L of k((t)) (nearly finite separable if k is imperfect) such that M ⊗_{R_K} R^L admits a filtration by (φ,∇)-submodules whose successive quotients are spanned by horizontal sections; equivalently M admits a filtration over R_K by (φ,∇)-submodules with quasi-constant successive quotients. The filtration may be taken to be the slope filtration refined as follows: each step M_i of the slope filtration is a (φ,∇)-submodule, each bounded model N_i is ∇-stable and becomes spanned by horizontal sections over R^{bd}_L (RD.2/slope-pieces-horizontal-after-finite-extension). (arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 1.1 and its precise form Theorem 6.12; SFR Theorem 7.2.5; Kedlaya overview Theorem 6.2.1.)
hypotheses: The Frobenius structure is an essential hypothesis: the ∇-module R_K e with ∇e = e ⊗ dt is not quasi-unipotent (RD.2/frobenius-hypothesis-is-necessary). Kedlaya's §1.2 records that the Christol-Mebkhout weight filtration exists with or without Frobenius, and André and Mebkhout prove quasi-unipotence of its graded pieces WHEN a Frobenius structure is present.
K must be discretely valued: the Frobenius (slope filtration) approach is not known for non-discrete K (overview Remarks 6.2.3-6.2.5).
The allowed extension is a finite étale extension of R^int (a finite cover of the thin annulus), not merely an extension of K; Bessel's isocrystal needs R_K[t^{1/2}] (arXiv:math/0110124 §1.5).
Kedlaya 2004 assumes φ is a composition power of a p-power Frobenius lift; SFR allows any Frobenius lift, and RD.1/change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures shows the choice of φ does not matter.

Modules are finite free (finite locally free over the Bézout ring R_K, RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains; finitely presented modules with connection are free, RD.2/finitely-presented-differential-module-is-free).
proofSteps: Horizontality of the slope filtration: RD.2/slope-filtration-is-horizontal (each M_i is a (φ,∇)-submodule).

It suffices to show each graded piece M_i/M_{i−1} is quasi-unipotent (quasi-unipotence is stable under extensions). Unipotence does not depend on the Frobenius lift, so one may apply [b]_* and twist to reduce to the unit-root case (SFR proof of Theorem 7.2.5).

A unit-root piece descends to an isoclinic (σ,∇)-module over R^bd (RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring (c) and RD.2/isoclinic-model-inherits-connection), which is quasi-constant by RD.2/tsuzuki-unit-root-finite-monodromy.
Precise form with nearly separable L: RD.2/slope-pieces-horizontal-after-finite-extension; the conclusion 'Theorem 1.1 follows immediately' (arXiv:math/0110124 p. 80).
Arbitrary Frobenius lift: RD.1/change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures.
acceptance: Bessel isocrystal (arXiv:math/0110124 §1.5; p odd, O = Z_p[π], π^{p−1} = −p, t^σ = t^p): a rank two (σ,∇)-module with generic slopes 0, 1 and special slopes 1/2, 1/2 which becomes unipotent over R_K[y], y = (t/4)^{1/2}: the permitted extension is a finite extension of R^int (adjoining a square root of t), not a coefficient extension.
Dwork's module at ∞ (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example): quasi-constant, trivialised only by a wildly ramified Artin-Schreier extension.

Nilpotent form (abstract of arXiv:math/0110124): after the finite cover M has a basis on which the connection acts by a nilpotent matrix, i.e. a unipotent basis with nilpotent residue (RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue); tested on SFR Example 7.2.6 by RD.2/unipotent-log-extension-nilpotent-residue-example.
Without Frobenius the conclusion fails: RD.2/frobenius-hypothesis-is-necessary.

nodes.title: Local monodromy theorem in finite étale form (the form used for finiteness of rigid cohomology)
nodes.statement: Let M be a free (σ,∇)-module over R_K. Then there exist an integer m ≥ 0, a finite unramified extension K_1 of K_0 = K^{σ^{-m}}, a finite Galois étale extension R' of R^int_{K_1}, and a continuous K_1-algebra isomorphism R'' := R_{K_1} ⊗_{R^int_{K_1}} R' ≅ R_{K_1}, such that M ⊗ R'' is unipotent, i.e. has a basis v_1, ..., v_n with ∇v_i ∈ (R'' v_1 + ... + R'' v_{i−1}) ⊗ dt/t. The conclusion does not depend on the choice of the isomorphism R'' ≅ R_{K_1}. (Kedlaya, Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients, Theorem 5.1.2.) If k is perfect one may take m = 0.
hypotheses: This is the local input for RD.5 (finiteness, duality); RD.5 also needs the relative version over dagger algebras (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Theorem 5.1.3), which is an additional construction owned by RD.5.
K_0 = K^{σ^{-m}} denotes K viewed as a K-algebra through σ^{-m}_K; its residue field, as an extension of k, is k^{q^{-m}} (adjoin the q^m-th roots of k).
proofSteps: By RD.1/change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures assume σ is a power of a p-power lift. By RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement (precise form), M becomes unipotent over the Robba ring of a nearly finite separable extension L of k_0((t)), k_0 = k^{q^{-m}}; enlarge L to be Galois and increase m so that the residue field k_1 of L is separable over k_0.

Let K_1 be the unramified extension of K_0 with residue field k_1; lift L to a finite étale R' over the henselian R^int_{K_1} (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (a)); the Cohen structure theorem L ≅ k_1((u)) and a lift of u give R'' ≅ R_{K_1} (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (c)) (Kedlaya, Finiteness, proof of Theorem 5.1.2).
acceptance: For M unipotent already (e.g. SFR Example 7.2.6) take m = 0, K_1 = K, R' = R^int.
For the Dwork module at ∞: R' = R^int[y]/(y^p − y − t^{-1}), K_1 = K (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example).
The Kummer module De = e/(q−1) over R_K becomes unipotent (indeed trivial) over the degree q−1 Kummer extension, which is identified with R_{K_1} via u = t^{1/(q−1)}.

nodes.title: Logarithmic form of the p-adic local monodromy theorem
nodes.statement: Let M be a (σ,∇)-module over R_K (K discretely valued, any k, any Frobenius lift). Then for some finite separable (nearly finite separable if k is imperfect) extension L of k((t)), M admits a basis over R^L_log of elements of ker ∇; i.e. the horizontal sections V_L(M) := (M ⊗_{R_K} R^L_log)^{∇=0} satisfy V_L(M) ⊗_{K'} R^L_log ≅ M ⊗ R^L_log, where K' is the field of constants of R^L. If k is algebraically closed, M ⊗ R^L_log is a direct sum of standard (σ,∇)-submodules. (arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 6.13, the form consumed by Berger's proof of the p-adic monodromy conjecture.)
hypotheses: Same hypotheses as RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement.

Inductively put w_i = v_i − Σ_{j<i} e_{ij} w_j where d/du e_{ij} = c_{ij} is solved in R^L_log by RD.2/log-robba-ring-antiderivative; then ∇w_i = 0 (Annals Theorem 6.13 proof; the printed indices '∇v_i = Σ_{j<i} A_ij v_i' and 'put ∇v_j = ...' are misprints for A_ij v_j and ∇v_i, already recorded by the decomposition).

nodes.title: The (φ, N, Gal)-module of logarithmic solutions (local monodromy representation)
nodes.statement: For a (σ,∇)-module M over R_K and L as in RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy (L/k((t)) Galois, k_L/k separable), define V_L(M) := (M ⊗_{R_K} R^L_log)^{∇=0}, a K'-vector space of dimension rank(M) (K' the constant field of R^L), with: φ := (F ⊗ φ)|_{V_L(M)}, σ-semilinear and bijective; N := (1 ⊗ N)|_{V_L(M)}, nilpotent, with N φ = q φ N; and a semilinear action of G_L := Gal(L/k((t))) commuting with φ and N. The natural map V_L(M) ⊗_{K'} R^L_log → M ⊗ R^L_log is an isomorphism compatible with φ, ∇ (via d on R^L_log), N and G_L. Passing to K^unr and letting L grow gives the monodromy representation of M: a permissible semilinear representation of G_log = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) × K (Kedlaya overview Definition 4.7.5).
hypotheses: L is only determined up to enlargement; V_L(M) ⊗_{K'} K'' = V_{L'}(M) for L ⊆ L' (compatible choices of ℓ).
q is the order of the Frobenius lift; in Fontaine's normalisation (q = p) the relation reads Nφ = pφN.
proofSteps: dim V_L(M) = rank M: RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy.
φ preserves V: F commutes with ∇ (compatibility) and φ on R^L_log is compatible with d.
N preserves V: N is R^L-linear on R^L_log and commutes with d (RD.2/log-robba-ring), hence 1 ⊗ N commutes with ∇; N is nilpotent since it lowers the ℓ-degree; Nφ = qφN from N∘φ = qφ∘N on R^L_log.
Galois action from the action on R^L_log (RD.2/log-robba-ring), commuting with ∇, φ, N.

nodes.title: Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules are classified by their monodromy representations
nodes.statement: Let K be complete discretely valued (more generally complete nonarchimedean of characteristic 0 with the overview's conventions). The monodromy representation M ↦ V(M) ⊗ K^unr is an equivalence from quasi-unipotent ∇-modules over R_K to permissible semilinear representations of G_log = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) × K on finite-dimensional K^unr-vector spaces (restriction to an open subgroup of the Galois factor trivial, restriction to K algebraic, hence unipotent). For k algebraically closed this is essentially André's Théorème 7.1.1 (the Tannakian group of (R_K̄, d)-modules with Frobenius structure is I × G_a).
hypotheses: The Frobenius structure is not part of the equivalence; restricted to modules admitting a Frobenius structure, the image consists of representations with the additional constraints of overview Proposition 6.1.5.
proofSteps: Full faithfulness as for quasi-constant modules (overview Lemma 4.3.2); essential surjectivity: indecomposable permissible representations are tensor products of a finite-image Galois representation (Lemma 4.3.2) and a unipotent representation of K (RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue), using Matsuda's decomposition E = ⊕ F_i ⊗ U_i (overview Theorem 4.6.6) (overview Theorem 4.7.6).
acceptance: (R_K, d) ↦ trivial one-dimensional representation; SFR Example 7.2.6 ↦ the two-dimensional unipotent representation of K (c acting by exp(cN)).

nodes.title: Comparison with Berger's Théorème 5.20 (the export to PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3)
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p (Berger's setting: k perfect, reduced to k algebraically closed in his proof), R_K = B†_rig,K Berger's Robba ring with Frobenius ϕ and derivation ∂ (∂f(π) = (1+π) df/dπ on B†_rig,F), and M a finitely presented R_K-module with a connection ∇_M (equivalently ∂_M) and a Frobenius structure (M a ϕ-module, ϕ*M = M, and ∂_M∘ϕ = pϕ∘∂_M). Then M is free, (M, ϕ, ∇) is a (φ,∇)-module over a Robba ring in Kedlaya's sense, and there is a finite extension L/K such that M has a basis of solutions in B†_log,L = R_L[log π]; equivalently (M ⊗_{R_K} B†_log,L)^{∂_M=0} has dimension rank M over L ∩ F^nr and generates M ⊗ B†_log,L. This is Berger's Théorème 5.20 (attributed by Berger to André, with Kedlaya's proof as an alternative), deduced here from RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy.
hypotheses: The identification of B†_rig,K with a Robba ring R_{F'}(π_K) (Berger Proposition 2.31), of its finite étale extensions with the rings B†_rig,L for finite L/K (field of norms), and the (ϕ, Γ) structures are owned by PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations and PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.0 and imported by request.

Berger's ϕ satisfies ϕ(π) ≡ π^p mod p (q = p), so it is a Frobenius lift in the sense of RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring; the condition ∂_M∘ϕ = pϕ∘∂_M is the compatibility ∇∘F = (F⊗dϕ)∘∇ because dx = (π∂x/(1+π)) dπ/π on R_F (Berger p. 57).
Berger's 'de présentation finie' is harmless: finitely presented modules with connection are free (RD.2/finitely-presented-differential-module-is-free).

R06.3 separately owns the bridge V ↦ N_dR(V) (Berger Théorèmes 3.6, 5.10, §5.4) and the deduction that de Rham representations are potentially semistable; RD.2 exports only the analytic statement above.
proofSteps: Transport: by the requested identification R_K ≅ R_{F'} (variable π_K), (M, ϕ, ∇) is a (φ,∇)-module over a Robba ring over a discretely valued field with perfect residue field.
Apply RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy: over the Robba ring R^{L'} of a finite separable extension L' of k_K((π̄_K)) and in R^{L'}_log, M has a basis of horizontal sections.

By the field of norms (request to PG.0), L' corresponds to a finite extension L/K with R^{L'} = B†_rig,L; the logarithms log u (u lifting a uniformiser of L') and log π differ by an element of B†_rig,L (RD.2/log-robba-ring, independence of u), so R^{L'}_log = B†_log,L and the solution spaces agree (RD.2/solution-space-phi-n-module).
Freeness of M: RD.2/finitely-presented-differential-module-is-free.
acceptance: For V = Q_p(1) (cyclotomic character, Hodge-Tate weight 1), N_dR(V) is a rank one ϕ-module with connection over R_{Q_p} trivialised over R_{Q_p} itself: L = Q_p suffices (V is crystalline).
SFR Remark 3.3.6: with π^σ = (1+π)^q − 1 the element log(1+π) of R satisfies x^σ = qx — Berger's t = log(1+π) — so H^0(R(−1)) depends on σ, which is why the comparison must fix Berger's ϕ.

nodes.title: Acceptance: a unipotent logarithmic extension and its nilpotent residue
nodes.statement: Let u^σ = u^q (standard Frobenius lift) and M = R_K e_1 ⊕ R_K e_2 with F e_1 = e_1, F e_2 = q e_2, ∇e_1 = 0, ∇e_2 = e_1 ⊗ du/u (SFR Example 7.2.6, whose printed 'u^σ = qu' must be read u^σ = u^q). Then: (a) M is a (σ,∇)-module; (b) M is unipotent but not quasi-constant; (c) M extends to the log-∇-module on the open disc with basis e_1, e_2 and connection d + N_0 du/u, whose residue N_0 = [[0,1],[0,0]] is nilpotent; (d) on the solution space V(M) = K e_1 ⊕ K(e_2 − ℓ e_1) the monodromy operator is N_0 and N_0 φ = q φ N_0 with φ = diag(1, q); (e) conversely, a Frobenius structure forces the residue of any logarithmic extension to be nilpotent (its eigenvalues are stable under multiplication by q and lie in K).
hypotheses: Characteristic 0 coefficients: residue eigenvalues killed by differentiation lie in K (Kedlaya, Notes Definition 7.2).
proofSteps: (a) ∇(F e_2) = q e_1 ⊗ du/u and (F ⊗ dσ)(∇e_2) = F e_1 ⊗ d(u^q)/u^q = q e_1 ⊗ du/u (verified symbolically in PARI/GP; with the printed u^σ = qu the right side would be e_1 ⊗ du/u ≠ q e_1 ⊗ du/u).

(b) unipotent basis e_1, e_2 (RD.2/unipotent-differential-module); not quasi-constant because by RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue M corresponds to (K², N_0) with N_0 ≠ 0, and pullback along a finite étale R^L multiplies N_0 by the ramification index (tame) or keeps it nonzero, so M ⊗ R^L is never spanned by horizontal sections (ker ∇ has rank 1 over every R^L).
(c),(d): RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue and RD.2/solution-space-phi-n-module: ∇(e_2 − ℓe_1) = 0, N(e_2 − ℓe_1) = e_1, φ(e_2 − ℓe_1) = q(e_2 − ℓe_1).

(e) If E is a log-(F-)isocrystal the Frobenius maps the residue to q times its σ-twist, so the finite set of eigenvalues is stable under multiplication by q, hence equal to {0} (Kedlaya, Notes Definition 7.2).
acceptance: N_0 φ = q φ N_0 for N_0 = [[0,1],[0,0]], φ = diag(1,q): checked in PARI/GP (N*F(3) == 3*F(3)*N returns 1).
Residue nilpotent of index 2; H^0(M) = K e_1 = ker N_0 and H^1(M) ≅ coker N_0 is one-dimensional (Crew, Remark after Proposition 6.7).

nodes.title: Acceptance: without a Frobenius structure the local monodromy theorem fails (an exponential of the wrong radius)
nodes.statement: Let M_λ = R_K e with ∇e = λ e ⊗ dt, λ ∈ K. (a) If |λ| ≤ p^{-1/(p−1)} (e.g. λ = π with π^{p−1} = −p), exp(−λt) ∈ R^int is a unit and M_λ is trivial. (b) If |λ| > p^{-1/(p−1)} (e.g. λ = 1), the generic radius is R(M_λ, ρ) = min(ρ, p^{-1/(p−1)}/|λ|), so lim_{ρ→1} R(M_λ, ρ)/ρ = p^{-1/(p−1)}/|λ| < 1: M_λ is not overconvergent (not solvable). Hence M_λ admits no Frobenius structure for any Frobenius lift (RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability) and is not quasi-unipotent (RD.2/quasi-unipotent-implies-overconvergent). In particular the conclusion of the local monodromy theorem fails for ∇-modules without Frobenius structure. (c) Independent check for λ = 1: if M_1 ⊗ R^L were constant for some finite separable L, a horizontal unit f with df/dt = −f would reduce (after scaling into (R^int_L)^×) to 0 ≠ f̄ ∈ L with D f̄ = −f̄, D = d/dt; but D^p is a derivation of L vanishing on k((t)), hence on the separable extension L, while D^p f̄ = (−1)^p f̄ ≠ 0 — contradiction; a rank one quasi-unipotent module is quasi-constant, so M_1 is not quasi-unipotent.
hypotheses: Uses the generic radius of RD.1/generic-radius in Kedlaya's normalisation R(E,ρ) = p^{-1/(p−1)}|T|^{-1}_{ρ,sp}, |T|_{ρ,sp} = max{p^{-1/(p−1)}ρ^{-1}, lim sup |D_s|_ρ^{1/s}} (the 'min' printed in the overview is corrected to 'max' by the author's errata).

Kedlaya's §1.2 of arXiv:math/0110124 only records that the Christol-Mebkhout weight filtration exists with or without Frobenius; this node supplies the sourced counterexample required by the stage acceptance.
proofSteps: (a) The coefficients π^n/n! of exp(πt) have valuation s_p(n)/(p−1) ≥ 0 (verified in PARI/GP for n ≤ 200, p = 3, 5), so exp(−πt) ∈ R^int with inverse exp(πt).
Overconvergence ⇔ lim R(E,ρ)/ρ = 1 (Kedlaya overview Remark 5.1.6); Frobenius ⇒ overconvergent (overview Lemma 6.1.4); quasi-unipotent ⇒ overconvergent (overview Remark 4.6.7).
(c) elementary; units of R^L lie in R^{bd}_L and have a unit multiple in (R^int_L)^× (RD.0/units-of-analytic-ring), and d preserves R^int_L.
acceptance: λ = 1, p odd or p = 2: R(M_1, ρ)/ρ → p^{-1/(p−1)} (1/√3 for p = 3), numerically confirmed.
λ = π: M_π is trivial; this is the connection of the Dwork isocrystal L_π at the finite points (Berthelot 4.2.3), which does carry a Frobenius structure.
