nodes.title: Acceptance: the Dwork isocrystal at ∞ is trivialised by an Artin-Schreier extension of the Robba ring
nodes.statement: Let p be odd or even, K = Q_p(π) with π^{p−1} = −p, and consider the Dwork F-isocrystal L_π on A^1_{F_p} (Berthelot 4.2.3: rank one, ∇(1) = π dt, Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t) for the lift t ↦ t^p). At the boundary point ∞, in the Robba ring R_K in the parameter s = 1/t, the (φ,∇)-module M = R_K e with ∇e = π e ⊗ dt has horizontal section candidate exp(−πt) = exp(−π/s), which does not converge near |s| = 1, so M is not constant. Over the Artin-Schreier extension R^int_L = R^int[y]/(y^p − y − t) (L = F_p((s))[ȳ]/(ȳ^p − ȳ − s^{-1}), wildly ramified, Swan conductor 1), exp(−πt) = exp(π(y − y^p)) = E(y) with Dwork's exponential E(z) = exp(π(z − z^p)), which converges for |z| < p^{(p−1)/p²}; since |y| = |s|^{-1/p} → 1 at the boundary, E(y) ∈ (R^L)^× and E(y)·e is a horizontal basis: M ⊗ R^L is constant. This realises concretely the finite étale (Artin-Schreier) extensions allowed by the local monodromy theorem.
hypotheses: The Frobenius structure Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t) of L_π is overconvergent ('dont la surconvergence est classique', Berthelot 4.2.3), so M is a (φ,∇)-module over R_K at ∞ with φ(s) = s^p.
proofSteps: y ∈ R^int_L exists: Y^p − Y − t is monic over R^int (t = s^{-1} ∈ R^int) with unit derivative mod π, so R^int[y] is finite étale with residue field L (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring).

Radius of E: the coefficients c_n of exp(π(z − z^p)) satisfy v_p(c_n) ≥ n(p−1)/p² (PARI/GP check for n ≤ 200 and p = 3, 5, 7: all inequalities hold, minimal slack at n = 1), so E converges on |z| < p^{(p−1)/p²}, a disc strictly containing the closed unit disc.
Horizontality: d(E(y)) = π(1 − p y^{p−1}) E(y) dy and dt = (p y^{p−1} − 1) dy, so dE(y) = −π E(y) dt; hence ∇(E(y) e) = 0.
acceptance: Exercise of Berthelot 4.2.4: H^*_rig(A^1/K, L_π) = H^*_c(A^1/K, L_π) = 0 (consistent with Swan conductor 1 at ∞ and the Euler characteristic χ(A^1)·1 − Swan = 1 − 1 = 0).

nodes.title: Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)
nodes.statement: Setting of RD.3: K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0, O = O_K, residue field k of characteristic p (perfect where stated), σ_K a Frobenius lift on K; schemes are separated of finite type over k (Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme with the morphism classes of SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0); formal O-schemes are separated and topologically of finite type, and P_K denotes the generic fibre of a formal scheme P as a rigid analytic space with specialisation map sp : P_K → P (both imported from AdicSpacesPartII:R2). A frame is a triple (X, Y, P) with j : X → Y an open immersion of k-schemes, i : Y → P a closed immersion of Y into the special fibre of a formal O-scheme P, such that P is smooth over Spf O in a neighbourhood of X; put Z = Y \ X. The frame is proper if Y is proper over k, and then P_K, ]Y[_P and all constructions only depend on a neighbourhood of Y. A morphism of frames (X', Y', P') → (X, Y, P) is a triple (w, v, u) of morphisms w : X' → X, v : Y' → Y, u : P' → P with i∘v = u∘i' and j∘w = v∘j'; it is smooth near X' if u is smooth in a neighbourhood of X'.
hypotheses: P need not be smooth at the points of Z: for X smooth affine with a smooth lift 𝔛 and Y = X̄ the closure in projective space, P = the formal completion of the closure of 𝔛 is not smooth along Z in general (Berthelot 2.3 remark), which is why only smoothness near X is required.

Frames exist locally: an affine Y admits a closed immersion into the special fibre of the formal affine space over O, which is smooth; global frames need not exist, and constructions are then glued (Čech), see RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety.
proofSteps: The data are Mathlib schemes and morphism classes (AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion, IsClosedImmersion, IsProper, Smooth) together with a formal scheme from AdicSpacesPartII:R2; smoothness of P near X is smoothness of the reductions P ⊗ O/π^n near X (Berthelot 1.1).
acceptance: Standard frame of the affine line: (A^1_k, P^1_k, P̂^1_O); the tube of A^1 is the closed unit disc and the tube of ∞ is the open disc |t| > 1 around ∞.

nodes.statement: For a formal O-scheme P (separated, topologically of finite type) and a locally closed subscheme T of its special fibre, the tube of T is ]T[_P := sp^{-1}(T), an admissible open of the generic fibre P_K. If P = Spf A is affine and T is closed, cut out by π and f_1, ..., f_r ∈ Γ(P, O_P), then ]T[_P = {x ∈ P_K : |f_i(x)| < 1 for all i}; for λ ∈ |K^×|^Q ∩ (0,1) the open tube of radius λ is ]T[_{P,λ} = {x : |f_i(x)| < λ for all i}, independent of the equations when |a| < λ for all a ∈ m_K (discrete valuation), which defines it for non-affine P.

nodes.title: Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[
nodes.statement: Let (X, Y, P) be a frame, Z = Y \ X, and for λ < 1 put U_λ := ]Y[_P \ ]Z[_{P,λ} (for P affine and f_1..f_r ∈ Γ(P, O_P) lifting equations of Z in Y, U'_λ := {x ∈ ]Y[ : max_i |f_i(x)| ≥ λ} may be used instead). An admissible open V ⊆ ]Y[_P is a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P if ]X[_P ⊆ V and for every affinoid W ⊆ ]Y[_P there is λ < 1 with W ∩ U_λ ⊆ W ∩ V. For P non-affine the condition is imposed locally.
hypotheses: Strict neighbourhoods form a filtered family stable under finite intersections; each U_λ (|π| < λ < 1) is a strict neighbourhood, and every strict neighbourhood contains W ∩ U_{λ(W)} for each affinoid W ⊆ ]Y[.

In adic terms (AdicSpacesPartII:F1), a strict neighbourhood is a neighbourhood of the closure of ]X[ in ]Y[; F1 owns the dagger-affinoid version (cofinal systems of strict neighbourhoods of an affinoid in a larger one), RD.3 owns the tube version.
proofSteps: Replacing U_λ by U'_λ does not change the notion (Berthelot 2.2).
Intersections: V_1 ∩ V_2 is a strict neighbourhood (take the larger λ on each W).

Pullback along a morphism of frames (w, v, u) with v^{-1}(X) = X' (equivalently v^{-1}(Z) = Z'): u_K^{-1}(V) ∩ ]Y'[ is a strict neighbourhood of ]X'[, since the pullbacks f_i∘u of equations of Z are equations of Z' and |f_i∘u| = |f_i|∘u_K (Berthelot 2.2).

nodes.title: Berthelot's functor j† of overconvergent sections
nodes.statement: Let (X, Y, P) be a frame and j_λ : U_λ ↪ ]Y[_P the inclusions of the complements of the tubes of radius λ of Z (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood). For an abelian sheaf E on ]Y[_P put j†E := lim_{λ→1} j_{λ*} j_λ^* E, the sheaf of germs of sections of E in a neighbourhood of ]X[; equivalently j†E = lim_V j_{V*} j_V^* E over strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[ in ]Y[. In particular j†O_{]Y[} is a sheaf of rings on ]Y[_P and j†E is a j†O_{]Y[}-module for E an O_{]Y[}-module. For a morphism of frames u : P' → P there is a canonical map j†E → u_* j'† u^{-1} E.
hypotheses: The family U_λ may be replaced by U'_λ = {x ∈ ]Y[ : max |f_i(x)| ≥ λ} for any lifts f_i of equations of Z (Berthelot 2.2).
j† depends only on a strict neighbourhood: if V is a strict neighbourhood then j†E is determined by E|_V and H*(]Y[, j†E) = H*(V, j†E) (Berthelot 2.5 a)).
proofSteps: Direct limit of sheaves (a sheaf on the G-topology of ]Y[ since the limit is filtered).
Module structure and the canonical map from the adjunctions (Berthelot 2.2, construction of (2.2.1)).

For (A^1, P^1, P̂^1): Γ(]P^1[, j†O) = lim_{ρ→1^+} O({|t| ≤ ρ}) = K⟨t⟩†, the overconvergent power series (RD.3/overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame).

nodes.title: Exactness of j† on coherent sheaves and the acyclicity of j_{λ*}
nodes.statement: Let (X, Y, P) be a frame with P affine. For a coherent O_{]Y[}-module E: (a) R^q j_{λ*}(j_λ^* E) = 0 for q > 0; (b) H^q(]Y[, j†E) = lim_λ H^q(U_λ, E) and, for Y quasi-compact, j† commutes with cohomology in this sense; (c) j† is exact on coherent sheaves and j†E = j†O ⊗ E.
hypotheses: P affine; the input is that j_λ : U_λ → ]Y[ is a quasi-Stein morphism (preimages of affinoids are increasing unions of affinoids with dense transition maps), so that Kiehl's Theorem B (AdicSpacesPartII:R3) applies, as Berthelot indicates.
proofSteps: Theorem B for quasi-Stein spaces (Kiehl; Kedlaya, Finiteness, Proposition 4.1.4) gives (a) (Berthelot 2.1: 'les faisceaux cohérents sont acycliques pour j_{λ*}').
(b) from (a) and quasi-compactness of ]Y[ pieces (cohomology commutes with filtered direct limits on quasi-compact quasi-separated sites).
(c) filtered colimits are exact.

nodes.title: Global overconvergent functions on an affine frame are the dagger algebra
nodes.statement: Let X = Spec A_0 be a smooth affine k-scheme, A a smooth O-algebra lifting A_0 with a presentation A = O[t_1..t_n]/I, 𝔛 = Spec A ⊂ A^n_O ⊂ P^n_O, X̄ the closure of X in P^n_k and P the formal completion of the closure of 𝔛 in P^n_O. Then for λ < 1, U_λ = 𝔛_K^an ∩ {closed ball of radius 1/λ}, and Γ(]X̄[_P, j†O) = lim_{λ→1} Γ(U_λ, O) = A† ⊗ K, the weak completion of A tensored with K (the Monsky-Washnitzer dagger algebra). More generally the direct limit of Γ(V, O_V) over strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[ is a dagger algebra of MW type with reduction A_0.
hypotheses: The frame (X, X̄, P) has P smooth near X but possibly singular along X̄ \ X (Berthelot 2.3 remark).
proofSteps: Identify the tube ]X̄[ with 𝔛_K^an ∩ P^{n,an}_K and ]Z[_λ with the complement of the ball of radius 1/λ by an exercise in projective coordinates (Berthelot 2.1).

Γ(U_λ, O) is the ring of functions on the affinoid 𝔛_K^an ∩ B(0, 1/λ); their union is A† ⊗ K by the definition of weak completion (AdicSpacesPartII:F1: dagger algebras as unions over radius-indexed presentations; Kedlaya, Finiteness, §2.2 and Remark 4.2.5).

X = G_m: A† ⊗ K = K⟨t, t^{-1}⟩†, the functions overconverging near |t| = 1 on both sides.

nodes.title: Weak fibration theorem: tubes along smooth morphisms are open polydisc fibrations
nodes.statement: Let X be a k-scheme, i : X ↪ P and i' : X ↪ P' immersions into formal O-schemes and u : P' → P a morphism smooth in a neighbourhood of X with u∘i' = i, of relative dimension n near X. Then u_K : ]X[_{P'} → ]X[_P is a fibration in open unit polydiscs: there is an affine covering (P_i) of P and isomorphisms ]X[_{P'} ∩ u_K^{-1}(P_{i,K}) ≅ (]X[_P ∩ P_{i,K}) × D(0,1^-)^n commuting with the projections. Consequently Ru_{K*} Ω^•_{]X[_{P'}/]X[_P} ≃ O_{]X[_P} (Poincaré lemma on open polydiscs and Theorem B), which gives Berthelot's Proposition 1.
hypotheses: u need only be smooth near X; P, P' need not be smooth.
proofSteps: Locally on P', choose t_1..t_n ∈ Γ(P', O) vanishing on X whose differentials form a basis of Ω_{P'/P} near X; then P' → P ×_O Â^n_O is étale near X and maps X into the zero section.
For an étale morphism inducing an isomorphism on X the tubes are isomorphic (Hensel/infinitesimal lifting on each residue class); the tube of the zero section of Â^n over P is ]X[_P × D(0,1^-)^n.

PROOF SOURCE GAP: Berthelot 1986 states Lemme 1 without proof ('les démonstrations seront publiées ailleurs'); the proof is in Berthelot's unpublished preprint [3a] ('Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide à supports propres') and in Le Stum's book 'Rigid Cohomology', neither in the public source set; the exact numbering there was not checked (see gaps).
acceptance: X = a point x ∈ A^1_k, P = Â^1_O, P' = Â^2_O → P the first projection: ]x[_{P'} = ]x[_P × D(0,1^-) (a residue polydisc).

nodes.title: Strong fibration theorem: strict neighbourhoods along smooth morphisms
nodes.statement: Let (w, v, u) : (X, Y', P') → (X, Y, P) be a morphism of frames with w = id_X, v proper (e.g. v = id), and u smooth in a neighbourhood of X of relative dimension n, with P, P' smooth near X. Then, locally on P, there are strict neighbourhoods V' of ]X[_{P'} in ]Y'[_{P'} and V of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P with an isomorphism V' ≅ V × D(0,1^-)^n over V; in particular, locally on P, u admits sections over strict neighbourhoods, and u_K induces isomorphisms on the cohomology of j†Ω^• and equivalences on overconvergent isocrystals.
hypotheses: This is the form used to prove Berthelot's Théorèmes 1 and 3 and the independence of frames; it strengthens RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem 'à la frontière' (Berthelot 2.3).
proofSteps: Reduce as in RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem to u étale-locally a projection P ×_O Â^n → P near X; the tube-level fibration extends to strict neighbourhoods by an analysis of the boundary of ]X[ (Berthelot 2.3: 'dont la démonstration nécessite une étude à la frontière de ]X[ complétant la proposition 1').

nodes.title: Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame
nodes.statement: Let (X, Y, P) be a frame, p_1, p_2 : ]Y[_{P×P} → ]Y[_P the projections (Y embedded diagonally) and j† the functors on ]Y[_{P^m}. An isocrystal on X overconvergent along Z = Y \ X (relative to K, realised on P) is a j†O_{]Y[_P}-module E, locally free of finite rank, with an isomorphism ε : p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E of j†O_{]Y[_{P²}}-modules satisfying the usual cocycle condition on ]Y[_{P³} (and ε restricting to the identity on the diagonal). Morphisms are j†O-linear maps compatible with ε. Equivalently (RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal-connection-form) it is a locally free module M with integrable connection ∇ on some strict neighbourhood V of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P whose Taylor series is induced by an analytic isomorphism p_2^*M ≅ p_1^*M on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P²} in ]Y[_{P²}, two such data being identified when they agree on a smaller strict neighbourhood. The category is denoted Isoc(X, Y, P/K) (Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) after RD.3/independence-of-frame).
hypotheses: The convergence condition on the Taylor isomorphism is real extra data without Frobenius (Kedlaya, Notes Remark 2.12); with a Frobenius structure it is automatic (Berthelot's unpublished Théorème 2.5.7, quoted by Kedlaya).

Coherent j†O-modules with such a stratification are automatically locally free (a coherent module with a connection on a smooth rigid space is locally free, Kedlaya Notes Remark 2.3; Kedlaya Finiteness Lemma 3.3.4 for dagger algebras).
proofSteps: Well-defined as a category: the cocycle condition is the usual one for stratifications; morphisms are germs on strict neighbourhoods (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood intersections).
acceptance: The constant object j†O with ε = canonical identification; the Dwork isocrystal L_π on (A^1, P^1, P̂^1) (Berthelot 4.2.3): M = O_V with ∇(1) = π dt, Taylor isomorphism ε(1) = exp π(t' − t), analytic on {|t − t'| < 1}, a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P²}.

nodes.title: Stratifications versus connections with overconvergent Taylor series
nodes.statement: For a frame (X, Y, P), the functor (E, ε) ↦ (E|_V, ∇) is an equivalence between overconvergent isocrystals in the stratification form (RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal) and locally free modules with integrable connection on strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P whose formal Taylor isomorphism ε(1 ⊗ m) = Σ_q (1/q!) ∇(D)^q(m) ⊗ τ^q (τ_i = 1 ⊗ t_i − t_i ⊗ 1 for local coordinates t_i on P near X) is induced by an analytic isomorphism p_2^*M ≅ p_1^*M on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P²} in ]Y[_{P²}.
hypotheses: P smooth near X with local coordinates t_1..t_n; the diagonal P → P × P is then a closed immersion with ]X[_P → ]X[_{P²} a fibration in open unit polydiscs (RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem).
proofSteps: ε ↦ ∇: restrict ε to the first-order infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal (Berthelot 4.1).

∇ ↦ ε: the Taylor series defines ε on the formal completion of the diagonal; the convergence hypothesis says it is induced by an analytic isomorphism on a strict neighbourhood; the cocycle condition holds formally, hence analytically since the tube of the diagonal is a polydisc fibration over ]X[ (RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem) and analytic functions on open polydiscs are determined by their Taylor expansion along the centre section (Berthelot 4.1, 4.2.1).

nodes.title: Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames
nodes.statement: For a morphism of frames (w, v, u) : (X', Y', P') → (X, Y, P) the pullback u^* : Isoc(X, Y, P/K) → Isoc(X', Y', P'/K) sends (E, ε) to (j'†u_K^* E, (u×u)^*ε), using that u_K maps strict neighbourhoods of ]X'[ into strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood); in connection form it is the usual pullback of modules with connection. It is compatible with composition up to canonical isomorphism, with ⊗ and duals, and (for Frobenius structures) with Frobenius pullbacks.
hypotheses: The functor depends on (w, v, u); RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks shows that for fixed (w, v) it is independent of u up to canonical isomorphism.
proofSteps: Pullback of stratifications along u × u : ]Y'[_{P'²} → ]Y[_{P²}; strictness of neighbourhoods by RD.3/strict-neighbourhood (pullback API); locally free modules pull back to locally free modules.
acceptance: Pullback along the identity is the identity; pullback of the unit object is the unit object.

nodes.title: Canonical isomorphisms between pullbacks along frame morphisms with the same reduction
nodes.statement: Let f, g : (X', Y', P') → (X, Y, P) be two morphisms of frames inducing the same morphisms X' → X and Y' → Y. For an overconvergent isocrystal (E, ε) on (X, Y, P), the pullback of ε along (f, g) : ]Y'[_{P'} → ]Y[_{P×P} defines an isomorphism χ_{f,g} : g^*E ≅ f^*E of overconvergent isocrystals; χ_{f,f} = id and χ_{f,g}∘χ_{g,h} = χ_{f,h}.
hypotheses: (f, g) maps X' into the diagonal image of X, hence ]X'[_{P'} into ]X[_{P×P}, and strict neighbourhoods into strict neighbourhoods (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood).
proofSteps: Pull back the stratification along (f, g); the cocycle identity for ε on ]Y[_{P³} pulled back along (f, g, h) gives the transitivity (standard crystal formalism; local analogue: Kedlaya overview Remark 4.1.9 for annuli).
acceptance: For f = g the isomorphism is the identity; for two Frobenius lifts f, g of P̂^1 inducing t ↦ t^p mod π, χ_{f,g} on L_π is multiplication by exp π(g(t) − f(t)).

but in fact there are canonical equivalences (via pullbacks, and relying on the convergence condition) between the categories constructed using different P .

nodes.title: Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals
nodes.statement: (a) If (id_X, id_Y, u) : (X, Y, P') → (X, Y, P) is a morphism of frames with u smooth in a neighbourhood of X, then u^* : Isoc(X, Y, P/K) → Isoc(X, Y, P'/K) is an equivalence of categories. (b) For two frames (X, Y, P_1), (X, Y, P_2) with the same (X, Y), the projections from the diagonal frame (X, Y, P_1 ×_O P_2) are smooth near X, and the composite equivalences E_{12} := (p_2^*)^{-1}∘p_1^* are canonical: independent of choices up to unique isomorphism and satisfying E_{23}∘E_{12} ≅ E_{13}. Hence Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) := Isoc(X, Y, P/K) depends only on (X ⊂ Y) up to canonical equivalence, is local on Y, and is functorial in (X ⊂ Y). The same holds with Frobenius structures (RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal).
hypotheses: P, P_i smooth near X; no hypothesis at the points of Z (Berthelot 2.3 remark).
For Y without a global embedding into a formal scheme smooth near X, the category is defined by gluing along a Čech covering by frames (RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety).
proofSteps: If u has a section s : P → P' over (X, Y), then s^* and u^* are quasi-inverse: s^*u^* = (us)^* = id and u^*s^* = (su)^* ≅ id^* by RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks (su and id_{P'} induce the same maps on X, Y).

In general, by RD.3/strong-fibration-theorem, locally on P there are strict neighbourhoods V' ≅ V × D(0,1^-)^n, so sections exist locally over strict neighbourhoods; the local quasi-inverses are compatible on overlaps by RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks and glue (descent of overconvergent isocrystals along admissible coverings of strict neighbourhoods, a stack property).

(b) The diagonal immersion Y → P_1 × P_2 is a closed immersion and the projections are smooth near X since P_i are; canonicity and the cocycle from RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks ('méthode du plongement diagonal', Berthelot 1.5).

PROOF SOURCE GAP for the gluing along the strong fibration: Berthelot 1986 states the result ('La catégorie ainsi obtenue ne dépend, à équivalence canonique près, que de X ⊂ Y'); the details are in his unpublished preprint and Le Stum's book (gaps).
acceptance: Two embeddings of affine space: (A^n, P^n, P̂^n) and (A^n, P^n, P̂^n ×_O P̂^n) (diagonal) give canonically equivalent categories; see RD.3/affine-space-two-embeddings-acceptance for two different compactifications.

For X smooth affine with lift A and two choices of presentation, the equivalence transports the (σ,∇)-module over A† ⊗ K realised in one presentation to the other by the Taylor isomorphism (Kedlaya Finiteness Remark 4.2.4: 'homotopy equivalences').

nodes.title: Independence of the compactification
nodes.statement: Let j : X ↪ Y and j' : X ↪ Y' be open immersions and v : Y' → Y a PROPER morphism with v∘j' = j and v^{-1}(X) = j'(X) (Kedlaya's formulation: f^{-1}(X) → X an isomorphism). Then v^* : Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) → Isoc†(X ⊂ Y'/K) is an equivalence of categories, compatible with Frobenius structures. Consequently, for a proper Y containing X as an open subscheme, Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) is independent of Y up to canonical equivalence (two compactifications are dominated by the closure of X in their product).
hypotheses: Proper compactifications exist for separated finite type X by Nagata's theorem (request to SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0); for quasi-projective X one may take a projective closure.
proofSteps: Choose frames Y ⊂ P and Y' ⊂ P' with a morphism u : P' → P lifting v (possible locally); after dévissage and base changes on P inducing an admissible covering of a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P, reduce to the case where a section P → P' extends the section X → P' ×_P X given by j'; then replace Y' by the image of Y in P' and apply RD.3/independence-of-frame (Berthelot, sketch of the proof of Théorème 2 in 2.4, applied to isocrystals in 4.2.2).
PROOF SOURCE GAP: the full proof is Berthelot's unpublished Théorème 2.3.5 (preprint 96-03) or Le Stum, Theorem 7.1.8; Kedlaya's Notes Lemma 2.6 records both references (gaps).
acceptance: X = A^2, Y = P^2 and Y' = the blow-up of P^2 at a point of the line at infinity: v^* is an equivalence although the boundaries Z = P^1 and Z' (two rational curves) differ.
X = A^1, Y = P^1, Y' = the closure of the diagonal in P^1 × P^1 with v a projection: v is an isomorphism and v^* is the identity up to canonical isomorphism.

sources.excerpt: On montre alors que le foncteur image inverse v^*, de la catégorie des cristaux sur X surconvergents le long de Z dans celle des cristaux sur X surconvergents le long de Z', est une équivalence de catégories.
Then the pullback functor F-Isoc(X, Y ) → F-Isoc(X, Y ′ ) is an equivalence of categories.
The original but unpublished reference is [12, Théorème 2.3.5]. An alternate reference is [81, Theorem 7.1.8].

nodes.title: The category Isoc†(X/K) of a separated finite type k-scheme
nodes.statement: For an open immersion X ⊂ Y of separated finite type k-schemes, Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) is defined, when Y embeds into a formal O-scheme P smooth near X, as Isoc(X, Y, P/K) (independent of P by RD.3/independence-of-frame), and in general by gluing along a Zariski covering of Y by opens Y_i admitting such embeddings (a Čech/stack construction, local on Y). For X separated of finite type over k, Isoc†(X/K) := Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) for some open immersion into a PROPER k-scheme Y (a compactification), independent of Y up to canonical equivalence by RD.3/independence-of-compactification. If X is proper, Isoc†(X/K) is the category of convergent isocrystals on X.
hypotheses: Compactifications exist by Nagata's theorem (requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0); frames exist Zariski-locally on Y (affine opens embed in formal affine spaces).
Isoc†(−/K) is a stack for the Zariski and étale topologies on X (Kedlaya, Notes Definition 2.4, Definition 2.7), which is what makes the gluing well defined.
proofSteps: Choose a covering of Y by affine opens Y_i with frames (X_i, Y_i, P_i); objects are families of overconvergent isocrystals on the frames of the Y_i together with gluing isomorphisms on the frames of Y_i ∩ Y_j (diagonal embeddings into P_i × P_j), satisfying the cocycle condition; independence of the covering by refinement and RD.3/independence-of-frame (Berthelot 1.5: 'une définition à la Čech').
PROOF SOURCE GAP: the stack property (effective descent for overconvergent isocrystals along Zariski and étale coverings) is stated by Kedlaya with reference to Le Stum's book, not available (gaps).
acceptance: X = A^n: Isoc†(A^n/K) is equivalent to the category of finite projective K⟨t_1..t_n⟩†-modules with integrable connection satisfying the overconvergence condition (RD.3/affine-smooth-description-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals).
X proper: Isoc†(X/K) = convergent isocrystals (Kedlaya, Notes Definition 2.7).

nodes.title: Overconvergent F-isocrystals
nodes.statement: Let σ_K be a Frobenius lift on K lifting the q-power map of k (q = p^a). The Frobenius pullback F^* on Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) is the composite of extension of scalars along σ_K and pullback along the relative q-power Frobenius of (X, Y) over k (realised on a frame by a lift σ : P → P of the q-power Frobenius compatible with σ_K, where such a lift exists, the result being independent of the lift by RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks). An overconvergent F-isocrystal on X is an object E ∈ Isoc†(X/K) with an isomorphism Φ : F^*E ≅ E; morphisms commute with Φ. The category is F-Isoc†(X/K) (F^a-Isoc† when the power a is to be recorded). Concretely on a frame with Frobenius lift σ (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 4.2.3): a finite locally free O_V-module E on a strict neighbourhood V of ]X[, with integrable connection satisfying the overconvergence condition, and an isomorphism F : σ^*E ≅ E of modules with connection.
hypotheses: The Frobenius structure forces the overconvergence condition on the Taylor isomorphism (Berthelot's unpublished Théorème 2.5.7, cited by Kedlaya), which is why Kedlaya's Definition 4.2.3 can leave it implicit; the condition is not automatic without Frobenius (Kedlaya, Notes Remark 2.12).
proofSteps: Existence of Frobenius lifts on frames: locally, for smooth affine pieces, by the lifting theorem for weakly complete algebras (RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra); globally F^* is defined by functoriality of Isoc† in (X ⊂ Y) (Berthelot 4.1-4.2).
Independence of the lift: RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks.
acceptance: The unit F-isocrystal O_X^† with Φ = id; the Dwork F-isocrystal L_π on A^1_{F_p} over K = Q_p(π) with σ_K = id, Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t) (Berthelot 4.2.3 c).

nodes.title: Rigid-analytic Quillen-Suslin: finite projective modules over K⟨t_1..t_n⟩† are free
nodes.statement: Every finite projective module over K⟨t_1, ..., t_n⟩† (overconvergent power series) is free; the same holds over O⟨t_1, ..., t_n⟩† when K is discretely valued. More precisely, for K complete with nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and ρ = (ρ_i) with some power of each ρ_i in |K^×|, every finite projective module over the ring K⟨t⟩_ρ of series converging on the closed polydisc of polyradius ρ is free.
hypotheses: The O-version requires K discretely valued, and Lemma 6.2 needs 'rank 1' in place of 'discrete' (published erratum by Davis-Schneider, Kedlaya's papers page).
proofSteps: Weierstrass preparation over o⟨t⟩_ρ (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Lemma 6.1) and Noether-normalisation changes of variables T_j (Lemmas 6.2, 6.3) reduce unimodular rows over K⟨t⟩_ρ to rows over polynomial rings in one variable over K⟨t'⟩_{ρ'}; Lang's Algebra Theorem XXI.3.4 and induction give the unimodular extension property (Proposition 6.4).
Finite free resolutions by induction (Proposition 6.5), so finite projective modules are stably free and hence free (Proposition 6.6); pass to the direct limit over ρ > 1 (Theorem 6.7).
acceptance: n = 1: for fixed ρ the ring K⟨t⟩_ρ is a principal ideal domain (Weierstrass preparation), so finite projective modules over it are free before passing to the limit over ρ > 1.

nodes.title: (σ,∇)-modules over a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type
nodes.statement: Let A be a dagger algebra of MW-type over K (a quotient of K⟨x_1,…,x_n⟩† that is regular and whose reduction A^int/πA^int is a smooth k-algebra), with its module of continuous differentials Ω^1_{A/K} (finite projective) and exterior powers Ω^i_{A/K} = ∧^i Ω^1_{A/K}, and let σ: A → A be a Frobenius lift (σ_K-semilinear, acting as the q-power map on the reduction). A (σ,∇)-module over A is a finite locally free A-module M together with (a) an integrable connection ∇: M → M ⊗_A Ω^1_{A/K}: a K-linear map with ∇(am) = a∇(m) + m ⊗ da and ∇_1 ∘ ∇ = 0, where ∇_i: M ⊗ Ω^i → M ⊗ Ω^{i+1} is the induced map; and (b) a Frobenius structure: an additive σ-semilinear map F: M → M (F(am) = σ(a)F(m)) whose linearisation σ^*M → M is an isomorphism; subject to ∇ ∘ F = (F ⊗ dσ) ∘ ∇, i.e. the linearisation is horizontal. Morphisms are A-linear maps commuting with ∇ and F. The trivial object is (A, d, σ).
hypotheses: A is a dagger algebra of MW-type; the regularity of A is part of the definition (Kedlaya's errata to Definition 3.2.1).
σ is a Frobenius lift in the sense of Kedlaya, Definition 3.2.3; its existence is RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra.
Over a regular A, a finitely generated A-module with connection is automatically locally free (Kedlaya, Lemma 3.3.4), so local freeness may be dropped from the input.
proofSteps: The dagger algebra, its differentials Ω^i_{A/K} and the exterior derivative d are supplied by AdicSpacesPartII:F1; tensor products are Mathlib's TensorProduct over A.
Leibniz and integrability are conditions on the data (∇, F); they are checked on the generators dx_j of Ω^1 for A a quotient of K⟨x_1,…,x_n⟩†.
Horizontality of the linearisation σ^*M → M is equivalent to ∇ ∘ F = (F ⊗ dσ) ∘ ∇ (Kedlaya, Remark 3.3.3).

Local freeness from a connection (Kedlaya, Lemma 3.3.4): at a maximal ideal a, a minimal nontrivial relation Σ c_i v_i = 0 among lifts of a basis of M/aM is differentiated along a vector field ∂_j with ∂_j c_1 of smaller order, producing a relation of smaller minimal order, a contradiction.
acceptance: The trivial module (A, d, σ) satisfies the axioms; its dual and tensor square are trivial.

The rank-one module over K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† with basis e, ∇e = a·e ⊗ dx/x and the standard Frobenius x ↦ x^q admits a Frobenius structure of the form e ↦ c·x^m·e exactly when (q−1)a ∈ ℤ, and then m = (q−1)a.

Let A be a regular affinoid or dagger algebra, and let M be a finitely generated A-module equipped with a connection ∇ : M → M ⊗ Ω1A/K . Then M is locally free.

nodes.title: Overconvergent F-isocrystals on a smooth affine variety are (σ,∇)-modules over its dagger algebra
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth affine k-scheme, A a dagger algebra of MW-type with special fibre X (it exists and is unique up to non-canonical isomorphism), and σ a Frobenius lift on A. Choose a frame (X, Y, P) with P smooth over O_K near X. Then A ≅ colim_V Γ(V, O_V) over the strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P, and E ↦ M_E := colim_V Γ(V, E_V) is an equivalence between F-Isoc†(X/K) and the category of (σ,∇)-modules over A, compatible with tensor products, duals and pullbacks. For overconvergent isocrystals carrying a Frobenius structure, the convergence (Taylor) condition in the definition is automatic.
hypotheses: X smooth affine over k; A of MW-type with A^int/πA^int ≅ O(X).
The equivalence depends on σ only through the canonical change-of-Frobenius equivalence (RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra, API changeOfFrobenius).
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness of A: van der Put, Theorem 2.4.4 (i), via Elkik's smooth lift and Artin approximation.

Identification of A with overconvergent functions: Berthelot (2.1) (the ring A† ⊗ K is the colimit of Γ(U_λ, O) over the affinoid neighbourhoods U_λ of the tube, which are strict neighbourhoods by (2.5) b)); with frames via RD.3/frame and RD.3/strict-neighbourhood.

Coherent sheaves on the affinoids U_λ correspond to finite Γ(U_λ)-modules (AdicSpacesPartII:R3), so a j†O-module locally free of finite rank gives a finite projective A-module M_E, and the connection gives ∇ on M_E.
The Frobenius structure F: σ^*E ≅ E gives the σ-semilinear F on M_E.

Essential surjectivity: for a (σ,∇)-module M over A, the Taylor isomorphism converges on a strict neighbourhood of the diagonal because of the Frobenius structure (Berthelot, preprint 96-03, Théorème 2.5.7, cited by Kedlaya, Remark 4.2.5); this step is recorded as a gap (source not public).
Full faithfulness: horizontal maps between overconvergent modules on V extend uniquely across the colimit.
acceptance: X = A^1, A† = O⟨t⟩†: L_π corresponds to K⟨t⟩† with ∇(1) = π dt and Frobenius Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t) for σ(t) = t^p.
For X = A^1 the equivalence sends the constant object to (K⟨x⟩†, d, σ) and Berthelot's Dwork F-isocrystal L_π to (K⟨t⟩†, ∇1 = π dt, Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t)) with K = ℚ_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p.

nodes.title: Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals
nodes.statement: For a frame (X, Y, P) (X smooth), restriction along ]X[_P ⊆ V (V a strict neighbourhood) defines a functor j^* : Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) → Isoc(X/K), (E, ε) ↦ (E|_{]X[_P}, ε|_{]X[_{P²}}): the restricted Taylor isomorphism converges on ]X[_{P²}, so the connection on ]X[_P is convergent in Berthelot's sense (4.1). With Frobenius structures it gives j^* : F-Isoc†(X/K) → F-Isoc(X/K), landing in the category of convergent F-isocrystals owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.3 (Berthelot's convergent F-crystals, equivalent by Ogus to F-crystals up to isogeny). j^* is compatible with ⊗, duals, pullbacks and Frobenius, and is independent of the frame up to canonical isomorphism.
hypotheses: The target category (convergent F-isocrystals, realised as O_{]X[_P}-modules with convergent integrable connection and Frobenius, or as isocrystals on the crystalline site) is imported from CrystallineCohomology:CR.3 by request; CR.3's text warns not to equate convergent and overconvergent F-isocrystals, which this functor keeps apart.
For X proper (Y = X) j^* is an equivalence (both categories are convergent isocrystals).
proofSteps: Restriction of a module with overconvergent Taylor isomorphism to the tube ]X[ ⊆ V; the Taylor isomorphism defined on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P²} restricts to ]X[_{P²} (Berthelot 4.1-4.2.1).
Independence of the frame: restriction commutes with the canonical equivalences of RD.3/independence-of-frame (both are pullbacks).
acceptance: j^*(L_π) is the convergent F-isocrystal O_{closed disc} with ∇(1) = π dt; its horizontal sections still do not exist globally (exp(−πt) diverges at |t| = 1).

nodes.title: Pushforward of (overconvergent) F-isocrystals along finite étale morphisms
nodes.statement: For a finite étale morphism f : X' → X of constant degree d of smooth k-schemes (extending to finite flat Y' → Y on compactifications), there are pushforward functors f_* : F-Isoc†(X'/K) → F-Isoc†(X/K) and f_* : F-Isoc(X'/K) → F-Isoc(X/K), compatible with j^*, multiplying ranks by d, right adjoint to f^* up to the trace, with H^0_F(X, f_*E) = H^0_F(X', E) (Frobenius-invariant horizontal sections). On dagger algebras: if A → B is finite étale, a (σ,∇)-module over B is viewed as a module over A. The functor f_* on F-Isoc†(X′/K) is exact and also left adjoint to f^*; the trace gives a splitting O_X → f_*O_{X′} → O_X whose composite is multiplication by the degree, and f_*O_{X′} is self-dual through the trace pairing (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 3.4.2).
hypotheses: X' → X finite étale; the construction on frames uses a finite flat extension of formal models (Kedlaya, Notes Remark 2.8).
proofSteps: Locally: a finite étale A_0 → B_0 lifts to finite étale A† → B†, and the Frobenius lift extends (unique lifting for étale algebras); M ↦ M viewed over A† with the same ∇ (Ω_{B†} = B† ⊗ Ω_{A†}) and Frobenius (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 3.4.2).

H^0 statement: horizontal Frobenius-invariant sections are the same set (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness §7, citing Tsuzuki [T2, Proposition 5.1.2]); compatibility with cohomology is Kedlaya Finiteness Proposition 4.4.2 (RD.4/RD.5).
PROOF SOURCE GAP: the global construction (gluing and independence of choices) is in Tsuzuki, Duke Math. J. 111 (2002), Proposition 5.1.2, not in the public source set (gaps).
acceptance: f = the Artin-Schreier cover y^p − y = t of A^1_{F_p} (Galois with group Z/p): f_*O^† has rank p, and if K contains the p-th roots of unity it splits under the Z/p-action into p rank one eigen-summands, one of them the unit object.
For f: G_m → G_m, x ↦ x^N with p ∤ N, f_*O decomposes as ⊕_{a=0}^{N−1} K_{a/N} (Kummer modules ∇e = (a/N)e dx/x).

There is a pushforward construction in the overconvergent and convergent categories [T2, Propo- sition 5.1.2] such that H 0 (X, E) = H 0 (An , f∗ E).

nodes.title: Extensions of (σ,∇)-modules over Γ_con with separated generic slopes split
nodes.statement: (a) Let M be a σ-module over Γ^K_con[1/p] (K finite over k((t))) with all generic slopes positive. Then v ↦ Fv − v is injective on M ⊗ Γ^K_an,con, and if Fv − v ∈ M then v ∈ M. (b) If 0 → M_1 → M → M_2 → 0 is an exact sequence of (σ,∇)-modules over Γ_con with every generic slope of M_1 greater than every generic slope of M_2, the sequence splits over Γ_con[1/p].
hypotheses: k is reduced to algebraically closed in the proof; the Frobenius σ = σ_0^f, q = p^f (the proof as printed uses p where q is meant, see sourceIssues).
proofSteps: (a) Use de Jong's descending slope filtration (a basis with F triangular, diagonal λ_i of positive valuation, RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent) and RD.1/cohomology-of-rank-one-frobenius-modules (a) coordinate by coordinate (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Lemma 3.2).

(b) The splitting is a solution X of −X + A X^σ D^{-1} = B. Over R_1 = Γ^L_an,con[log u] ⊗ O' it exists by the logarithmic form of local monodromy (RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy) and surjectivity of d/du on R_1 (RD.2/log-robba-ring-antiderivative). The matrices X form a σ-module with positive generic slopes, so by (a) the solution is unique and descends successively to Γ^L_an,con (no log terms), to Γ^L_an,con (no O'), to Γ^L_con[1/p] (by (a)), to Γ^K_con[1/p] (Galois invariance and uniqueness), and finally to Γ_con[1/p] (an eigenvector argument on a Frobenius-integral basis) (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Proposition 3.3).
acceptance: For M_1 = Γ_con(1) (slope 1) and M_2 = Γ_con (slope 0) with trivial connections, every extension of (σ,∇)-modules splits over Γ_con[1/p].

whose generic slopes are all positive.

nodes.title: de Jong's injectivity: Γ^alg_con ⊗_{Γ_con} Γ → Γ^alg is injective
nodes.statement: For k algebraically closed (more generally for K admitting a valuation p-basis, SFR Proposition 2.2.21), the multiplication map Γ^alg_con ⊗_{Γ_con} Γ → Γ^alg is injective; moreover if x_1..x_n ∈ Γ are Γ_con-linearly independent and Σ x_i y_i ∈ Γ with y_i ∈ Γ^alg_con, then y_i ∈ Γ_con.
hypotheses: Γ = Γ^{k((t))} (p-adic completion of R^int), Γ_con = R^int; Γ^alg, Γ^alg_con as in RD.0/extended-robba-ring.
proofSteps: Embed into the maximal immediate extension (Hahn-Kaplansky generalised power series) and expand every element uniquely as Σ_{α∈[0,1)} x_α w^α with x_α ∈ Γ and w the Teichmüller lift of t; overconvergent elements have overconvergent coefficients x_α; conclude by the uniqueness of the expansion and the minimal-counterexample argument (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Proposition 4.1, after de Jong Proposition 8.1). Alternatively: Galois invariance plus a Γ-linear section f : Γ^perf → Γ preserving overconvergence (SFR Lemma 2.2.19, Proposition 2.2.21).
acceptance: For x = 1 the statement says Γ ∩ Γ^alg_con = Γ_con inside Γ^alg (compare arXiv:math/0110124 Corollary 3.8).

nodes.title: Maps to Γ with Frobenius eigenvalue p^m detect a rank one slope-ℓ submodule
nodes.statement: Let M be a nonzero σ-module over Γ_con (K = k((t)), k algebraically closed) and φ : M → Γ an injective Γ_con-linear map with φ(Fv) = p^m φ(v)^σ for all v and some integer m ≥ 0. Then the largest generic slope of M is m, with multiplicity 1, and φ^{-1}(Γ_con) is a σ-submodule of M of rank 1 and slope m.
hypotheses: Slopes here are p-adic valuations of eigenvalues, as in the source (an eigenvector with F v = λ v has slope v_p(λ)); σ = σ_0^f is a q-power Frobenius lift, q = p^f, and the Tate twist by ℓ multiplies F by q^ℓ, so the lemma is applied with m = fℓ (see RD.3/local-full-faithfulness).
proofSteps: φ extends injectively to M ⊗ Γ^alg_con by RD.3/de-jong-tensor-injectivity; eigenvectors of maximal slope s from the descending generic filtration (RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent) satisfy λφ(v) = p^m φ(v)^σ, forcing s = v_p(λ) = m, and then φ(v) lies in the σ-fixed constants, forcing multiplicity 1; nonemptiness of φ^{-1}(Γ_con) via the generalised power series expansion (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Lemma 4.2, after de Jong Corollary 8.2).
acceptance: M = Γ_con with F(1) = p^m (a rank one σ-module of slope m, for σ fixing p) and φ the inclusion into Γ: φ^{-1}(Γ_con) = M.

sources.excerpt: Then the largest generic slope of M is equal to ℓ, occurring with multiplicity 1. Moreover, φ−1 (Γcon ) is a σ-submodule of M of dimension 1 with slope ℓ.

nodes.title: Local full faithfulness: morphisms of (σ,∇)-modules over Γ_con are determined over Γ
nodes.statement: Let M_1, M_2 be (σ,∇)-modules over Γ_con = R^int (K = k((t))) and f : M_1 ⊗ Γ → M_2 ⊗ Γ a morphism of (σ,∇)-modules over Γ. Then f is induced by a (unique) morphism g : M_1 → M_2 over Γ_con. Equivalently, F-Isoc†(k((t))) → F-Isoc(k((t))) is fully faithful (Tsuzuki's Conjecture 2.3.2 in [T2]).
hypotheses: The local model of the global theorem (Kedlaya, Notes Remark 5.5).
proofSteps: Reduce to a Γ_con-linear φ : M = M_1^∨(ℓ) ⊗ M_2 → Γ (ℓ large, so that the twist is defined over Γ_con) with φ(Fv) = q^ℓ φ(v)^σ = p^{fℓ} φ(v)^σ and φ(∇v) = u d/du φ(v), and k algebraically closed; show φ(M) ⊆ Γ_con (the printed proof writes p^ℓ φ(v) for q^ℓ φ(v)^σ, see sourceIssues).

Replace M by M/ker φ; by RD.3/de-jong-rank-one-image with m = fℓ, P = ψ^{-1}(Γ_con) is of rank one and of slope fℓ, strictly greater than all other generic slopes; P is ∇-stable because du^σ/du is divisible by π (u^σ ≡ u^q mod π), which makes the two sides of the Frobenius equation for ψ(∇v) have different valuations unless ∇v = 0.

0 → P → M/N → (M/N)/P → 0 splits by RD.3/splitting-of-slope-separated-extensions; the complement Q must vanish by RD.3/de-jong-rank-one-image again; hence φ(M) = ψ(P) ⊆ Γ_con (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Theorem 5.1).
acceptance: For M_1 = M_2 = Γ_con with the trivial (σ,∇)-structure, a morphism over Γ is multiplication by an element c of Γ with c^σ = c and dc = 0, and such c already lie in the constants of Γ_con (the fixed field of σ on the coefficient ring), so the statement holds trivially in rank one with trivial structure.

sources.excerpt: Let M1 and M2 be (σ, ∇)-modules over Γcon , and let f : M1 ⊗Γcon Γ → M2 ⊗Γcon Γ be a morphism of (σ, ∇)-modules over Γ. Then there exists a morphism g : M1 → M2 that induces f .

nodes.title: Open dense affines finite étale over affine space in positive characteristic
nodes.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0 and X a separated, geometrically reduced k-scheme of finite type and pure dimension n, and x a smooth (geometric) point of X. Then X contains an open dense affine subscheme U containing x with a finite étale morphism U → A^n_k. (Kedlaya's Proposition 9.1.2 says 'of dimension n'; purity is needed, see sourceIssues.)
hypotheses: Pure dimension n (a finite étale map to A^n has all components of dimension n and U must meet every component).
Geometrically reduced (each component generically smooth).
proofSteps: Kedlaya, More étale covers, Theorem 1: a geometrically reduced projective X of pure dimension n admits a finite morphism to P^n induced by sections of a power of an ample line bundle, étale away from the hyperplane H at infinity, sending a chosen divisor D into H and chosen smooth points outside H; the proof is a Noether normalisation by sections vanishing on D (Lemmas 3–6, with care for finite k), with unramifiedness at the chosen points.
Theorem 2 there deduces the statement for separated finite-type X: compactify, apply Theorem 1 with D containing the boundary and the non-smooth locus, and restrict to the preimage of A^n = P^n \ H.
acceptance: For X = A^n itself, U = A^n with the identity.
X = A^1: U = A^1 with the identity. X = G_m: x ↦ x + x^{-1}… is not étale in characteristic 2; an Artin–Schreier-type map exists by the theorem (the case n = 1 is attributed to Abhyankar).

nodes.title: Kedlaya's full faithfulness theorem: overconvergent F-isocrystals embed fully faithfully into convergent ones
nodes.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p, K as in the setting, X a SMOOTH separated k-scheme of finite type and a ≥ 1. Then the restriction functor j^* : F^a-Isoc†(X/K) → F^a-Isoc(X/K) (RD.3/restriction-to-convergent) is fully faithful. More generally (de Jong, Kedlaya, Shiho; Kedlaya Notes Theorem 5.3), for X ⊆ Y and U ⊆ X open dense, U ⊆ W ⊆ Y open, F-Isoc(X, Y) → F-Isoc(U, W) is fully faithful. Proven range: WITH Frobenius structures; for isocrystals without Frobenius the analogue for F-Isoc† → F-Isoc fails (Kedlaya Notes Remark 5.6, citing Abe), and the full faithfulness is not an essential surjectivity (the image is a proper subcategory).
hypotheses: Unit-root case earlier: Tsuzuki (X with smooth compactification) and Étesse (general X).
The theorem uses the p-adic local monodromy theorem in logarithmic form (RD.2) through RD.3/splitting-of-slope-separated-extensions.
proofSteps: Reduce to H^0: Hom(E_1, E_2) = H^0_F(X, E_1^∨ ⊗ E_2) (Frobenius-fixed horizontal sections) in both categories, so it suffices that H^0_F has the same rank (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness §7).

The question is local on X; by RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space cover X by opens U finite étale over A^n, and by RD.3/finite-etale-pushforward-of-isocrystals (H^0_F(X, E) = H^0_F(A^n, f_*E)) reduce to X = A^n.

On A^n (with a = f, q = p^a), E is a (σ,∇)-module M over R = O⟨x_1..x_n⟩†[1/p]; a twist M(ℓ) is defined over R and free by RD.3/rigid-quillen-suslin; a Frobenius-invariant horizontal v over the p-adic completion R^∧ lies in M(ℓ) ⊗ R_i for each i by RD.3/local-full-faithfulness applied in the variable x_i (R_i = S_i⟨x_i⟩†), and ∩_i R_i = R gives v ∈ M(ℓ) (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness §7).
acceptance: Unit-root case: F-Isoc† unit-root objects ↔ potentially unramified p-adic local systems ⊂ all p-adic local systems ↔ unit-root convergent objects (Katz-Crew, Tsuzuki; Notes Theorems 3.7, 3.9): the embedding is fully faithful but not essentially surjective.

On the ordinary locus U of X(N), the unit-root line subobject of E|_U exists convergently but not overconvergently (Notes Example 4.6, Remark 5.12): full faithfulness does not give extension of subobjects.

nodes.title: Acceptance: the frames A^n ⊂ P^n and A^n ⊂ (P^1)^n give equivalent categories
nodes.statement: Let X = A^n_k with the two compactifications Y_1 = P^n_k and Y_2 = (P^1_k)^n and frames (X, Y_1, P̂^n_O), (X, Y_2, (P̂^1_O)^n). (a) In both frames the tube ]X[ is the closed unit polydisc {|t_i| ≤ 1}, and the polydiscs V_λ = {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1} for all i} (λ < 1, λ → 1) form a cofinal family of strict neighbourhoods, so Γ(]Y_i[, j†O) = K⟨t_1, ..., t_n⟩† in both cases. (b) The equivalence Isoc†(A^n ⊂ P^n/K) ≃ Isoc†(A^n ⊂ (P^1)^n/K) of RD.3/independence-of-compactification is realised through the closure Y_3 of the diagonal of A^n in P^n × (P^1)^n, whose projections to Y_1 and Y_2 are proper and are isomorphisms over A^n, with the frame (X, Y_3, P̂^n × (P̂^1)^n) mapping to both frames; on the pullback of the Dwork isocrystal along the first coordinate it sends (K⟨t_1..t_n⟩†, ∇(1) = π dt_1) to itself.
hypotheses: n ≥ 1; for n = 1 the two compactifications coincide and the statement is the identity.
proofSteps: (a) In P^n with homogeneous coordinates x_0..x_n and Z = {x_0 = 0}: ]Z[_λ = {|x_0| < λ max_i |x_i|}, whose complement is {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1}}, t_i = x_i/x_0 (Berthelot 2.1: 'un exercice facile sur les coordonnées projectives'). In (P^1)^n, Z = ∪_i {t_i = ∞} is cut out near a boundary point by the product of the coordinates s_i = 1/t_i with |t_i| ≥ 1, so the complement W_λ of ]Z[_λ is {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1} for all i, and |Π_{i∈I} t_i| ≤ λ^{-1} for the set I of indices with |t_i| ≥ 1}; hence W_λ ⊆ V_λ ⊆ W_{λ^n}, and the two families are cofinal. Global sections: RD.3/overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame.

(b) The graph closure Y_3 ⊆ Y_1 × Y_2 contains X as an open subscheme with v_i^{-1}(X) = X for both projections v_i (both are isomorphisms over A^n), so RD.3/independence-of-compactification applies to v_1 and v_2; the diagonal frame is smooth over O (RD.3/independence-of-frame (b)).

Computation: under both identifications the pullback of the Dwork isocrystal along the first coordinate t_1 is the free rank one K⟨t_1..t_n⟩†-module with ∇(1) = π dt_1, and its Taylor isomorphism exp π(t'_1 − t_1) is analytic on the strict neighbourhood {|t_1 − t'_1| < 1} of the diagonal tube in either frame (Berthelot 4.2.3 b for n = 1).
acceptance: Test: strict neighbourhoods agree: for λ < 1 the complement of ]Z_1[_λ in (P^n)^an is exactly the polydisc V_λ = {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1}}, and the complement W_λ of ]Z_2[_λ in ((P^1)^n)^an satisfies W_λ ⊆ V_λ ⊆ W_{λ^n} (for n = 2 and |t_1|, |t_2| ≥ 1, W_λ is {|t_1 t_2| ≤ λ^{-1}}, strictly smaller than V_λ).
Test: global sections of j†O in both frames equal K⟨t_1..t_n⟩† (the union over λ of the Tate algebras of the polydiscs of radius λ^{-1}).

nodes.title: Acceptance: on punctured curves the boundary behaviour separates overconvergent from convergent
nodes.statement: (a) On X = A^1_{F_p} = P^1 − {∞} over K = Q_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p, the Dwork isocrystal L_π (∇(1) = π dt) is overconvergent: its Taylor isomorphism exp π(t' − t) is analytic on |t − t'| < 1, a strict neighbourhood of the diagonal tube, and its Frobenius exp π(t^p − t) converges on |t| < p^{(p−1)/p²}; it has H^*_rig(X/K, L_π) = H^*_c(X/K, L_π) = 0, and its local monodromy at ∞ is trivialised by an Artin-Schreier extension (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example). (b) Convergence alone is insufficient: the naive (convergent) de Rham cohomology of A^n is that of the closed polydisc and is infinite-dimensional over K; the convergent F-isocrystal E on A^1 given by ∇e_1 = 0, ∇e_2 = (Σ_{k≥0} p^k t^{p^k − 1} dt) e_1, F(σ^*e_1) = e_1, F(σ^*e_2) = e_2 − t e_1 (σ(t) = t^p) is an extension of the constant object by itself which is not overconvergent; and on the ordinary locus U = X(N) − Z of the modular curve (a curve punctured at the supersingular points) the unit-root subobject of the crystalline H^1 of the universal elliptic curve exists as a convergent but not as an overconvergent F-isocrystal.
hypotheses: p odd in the Dwork computations; K = Q_p(π) with σ_K = id and q = p.
The extension E of (b) is the explicit form of Kedlaya's Notes Remark 5.13, whose printed 'X = A^1_K' should read A^1_k (sourceIssues).
proofSteps: (a) Overconvergence of L_π: Berthelot 4.2.3 b)-c); the Frobenius series: PARI/GP check that v_p of the n-th coefficient of exp π(t − t^p) is at least n(p−1)/p² for n ≤ 200 and p = 3, 5, 7 (checks/dwork.out), in agreement with Dwork's estimate. Vanishing of rigid cohomology: Berthelot's exercise at the end of 4.2.4 (to be carried out in RD.4).

(b1) Naive cohomology: H^1_dR of the closed disc K⟨t⟩ is infinite-dimensional because an antiderivative of Σ a_n t^n dt lies in K⟨t⟩ only if a_n/(n+1) → 0 (Berthelot 1.5, Remarque after Proposition 2); the form ω below is Part A's example RD.0/completion-versus-overconvergence (b).

(b2) E is a convergent F-isocrystal: ω = Σ p^k t^{p^k−1} dt lies in K⟨t⟩dt, its antiderivative G = Σ t^{p^k} converges on every open disc of radius 1 (convergence of the connection), and σ^*ω − ω = d(G(t^p) − G(t)) = −dt, which is the compatibility of ∇ with F(σ^*e_2) = e_2 − t e_1 (PARI/GP check of σ^*ω − ω = −dt through degree p^6, checks/algebra.out). E is not overconvergent: if E ≅ j^*E', then by RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent the sequence comes from an extension of O^† by O^† in F-Isoc†(A^1), so ω − dg ∈ K⟨t⟩†dt for some g ∈ K⟨t⟩; since K⟨t⟩† is stable under antiderivatives, G − g ∈ K⟨t⟩†, hence G ∈ K⟨t⟩, contradicting that the coefficients of G do not tend to 0.
(b3) The unit-root subobject on the ordinary locus: Kedlaya Notes Example 4.6 and Remark 5.12 (a supersingular elliptic curve has no distinguished line in its rigid cohomology).
acceptance: Test: exp π(t − t^p) has coefficient valuations ≥ n(p−1)/p² (numerically checked), while exp(πt) has coefficient valuations exactly s_p(n)/(p−1) (radius exactly 1, checked for n ≤ 200, p = 3, 5): the Frobenius structure is overconvergent although the horizontal section is not.
Test: σ^*ω − ω = −dt for ω = Σ p^k t^{p^k−1} dt (checked for p = 3, 5 through degree p^6 up to the truncated top term).

nodes.title: Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology of a (σ,∇)-module
nodes.statement: For a (σ,∇)-module M over a dagger algebra A of MW-type, the Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology H^i(M) is the i-th cohomology of the de Rham complex 0 → M → M ⊗ Ω^1_{A/K} → M ⊗ Ω^2_{A/K} → ⋯ with differentials ∇_i. The Frobenius F ⊗ ∧^i dσ on M ⊗ Ω^i commutes with the differentials and induces a σ_K-semilinear endomorphism F of each H^i(M) (K-linear when σ_K = id). H^0(M) = ker ∇ is the space of horizontal sections. When the special fibre of A has dimension one, Ω^2_{A/K} = 0 and H^0(M) = ker ∇, H^1(M) = coker(∇: M → M ⊗ Ω^1), H^i(M) = 0 for i ≥ 2. For M = A this is the cohomology H^i(A; K) of Monsky–Washnitzer and van der Put.
hypotheses: The output is a K-vector space with a semilinear endomorphism; no finite-dimensionality is built into the definition (it is RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves-constant-coefficients, RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves and RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology).
proofSteps: The de Rham complex is a cochain complex of K-vector spaces because ∇_{i+1} ∘ ∇_i = 0 (integrability); its cohomology is Mathlib's HomologicalComplex.homology of this complex.
The Frobenius of M and ∧^i dσ give a morphism of complexes σ^*(M ⊗ Ω^•) → M ⊗ Ω^• by horizontality of F, hence the semilinear F on H^i(M).
In dimension one the complex has two terms, so H^0 and H^1 are the kernel and cokernel of ∇.
acceptance: For A = K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† and M = A, H^1(M) is one-dimensional, spanned by dx/x, and the standard Frobenius x ↦ x^q acts by q.
For A = K⟨x⟩† and M = A, H^0(M) = K and H^1(M) = 0.

nodes.title: The trace map on de Rham complexes for a finite flat morphism of dagger algebras
nodes.statement: Let f: R → S be an injective morphism of dagger algebras of MW-type with S finite and locally free of constant degree n over R. There is an R-linear morphism of complexes Tr: Ω^•_{S/K} → Ω^•_{R/K} with Tr ∘ f = n·id and Tr(ω ∧ η) = ω ∧ Tr(η) for ω ∈ Ω^•_{R/K}, η ∈ Ω^•_{S/K}; in degree 0 it is the algebra trace S → R.
hypotheses: R and S are dagger algebras of MW-type (Monsky–Washnitzer's proof uses that dagger algebras are noetherian; Kedlaya, Remark 3.2.7).
S is finite and locally free over R of constant rank n.
proofSteps: Over the fraction fields, Ω^1_{S/K} ⊗ Frac(S) = Ω^1_{R/K} ⊗ Frac(S) because Frac(S)/Frac(R) is finite separable (characteristic 0); define Tr on Ω^i ⊗ Frac(S) as the field trace Frac(S) → Frac(R) tensored with Ω^i_{R/K} (van der Put, Proposition 3.1).

Show Tr maps Ω^i_{S/K} into Ω^i_{R/K}: since Ω^i_{R/K} is projective and R normal, it suffices to check at height-one primes, where it follows from the discriminant description of differentials (van der Put, proof of Proposition 3.1, citing R. Berger).
Tr commutes with d because the field trace commutes with the derivation of the separable extension; Tr ∘ f = n and the projection formula hold by construction.
acceptance: For S = K⟨x⟩† over R = K⟨y⟩† with y = x^q: Tr(dx/x) = dy/y and Tr(1) = q.

nodes.title: Cohomology injects under finite flat pullback, and Frobenius is injective on cohomology
nodes.statement: Let f: R → S be an injective morphism of dagger algebras of MW-type with S finite projective over R, and σ a Frobenius lift on S preserving R. For every (σ,∇)-module M over R, the map H^i(M) → H^i(f^*M) is injective and its image is the image of the canonical projector (1/n)·f ∘ Tr on H^i(f^*M), n = deg(S/R). In particular (taking f = σ, which is finite flat because Frobenius on a smooth k-algebra is) the Frobenius F is injective on each H^i(M).
hypotheses: R, S of MW-type (or one of the two Robba-ring situations of Kedlaya, Remark 3.2.7).
Characteristic 0, so n is invertible in K.
proofSteps: Tensor the trace Tr: Ω^•_S → Ω^•_R (RD.4/de-rham-trace) with M to get H^i(f^*M) → H^i(M) whose composite with H^i(M) → H^i(f^*M) is multiplication by n.
Since n ≠ 0 in K, the first map is injective and (1/n) f ∘ Tr is a projector onto its image.
For f = σ: σ is finite flat (Kedlaya, Remark 3.2.4) and the Frobenius structure identifies σ^*M with M, so F on H^i(M) is the composite of the injection H^i(M) → H^i(σ^*M) with an isomorphism.
acceptance: For S = K⟨x⟩† over R = K⟨x^q⟩†, H^1(R) = 0 = H^1(S), and on K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† the Frobenius q on H^1 is injective.

nodes.title: Finite étale pushforward preserves Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology
nodes.statement: Let f: R → S be a finite étale morphism of dagger algebras and M a (σ,∇)-module over S. Then H^i(M) ≅ H^i(f_*M) canonically for all i, where f_*M is M viewed as an R-module.
hypotheses: f is finite étale.
proofSteps: Because f is étale, S ⊗_R Ω^i_{R/K} ≅ Ω^i_{S/K}; tensoring with M gives an equality of de Rham complexes M ⊗_S Ω^•_{S/K} = M ⊗_R Ω^•_{R/K}.
The Frobenius structures agree, so the identification is F-equivariant.
acceptance: Pushing the trivial module forward along x ↦ x^N on K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† (N prime to p, étale on G_m) gives a rank-N module with H^1 one-dimensional.

nodes.title: Berthelot's functor j† and the overconvergent de Rham complex of a frame
nodes.statement: Let (X, Y, P) be a frame (RD.3/frame): X ⊂ Y open, Y ⊂ P closed, P a formal O_K-scheme smooth near X; let Z = Y \ X. For a strict neighbourhood V of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P with inclusion j_V: V → ]Y[_P and a sheaf F of abelian groups on ]Y[_P, put j†F := colim_V j_{V*} j_V^{-1} F over all strict neighbourhoods (the sheaf of germs of sections of F near ]X[). For E ∈ Isoc†(X, Y/K) realised as a locally free O_V-module E_V with integrable connection on some V, the overconvergent de Rham complex is DR†(E) := j†(E_V ⊗ Ω^•_V), a complex of sheaves of K-vector spaces on ]Y[_P with differentials induced by ∇; its hypercohomology H^i((X,Y,P)/K, E) := H^i(]Y[_P, DR†(E)) is the frame cohomology. For a morphism of frames u: (X', Y', P') → (X, Y, P) (with u(X') ⊂ X) there is a canonical morphism DR†_P(E) → Ru_*DR†_{P'}(u^*E) in the derived category of sheaves on ]Y[_P (Berthelot (2.2.1)).
hypotheses: Strict neighbourhoods in Berthelot's sense (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood); the colimit may be taken over any cofinal system, for instance the U'_λ = {x ∈ ]Y[ : some |f_i(x)| ≥ λ}, f_i lifting equations of Z, λ → 1^-.
The frame need not have Y proper for DR†(E) and frame cohomology; properness of Y is imposed in RD.4/rigid-cohomology.
proofSteps: Define j†F as the colimit of j_{V*}j_V^{-1}F; since the strict neighbourhoods form a filtered system, j† is an exact functor on sheaves of abelian groups (Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Proposition 2.7.2).
j†F depends only on the restriction of F to any strict neighbourhood V, and H^*(]Y[, j†F) = H^*(V, j†F) (Berthelot (2.5) a)).
For E realised on V with connection ∇ (RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal), E_V ⊗ Ω^•_V is a complex of sheaves on V (differential forms on the rigid space V, supplied by AdicSpacesPartII:F1); apply j†.
For a morphism of frames u, the canonical maps j†F → u_*j'†u^{-1}F composed with u^{-1}Ω^•_{]Y[_P} → Ω^•_{]Y'[_{P'}} and an injective resolution give (2.2.1).
acceptance: If X = Y (Z empty) then j† = id and DR†(E) = E ⊗ Ω^•_{]X[_P}.
For X = A^1_k ⊂ Y = P^1_k ⊂ P = P̂^1: Γ(]Y[, j†O) = K⟨x⟩†, series converging on some disc |x| ≤ ρ with ρ > 1.

nodes.title: Independence of rigid cohomology from the smooth formal embedding (Berthelot, Théorème 1)
nodes.statement: Let X ⊂ Y be an open immersion of k-schemes, i: Y → P and i': Y → P' closed immersions into formal O_K-schemes, and u: P' → P a morphism with u ∘ i' = i which is smooth in a neighbourhood of X. Then for every E ∈ Isoc†(X, Y/K) the canonical morphism DR†_P(E) → Ru_*DR†_{P'}(E) of (2.2.1) is an isomorphism; hence H^i((X,Y,P)/K, E) ≅ H^i((X,Y,P')/K, E). Given two embeddings Y → P_1, Y → P_2 smooth near X, applying this to the projections of P_1 × P_2 (diagonal embedding) gives a canonical isomorphism, and these isomorphisms are compatible.
hypotheses: u smooth in a neighbourhood of X; no hypothesis on u at the points of Z = Y \ X (Berthelot's remark after Théorème 1).
proofSteps: Weak fibration (Berthelot, Lemme 1): if u is smooth near X, then u^{an} makes ]X[_{P'} locally (over an affine cover of P) isomorphic to ]X[_P × D(0,1^-)^d, a fibration in open unit polydiscs; this is the geometric input of RD.3/independence-of-frame.

Relative Poincaré lemma (Berthelot, Proposition 1): on an open polydisc fibration, Ω^•_{]X[_P} → Ru'_*Ω^•_{]X[_{P'}} is a quasi-isomorphism and R^q u'_* of the relative forms vanish for q ≥ 1, using global primitives on open discs and Theorem B (AdicSpacesPartII:R3).

Strong fibration theorem: the polydisc fibration extends over a cofinal system of strict neighbourhoods of ]X[, giving the statement for DR† (Berthelot's 'étude à la frontière'). The public sources state this step without proof; it is recorded as a gap.
Compatibility of the isomorphisms for three embeddings follows from functoriality of (2.2.1) in the triple product.
acceptance: For X = A^1 embedded in P̂^1 and in P̂^2 (via the diagonal of P^1 × P^1 composed with a linear embedding), both frame cohomologies are K in degree 0 and 0 otherwise.

Cela explique l'absence d'hypothèse sur u aux points de Z dans l'énoncé du théorème 1, dont la démonstration nécessite une étude "à la frontière" de ]X[ complétant la proposition 1.

nodes.title: Independence of rigid cohomology from the compactification (Berthelot, Théorème 2)
nodes.statement: Let j: X → Y and j': X → Y' be open immersions and v: Y' → Y a proper morphism with v ∘ j' = j. Then v^*: H^i((X ⊂ Y)/K, E) → H^i((X ⊂ Y')/K, v^*E) is an isomorphism for all i and all E ∈ Isoc†(X, Y/K) (frame cohomology computed with any embeddings smooth near X, by RD.4/independence-of-embedding).
hypotheses: v proper; frames exist for Y and Y' (for instance Y, Y' projective), or use the hypercovering construction of Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Section 10.
proofSteps: Berthelot's sketch: compute v^* with embeddings Y → P, Y' → P' and a morphism u: P' → P; by dévissage and base changes of P inducing admissible covers of a strict neighbourhood, reduce to the case of a section P → P' extending the section X → P' ×_P X given by j'; then replace Y' by the image of Y in P' and apply Théorème 1.

Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki give the statement for their definition (Corollary 10.5.4: if the compactification is proper over the base, cohomology is independent of it) and prove agreement with Berthelot's definition (Theorem 10.6.1). Their proofs (Sections 6, 8, 10) were read only at the level of statements; recorded as coverage remaining.
acceptance: For X = A^1, the compactifications P^1 and P^1 blown up at a point of the boundary give the same cohomology.

sources.excerpt: Soient j : X ↪ Y, j' : X ↪ Y' deux immersions ouvertes, et v : Y' → Y un morphisme tel que j = v∘j'. Si v est propre, l'homomorphisme canonique v* : H*rig(X ⊂ Y/K) → H*rig(X ⊂ Y'/K) est un isomorphisme.

nodes.title: Rigid cohomology H^i_rig(X/K, E)
nodes.statement: Let X be a separated k-scheme of finite type and E an overconvergent (F-)isocrystal on X/K. Choose a compactification X ⊂ Y (Y proper over k; Nagata) and a closed immersion Y → P into a formal O_K-scheme P smooth in a neighbourhood of X (such a frame exists when X is quasi-projective: take Y the closure of X in P^n_k and P = P̂^n_{O_K}). The rigid cohomology complex is RΓ_rig(X/K, E) := RΓ(]Y[_P, DR†(E)) in the derived category of K-vector spaces and H^i_rig(X/K, E) := H^i(]Y[_P, j†(E ⊗ Ω^•)). By RD.4/independence-of-embedding and RD.4/independence-of-compactification this is independent of (Y, P) up to canonical, compatible isomorphisms. For X admitting no global frame the definition is made with universally de Rham descendable hypercoverings (Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Section 10), which agrees with the frame definition whenever a frame exists (their Theorem 10.6.1). Each H^i_rig(X/K, E) is a K-vector space; finite dimensionality is a theorem (RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology), not part of the output type.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over k; K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with residue field k.
No finite-dimensional output type: the construction produces K-vector spaces and complexes.
proofSteps: Choose a frame with Y proper: Nagata compactification (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2) and, for quasi-projective X, the projective embedding; form DR†(E) (RD.4/overconvergent-de-rham-complex) and take hypercohomology (Mathlib's derived category of sheaves of K-vector spaces on the G-topology of ]Y[_P).

Independence: the category of frames for X with Y proper is connected by products and proper maps; RD.4/independence-of-embedding and RD.4/independence-of-compactification give canonical isomorphisms, and their compatibility for three frames makes the resulting object well defined up to unique isomorphism.

General X: Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki construct universally de Rham descendable hypercoverings (Proposition 10.1.4), define rigid cohomology as the derived Čech complex (10.4) independent of choices, and prove agreement with Berthelot's definition (Theorem 10.6.1).
acceptance: H^0_rig(Spec k/K, E) is the underlying K-space of the fibre E, and H^i_rig(Spec k/K, E) = 0 for i > 0.
H^i_rig(A^n_k/K) = K for i = 0 and 0 otherwise (RD.4/cohomology-of-affine-space).

sources.excerpt: This construction is independent of the choice of compactification; see [Be2, 2.3].
D'après un théorème de Nagata, tout k-schéma séparé de type fini X est isomorphe à un ouvert d'un k-schéma propre X̄ (on dit que X̄ est une compactification de X).
Les théorèmes 1 et 2 s'étendent à celui-ci, et permettent de définir la cohomologie rigide de X à coefficients dans E
Hence, our rigid cohomology coincides with Berthelot's original definition of rigid cohomology in [3, Section 2].
sources.match: The hypercovering definition for general X agrees with Berthelot's.

nodes.title: Functoriality of rigid cohomology in the variety and the coefficient
nodes.statement: For a morphism f: X' → X of separated k-schemes of finite type and E ∈ Isoc†(X/K) there are K-linear maps f^*: H^i_rig(X/K, E) → H^i_rig(X'/K, f^*E) with (id)^* = id and (g ∘ f)^* = f^* ∘ g^* (under f^*g^*E ≅ (gf)^*E), and a morphism h: E_1 → E_2 of overconvergent isocrystals induces h_*: H^i_rig(X/K, E_1) → H^i_rig(X/K, E_2), functorially and compatibly with f^*. Constructed on frames: choose frames (X, Y, P), (X', Y', P') and replace P' by P' × P with Y' the closure of the graph (diagonal embedding method); the morphism of frames gives (2.2.1), and independence makes the result canonical.
hypotheses: X, X' separated of finite type over k.
proofSteps: Diagonal embedding: given frames for X and X', the frame (X', Ȳ', P' × P) with Ȳ' the closure of the graph of f dominates both, the projection to P' being smooth near X' (RD.4/independence-of-embedding).
The morphism of frames to (X, Y, P) induces f^* via (2.2.1) and hypercohomology.
Independence of choices and composition follow from RD.4/independence-of-embedding and RD.4/independence-of-compactification applied to products of frames.
For morphisms of coefficients, apply j† to the morphism of de Rham complexes.
acceptance: For the structure map A^1 → Spec k, f^*: K = H^0_rig(Spec k) → H^0_rig(A^1) = K is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Rigid cohomology with compact supports H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)
nodes.statement: Let X be separated of finite type over k with a frame (X, Y, P), Y proper over k, P smooth near X; let Z = Y \ X, let V be a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P on which E is realised with its connection, and ι: ]Z[_P ∩ V → V the inclusion (]Z[_P is admissible open in ]Y[_P). For a sheaf F of abelian groups on V put Γ_{]X[}(F) := ker(F → ι_*ι^*F); this is left exact, and for F coherent Theorem B gives R^qι_*ι^*F = 0 for q ≥ 1, so RΓ_{]X[}(F) is represented by the two-term complex [F → ι_*ι^*F] (degrees 0, 1). The compactly supported rigid cohomology is H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) := H^i(V, RΓ_{]X[}(E_V ⊗ Ω^•_V)), with complex RΓ_{c,rig}(X/K, E). It is independent of V, of P (RD.4/compact-support-independence-of-embedding) and of Y (RD.4/compact-support-independence-of-compactification).
hypotheses: Y proper over k is essential (for Y not proper this computes cohomology with supports in X relative to Y).
ι^* and ι_* on the admissible open ]Z[ ∩ V; the two-term description uses coherence of E_V ⊗ Ω^i_V and quasi-Stein acyclicity (Kiehl's Theorem B, requested from AdicSpacesPartII:R3).
proofSteps: Γ_{]X[} is the kernel of a morphism of left exact functors, hence left exact; its right derived functors exist on sheaves of abelian groups on V (Mathlib's derived category).
For F coherent, the exact sequence 0 → Γ_{]X[}F → F → ι_*ι^*F and the vanishing R^qι_*ι^*F = 0 (q ≥ 1) identify RΓ_{]X[}F with [F → ι_*ι^*F].
Apply to the complex E_V ⊗ Ω^•_V termwise and take hypercohomology on V; independence of V because RΓ_{]X[} of the complex depends only on a strict neighbourhood (Berthelot (3.4) b)).
acceptance: H^i_{c,rig}(A^1_k/K) = 0, 0, K(−1) for i = 0, 1, 2 (Berthelot (3.4), Exemple).
For X proper, Z = ∅ and H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) = H^i_rig(X/K, E).

nodes.title: Compact-support cohomology is independent of the formal embedding (Berthelot, Théorème 3)
nodes.statement: Let i: Y → P and i': Y → P' be closed immersions into formal O_K-schemes, u: P' → P with u ∘ i' = i, and X ⊂ Y open. If u is smooth in a neighbourhood of X, the canonical morphism RΓ_{]X[}(Ω^•_{]Y[_P}) → Ru_*RΓ_{]X[}(Ω^•_{]Y[_{P'}}) (Berthelot (3.2.1)), and its version with coefficients E, is an isomorphism; hence H^i_c((X ⊂ Y)/K, E) does not depend on P. Also H^i_c does not depend on the strict neighbourhood V used.
hypotheses: u smooth near X.
proofSteps: If u is smooth in a neighbourhood of Y, combine the relative Poincaré lemma (Berthelot, Proposition 1, as in RD.4/independence-of-embedding) with the two-term description of RΓ_{]X[} on coherent sheaves.

In general, RΓ_{]X[}(Ω^•) and its cohomology depend only on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[ in ]Y[; reduce to the previous case using the structure of a small strict neighbourhood as in (2.3). The boundary part of this reduction is the same strong fibration input recorded as a gap for RD.4/independence-of-embedding.
acceptance: For A^1 embedded in P̂^1 and in P̂^1 × P̂^1 (diagonal), both computations give K(−1) in degree 2 only.

Si on suppose u lisse au voisinage de Y, le théorème 3 est une conséquence immédiate de la proposition 1, compte tenu de la description donnée plus haut de ℝΓ]X[(E) pour E cohérent.

nodes.title: Compact-support cohomology is independent of the compactification (Berthelot, Théorème 4)
nodes.statement: Let j: X → Y and j': X → Y' be open immersions and v: Y' → Y a morphism with v ∘ j' = j and v(Z') ⊂ Z (Z = Y \ X, Z' = Y' \ X). If v is proper, the canonical map H^i_c((X ⊂ Y)/K, E) → H^i_c((X ⊂ Y')/K, E) is an isomorphism. Consequently H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) := H^i_c((X ⊂ X̄)/K, E) for a compactification X̄ is independent of X̄ up to canonical isomorphism.
hypotheses: v proper with v(Z') ⊂ Z (automatic when v is proper and X dense in Y').
proofSteps: Berthelot states the theorem without proof (proofs announced for his preprint on rigid cohomology with compact supports, which is not public); the argument parallels Théorème 2: dévissage over P, reduction to the case of a section, then Théorème 3. Recorded as a gap.
acceptance: For G_m ⊂ P^1 and G_m ⊂ P^1 × P^1 (closure of the graph of x ↦ x^{-1}), both give H^1_c = K and H^2_c = K(−1).

sources.excerpt: Soient j : X ↪ Y, j' : X ↪ Y' deux immersions ouvertes, v : Y' → Y un morphisme tel que v∘j' = j, et que v(Z') ⊂ Z. Si v est propre, l'homomorphisme canonique H*c(X ⊂ Y/K) → H*c(X ⊂ Y'/K) est un isomorphisme.
Le théorème 4 entraîne que H*c(X/K) ne dépend pas, à isomorphisme canonique près, du choix de X̄, et est un foncteur contravariant en X par rapport aux morphismes propres.

nodes.title: Functoriality of compact-support cohomology: proper pullback and extension by zero
nodes.statement: Compact-support rigid cohomology is contravariant for proper morphisms and covariant for open immersions: a proper f: X' → X induces f^*: H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) → H^i_{c,rig}(X'/K, f^*E), and an open immersion j: U → X induces j_!: H^i_{c,rig}(U/K, E|_U) → H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E), each compatible with identities and composition and with morphisms of coefficients.
hypotheses: Proper pullback uses compactifications X̄' → X̄ extending f with the preimage of the boundary in the boundary (possible because f is proper).
proofSteps: Proper f: choose compactifications with f̄: X̄' → X̄ and f̄^{-1}(X̄ \ X) = X̄' \ X'; then Γ_{]X[} → f̄_*Γ_{]X'[}f̄^{-1} gives (3.2.1) and f^*; independence by RD.4/compact-support-independence-of-compactification.
Open immersion j: U ⊂ X with the same compactification Y of X: ]Y \ X[ ⊂ ]Y \ U[, so Γ_{]U[}F ⊂ Γ_{]X[}F; this inclusion of functors gives j_!.
Compatibility with composition and coefficients follows from the corresponding identities of functors.
acceptance: For G_m ⊂ A^1, j_!: H^2_{c,rig}(G_m/K) → H^2_{c,rig}(A^1/K) is an isomorphism K(−1) ≅ K(−1).

sources.excerpt: H*c(X) est un foncteur contravariant par rapport aux morphismes propres, covariant par rapport aux immersions ouvertes.

nodes.title: F-spaces: vector spaces with a semilinear Frobenius
nodes.statement: Fix (K, σ_K). An F-space is a K-vector space V with a σ_K-semilinear endomorphism F: V → V (F(av) = σ_K(a)F(v)). Morphisms are K-linear maps commuting with F. The unit object is K with F = σ_K; tensor products carry F ⊗ F, and when F is bijective and V finite dimensional the dual V^∨ carries the inverse transpose F^∨(λ) = σ_K ∘ λ ∘ F^{-1}. When k = F_q and σ_K = id, F is K-linear and has a characteristic polynomial det(1 − Ft; V) for V finite dimensional. The finite-dimensional F-spaces with bijective F are the F-isocrystals over k, i.e. F-Isoc†(Spec k/K).
hypotheses: F is not required to be bijective in the definition: rigid cohomology groups are F-spaces before their finite dimensionality is known; bijectivity on cohomology is RD.5/frobenius-bijective-on-cohomology.
proofSteps: Semilinear maps are Mathlib's LinearMap with ring homomorphism σ_K; tensor products and duals of semilinear maps are defined through the linearisations σ_K^*V → V.
When σ_K = id the linear case uses Mathlib's LinearMap.charpoly.
acceptance: The unit K with F = σ_K; for K = FractionRing(W(k)), q = p, finite-dimensional F-spaces with bijective F are Mathlib's WittVector.Isocrystal.

sources.excerpt: We will frequently consider modules over various rings equipped with a linear or semi-linear endomorphism.

The fibre over Spec k ′ , for k ′ a finite extension of k, is equivalent to the category of finite dimensional K ′ -vector spaces, for K ′ the unramified extension of K with residue field k ′ , equipped with a bijective σK ′ -linear transformation F .

nodes.title: The Frobenius on rigid cohomology
nodes.statement: For E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) with Frobenius structure F_E: Fr^*E ≅ E (Fr the q-power Frobenius of X over σ_K), the Frobenius Φ on H^i_rig(X/K, E) (and on H^i_{c,rig}, H^i_{Z,rig}) is the composite of base change along σ_K, pullback along the relative Frobenius F_{X/k} (functoriality) and the map induced by F_E. It is σ_K-semilinear, so each group is an F-space (RD.4/frobenius-vector-space); K-linear when σ_K = id. On a frame (X, Y, P) with a lift σ: P → P of the q-power Frobenius over σ_K, Φ is induced by σ^* on DR†(E) composed with F_E ⊗ ∧dσ. On the Monsky–Washnitzer complex of a (σ,∇)-module it is F ⊗ ∧dσ.
hypotheses: A lift of Frobenius to a frame exists locally when P is smooth; the definition through functoriality needs no lift (Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Section 12.2).
proofSteps: Functorial definition: Φ = H(F_E) ∘ F_{X/k}^* ∘ g^*, g the base change along σ_K (Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Section 12.2, with RD.4/functoriality-of-rigid-cohomology).

With a lift σ on the frame, the pair (σ, σ) is a morphism of frames over σ_K lifting Frobenius, so (2.2.1) gives σ^*: RΓ_rig(X/K, E) → RΓ_rig(X/K, σ^*E); compose with F_E. Compact supports: the same with RΓ_{]X[}, since σ preserves the tubes of X and Z.
Agreement of the two definitions is RD.4/frobenius-independent-of-lift.
acceptance: Φ acts by q on H^1_rig(G_m/K) and by q^n on H^{2n}_{c,rig}(A^n/K).

nodes.title: The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology
nodes.statement: Let X be separated of finite type over k, Z ⊂ X a closed subscheme, U = X \ Z and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K). There is a distinguished triangle RΓ_{c,rig}(U/K, E|_U) → RΓ_{c,rig}(X/K, E) → RΓ_{c,rig}(Z/K, E|_Z) → +1, hence a long exact sequence ⋯ → H^i_{c,rig}(U/K, E) → H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) → H^i_{c,rig}(Z/K, E) → H^{i+1}_{c,rig}(U/K, E) → ⋯, natural in E, whose maps between groups of the same degree are the extension by zero and the (proper) restriction; the triangle is one of complexes with Frobenius, so every map of the sequence, the connecting maps H^i_{c,rig}(Z/K, E) → H^{i+1}_{c,rig}(U/K, E) included, is Frobenius-equivariant.
hypotheses: Z closed in X (reduced structure allowed: rigid cohomology does not see nilpotents).
proofSteps: Choose a compactification Y of X and a frame (X, Y, P); let Z̄ be the closure of Z in Y. Then ]Y \ U[ is covered by ]Y \ X[ and ]Z̄[, and (Y, Z̄) is a compactification of Z.

For coherent F, the two-term descriptions give a short exact sequence of complexes 0 → [F → ι_{U*}ι_U^*F]' → [F → ι_{X*}ι_X^*F] → (sections on ]Z̄[ with support in ]Z[) → 0 up to quasi-isomorphism, i.e. a triangle RΓ_{]U[} → RΓ_{]X[} → i_{Z*}RΓ_{]Z[}i_Z^{-1}; apply to E ⊗ Ω^• and take hypercohomology (Berthelot: properties (i)–(iii) 'résultent facilement des définitions').

The Frobenius is compatible with each map by naturality of the construction (Kedlaya, Weil II (2.1.1)). The detailed verification is in Tsuzuki (Hiroshima Math. J. 29, Proposition 2.5.1), which is not publicly accessible; recorded as coverage remaining.

nodes.title: Rigid cohomology with supports in a closed subscheme H^i_{Z,rig}(X/K, E)
nodes.statement: Let X be separated of finite type over k with a frame (X, Y, P), Z ⊂ X closed and U = X \ Z. For E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) the restriction to U gives a surjection of complexes of sheaves j_X†(E ⊗ Ω^•) → j_U†(E ⊗ Ω^•) on ]Y[_P (the second is the colimit of direct images of the restrictions to strict neighbourhoods of ]U[). Its kernel Γ†_Z(E ⊗ Ω^•) has hypercohomology H^i_{Z,rig}(X/K, E), the rigid cohomology of X with supports in Z.
hypotheses: Z closed in X; the definition is independent of the frame by the same arguments as RD.4/independence-of-embedding and RD.4/independence-of-compactification.
proofSteps: Surjectivity of j_X† → j_U†: every strict neighbourhood of ]U[ contains a strict neighbourhood of ]X[ intersected with the complement of a tube of Z of radius λ < 1, and j† is exact.
Define Γ†_Z as the kernel and take hypercohomology; functoriality in E and in (X, Z) by functoriality of j†.
