nodes.title: Localisation sequences for rigid cohomology with supports
nodes.statement: (a) For Z ⊂ X closed with complement U there is a long exact sequence ⋯ → H^i_{Z,rig}(X/K, E) → H^i_rig(X/K, E) → H^i_rig(U/K, E) → H^{i+1}_{Z,rig}(X/K, E) → ⋯. (b) For T ⊂ Z closed there is a long exact sequence ⋯ → H^i_{T,rig}(X/K, E) → H^i_{Z,rig}(X/K, E) → H^i_{Z\T,rig}(X \ T/K, E) → H^{i+1}_{T,rig}(X/K, E) → ⋯. Both are natural and Frobenius-equivariant.
hypotheses: Z closed in X, T closed in Z.
proofSteps: (a) is the long exact hypercohomology sequence of 0 → Γ†_Z(E ⊗ Ω^•) → j_X†(E ⊗ Ω^•) → j_U†(E ⊗ Ω^•) → 0 (RD.4/rigid-cohomology-with-supports).

(b): the kernels for T ⊂ Z ⊂ X form a short exact sequence 0 → Γ†_T → Γ†_Z → (kernel for Z \ T in X \ T) → 0 by the same surjectivity argument; the identification of the last term with Γ†_{Z\T} on X \ T uses excision for supports. Berthelot proves (b) for constant coefficients ([Be5, Proposition 2.5], not public); Kedlaya states that the general case is similar. Recorded as coverage remaining.

nodes.title: Tate twists of F-spaces
nodes.statement: For an F-space (V, F) and n ∈ ℤ, the Tate twist V(n) is V with Frobenius q^{−n}F; in particular V(−i) is V with q^i F (Kedlaya's convention). K(n) denotes the unit object twisted by n, i.e. K with F = q^{−n}σ_K. Twisting is exact, V(0) = V, V(n)(m) = V(n + m), V(n) ⊗ W(m) = (V ⊗ W)(n + m), and for bijective F, V(n)^∨ = V^∨(−n). If F v = αv then in V(n) one has F v = q^{−n}αv.
hypotheses: q = p^a is the cardinality of the Frobenius used (Kedlaya's 'Frobenius always means the q-power Frobenius'); q is invertible in K since char K = 0.
proofSteps: Define the twist by scaling the semilinear map by the scalar q^{−n} ∈ K^×; scaling commutes with the K-structure and with semilinearity because σ_K(q) = q.
acceptance: H^1_rig(G_m/K) = K(−1) (Frobenius q); H^{2n}_{c,rig}(A^n/K) = K(−n) (Frobenius q^n).

nodes.title: Independence of the Frobenius from the chosen lift
nodes.statement: (a) The Frobenius Φ on H^i_rig(X/K, E) and H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) computed with a lift σ of the q-power Frobenius to a frame (together with the Frobenius structure of E relative to σ) does not depend on the frame or on σ: it equals the functorial Frobenius of RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology. (b) Monsky–Washnitzer form: let A be a dagger algebra of MW-type, σ, σ' two Frobenius lifts on A (both σ_K-semilinear, both lifting the q-power map), M a (σ,∇)-module and F' the Frobenius structure of M relative to σ' obtained by the change-of-Frobenius equivalence (the Taylor isomorphism σ^*M ≅ σ'^*M composed with F). Then F ⊗ ∧dσ and F' ⊗ ∧dσ' induce the same endomorphism of H^i(M). For M = A (constant coefficients) this says σ^* = σ'^* on H^i(A ⊗ Ω^•).
hypotheses: σ ≡ σ' modulo π on A^int (both lift the q-power map).
proofSteps: (b), constant coefficients: σ and σ' are congruent modulo π, so by van der Put's Theorem 2.4.4 (iii) (supplied as RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra) there is F: A → A⟨T⟩† with F(T = 0) = σ and F(T = 1) = σ'; the maps induced by T ↦ 0 and T ↦ 1 on the de Rham complex of A⟨T⟩† are homotopic via integration in T, so σ^* and σ'^* are homotopic.

(b), coefficients: pull M back along F to A⟨T⟩†; the connection in the T-direction and its Taylor series give the change-of-Frobenius isomorphism σ^*M ≅ σ'^*M (Kedlaya, Weil II, Section 2.4: the category is independent of σ), and the same integration-in-T homotopy compares F ⊗ ∧dσ with F' ⊗ ∧dσ'.

(a): on each frame the lift gives the same map as the functorial Frobenius because the functoriality maps (2.2.1) are canonical (RD.4/independence-of-embedding) and any two lifts on a smooth frame are compared, over a strict neighbourhood, by the same homotopy argument; Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki record that Φ depends only on σ_K.
Consequence for curves (ColemanIntegration's request): RD.4/mw-comparison-for-affine-curves.
acceptance: On G_m with σ(x) = x^q and σ'(x) = x^q + px = x^q(1 + p x^{1−q}): σ'^*(dx/x) = q·dx/x + d log(1 + p x^{1−q}), and log(1 + p x^{1−q}) ∈ K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩†, so both lifts act by q on H^1.

nodes.title: The Monsky–Washnitzer comparison: rigid cohomology of a smooth affine is the de Rham cohomology of its dagger algebra
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth affine k-scheme with a smooth lift 𝒳 = Spec 𝒜 over O_K, A = 𝒜† ⊗ K the weak completion (a dagger algebra of MW-type with special fibre X), σ a Frobenius lift on A and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) with associated (σ,∇)-module M (RD.3/affine-smooth-description-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals). Then there is a canonical isomorphism H^i_rig(X/K, E) ≅ H^i(M ⊗_A Ω^•_{A/K}) for all i, functorial in E and in X, and compatible with the Frobenius (Φ on the left, F ⊗ ∧^i dσ on the right).
hypotheses: X smooth affine; the lift 𝒜 exists (Elkik) and A is unique up to non-canonical isomorphism, the comparison being canonical.
proofSteps: Frame: Y = closure of X in a projective space, P = formal completion of the closure of 𝒳; the tube ]X[ is the affinoid 𝒳^an ∩ closed unit ball, and the affinoids U_λ = 𝒳^an ∩ {|x| ≤ 1/λ}, λ → 1^-, are cofinal strict neighbourhoods (Berthelot (2.1), (2.5) b)).

Γ(U_λ, O) is an affinoid algebra and colim_λ Γ(U_λ, O) = A (Berthelot (2.1)); by Kiehl's Theorem B coherent sheaves on the affinoids U_λ are acyclic for j_{λ*} and for global sections (AdicSpacesPartII:R3), and ]Y[ is quasi-compact, so the hypercohomology of j†(E ⊗ Ω^•) is the cohomology of colim_λ Γ(U_λ, E ⊗ Ω^•) = M ⊗ Ω^•_A (Crew (8.1.1) for curves).
Frobenius: σ extends to a morphism of the system of strict neighbourhoods over σ_K, and the identification is compatible with σ^* and F_E (RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology).
Canonicity: another lift gives an isomorphic dagger algebra, and the comparison maps differ by the functoriality isomorphism (van der Put, Corollary 2.4.5).

The detailed statement for coefficients is in Berthelot's Finitude, Proposition 1.10 (constant coefficients; not public); the argument above covers coefficients because only coherence of E ⊗ Ω^i is used.

nodes.title: The compact-support complex of a coherent sheaf on the overconvergent polydisc
nodes.statement: Let X = A^n_k ⊂ Y = P^n_k ⊂ P = P̂^n_{O_K}, x_i = z_i/z_0, t_i = x_i^{-1}, and for ρ > 1 let V_ρ = {|z_0| ≥ ρ^{-1}} = Sp T_{n,ρ} (a strict neighbourhood of ]X[). For T ⊆ {1, …, n} let W_T ⊆ V_ρ be the locus |x_i| > 1 (i ∈ T); W_T is quasi-Stein with Γ(W_T) = S^{(n),T}_r (series in t allowing positive powers of t_i only for i ∈ T, r = log_p ρ), S^{(n),∅}_r = T_{n,ρ}, S^{(n)}_r = S^{(n),{1..n}}_r. For F the coherent sheaf of a finite locally free T_{n,ρ}-module E, the complex RΓ_{]X[}(F) = [F → ι_*ι^*F] has cohomology (E ⊗ S^{(n)}_r)/Σ_i (E ⊗ S^{(n),i'}_r) in degree n (i' = {1..n} \ {i}) and zero in other degrees; this does not depend on r.
hypotheses: The complement V_ρ \ ]X[ is not quasi-Stein for n > 1; the W_T cover it by quasi-Stein spaces.
proofSteps: W_T is quasi-Stein: it is the increasing union of the affinoids X_η = {η ≤ |x_i| ≤ ρ, i ∈ T}, η → 1^+, and Laurent polynomials are dense in each Γ(X_η) (Kedlaya, Lemma 8.1.5); Theorem B for quasi-Stein spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R3).

Resolve both terms of [F → ι_*ι^*F] by Čech complexes for the admissible cover U_0, U_1 ∩ V_ρ, …, U_n ∩ V_ρ (U_i = {|z_i| = 1}); the intersections are affinoid or equal to W_T, hence acyclic, so the complex is the total complex of global sections.

Compute with the Leray (row) spectral sequence: the Čech complex of the S^{(n),T}_r has cohomology T_{n,ρ} in degree 0 and S^{(n)}_r/Σ_i S^{(n),i'}_r in degree n − 1 (induction on n); the degree-0 row cancels against E, and the sequence degenerates at E_2.
acceptance: n = 1: the cohomology is E ⊗ R_{K,r}/E ⊗ T_{1,ρ}, i.e. series Σ_{m ≥ 1} a_m t^m converging on |t| < 1 (Berthelot's M), in degree 1.

nodes.statement: For n ≥ 0: H^i_{c,rig}(A^n_k/K) = 0 for i ≠ 2n and H^{2n}_{c,rig}(A^n_k/K) = K(−n), spanned by the class of dt_1/t_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dt_n/t_n (t_i = 1/x_i); the standard Frobenius t_i ↦ t_i^q acts on it by q^n.
hypotheses: Constant coefficients; σ_K = id for the eigenvalue statement (in general the Frobenius is q^n·σ_K on the generator).
proofSteps: By RD.4/compact-support-cohomology-of-affine-space-with-coefficients with M = O, the complex is (Ω^• ⊗ S^{(n)})/Σ_i(Ω^• ⊗ S^{(n),i'}). Writing forms in the basis dt_J/t_J, the quotient in degree |J| consists of the series Σ c_I t^I dt_J/t_J with i_j ≥ 0 for j ∈ J and i_j ≥ 1 for j ∉ J (because Ω^1 of S^{(n),i'} is spanned by x_i·dt_i/t_i and the dt_j/t_j, j ≠ i). The complex splits along monomials t^I: for I = 0 only dt_1/t_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dt_n/t_n occurs, and for I ≠ 0 the summand is the Koszul complex of the nonzero integers i_j, acyclic in characteristic 0 (Kedlaya, Corollary 8.1.9; Berthelot's Exemple for n = 1).
Frobenius: σ^*(dt_i/t_i) = q·dt_i/t_i for σ(t_i) = t_i^q, so the generator is multiplied by q^n: H^{2n}_{c,rig} = K(−n) (RD.4/tate-twist).

nodes.title: The Gysin isomorphism for smooth liftable pairs
nodes.statement: Suppose Z → X is a closed immersion of smooth k-schemes, dim Z ≤ n, which lifts to a closed immersion of smooth O_K-schemes 𝒵 → 𝒳 such that there is an étale morphism 𝒳 → Spec O_K[x_1, …, x_d] under which 𝒵 maps to the vanishing locus of d − n of the x_i (Kedlaya's Hypothesis 4.4.1). Then for E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) there is a Frobenius-compatible isomorphism H^i_{Z,rig}(X/K, E) ≅ H^{i−2c}_rig(Z/K, E|_Z)(−c), c = dim X − dim Z. With RD.4/localisation-sequence (a) this gives the Gysin sequence ⋯ → H^{i−2c}_rig(Z)(−c) → H^i_rig(X) → H^i_rig(X \ Z) → H^{i+1−2c}_rig(Z)(−c) → ⋯.
hypotheses: Hypothesis 4.4.1 of Kedlaya (smooth liftable pair with étale coordinates).
The Tate twist (−c) is part of the Frobenius-equivariant form; Kedlaya states the isomorphism without the twist (the twist is fixed by the case X = A^1, Z = {0}).
proofSteps: Tsuzuki's construction (Hiroshima Math. J. 29 (1999), Theorem 4.1.1): in the étale coordinates the tube of Z in X is a product of ]Z[ with an open polydisc of dimension c; the kernel complex Γ†_Z(E ⊗ Ω^•) is quasi-isomorphic to E|_Z ⊗ Ω^•_Z tensored with the compactly supported de Rham complex of the open c-polydisc, whose cohomology is K(−c) in degree 2c (RD.4/compactly-supported-cohomology-of-affine-space).

nodes.title: H^1 of the dagger algebra of a smooth affine curve is H^1_rig, with a lift-independent Frobenius
nodes.statement: Let Y_k be a smooth affine curve over F_q with a smooth lift 𝒴 = Spec 𝒜 over O_K (K finite over ℚ_p with residue field F_q, σ_K = id), let A† = 𝒜† ⊗ K be its dagger algebra and Ω^1_{A†} its module of continuous differentials. Then H^0(A† → Ω^1_{A†}) = ker d ≅ H^0_rig(Y_k/K) and H^1(A† → Ω^1_{A†}) = Ω^1_{A†}/dA† ≅ H^1_rig(Y_k/K) canonically. For every Frobenius lift φ of A† (a K-algebra endomorphism with φ(x) ≡ x^q mod π on 𝒜†), the endomorphism φ^* of Ω^1_{A†}/dA† corresponds to the Frobenius Φ of H^1_rig(Y_k/K); in particular it does not depend on φ.

nodes.title: The Robba ring over a reduced dagger algebra
nodes.statement: Let A be a reduced dagger algebra over K with completion Â (an affinoid algebra). For r > 0, R_{Â,r} is the ring of series Σ_{i∈ℤ} x_i t^i with x_i ∈ Â and v_Â(x_i) + si → ∞ as i → ±∞ for 0 < s ≤ r, with the Fréchet topology of the valuations w_{Â,s}(x) = min_i(v_Â(x_i) + si). The Robba ring R_A over A consists of the series Σ x_i t^i with coefficients in A such that for each sufficiently small r > 0 there is a fringe algebra B of A containing all x_i with v_B(x_i) + ri → ∞ as i → ±∞; R_{A,r} is the union over fringe algebras B of R_{B,r}. Subrings: the plus part R_A^+ (only t^i, i ≥ 0), the integral subring R_A^int (integral coefficients). The module of continuous differentials relative to A is Ω^1_{R_A/A} = R_A·dt, and a Frobenius lift σ_A on A extends to the standard Frobenius Σ b_I t^I ↦ Σ b_I^{σ_A} t^{qI}. For A = K this is the Robba ring R_K of RD.0/robba-ring.
hypotheses: A reduced, so that spectral seminorms are norms on fringe algebras.
The definition is not the colimit of the R_B over fringe algebras B (the quantifiers are in the other order); see the non-example.
proofSteps: Ring structure: products of series satisfying the growth conditions satisfy them (the ultrametric inequality on the w_{B,r}).
Membership criterion (Kedlaya, Proposition 2.5.4, Corollary 2.5.5): x ∈ R_A iff x ∈ R_Â and x_i p^{⌊ri⌋} → 0 in the fringe topology for one r > 0; the proof uses RD.5/fringe-norm-interpolation.
Derivative (Kedlaya, Proposition 3.1.4): for x = Σ c_i t^i, ker ∂/∂t = {c_i = 0 for i ≠ 0}, im ∂/∂t = {c_{−1} = 0}, and R_A/ker → im is a homeomorphism.
Standard Frobenius: t ↦ t^q preserves the growth conditions (radius r ↦ r/q); Kedlaya, Definition 3.2.3.
acceptance: For A = K⟨x⟩†, 1 − xt is a unit in R_A (its inverse Σ x^i t^i lies in R_A), but not in R_B for any fringe algebra B.

nodes.statement: Let A be a reduced dagger algebra with a Frobenius lift σ_A, and R_A its Robba ring with the standard Frobenius σ (RD.5/relative-robba-ring). A (σ,∇)-module over R_A relative to A is a finite free R_A-module M with an A-linear connection ∇: M → M ⊗ Ω^1_{R_A/A} = M·dt satisfying the Leibniz rule and a σ-semilinear F with bijective linearisation such that ∇ ∘ F = (F ⊗ dσ) ∘ ∇; write ∇v = D(v) ⊗ dt/t. A module with connection over R_{A,r} is the same without F (Kedlaya, Definition 5.2.2). The relative local cohomology is H^0(M) = ker ∇ and H^1(M) = coker ∇, which are A-modules with a σ_A-semilinear Frobenius.
hypotheses: M free (over R_K finite locally free modules are free by the Bézout property; over R_A freeness is assumed).
proofSteps: The axioms are those of Kedlaya, Definition 3.3.1 with R = R_A and relative differentials; integrability is automatic since Ω^1_{R_A/A} has rank one (Remark 3.3.2).
Base change along A → B: M ⊗_{R_A} R_B with the induced structures; in particular the generic fibre M ⊗ R_L for L the completion of Frac A in the affinoid topology.

nodes.statement: Let M be a unipotent module with connection over R_{K,r} (r > 0) and e the nilpotency index of the matrix of D on a strongly unipotent basis. Define f_0(w) = D^{e−1}w and f_l(w) = (1 − D^2/l^2)^e f_{l−1}(w) for l ≥ 1. For every w ∈ M the sequence f_l(w) converges for w_{K,r} to an element f(w) ∈ M with ∇f(w) = 0; f(w) lies in the K-span of the strongly unipotent basis, in the image of D^{e−1} on it.

Hence w_{K,r}(f_{l+1}(w) − f_l(w)) ≥ c'l − d' for some c' > 0, so the sequence converges; the limit is in the image of D^{e−1} on the K-span of the basis, hence killed by D.

nodes.title: Generic unipotence over R_{L,r} spreads out to a localisation (modules with connection)
nodes.statement: Let A be a reduced integral dagger algebra, L the completion of Frac A, and M a module with connection over R_{A,r} with M ⊗ R_{L,r} unipotent. Then M ⊗ R_{B,r} is unipotent for some localisation B of A.
hypotheses: A reduced integral dagger algebra; localisations are the dagger localisations A⟨f^{-1}⟩†.
proofSteps: Induction on rank. Let M_0 be the span of a strongly unipotent basis of M ⊗ R_{L,r} and e the nilpotency index; f(w) runs over the image of D^{e−1} on M_0 as w runs over the dense subspace M ⊗_A L, so some f(w) with w ∈ M is nonzero; by RD.5/horizontal-sections-descend it lies in M and is horizontal.

Its span is a direct summand of M ⊗ R_{L,r} (it lies in the L-span of a strongly unipotent basis, RD.5/strongly-unipotent-span-unique); a row vector that is the first row of an invertible matrix over R_{L,r} is so over R_{B,r} for a localisation B (approximation), so the span is a summand over R_{B,r}; quotient and induct.

nodes.title: Near-injections, near-surjections and near-isomorphisms of K-vector spaces
nodes.statement: A K-linear map f: V → W is a near-injection if ker f is finite dimensional, a near-surjection if coker f = W/im f is finite dimensional, and a near-isomorphism if both hold; equivalently f becomes injective, surjective or bijective in the quotient of the category of K-vector spaces by the Serre subcategory of finite-dimensional spaces. If g ∘ f is a near-injection so is f; if g ∘ f is a near-surjection so is g; if two of f, g, g ∘ f are near-isomorphisms so is the third; in a commutative square, if three maps are near-isomorphisms so is the fourth.
hypotheses: Linear maps of K-vector spaces, of arbitrary dimension.
proofSteps: The two-of-three and square properties follow from the exact sequence 0 → ker f → ker gf → ker g → coker f → coker gf → coker g → 0 of K-vector spaces (snake lemma for the composite), since finite-dimensional spaces form a Serre subcategory.
acceptance: The derivative d: K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† → K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩†·dx/x is a near-isomorphism with kernel and cokernel both of dimension 1.

nodes.title: Local Robba algebras at the missing points of an affine curve
nodes.statement: Let A be a dagger algebra of MW-type whose special fibre X = Spec R is a smooth affine irreducible curve over k, with smooth compactification X̄ whose boundary points x_1, …, x_m are geometrically reduced (automatic for k perfect). Let K_i be the unramified extension of K with residue field k_i = κ(x_i) and R_i a copy of the Robba ring over K_i with parameter t_i. Choosing a dagger algebra B of an affine neighbourhood U of the x_i, embeddings B^int → R_i^{+,int} (Cohen structure theorem at x_i) and an embedding A → C (C the dagger localisation of B with special fibre U \ {x_i}) gives embeddings ρ_i: A → R_i and ρ = ⊕ρ_i: A → ⊕_i R_i, compatible with Frobenius lifts. Geometrically (Crew), R_i is the ring of functions on V ∩ ]x_i[ for strict neighbourhoods V of the tube of X, i.e. germs of functions on annuli at the boundary.

nodes.title: Riemann–Roch on the special fibre: principal parts at the boundary are near-isomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let X = Spec R be a smooth affine irreducible curve over k with smooth compactification X̄ and boundary points x_1, …, x_m. Then the maps R → ⊕_i k_i((t_i))/k_i[[t_i]] and Ω^1_{R/k} → ⊕_i Ω^1_{k_i((t_i))}/Ω^1_{k_i[[t_i]]} (principal parts at the missing points) are near-isomorphisms of k-vector spaces: the first has kernel the constants of X̄ and cokernel H^1(X̄, O), of dimension the genus g; the second has kernel the regular differentials (dimension g) and one-dimensional cokernel (for X̄ geometrically connected). Moreover (Kedlaya, Lemma 6.2.6) every r ∈ R lifts to a polynomial of degree at most c·d(r), d(r) the maximal pole order of r at the x_i.
hypotheses: X̄ smooth projective; k the field of constants of X̄ for the dimension statements.
proofSteps: Let F = k(X̄). The kernel of R → ⊕ k_i((t_i))/k_i[[t_i]] is the functions without poles on X̄, a finite-dimensional space (Tau Ceti: finiteDimensional_riemannRochSpace, equal to the constants when k is exact, Divisor.dim_zero_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn).

The cokernel: principal parts at all places modulo principal parts of global functions regular on X is the repartition space modulo A_F(0) + F; it is finite dimensional of dimension g (Tau Ceti: finiteDimensional_quotient_repartitionSpace, finrank_quotient_repartitionSpace_zero), using that k_i((t_i))/k_i[[t_i]] = F/O_{x_i} (completion does not change principal parts).

Differentials: the kernel is the space of regular differentials, of dimension g (Tau Ceti: finrank_weilDifferentialFiltration_zero, via the identification of Kähler differentials of F with Weil differentials, a comparison supplied by the Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves roadmap; see requests); the cokernel is dual to the constants by the residue pairing (dimension 1).
Degree bound: by Riemann–Roch the monoid of pole-order vectors p(r) ∈ ℤ^m_{≥0} is finitely generated; choose z_1, …, z_l generating it and divide leading pole terms (Kedlaya, proof of Lemma 6.2.6).

nodes.title: Finite dimensionality of H^0_rig and H^1_rig of a smooth affine curve (constant coefficients)
nodes.statement: Let A be a dagger algebra of MW-type whose special fibre X is a (smooth affine) curve over k. Then d: A → Ω^1_{A/K} is a near-isomorphism; equivalently H^0_rig(X/K) and H^1_rig(X/K) are finite dimensional over K. nodes.title: Van der Put's computation of H^1 of an affine Legendre elliptic curve
nodes.statement: Let p ≠ 2, u ∈ W(F_q) lifting ū ∉ {0, 1}, and E* the affine curve y^2 = x(x − 1)(x − ū) over F_q (the Legendre elliptic curve minus its point at infinity). Then H^0(E*; K) = K and H^1(E*; K) is two dimensional over K = W(F_q)[1/p], with basis the classes of dx/y and x dx/y. The Frobenius eigenvalues α_1, α_2 on H^1 satisfy α_1α_2 = q and α_1 + α_2 = q + 1 − #E(F_q) (van der Put's normalisation through the operator ψ = q F^{-1}); they lie in W(F_q)[1/p] when E is ordinary but in general only in a quadratic extension (van der Put asserts a_1, a_2 ∈ W(F_q); see sourceIssues).
hypotheses: p ≠ 2; ū ≠ 0, 1 so that the curve is smooth.
proofSteps: The polynomial algebra A_∞ = W[x, y]/(y^2 − x(x − 1)(x − u)) ⊗ K has algebraic de Rham H^1 spanned by dx/y, x dx/y and H^0 = K (explicit formula for d on a_0(x) + a_1(x)y).
Topologise A = A†⊗K by the norms ‖·‖_ρ; the embedding φ: A → W[[T]]⟨T^{-1}⟩ with x = T^{-2}, y = T^{-3}√((1 − T^2)(1 − uT^2)) is isometric (van der Put, Lemma 7.2).

The image of d on A is closed (van der Put, Lemma 7.3), so H^1 of A is Hausdorff; the dense subspace coming from A_∞ has finite-dimensional image, hence H^1(A) is the image of the algebraic H^1, and injectivity follows because f ∈ A with df algebraic lies in A_∞.
The Frobenius relation α_1α_2 = q follows from duality of H^1 (van der Put, Remarks 7.4).

nodes.title: Factorisation of invertible matrices over the Robba ring
nodes.statement: Every invertible n × n matrix U over R_K can be written as U = VW with V invertible over R_K^int and W invertible over R_K^+.

Shift denominators: for U invertible over R_K^int[1/p] with integral entries, induct on v_K(det U); if positive, the reduction over k((t)) has deficient rank, elementary row operations over k[[t]] (Euclidean algorithm column by column) produce a zero row; lift them to O[[t]] and divide the row by π, lowering v_K(det U).

nodes.title: Simultaneous correction of local matrices by a global matrix on an affine curve
nodes.statement: Under Hypothesis 6.2.1 with boundary points x_1, …, x_m and local Robba rings R_i: for invertible n × n matrices U_i over R_i (i = 1, …, m) there is a matrix V over Frac A such that U_iρ_i(V) is invertible over R_i^+ for i = 1, …, m.

nodes.title: Finite dimensionality on a curve for coefficients with unipotent local monodromy
nodes.statement: Under Hypothesis 6.2.1, let M be a (σ,∇)-module over A such that M ⊗ R_i is unipotent for each boundary point x_i. Then in the commutative square with top row M → ⊕_i(R_i/R_i^+)^n, bottom row M ⊗ Ω^1_{A/K} → ⊕_i(Ω^1_{R_i/K}/t_i^{-1}Ω^1_{R_i^+/K_i})^n and vertical maps ∇, the horizontal maps and the right vertical map are near-isomorphisms; hence ∇: M → M ⊗ Ω^1_{A/K} is a near-isomorphism, and H^0(M), H^1(M) are finite dimensional.
hypotheses: Unipotent local monodromy at every boundary point.
proofSteps: Choose a basis e_1, …, e_n of M over A[a^{-1}]; the connection matrices N_i over R_i; by unipotence and RD.5/strongly-unipotent-basis-exists there are U_i with U_i^{-1}N_iU_i + U_i^{-1}t_i dU_i/dt_i = X_i nilpotent over K_i.

By RD.5/simultaneous-matrix-approximation there is V over Frac A with W_i = U_i^{-1}ρ_i(V) and its inverse over R_i^+; the connection matrix N'_i in the basis v_l = Σ V_{jl}e_j has entries in R_i^+, which makes the right vertical map an isomorphism (RD.5/unipotent-local-residue-isomorphism).

The horizontal maps factor through M → u^{-1}A^n and principal parts, near-isomorphisms by Lemma 6.2.2 and RD.5/principal-parts-near-isomorphism; conclude by the square property of RD.5/near-isomorphism.

nodes.title: Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology of an overconvergent F-isocrystal on a smooth affine curve
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth affine curve over k and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K). Then H^i_rig(X/K, E) is finite dimensional over K for all i (and zero for i ≥ 2).
hypotheses: Frobenius structure on E (used to invoke the local monodromy theorem at the boundary).
proofSteps: Realise E as a (σ,∇)-module M over a dagger algebra A of MW-type (RD.3/affine-smooth-description-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals) and H^i_rig = H^i(M) (RD.4/monsky-washnitzer-comparison).

By the local monodromy theorem (RD.2/local-monodromy-finite-etale-form) each M ⊗ R_i becomes unipotent over a finite étale extension of R_i^int identified with a Robba ring; realise these extensions by a finite cover of X (and a finite extension of k), which is allowed by RD.4/finite-flat-pullback-injective (cohomology injects as a direct summand) and RD.4/finite-etale-pushforward-de-rham.
With unipotent local monodromy, RD.5/unipotent-curve-near-isomorphism gives finiteness of H^0 and H^1; H^i = 0 for i ≥ 2 since Ω^2 = 0.

nodes.title: Strict maps and the LF, Fréchet and Montel conditions over a discretely valued field
nodes.statement: For topological K-vector spaces: V is locally convex if 0 has a basis of O_K-convex neighbourhoods; Fréchet if it is Hausdorff, complete and its topology is defined by countably many seminorms; LF if it is separated, locally convex and a locally convex direct limit of countably many Fréchet spaces (Kedlaya's errata: 'direct limit' means locally convex direct limit); barreled and Montel as in Bourbaki. The strong dual V^∨ is the space of continuous linear forms with the topology of uniform convergence on bounded sets. A continuous linear map f: V → W is strict if the continuous bijection V/ker f → im f is a homeomorphism. A sequence is strict exact if its maps are strict.
hypotheses: K complete discretely valued, hence spherically complete (needed for Hahn–Banach).
proofSteps: Definitions only; the basic stability facts: a finite direct sum of maps is strict (resp. strict with closed image) iff each summand is (Crew 3.7); a composite of strict maps with closed image is strict with closed image if the first is surjective or the second injective, and not in general.
acceptance: The map K⟨x⟩ → K⟨x, y⟩/(x − py) ≅ K⟨y⟩ (composite of strict maps with closed image) is not strict (Kedlaya's referee example).

sources.excerpt: A continuous linear map f : V → W of spaces is strict if the induced continuous bijection V / ker(f ) → im(f ) is a homeomorphism.

The notion of strictness is somewhat delicate: for example, a composition g ◦ f of strict maps with closed image is only guaranteed to be strict with closed image if f is surjective or g is injective.
A separated locally convex K-space is an LF-space if there is a countable inductive system {Vi}i of Frechet spaces such that V = lim Vi.

nodes.title: A map of Fréchet–Montel spaces is strict iff its transpose is
nodes.statement: Let f: V → W be a continuous linear map of Fréchet–Montel spaces over K. Then f is strict iff f^∨: W^∨ → V^∨ is strict (strong duals). More generally (Crew 3.8–3.11), for Fréchet spaces f is strict iff its transpose is strict for the linearly compact dual topology, and then ker f^∨ = (im f)^⊥, im f^∨ = (ker f)^⊥; the transpose of a strict exact sequence of separated locally convex spaces is exact.
hypotheses: V, W Fréchet–Montel (so the strong and linearly compact duals agree).
proofSteps: Crew, Proposition 3.8 (Bourbaki EVT IV §4 no. 1 Prop. 2): strictness ⇔ closed image of the transpose + lifting of equicontinuous sets; Proposition 3.10 (for semi-complete spaces with the linearly compact dual); Proposition 3.11 (Fréchet case, using sequences converging to 0 and linear compactness of their closed convex hulls); Corollary 3.12 for Montel spaces. The Hahn–Banach theorem over the spherically complete K enters (RD.5/nonarchimedean-hahn-banach). Crew states the proofs rely on Bourbaki and Schikhof; they were read at the level of statements and proof outlines.
acceptance: For finite-dimensional V, W every map and its transpose are strict.

sources.excerpt: Let f : V → W be a continuous linear map between Fréchet-Montel spaces. Then f is strict if and only if f ∨ : W ∨ → V ∨ is strict.

nodes.title: Crew's finiteness and duality theorem on curves, made unconditional by local monodromy
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth affine curve over a perfect field k and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K). Then E is quasi-unipotent, hence strict, and: H^i_rig(X/K, E), H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) and the parabolic cohomology H^1_p(X, E) = im(H^1_c → H^1) are finite dimensional; the pairings H^i_{c,rig}(X, E) × H^{2−i}_rig(X, E^∨) → H^2_{c,rig}(X, K) → K and H^1_p(X, E) × H^1_p(X, E^∨) → K are perfect; for X geometrically connected the trace H^2_{c,rig}(X, K) → K is an isomorphism and H^2_{c,rig}(X, K) ≅ K(−1) as F-spaces, so the pairings are Frobenius-equivariant into K(−1). There is an exact sequence 0 → H^0 → H^0_loc → H^1_c → H^1 → H^1_loc → H^2_c → 0 with H^i_loc the cohomology of E ⊗ A^loc.
hypotheses: k perfect (Crew's standing hypothesis); the finiteness part holds without it by RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves.

Crew proves the theorem for strict isocrystals; strictness of quasi-unipotent isocrystals is Crew, Proposition 10.2, and quasi-unipotence of overconvergent F-isocrystals is the local monodromy theorem (RD.2).
proofSteps: Quasi-unipotence: by RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement each local module M ⊗ A(x) becomes unipotent after a finite étale cover of the annulus, which is realised by a finite étale cover of X (Kedlaya, Weil II, Section 2.6).
Crew, Proposition 10.2: quasi-unipotent ⇒ strict (reduce by 9.3 to the unipotent case, strict by 6.6).

Crew, Theorem 9.5 (steps 1–7): the diagram 0 → M → M ⊗ A^loc → M ⊗ A^qu → 0 over ∇ is strict exact with Fréchet and dual-of-Fréchet terms (Theorem 7.5); the local connection ∇_loc is strict with finite-dimensional separated cohomology (6.3); the dual of the strict sequence gives the duality isomorphism H^1_c(M) ≅ H^1(M^∨)^∨ (3.12, RD.5/frechet-montel-transpose-strict); a space both Fréchet and dual-of-Fréchet is finite dimensional (Crew, Proposition 2.8).

The trace H^2_c(X, K) → K is the residue sum (Crew (8.1.7), well defined by the residue theorem, Lemma 7.4); H^0(X, K) = K gives that it is an isomorphism; Frobenius: H^2_c(X, K) ≅ K(−1) (Crew (9.6.2), via excision and RD.4/cohomology-of-projective-line).

nodes.title: Relative local cohomology of a unipotent module is finitely generated, with closed image
nodes.statement: Let A be a reduced dagger algebra with a Frobenius lift and M a free unipotent (σ,∇)-module over R_A relative to A. Then H^0(M) = ker ∇ and H^1(M) = coker ∇ are finitely generated A-modules; moreover the image of ∇ is closed and M/ker ∇ → im ∇ is a homeomorphism.
hypotheses: M unipotent.
proofSteps: Choose a strongly unipotent basis (RD.5/strongly-unipotent-basis-exists). Every horizontal element lies in the A-span of the v_i (RD.5/strongly-unipotent-span-unique), a finitely generated A-module, and A is noetherian (dagger algebras are noetherian; AdicSpacesPartII:F1).

Write an element of M ⊗ Ω^1 as Σ_i Σ_l f_{il}t^l v_i ⊗ dt/t; it is in the image of ∇ when all f_{i0} = 0 (integrate using RD.5/relative-robba-ring, derivative_ker_range), so coker ∇ is a quotient of A^n.
Closedness and strictness are read off the same description (Kedlaya, Remark 7.1.2).

nodes.statement: Let A be an integral dagger algebra of MW-type with a Frobenius lift, M a free (σ,∇)-module over R_A relative to A, and B a localisation satisfying the conclusion of RD.5/relative-local-monodromy-theorem. Then H^0(M ⊗ R_B) and H^1(M ⊗ R_B) are finitely generated B-modules.
hypotheses: B as provided by the relative local monodromy theorem.
proofSteps: The extension R'' of the theorem is a composite of two extensions admitting traces (Kedlaya, Remark 3.2.7: coefficientwise trace for B_1/B^{σ^{-m}}, which is flat by Remark 3.2.4, and the Galois trace for R'/R^int_{B_1}); so H^i(M ⊗ R_B) injects into H^i(M ⊗ R'') (as in RD.4/finite-flat-pullback-injective).

M ⊗ R'' is unipotent, so H^i(M ⊗ R'') is finitely generated (RD.5/unipotent-local-cohomology-finitely-generated); submodules of finitely generated modules over the noetherian B are finitely generated.

nodes.title: The generic higher direct images of a (σ,∇)-module along A → A⟨x⟩†
nodes.statement: Let A be a dagger algebra of MW-type, f: A → A⟨x⟩† the inclusion, and A⟨x⟩† ⊂ R_A via x ↦ t^{-1}. For a (σ,∇)-module M over A⟨x⟩† let ∇_v: M → M ⊗ Ω^1_{A⟨x⟩†/A} = M·dx be the vertical connection, ∇_v^loc: M ⊗ R_A → M ⊗ Ω^1_{R_A/A} its extension and ∇_v^qu: (M ⊗ R_A)/M → (M ⊗ Ω^1_{R_A/A})/(M ⊗ Ω^1_{A⟨x⟩†/A}) the induced map. Define the A-modules R^0f_*M = ker ∇_v, R^1f_*M = coker ∇_v, R^0_loc f_*M = ker ∇_v^loc, R^1_loc f_*M = coker ∇_v^loc, R^1f_!M = ker ∇_v^qu, R^2f_!M = coker ∇_v^qu. The snake lemma gives an exact sequence 0 → R^0f_*M → R^0_loc f_*M → R^1f_!M → R^1f_*M → R^1_loc f_*M → R^2f_!M → 0, and R^1_p f_*M := im(R^1f_!M → R^1f_*M). Each carries a Frobenius and the horizontal connection ∇_h induced by M → M ⊗_A Ω^1_{A/K}.
hypotheses: A of MW-type; Ω^1_{A/K} projective, so kernels and cokernels of the vertical maps commute with ⊗ Ω^1_{A/K} and ∇_h is defined even without finiteness.
proofSteps: The rows 0 → M → M ⊗ R_A → (M ⊗ R_A)/M → 0 and the corresponding rows of 1-forms are exact; ∇_v, ∇_v^loc, ∇_v^qu form a morphism of short exact sequences; the snake lemma gives (7.3.2.2) (Mathlib: CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.SnakeInput).
Frobenius acts because σ preserves A⟨x⟩† ⊂ R_A (standard extension) and the vertical connection; the horizontal connection ∇_h is the component of ∇ along Ω^1_{A/K}.

tests.statement: For A = K the modules are H^0, H^1 of A^1 with coefficients, the local cohomology at ∞, and H^1_c, H^2_c of A^1 (RD.4/compact-support-cohomology-of-affine-space-with-coefficients).

tests.name: pushforward_exact_test
tests.statement: The sequence 0 → R^0f_* → R^0_loc f_* → R^1f_! → R^1f_* → R^1_loc f_* → R^2f_! → 0 is exact; for A = K it is Crew's sequence (8.1.4) for the affine line.

tests.name: pushforward_not_finite_nonexample
tests.statement: Without localising A the modules need not be finitely generated: the theorem RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem only holds after replacing A by a localisation (the relative local monodromy theorem is generic).

nodes.title: A finite-dimensional L-subspace of L^S meets R^S in a finitely generated R-module
nodes.statement: Let R be a noetherian domain, L a field containing R, S any set and N a finite-dimensional L-subspace of the product L^S. Then N ∩ R^S is a finitely generated R-module.
hypotheses: R noetherian domain; R → L injective.
proofSteps: Induct on the dimension of the L-span of N ∩ R^S. If it is nonzero, choose s ∈ S with π_s(N ∩ R^S) ≠ 0; this is an ideal of R, finitely generated; lift generators v_1, …, v_n. Every element is an R-combination of the v_i plus an element of (N ∩ π_s^{-1}(0)) ∩ R^S, whose L-span has smaller dimension.
acceptance: R = ℤ, L = ℚ, S = ℕ: for N = ℚ·(1, 1/2, 1/3, …), N ∩ ℤ^ℕ = 0 (no nonzero rational multiple is integral in every coordinate); for N = ℚ·(1, 1, 1, …), N ∩ ℤ^ℕ = ℤ·(1, 1, 1, …).

sources.excerpt: Let R be a noetherian domain, let L be a field containing R, and let S be an arbitrary set. Let N be a finite dimensional L-subspace of the direct product LS . Then N ∩ RS is a finitely generated R-module.

nodes.title: Generic pushforwards are (σ,∇)-modules (Kedlaya, Theorem 7.3.3)
nodes.statement: Let A be an integral dagger algebra of MW-type and M a (σ,∇)-module over A⟨x⟩†. After replacing A by a suitable localisation, the modules R^if_*M, R^i_loc f_*M, R^if_!M and R^1_p f_*M are (σ,∇)-modules over A (finite locally free with connection ∇_h and Frobenius whose linearisation is an isomorphism).
hypotheses: Frobenius structure on M (used through the relative local monodromy theorem; Kedlaya, Remark 7.3.6).
proofSteps: Choose g ∈ A⟨x⟩† with M free over A[g^{-1}]; for g = Σ g_i x^i with i maximal among |g_i| maximal, g is invertible in R^int_B[1/p] for localisations B of A⟨g_i^{-1}⟩† (Lemma 2.5.13), so M ⊗ R_B is free; shrink B to satisfy the relative local monodromy theorem.
R^i_loc f_*M is finitely generated (RD.5/relative-local-cohomology-finitely-generated); by the exact sequence it suffices to treat R^1_p f_*M.

Over the completion L of Frac A, R^1f_*M_L and R^0_loc f_*M_L are finite dimensional (RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves applied to the curve A^1 over L, and RD.5/relative-local-cohomology-finitely-generated), so R^1f_!M_L is; R^1f_!M is the intersection of R^1f_!M_L with (M ⊗ R_A)/M inside a product of copies of L, hence finitely generated by RD.5/finitely-generated-intersection.

Each module N is finitely generated with a connection, hence locally free (RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra, locallyFree_of_connection); F is injective on N (RD.4/finite-flat-pullback-injective); the cokernel of σ^*N → N carries a connection so is locally free, of rank zero, hence zero; likewise the kernel; so σ^*N ≅ N.
acceptance: For M trivial no localisation is needed: R^0f_* = A, R^1f_* = 0, R^2f_! = A(−1).

sources.excerpt: Then after replacing A by a suitable localization, the modules Ri f∗ M, Rloc i f∗ M, Ri f! M, Rp1 f∗ M become (σ, ∇)-modules over A.
Note the essential use of the nonrelative case (Theorem 6.4.2).
Although our argument essentially uses the presence of the Frobenius structure, in order to invoke the p-adic local monodromy theorem, it is conceivable that this dependence could be lifted.

nodes.title: The Leray long exact sequence for the projection A⟨x⟩† → A
nodes.statement: Let A be a dagger algebra, M a (σ,∇)-module over A⟨x⟩†, and P, Q the kernel and cokernel of the vertical connection ∇_v: M → M ⊗ Ω^1_{A⟨x⟩†/A} (so P = R^0f_*M, Q = R^1f_*M, with their horizontal connections). Then there is a long exact sequence ⋯ → H^i(P) → H^i(M) → H^{i−1}(Q) → H^{i+1}(P) → ⋯ of de Rham cohomology groups.
hypotheses: No finiteness is needed for the existence of the sequence.
proofSteps: The de Rham complex of M is the total complex of the double complex E_0^{pq} = M ⊗_A Ω^p_{A/K} ⊗ Ω^q_{K⟨x⟩†/K} (q = 0, 1).

By flatness of Ω^p_{A/K} over A, E_1^{p0} = P ⊗ Ω^p_{A/K}, E_1^{p1} = Q ⊗ Ω^p_{A/K}, so E_2^{p0} = H^p(P) and E_2^{p1} = H^p(Q); d_2: E_2^{p1} → E_2^{p+2,0} and the sequence degenerates at E_3 since there are two rows.
A two-row spectral sequence gives the stated long exact sequence (Bott–Tu, Section 14).
acceptance: For M trivial over A = K⟨y⟩†: P = A, Q = 0, so H^i(A^2) = H^i(A^1).

sources.excerpt: Then there is a long exact sequence
The claim is a formal consequence of the Leray spectral sequence associated to the double complex

nodes.title: A six-term five lemma
nodes.statement: In a commutative diagram of abelian groups with exact rows 0 → A → B → C → D → E → F → 0 and 0 → A' → B' → C' → D' → E' → F' → 0 and vertical maps a, …, f, if c is injective, b and e are isomorphisms and d is surjective, then all six vertical maps are isomorphisms.
hypotheses: Exact rows.
proofSteps: Apply the five lemma first to c and d (the four lemma halves: mono and epi), then to a and f (Mathlib: CategoryTheory.Abelian.isIso_of_epi_of_isIso_of_isIso_of_mono and the four lemmas).
acceptance: If all six maps are identities the conclusion is trivial.

sources.excerpt: Also suppose that c is injective, b and e are isomorphisms, and d is surjective. Then all six vertical arrows are isomorphisms.
Apply the five lemma first to c and d, then to a and f .

nodes.title: Continuous maps of LF-spaces with complemented image or finite separated cokernel are strict
nodes.statement: Let f: V → W be a continuous map of LF-spaces. If im f is a topological direct summand of W then f is strict. If coker f is separated and finite dimensional then im f is closed and complemented, so f is strict.
hypotheses: LF-spaces in the sense of RD.5/strict-map.
proofSteps: If im f is a summand it is a quotient of W, hence LF (Crew 3.2), and the open mapping theorem for LF-spaces (Crew 3.4, Bourbaki EVT II.36) gives strictness (Crew, Proposition 3.5).
A closed subspace of finite codimension is a summand (Bourbaki EVT I.15 Prop. 3), giving Crew, Corollary 3.6.
acceptance: For the derivative on K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩†, the cokernel is K (separated), so d is strict.

sources.excerpt: If f : V → W is a continuous map of LF-spaces such that Im f is a direct summand of W, then f is strict.
If f : V → W is a continuous map of LF-spaces such that Coker f is separated and finite-dimensional, then f is strict.

nodes.title: Dagger localisation at a function of spectral norm one is strict
nodes.statement: Let A be an integral dagger algebra of MW-type and f ∈ A with |f|_{sup,Â} = 1. Then A → A⟨f^{-1}⟩† is strict (for the fringe topologies).
hypotheses: |f|_sup = 1; this replaces an incorrect claim of arXiv v5 (strictness with closed image for every f; see sourceIssues).
proofSteps: Pass to finite extensions of K and to covers by open affines freely. If the completion of X along X \ U is a fibration over X \ U (true locally if X \ U is smooth), there is a strict injection A → R_B^+ with f ↦ t, and R_B^+ → R_B is strict, giving the claim.

In general, stratify X \ U by successively removing smooth loci of components (after enlarging k so that components are generically smooth), embed each smooth stratum in a smooth divisor (passing to a cover so the complement is basic open) and cut out the strata from smallest to largest (Kedlaya, Proposition 8.4.1).
acceptance: A = K⟨x⟩†, f = x: A → K⟨x, x^{-1}⟩† is strict with closed image.

sources.excerpt: Let A be an integral dagger algebra of MW-type, and suppose f ∈ A satisfies |f |sup,Ab = 1. Then the map A → Ahf −1 i† is strict.

nodes.title: The connection of a relative (σ,∇)-module is strict after localisation
nodes.statement: (a) For A a reduced dagger algebra, d: R_A → Ω^1_{R_A/A} is strict with closed image. (b) For A an integral dagger algebra of MW-type and M a (σ,∇)-module over R_A relative to A, there is a localisation A' of A such that ∇: M ⊗ R_{A'} → M ⊗ Ω^1_{R_{A'}/A'} is strict with closed image, and remains so after further localisation.
hypotheses: (b) needs a localisation: arXiv v5 claimed it over A itself; see sourceIssues.
proofSteps: (a) follows from the explicit kernel and image of ∂/∂t (RD.5/relative-robba-ring, derivative_ker_range).

(b): with the extension R'' of RD.5/relative-local-monodromy-theorem, M ⊗ R'' is unipotent and ∇ on it is strict by (a) and a direct calculation in a strongly unipotent basis (as in RD.5/unipotent-local-cohomology-finitely-generated); the traces of Kedlaya's Remark 3.2.7 make M ⊗ R_{A'} a topological direct summand, and a direct summand of a strict map is strict (Crew 3.7).
acceptance: M = R_A trivial: ∇ = d is strict with closed image, no localisation needed.

sources.excerpt: For any reduced dagger algebra A, the map d : RA → Ω1RA /A is strict with closed image.
Then there exists a localization A′ of A such that ∇ : M ⊗RA RA′ → M ⊗RA Ω1RA′ /A′ is strict with closed image, and remains so after further localization.

nodes.title: The vertical connection over A⟨x⟩† is strict after localisation
nodes.statement: Let A be an integral dagger algebra of MW-type and M a (σ,∇)-module over A⟨x⟩†. There is a localisation A' of A such that ∇_v: M ⊗ A'⟨x⟩† → M ⊗ Ω^1_{A'⟨x⟩†/A'} is strict with closed image, and remains so after further localisation. In particular (Kedlaya, Lemma 7.5.1) the image of ∇_v is closed for the fringe topology after localising.
hypotheses: Localisation as provided by RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem and RD.5/strictness-of-relative-connection.
proofSteps: Localise so that the generic pushforward theorem and RD.5/strictness-of-relative-connection hold. The rows of the pushforward diagram are strict exact, so im ∇_v is homeomorphic to the image of M → M ⊗ Ω^1_{R_A/A}; since ∇_v^loc is strict with closed image it suffices that the image of ker ∇_v^loc in (M ⊗ R_A)/M is closed, which holds because it is finitely generated over A.
Then R^1f_*M is separated; localise further so it is finite free, lift generators to get a topological complement of im ∇_v, and apply RD.5/finite-cokernel-strict (Crew, Proposition 3.5).
acceptance: M trivial: ∇_v = d/dx on A⟨x⟩† is surjective, hence strict.

sources.excerpt: Then there exists a localization A′ of A such that ∇v : M ⊗Ahxi† A′ hxi† → M ⊗Ahxi† Ω1A′ hxi† /A′ is strict with closed image, and remains so after further localization.
Then there exists a localization A′ of A for which the image of ∇ on M ⊗Ahxi† A′ hxi† is closed for the fringe topology.
sources.match: The consequence used for base change.

nodes.title: Finite-dimensional separated cohomology forces strict differentials
nodes.statement: Let M be a (σ,∇)-module over a dagger algebra A such that every H^i(M) is finite dimensional and separated. Then every differential ∇_i: M ⊗ Ω^i_{A/K} → M ⊗ Ω^{i+1}_{A/K} is strict with closed image.
hypotheses: Finite dimensionality and separatedness of all H^i(M) are hypotheses (they are arranged in Kedlaya's proofs of Lemma 9.3.2 and Theorem 1.2.3 by shrinking and pushing forward).
proofSteps: The map M ⊗ Ω^i → ker ∇_{i+1} has cokernel H^{i+1}(M), finite dimensional and separated, so it is strict with closed image (RD.5/finite-cokernel-strict); ∇_i is its composite with the inclusion of the closed subspace ker ∇_{i+1}.
acceptance: For K⟨x⟩† with M trivial: H^0 = K, H^1 = 0, so d is strict with closed (whole) image.

sources.excerpt: Let M be a (σ, ∇)-module over a dagger algebra A, and suppose that the spaces H i (M) are finite-dimensional and separated for all i. Then all of the differentials ∇i : M ⊗A ΩiA/K → M ⊗A Ωi+1 A/K are strict with closed image.

nodes.title: The residue pairing between the overconvergent polydisc and its dual is perfect
nodes.statement: The pairing K⟨x_1, …, x_n⟩† ⊗_K S^{(n)}_r/Σ_i S^{(n),i'}_r → K sending a ⊗ b to the coefficient of t_1⋯t_n in ab (t_i = x_i^{-1}) is perfect: each space is, topologically, the strong dual of the other. The second space is Fréchet–Montel (homeomorphic to t_1⋯t_n R^{{t_1..t_n},+}_K).
hypotheses: Topologies: fringe (LF) topology on K⟨x⟩†, Fréchet topology on the quotient.
proofSteps: Montel property of R^{{t},+}_K as in Crew, Corollary 5.3; the one-variable duality is Crew, Proposition 5.5 (local duality between A^† and the plus part); the n-variable case is proved the same way (Kedlaya, Lemma 8.5.1). Crew's proofs of 5.3–5.5 were not read in detail; recorded as coverage remaining.
acceptance: n = 1: x^m pairs with t^{m+1} to 1 and with other monomials to 0.

sources.excerpt: taking a ⊗ b to the coefficient of t1 · · · tn in ab is perfect: that is, the induced map of each space to the strong dual of the other is an isomorphism of topological vector spaces.

nodes.title: Poincaré duality on affine space via the residue pairing
nodes.statement: Let E ∈ F-Isoc†(A^n/K) and assume H^i_rig(A^n, E^∨) is finite dimensional and separated for each i. Then the Poincaré pairing H^{n+i}_{c,rig}(A^n, E) ⊗_K H^{n−i}_rig(A^n, E^∨) → K, induced on cochains by pairing M ⊗ Ω^i_{S^{(n)}} with M^∨ ⊗ Ω^{n−i}_{K⟨x⟩†} and taking the residue (coefficient of dt_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dt_n/(t_1⋯t_n)), is nondegenerate: each factor injects into the dual of the other.
hypotheses: Finite dimensionality and separatedness of H^i_rig(A^n, E^∨) (added hypothesis in arXiv v6; see sourceIssues).
proofSteps: Chain level: C^i = (M ⊗ Ω^i_{S^{(n)}})/Σ_j(M ⊗ Ω^i_{S^{(n),j'}}) computes H^{n+i}_{c,rig} (RD.4/compact-support-cohomology-of-affine-space-with-coefficients) and D^{n−i} = M^∨ ⊗ Ω^{n−i}_{K⟨x⟩†} computes H^{n−i}_rig; [v, ∇w] = −[∇v, w] by Leibniz; by RD.5/residue-pairing-perfect each of C^i, D^{n−i} is the strong dual of the other.
By RD.5/strictness-from-finite-cohomology the differentials of D^• are strict; by RD.5/frechet-montel-transpose-strict (D^i Fréchet–Montel) so are those of C^•.
Right nondegeneracy: for v ∉ im(D^{n−i−1}), extend the functional killing the closed image and sending v to 1 by RD.5/nonarchimedean-hahn-banach; it is a cocycle w ∈ C^i pairing nontrivially with v.
Left nondegeneracy: for w pairing to zero with cocycles, the induced functional on im(D^{n−i} → D^{n−i+1}) is continuous by strictness, extends by Hahn–Banach, and gives x with w + ∇x = 0.
acceptance: n = 1, E = O: H^2_{c,rig}(A^1) = K·[dt/t] pairs with H^0_rig(A^1) = K·1 to 1.

sources.excerpt: Let E be an overconvergent F -isocrystal on An , and assume that Hrig (An , E ∨) is finite dimensional and separated for each i.
is nondegenerate (i.e., each factor injects into the dual of the other).

nodes.title: Generic pushforwards commute with flat base change
nodes.statement: Let A → B be a flat morphism of integral dagger algebras of MW-type, f: A → A⟨x⟩† and g: B → B⟨x⟩† the inclusions, M a (σ,∇)-module over A⟨x⟩† for which the conclusion of RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem holds without further localisation, and M_B = M ⊗ B⟨x⟩†. Then the base change maps (R^if_*M) ⊗_A B → R^ig_*M_B, (R^i_loc f_*M) ⊗_A B → R^i_loc g_*M_B, (R^if_!M) ⊗_A B → R^ig_!M_B and (R^1_p f_*M) ⊗_A B → R^1_p g_*M_B are isomorphisms; in particular the theorem holds for M_B without localisation. The same holds with B the completion of Frac A, so the pushforwards have the generic ranks.
hypotheses: B flat over A.
proofSteps: R^i_loc: RD.5/relative-local-cohomology-base-change. As in RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem, R^1_p g_*M_B is finitely generated, so all pushforwards for M_B are finitely generated.
Injectivity of the maps on R^0f_* and R^1f_!: they are kernels of injective maps of complexes.

Surjectivity on R^1f_*: may be checked after localising B (both sides are ∇-modules), so assume the image N_2 of ∇ on M_B is closed (RD.5/strictness-of-vertical-connection, Lemma 7.5.1); N_1 = M ⊗ Ω^1 ⊗ B is dense, and N_1 + N_2 is closed (finitely generated image in the noetherian quotient) and dense, hence everything.
Conclude with RD.5/six-term-isomorphism-lemma applied to the two exact sequences (7.3.2.2).
acceptance: M trivial and B arbitrary flat: all base change maps are the identity maps of B, 0, B, B(−1).

sources.excerpt: Suppose that the conclusion of Theorem 7.3.3 holds for M without further localization. Then the canonical base change morphisms
This implies that the pushforwards all have the “correct” ranks, namely the ranks over the generic fibre.

nodes.title: Relative Poincaré duality for generic pushforwards
nodes.statement: Let A be an integral dagger algebra of MW-type, f: A → A⟨x⟩† the inclusion, and M a (σ,∇)-module over A⟨x⟩† such that M and M^∨ satisfy the conclusion of RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem without further localisation. Then there are canonical perfect pairings R^0f_*M ⊗_A R^2f_!M^∨ → A, R^i_loc f_*M ⊗_A R^{1−i}_loc f_*M^∨ → A, R^1f_!M ⊗_A R^1f_*M^∨ → A and R^1_p f_*M ⊗_A R^1_p f_*M^∨ → A, induced by M ⊗ M^∨ → A⟨x⟩† and the residue Ω^1_{R_A/A} → A (coefficient of dt/t).
hypotheses: Kedlaya records that this result is not used in the proofs of the main theorems; it controls the shape of pushforwards (used in the Weil II paper).
proofSteps: By flat base change to the completion L of Frac A (RD.5/pushforward-flat-base-change, Remark 7.5.4), duality on A^1_L (RD.5/poincare-duality-on-affine-space, whose finiteness and separatedness hypotheses hold as in Crew's proof of Theorem 9.5) and finite dimensionality, R^0f_*M → (R^2f_!M^∨)^∨ becomes an isomorphism over L.

Its kernel and cokernel are finitely generated A-modules with connection, hence locally free (RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra, locallyFree_of_connection) of rank zero, so zero; the same for R^1f_*M → (R^1f_!M^∨)^∨; the other two follow by the five lemma.
acceptance: M trivial: R^0f_* = A pairs with R^2f_! ≅ A (class of dt/t) to A.

sources.excerpt: Suppose M and M ∨ satisfy the conclusion of Theorem 7.3.3 without further localization. Then there are canonical perfect pairings
Although we will not use this fact hereafter, it provides a useful tool for controlling the shape of the pushforwards; see for instance [Ke6].

nodes.title: Generic pushforwards commute with external products
nodes.statement: Let A, B be integral dagger algebras of MW-type, M a (σ,∇)-module over A⟨x⟩† satisfying the conclusion of RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem without localisation, N a (σ,∇)-module over B, and g: A ⊗̂ B → (A ⊗̂ B)⟨x⟩† the inclusion. With the external product M ⊠ N = M ⊗_A (A ⊗̂ B) ⊗_B N, the natural maps (R^if_*M) ⊠_{A,B} N → R^ig_*(M ⊠_{A⟨x⟩†,B} N) are isomorphisms (and likewise for R_loc, R f_! and R^1_p), and the conclusion of the generic pushforward theorem holds for M ⊠ N without localisation.
hypotheses: A ⊗̂ B is flat over A (reductions are smooth; Kedlaya, Lemma 2.2.3 and Remark 2.3.9 with the reducedness hypothesis of the errata).
proofSteps: Lemma 7.6.1: for N a (σ,∇)-module over A (flat), (R^if_*M) ⊗_A N ≅ R^if_*(M ⊗_A N) since pushforwards are kernels and cokernels of A-linear maps.
Apply RD.5/pushforward-flat-base-change to A → A ⊗̂ B, then Lemma 7.6.1 over A ⊗̂ B with the pullback of N.
acceptance: M = A⟨x⟩†, N = B trivial: both sides are (A ⊗̂ B) in degree 0 for R^0f_*.

sources.excerpt: Suppose that the conclusion of Theorem 7.3.3 holds for M without further localization. Then the natural maps
Since N is flat over A, these computations commute with tensoring with N .

nodes.title: Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology on smooth varieties, and with supports
nodes.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K). (a) If X is smooth over k, H^i_rig(X/K, E) is finite dimensional for all i. (b) If X is smooth over k and Z ⊂ X is a closed immersion of a geometrically reduced k-scheme of finite type, H^i_{Z,rig}(X/K, E) is finite dimensional for all i.
hypotheses: Frobenius structure on E; smooth X.
proofSteps: Induction on n: (a)_n for dim X ≤ n, (b)_n for dim Z ≤ n; (a)_0 is trivial and (b)_{−1} vacuous.

(b)_{n−1} + (a)_n ⇒ (b)_n: if Z ⊂ X satisfies Kedlaya's Hypothesis 4.4.1, the Gysin isomorphism (RD.4/gysin-isomorphism) and (a)_n give finiteness; in general remove a closed T of dimension ≤ n − 1 so that Z \ T ⊂ X \ T satisfies it and use RD.4/localisation-sequence (b) with (b)_{n−1}.

(a)_{n−1} + (b)_{n−1} ⇒ (a)_n: one may (i) enlarge K (RD.4/finite-flat-pullback-injective or RD.4/finite-flat-base-change), (ii) shrink X to a dense open (localisation sequence and (b)_{n−1}), (iii) push forward along finite étale maps (RD.4/finite-etale-pushforward-cohomology). By RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space reduce to (A^n, f_*j^*E); write A^n = A^1 × A^{n−1}; by RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem the kernel and cokernel of ∇_v are overconvergent F-isocrystals on an open W ⊆ A^{n−1}, finite by (a)_{n−1}; conclude by RD.5/leray-long-exact-sequence.
acceptance: X = G_m^n: all H^i finite, of dimension binom(n, i).

sources.excerpt: Let E be an overconvergent F -isocrystal on a smooth scheme X over a field k of characteristic p > 0. Then the rigid cohomology spaces

is finite dimensional for any closed immersion Z ֒→ X of a geometrically reduced scheme Z of finite type over k of dimension at most n into a scheme X smooth over k, and for any overconvergent F -isocrystal E on X.
This result allows us to “go down” to simpler spaces (namely affine space).

nodes.title: Proper hypercoverings by smooth schemes over purely inseparable extensions
nodes.statement: For X separated of finite type over k there are a proper hypercovering f_•: Y_• → X over Spec k and finite purely inseparable extensions k ⊆ k_0 ⊆ k_1 ⊆ ⋯ such that each Y_n is smooth over k_n; for finite extensions K_n of K with residue fields k_n, the nilpotent immersion Y_n → Y_n ×_k k_n induces H^i_rig(Y_n ×_k k_n/K_n, f_n^*E) ≅ H^i_rig(Y_n/K_n, f_n^*E).
hypotheses: The alterations are de Jong's (Theorem 4.1), requested from AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5 together with the simplicial construction.
proofSteps: Construct Y_• inductively by the coskeleton method: at each stage alter (de Jong, Theorem 4.1, from AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5) the relevant coskeleton term to a scheme smooth over a finite purely inseparable extension of k (Tsuzuki, Invent. Math. 151, Section 4, as cited by Kedlaya).
Rigid cohomology does not see nilpotents (RD.4/rigid-cohomology, API rigidCohomology_of_reduced), giving the comparison for Y_n ×_k k_n.
acceptance: X smooth: Y_• the constant hypercovering X.

sources.excerpt: The alterations theorem of de Jong [dJ1, Theorem 4.1] and the construction of [T5, Section 4] produce a proper hypercovering f. : Y. → X over Spec k and an increasing sequence k0 ⊆ k1 ⊆ · · · of finite purely inseparable extensions of k, such that Yn is smooth over kn for each n.

hypotheses: Proper hypercovering; the étale-hypercovering version is proved by Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki (Theorem 11.7.1).
proofSteps: Tsuzuki (Invent. Math. 151 (2003), Theorem 4.5.1 and Corollary 2.2.3) proves descent for proper hypercoverings; the source is not public and was not read: recorded as a gap.

The étale and étale-proper cases (Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Theorem 11.1.1, Theorem 11.7.1) follow from universally de Rham descendable hypercoverings (their Sections 7–9), read at the level of statements.

nodes.title: Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.1)
nodes.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0, X a separated k-scheme of finite type and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K). Then H^i_rig(X/K, E) is a finite-dimensional K-vector space for every i. Moreover (Remark 9.2.1) H^i_{Z,rig}(X/K, E) is finite dimensional for every closed Z ⊆ X, and finite base change holds.
hypotheses: Frobenius structure on E is essential (RD.5/no-finiteness-without-frobenius).
proofSteps: Finite flat base change (RD.4/finite-flat-base-change): H^i_rig(X/K, E) ⊗ K' ≅ H^i_rig(X_{k'}/K', E).

Take the proper hypercovering Y_• → X of RD.5/smooth-proper-hypercovering; each H^r_rig(Y_q/K_q, f_q^*E) is finite dimensional by RD.5/finiteness-for-smooth-varieties, hence finite over K after base change; the spectral sequence of RD.5/cohomological-descent-for-proper-hypercoverings has finite-dimensional E_1-terms (only finitely many contribute in each total degree), so the abutment is finite dimensional.
Supports: excision (RD.4/localisation-sequence).

nodes.title: Frobenius is bijective on rigid cohomology
nodes.statement: Assume σ_K is an automorphism of K (e.g. k perfect). For E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K), the linearisation σ_K^*H^i_rig(X/K, E) → H^i_rig(X/K, E) of the Frobenius is an isomorphism; in particular for k = F_q, σ_K = id, the Frobenius is a K-linear automorphism, and each H^i_rig(X/K, E) (with Φ) is an F-isocrystal over k. The same holds for H^i_{c,rig} once it is known to be finite dimensional.
hypotheses: σ_K automorphism; finite dimensionality (RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology, RD.5/finiteness-of-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology).
proofSteps: Injectivity of Φ on smooth affines: RD.4/finite-flat-pullback-injective; in general by the Čech/hypercovering spectral sequences built from smooth affines, compatible with Φ (Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Section 12.2, who note that in the relative setting the linearised Frobenius on higher direct images need not be an isomorphism).
An injective semilinear map of a finite-dimensional space along an automorphism σ_K has injective linearisation between spaces of the same dimension, hence bijective.

For compact supports: Poincaré duality (RD.5/poincare-duality) identifies Φ with the inverse transpose of Φ on H^{2d−i}_rig(E^∨) multiplied by q^d on smooth X; excision reduces the general case to the smooth one.
acceptance: H^1_rig(G_m/K): Φ = q, invertible in K.

proofSteps: Induction on n; base change to make X geometrically reduced (RD.4/finite-flat-base-change); by excision (RD.4/excision-sequence) replace X by an open dense U with a finite étale f: U → A^n (RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space, applied to each component of top dimension; lower-dimensional pieces are covered by induction).

nodes.title: The trace map on top-degree compact-support cohomology
nodes.statement: For X separated of finite type over k of pure dimension n there is a canonical Frobenius-equivariant trace Tr_X: H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X/K)(n) → H^0_{c,rig}(Spec k/K) = K, i.e. Tr_X: H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X/K) → K(−n). For a smooth affine curve it is Crew's residue sum; for A^n it sends the class of dt_1/t_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dt_n/t_n to 1 (up to the sign convention fixed here).
hypotheses: Pure dimension n; the construction uses H^d_{c,rig} = 0 for d > 2n (RD.5/compact-support-vanishing-above-twice-dimension).
proofSteps: Berthelot (Dualité de Poincaré, 1.2, not public) constructs the trace by reduction to coherent cohomology; Kedlaya uses it as given. Construction used here: for X smooth affine, lift and use the residue of the compact-support complex (Crew (8.1.7) for curves; Kedlaya, Section 8.5 for A^n); glue by excision, which is legitimate because H^{2n}_{c,rig} of the complement of an open dense subset vanishes (RD.5/compact-support-vanishing-above-twice-dimension) so H^{2n}_{c,rig}(U) → H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X) is surjective; independence of choices from finite étale pushforward compatibility (trace of f_*O → O).

Frobenius: σ^*(dt/t) = q·dt/t on each factor, and the residue of σ^*ω equals q^n times σ_K of the residue of ω, so Tr is equivariant as a map H^{2n}_c → K(−n). The full construction in Berthelot's note is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: X = A^1: Tr[dt/t] = 1 and Φ acts by q on H^2_{c,rig}(A^1).

nodes.title: Top-degree compact-support cohomology of a geometrically irreducible variety
nodes.statement: Let X be a separated, geometrically irreducible k-scheme of finite type of dimension n. Then H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X/K) is one-dimensional, and as an F-space H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X/K) ≅ K(−n); the trace is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Geometric irreducibility (otherwise the dimension is the number of geometric irreducible components of dimension n).
proofSteps: Reduce to X geometrically reduced; by excision and RD.5/compact-support-vanishing-above-twice-dimension replace X by a dense open U with finite étale f: U → A^n; arrange by successive shrinking and pushforward (A^n = A^1 × A^{n−1}, RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem, RD.5/strictness-of-vertical-connection, RD.5/strictness-from-finite-cohomology) that the H^i_rig(A^n, f_*O) are finite dimensional and separated.

Poincaré duality on A^n (RD.5/poincare-duality-on-affine-space) gives H^{2n}_{c,rig}(A^n, f_*O) ≅ H^0_rig(A^n, f_*O^∨)^∨ ≅ H^0_rig(U)^∨ (self-duality of f_*O via the trace, RD.3/finite-etale-pushforward-of-isocrystals) = K (U geometrically connected; Monsky–Washnitzer, Theorem 7.1).

nodes.title: The Poincaré pairing between rigid cohomology and compact-support cohomology
nodes.statement: For X separated of finite type over k of pure dimension d and F, G ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) there is a natural cup product H^j_rig(X/K, F) ⊗_K H^l_{c,rig}(X/K, G) → H^{j+l}_{c,rig}(X/K, F ⊗ G), Frobenius-equivariant. With G = F^∨, the evaluation F ⊗ F^∨ → O and the trace (RD.5/trace-map) it gives the Poincaré pairing ⟨ , ⟩: H^i_rig(X/K, F) ⊗ H^{2d−i}_{c,rig}(X/K, F^∨) → H^{2d}_{c,rig}(X/K) → K(−d); more generally H^i_{Z,rig}(X/K, F) ⊗ H^{2d−i}_{c,rig}(Z/K, F^∨) → K(−d) for Z ⊆ X closed.
hypotheses: The natural isomorphism Hom(j†F, G) ≅ Γ(Hom_K(F, G)) (Berthelot, Dualité, Lemme 2.1, not public) is used to construct the cup product; recorded as a gap.
proofSteps: On a frame (X, Y, P) with strict neighbourhood V: the tensor product of complexes j†(F ⊗ Ω^•) ⊗ RΓ_{]X[}(G ⊗ Ω^•) → RΓ_{]X[}(F ⊗ G ⊗ Ω^•) (wedge product of forms), using Hom(j†F, G) ≅ Γ(Hom_K(F, G)) to see that sections with support in ]X[ pair with overconvergent germs (Kedlaya, Section 8.2).

On A^n the pairing is explicit at the chain level: v ∈ M ⊗ Ω^i_{S^{(n)}}, w ∈ M^∨ ⊗ Ω^{n−i}_{K⟨x⟩†}, pair and take the residue (RD.5/poincare-duality-on-affine-space); on curves it is Crew's pairing (8.1.8).
Frobenius-equivariance: ⟨Φa, Φb⟩ = Φ⟨a, b⟩ in H^{2d}_c = K(−d), i.e. q^d·σ_K⟨a, b⟩ after the trace (Kedlaya, Weil II, Section 2.1).

nodes.title: Compatibility of the Poincaré pairing with the two excision sequences
nodes.statement: For X smooth of pure dimension d, Z ⊆ X closed and U = X \ Z, the compact-support excision sequence of E^∨ in degrees 2d − i and the dual of the localisation sequence of E in degree i form a commutative ladder: ⋯ → H^{2d−i}_{c,rig}(Z, E^∨) → H^{2d−i}_{c,rig}(X, E^∨) → H^{2d−i}_{c,rig}(U, E^∨) → ⋯ maps to ⋯ → H^i_{Z,rig}(X, E)^∨ → H^i_rig(X, E)^∨ → H^i_rig(U, E)^∨ → ⋯ through the Poincaré pairings.
hypotheses: X smooth; the dual spaces are of finite-dimensional spaces by RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology.
proofSteps: Functoriality of the cup product with respect to the distinguished triangles of RD.4/excision-sequence and RD.4/localisation-sequence (the pairing is induced by a pairing of complexes compatible with the maps in both triangles; Tsuzuki, Hiroshima Math. J. 29, Section 6.2, not public: recorded as a gap).

nodes.title: Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth over k of pure dimension d, E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K), and Z ⊆ X closed. Then the Poincaré pairing H^i_{Z,rig}(X/K, E) ⊗_K H^{2d−i}_{c,rig}(Z/K, E^∨) → K(−d) is perfect (between finite-dimensional spaces) and Frobenius-equivariant: for k = F_q and the linear q-power Frobenius Φ, ⟨Φa, Φb⟩ = q^d⟨a, b⟩. It is natural for restriction to open subschemes and compatible with the excision sequences (RD.5/excision-duality-compatibility). For Z = X: H^i_rig(X/K, E) ≅ H^{2d−i}_{c,rig}(X/K, E^∨)^∨(−d) as F-spaces; in particular, for k = F_q, if α is an eigenvalue of Φ on H^i_rig(X/K, E) then q^d/α is an eigenvalue on H^{2d−i}_{c,rig}(X/K, E^∨).
hypotheses: X smooth of pure dimension d; E an overconvergent F-isocrystal and E^∨ its dual (Frobenius the inverse transpose).
proofSteps: Simultaneous induction on n: (a)_n perfectness for Z = X, dim X ≤ n; (b)_n for dim Z ≤ n. (a)_0 is linear algebra.
(b)_{n−1} + (a)_n ⇒ (b)_n: as in RD.5/finiteness-for-smooth-varieties, using RD.5/excision-duality-compatibility and the five lemma (and the Gysin isomorphism in the liftable case).

(b)_{n−1} ⇒ (a)_n: choose U ⊆ X open dense with f: U → A^n finite étale (RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space); by the ladder and (b)_{n−1} for Z = X \ U, reduce to U, then to (A^n, f_*E) (RD.4/finite-etale-pushforward-cohomology); arrange f so that the H^i_rig(A^n, f_*E) are finite dimensional and separated (successive pushforward and shrinking, as in RD.5/top-compact-support-cohomology); RD.5/poincare-duality-on-affine-space gives nondegeneracy, hence H^{2n−i}_{c,rig}(A^n, f_*E^∨) is finite dimensional and the pairing perfect.
Frobenius-equivariance and the twist: RD.5/poincare-pairing (poincarePairing_frobenius) with RD.5/trace-map.
acceptance: Smooth nonproper curve (RD.5/affine-curve-duality-acceptance): for U = P^1 minus N ≥ 1 rational points, H^0(U) = K pairs with H^2_c(U) = K(−1), and H^1(U) = K(−1)^{N−1} with H^1_c(U) = K^{N−1}.

nodes.title: The Künneth morphisms
nodes.statement: For separated k-schemes of finite type X_1, X_2, X = X_1 ×_k X_2 with projections pr_i and E_i ∈ F-Isoc†(X_i/K), E = pr_1^*E_1 ⊗ pr_2^*E_2 = E_1 ⊠ E_2, there are natural Frobenius-compatible K-linear maps ⊕_{j+l=i} H^j_{c,rig}(X_1, E_1) ⊗_K H^l_{c,rig}(X_2, E_2) → H^i_{c,rig}(X, E) (1.2.4.1) and, for Z_i ⊆ X_i closed, ⊕_{j+l=i} H^j_{Z_1,rig}(X_1, E_1) ⊗_K H^l_{Z_2,rig}(X_2, E_2) → H^i_{Z_1 ×_k Z_2,rig}(X, E) (1.2.4.2); in particular H^j_rig(X_1, E_1) ⊗ H^l_rig(X_2, E_2) → H^{j+l}_rig(X, E). They are induced by the external product of complexes (on product frames, the external product of the overconvergent de Rham complexes, and of the two-term complexes RΓ_{]X_i[}).
hypotheses: Construction and functoriality are Tsuzuki's (Hiroshima Math. J. 29, Section 6.3, not public); recorded as a gap. The explicit Monsky–Washnitzer version on smooth affines is Kedlaya's external product M ⊠ N (Section 7.6).

nodes.title: Finite dimensionality fails for overconvergent isocrystals without Frobenius structure
nodes.statement: Let a ∈ ℤ_p be a p-adic Liouville number that is not an integer: there are r < 1 and infinitely many n ∈ ℤ with |a − n| < r^{|n|}. On G_m over F_p (K = ℚ_p), the rank-one overconvergent isocrystal K_a = (K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩†, ∇ = d + a·dx/x) has infinite-dimensional H^1_rig(G_m/K, K_a) = coker(x d/dx + a). K_a has no Frobenius structure. Hence the finiteness theorems RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology and RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves do not extend to overconvergent isocrystals without Frobenius. Such a exist, for example a = Σ_{m ≥ 1} p^{e_m} with e_1 = 1, e_{m+1} = p^{e_m}.
hypotheses: a ∈ ℤ_p ensures that the Taylor series (x'/x)^{−a} = Σ binom(−a, j)((x' − x)/x)^j converges on |x' − x| < |x|, so K_a is an overconvergent isocrystal (by the same convergence as in Berthelot's Dwork example (4.2.3)).
proofSteps: On coefficients (Σ c_m x^m) the operator x d/dx + a acts by c_m ↦ (m + a)c_m, injective since a ∉ ℤ; a series Σ b_m x^m is in the image iff Σ b_m/(m + a) x^m is overconvergent.

Choose infinitely many integers n_k with |a − n_k| < r^{|n_k|} and put m_k = −n_k, so |m_k + a| < r^{|m_k|}; partition {m_k} into infinitely many infinite subsets S_1, S_2, …; for r < s < 1 put g_j = Σ_{m ∈ S_j} s^{|m|} x^m, an element of K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† (coefficients decay like s^{|m|}).

A nonzero finite combination Σ λ_j g_j has preimage coefficients λ_j s^{|m|}/(m + a) of absolute value ≥ |λ_j|(s/r)^{|m|} → ∞ along S_j, so it is not overconvergent: the classes of the g_j are linearly independent in H^1, which is infinite dimensional.

No Frobenius structure: if K_a carried a Frobenius structure it would be an overconvergent F-isocrystal on G_m, and RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves would make H^1 finite dimensional, contradicting the previous step. (For Frobenius structures of the form e ↦ c·x^m·e this is visible directly: (q − 1)a ∈ ℤ would be needed, RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra, test kummer_frobenius_iff.)
Local form: Crew, Proposition 6.10: the connection x d/dx − a on the Robba ring is strict iff a is not p-adic Liouville; the global computation above is its analogue on G_m.

Existence: for a = Σ p^{e_m}, n_m = Σ_{j ≤ m} p^{e_j} ≤ 2p^{e_m} and v_p(a − n_m) = e_{m+1} = p^{e_m} ≥ n_m/2, so |a − n_m| < (p^{−1/4})^{n_m}; a ∉ ℤ because its base-p digits are 0 or 1, infinitely many 1s, not eventually constant.
acceptance: Checked numerically (PARI/GP): for p = 3, n_1 = 3 with v_3(a − 3) = 3 > 3/4, n_2 = 30 with v_3(a − 30) = 27 > 30/4.

nodes.title: The linear q-power Frobenius on rigid cohomology over F_q
nodes.statement: Let q = p^a, k = F_q and let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with residue field F_q (so K is a finite extension of K_0 = W(F_q)[1/p]). Take the Frobenius lift σ_K = id_K, which is allowed because the q-power map is the identity on F_q. For a separated scheme X of finite type over F_q and an overconvergent F-isocrystal E on X relative to (K, σ_K) with its q-power Frobenius structure F : σ*E ≅ E (RD.3), the Frobenius on H^i_rig(X/K, E) and on H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) (RD.4) is K-linear; this K-linear endomorphism is denoted F and called the linear q-Frobenius. If K = K_0 and E carries a p-power Frobenius structure Φ relative to the Witt-vector Frobenius σ_0 of K_0, its q-power Frobenius structure is the a-fold composite Φ ∘ σ_0^*Φ ∘ ⋯ ∘ (σ_0^{a−1})^*Φ, which is σ_0^a = id-semilinear, and the linear q-Frobenius on cohomology is the a-th iterate of the σ_0-semilinear p-Frobenius. Throughout RD.6 and RD.7, 'Frobenius' means this linear q-Frobenius F.
hypotheses: k = F_q with q = p^a; K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with residue field F_q; σ_K = id_K.
E an overconvergent F-isocrystal on a separated finite-type F_q-scheme X (RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal).
proofSteps: Frobenius on cohomology is supplied by RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology: it is σ_K-semilinear and independent of the choice of Frobenius lift on frames or dagger algebras.
With σ_K = id_K it is K-linear (Kedlaya, Weil II §5 opening).

For a p-power structure Φ over K_0: σ_0 has order a on K_0 = W(F_q)[1/p] (it is induced by the Witt vector Frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius), so the a-fold composite of Φ with its σ_0-twists is K_0-linear, and functoriality of cohomology in the Frobenius structure gives F = Φ_*^a on cohomology.
acceptance: On H^0_rig(Spec F_q/K) = K the linear q-Frobenius is the identity; on H^2_rig(P^1/K) it is multiplication by q (see RD.6/projective-line-frobenius-eigenvalues).
For a = 2 the p-power Frobenius of the unit object on Spec F_{p^2} is the Galois conjugation of K_0 = Q_{p^2}, which is not K_0-linear, while its square is the identity.

nodes.title: Fibres and the linear Frobenius at a closed point
nodes.statement: Let X be a separated F_q-scheme of finite type, E an overconvergent F-isocrystal on X relative to (K, σ_K = id), and x a closed point of X of degree d = [κ(x) : F_q]. Let K_x be the unramified extension of K of degree d with residue field κ(x), and σ_x ∈ Gal(K_x/K) the lift of the q-power map. The fibre E_x := i_x^*E is (by RD.3, over Spec κ(x)) a finite-dimensional K_x-vector space with a σ_x-semilinear bijection F; the Frobenius at x is the K_x-linear map F_x := F^d. Its reversed characteristic polynomial P_x(t) := det_{K_x}(1 − t F_x | E_x) has coefficients in K and depends only on (E, x). Moreover, regarding E_x as a K-vector space of dimension d·rank(E) on which F is K-linear, det_K(1 − tF | E_x) = P_x(t^d).
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over F_q; E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) with σ_K = id.
x a closed point of degree d.
proofSteps: Pullback along i_x : Spec κ(x) → X and the description of F-Isoc†(Spec κ(x)/K) as finite-dimensional K_x-spaces with a bijective σ_x-semilinear map (RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal).
F^d is σ_x^d = id-semilinear, hence K_x-linear.
Coefficients in K: conjugating F^d by the σ_x-semilinear bijection F gives F·F^d·F^{−1} = F^d, so the characteristic polynomial of F_x is fixed by σ_x, which generates Gal(K_x/K).

Restriction of scalars: over K^alg, E_x ⊗_K K^alg splits into d blocks permuted cyclically by F, and the d-th power of the cyclic block matrix is conjugate on each block to F_x; hence det_K(1 − tF | E_x) = det_{K_x}(1 − t^d F_x | E_x) (standard block-cyclic determinant, computed with mathlib:LinearMap.charpoly and mathlib:Matrix.charpolyRev).
acceptance: For E = O_X, F_x = 1 and P_x(t) = 1 − t at every closed point.
For x of degree 2 and E = O_X: det_K(1 − tF | K_x) = 1 − t^2, since F is the nontrivial automorphism of K_x with eigenvalues ±1.

nodes.title: Tate twists of overconvergent F-isocrystals
nodes.statement: For an overconvergent F-isocrystal E on X/F_q (σ_K = id) and n ∈ Z, the Tate twist E(n) is E with Frobenius structure q^{−n}F; for a module M with Frobenius F, M(−i) is M with q^i F (Kedlaya's convention). Thus K(−1) is the unit object with F = q, of weight 2. The underlying de Rham data of E(n) and E agree, so H^i_rig(X/K, E(n)) = H^i_rig(X/K, E)(n) and H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E(n)) = H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)(n) as spaces with linear Frobenius.
hypotheses: X separated finite type over F_q; E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K); n ∈ Z.
proofSteps: Multiplying F by the central scalar q^{−n} ∈ K^× preserves horizontality (q^{−n} is a constant) and bijectivity, so E(n) is again an overconvergent F-isocrystal (RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal).
Cohomology is computed from the underlying module with connection; the Frobenius on cohomology is induced by F (RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology), so it is multiplied by q^{−n}.

nodes.title: The L-function of an overconvergent F-isocrystal
nodes.statement: Let X be a separated scheme of finite type over F_q and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) (σ_K = id). The L-function of E is L(X, E, t) := ∏_{x ∈ |X|} det_{K_x}(1 − t^{deg x} F_x | E_x)^{−1} ∈ 1 + tK[[t]], the product running over closed points; it converges t-adically because X has finitely many closed points of each degree. Equivalently L(X, E, t) = ∏_x det_K(1 − tF | E_x)^{−1}, and t·L'/L = Σ_{r ≥ 1} S_r(X, E) t^r where S_r(X, E) := Σ_{x : deg x | r} deg(x)·Tr(F_x^{r/deg x} | E_x), i.e. L = exp(Σ_r S_r t^r / r).
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over F_q; E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K); K of characteristic 0.
proofSteps: Finiteness of the set of closed points of each degree and the relation #X(F_{q^r}) = Σ_{m | r} m·a_m are supplied by WeilConjectures:WC.1.
Each factor lies in 1 + t^{deg x}K[t] by RD.6/frobenius-at-closed-point, so the product converges in K[[t]].

The identity det(1 − tA)^{−1} = exp(Σ_r Tr(A^r) t^r / r) for an endomorphism A of a finite-dimensional space over a field of characteristic 0 (requested from WeilConjectures:WC.1, 'determinant formula') gives the logarithmic-derivative form.
acceptance: For X = Spec F_q and E given by (K, α): L = (1 − αt)^{−1}.
For E = O_X, L(X, O_X, t) = Z(X, t) = exp(Σ_r #X(F_{q^r}) t^r / r).

nodes.title: Dwork operators
nodes.statement: Let A be a dagger algebra over K (a quotient of W_n = K⟨x_1, …, x_n⟩†) with a Frobenius lift σ (RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra) acting as the identity on K, and let M be a finitely generated A-module. A Dwork operator on M with respect to σ is an additive map θ : M → M such that θ(σ(a)·v) = a·θ(v) for all a ∈ A and v ∈ M; equivalently, an A-linear map σ_*M → M, where σ_* is restriction of scalars along σ. Every Dwork operator is K-linear.
hypotheses: A a dagger algebra over K with Frobenius lift σ, σ|_K = id_K.
M a finitely generated A-module.
proofSteps: The equivalence with Hom_A(σ_*M, M) is the definition of restriction of scalars.
K-linearity: for c ∈ K, σ(c) = c, so θ(cv) = cθ(v).
acceptance: On A = K⟨x⟩† with σ(x) = x^q, the map Σ c_n x^n ↦ Σ c_{qn} x^n is a Dwork operator.
