nodes.title: Dwork operators are nuclear
nodes.statement: Let A be a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type over K with Frobenius lift σ, and M a finitely generated A-module. Every Dwork operator θ on M is a nuclear K-linear endomorphism of M (for its fringe topology); its trace Tr(θ) and Fredholm determinant det(1 − tθ) (entire in t) are defined, Tr is additive in θ, and Tr(θ ∘ g) = Tr(g ∘ θ) for every continuous K-linear g : M → M (in particular for multiplication by a ∈ A).
hypotheses: A of MW-type over K (special fibre smooth, integral subring as in Kedlaya §2.3); σ a Frobenius lift.
M finitely generated over A.
proofSteps: Reduction to free modules over W_n: choose a surjection W_n → A and a Frobenius lift on W_n compatible with σ (lift the images σ(x̄_i) to elements ≡ x_i^q mod m; the kernel is preserved); W_n is noetherian and regular (AdicSpacesPartII:F1), so M has a finite projective resolution P_• → M over W_n; σ is finite flat (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Remark 3.2.4), so σ_*P_j is projective and θ lifts to Dwork operators θ_j on the P_j with alternating traces adding up; a projective P_j is a summand of a free module, and θ_j ⊕ 0 is a Dwork operator on the free module with the same trace.
Free case M = ⊕_{i ≤ m} W_n e_i: θ is determined by the finitely many values θ(t^α e_i), 0 ≤ α_j < q, since θ(Σ σ(a_{α,i}) t^α e_i) = Σ a_{α,i} θ(t^α e_i).

For r > 1 let M(r) = ⊕ T_{n,r} e_i (Banach spaces). For r close to 1, θ(M(r)) ⊂ M(r^q) continuously, and M(r^q) ↪ M(r) is completely continuous (a uniform limit of finite-rank maps); so θ_r : M(r) → M(r) is completely continuous, hence nuclear, with trace and Fredholm determinant given by LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4.
The M(r) share the orthogonal basis t^α e_i, so Tr(θ_r) and det(1 − tθ_r) do not depend on r; θ = lim θ_r on M = ∪_r M(r) is nuclear with the same trace and determinant.
The trace axioms (linearity, Tr(θg) = Tr(gθ) for nuclear θ and continuous g) are part of the operator theory supplied by LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4.
acceptance: For θ(Σ c_n x^n) = Σ c_{qn} x^n on K⟨x⟩†, the basis x^n is mapped to x^{n/q} or 0, so the only diagonal entry is at n = 0 and Tr(θ) = 1; the canonical Dwork operator ψ = qθ on A has trace q and ψ(x^{qj−1}dx) = x^{j−1}dx on Ω^1 has trace 0, so Tr(ψ | A) − Tr(ψ | Ω^1) = q = #A^1(F_q).

sources.excerpt: Then for each Dwork operator Θ on M (with respect to σ), Θ is nuclear, and Trace(Θ) is an additive function of Θ.
The reader who wishes to derive the result by hand should start with the case M = A = Wn , then reduce to this case by an analogue of the Hilbert syzygy theorem for dagger algebras.

nodes.title: Galois Frobenius lifts
nodes.statement: Let A be a dagger algebra of MW-type over K of pure dimension n with a Frobenius lift σ. Then σ is finite flat of degree q^n. The lift σ is Galois if A is a Galois extension of σ(A) with group G := Aut(A/σ(A)) of order q^n, i.e. the automorphisms of A fixing σ(A) pointwise form a group of order q^n whose fixed subring is σ(A). (Kedlaya's text says 'of order q'; the degree of σ forces q^n; see sourceIssues.)
hypotheses: A of MW-type over K, pure dimension n; σ a Frobenius lift with σ|_K = id.
proofSteps: Degree: the reduction of σ is the q-power Frobenius of the smooth n-dimensional special fibre, finite flat of degree q^n (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Remark 3.2.4), so σ is finite flat of degree q^n.
Galois means |Aut(A/σ(A))| = deg σ = q^n and A^G = σ(A).
acceptance: For A = K⟨x⟩† with σ(x) = x^q and μ_q ⊂ K, G = {x ↦ ζx : ζ ∈ μ_q} has order q.

nodes.title: Existence of Galois Frobenius lifts over finite étale covers of affine space
nodes.statement: Let U ⊂ A^n_{F_q} be an open dense affine subscheme, B a dagger algebra of MW-type with special fibre U obtained by localizing W_n, and A a dagger algebra of MW-type finite étale over B with special fibre X. After replacing K by K(μ_q) (harmless for rigid cohomology), the standard Frobenius x_i ↦ x_i^q on W_n induces a Galois Frobenius lift on B, which extends uniquely to a Galois Frobenius lift σ on A, with Aut(A/σ(A)) ≅ μ_q^n.
hypotheses: U ⊂ A^n open dense affine; A finite étale over B = dagger lift of U.
K ⊇ μ_q after a finite extension.
proofSteps: On W_n the standard lift is Galois with group μ_q^n acting diagonally (RD.6/galois-frobenius-lift); it extends to the localization B.
Frobenius lifts extend uniquely along finite étale maps of MW-type algebras (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 3.2.3 and the sentence after it; RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra).

Each τ ∈ Aut(B/σ(B)) reduces to the identity on the special fibre, so by uniqueness of étale lifts it extends uniquely to an automorphism of A reducing to the identity; the extensions of τσ and σ agree because both lift the same map, so the extension fixes σ(A).

Fixed ring: the relative Frobenius of the étale map of special fibres is an isomorphism, so A ≅ B ⊗_{σ(B)} σ(A) (both are finite étale over B with the same reduction); G acts through the first factor, hence A^G = B^G ⊗_{σ(B)} σ(A) = σ(A), and |G| = q^n = deg σ, so σ is Galois.
Cohomology commutes with finite extension of K (Kedlaya, Weil II §2.2), so enlarging K is harmless.
acceptance: X = G_m ⊂ A^1 with A = K⟨x, x^{−1}⟩†: σ(x) = x^q and G = μ_q.

sources.excerpt: Then A admits a Galois Frobenius, by extension from the standard Frobenius on a dagger algebra with special fibre U

nodes.title: Parallel transport along the Galois group of a Frobenius lift
nodes.statement: Let A be of MW-type with a Galois Frobenius σ and G = Aut(A/σ(A)). For every (σ, ∇)-module M over A and τ ∈ G there is a canonical horizontal isomorphism τ^*M → M; these form a semilinear action of G on M (and on M ⊗ Ω^i_A through the functorial action on forms) commuting with ∇, and the invariants of this action are exactly F(M) ⊂ M.
hypotheses: A of MW-type with Galois Frobenius σ; M a (σ, ∇)-module over A (RD.3 in the local description).
proofSteps: In local coordinates t_1, …, t_n with E_i the contraction of ∇ with ∂/∂t_i, set a ⊗ v ↦ a Σ_I (t_1^τ − t_1)^{i_1} ⋯ (t_n^τ − t_n)^{i_n} E_1^{i_1} ⋯ E_n^{i_n} v / (i_1! ⋯ i_n!).
Convergence: applying F produces a basis on which each E_i acts by a matrix of norm < |p|^{1/(p−1)} (the factor d(t_i^σ)/dt_i · t_i/t_i^σ has norm < 1), and τ − id is topologically nilpotent.
Independence of coordinates is a routine calculation, so the local isomorphisms glue; horizontality and the cocycle condition follow from integrability of ∇.
Invariants: G fixes F(M) because τσ = σ; conversely a G-invariant element is in F(M), as seen by expanding in series about any point (Kedlaya).
acceptance: For M = A (trivial module) the action is the given action of G on A, with invariants σ(A) = F(A).

sources.excerpt: Then for any (F, ∇)-module M over A and any τ ∈ Aut(A/Aσ ), there is a canonical isomorphism τ ∗ M → M of modules with connection.
gives us a canonical action of G = Aut(A/Aσ ) on M, and the invariants of M under G are precisely F (M)

nodes.title: The canonical Dwork operator ψ
nodes.statement: Let A be of MW-type of pure dimension n with Galois Frobenius σ and group G (|G| = q^n), and M a (σ, ∇)-module over A. Define ψ : M ⊗_A Ω^i_A → M ⊗_A Ω^i_A by ψ(v) := F^{−1}(Σ_{τ ∈ G} τ(v)), using the action of RD.6/parallel-transport-action and the fact that Σ_τ τ(v) is G-invariant, hence lies in F(M ⊗ Ω^i) (F acting on forms through dσ). Then ψ is a Dwork operator commuting with ∇, and ψ ∘ F = q^n on M ⊗ Ω^i_A. On the cohomology H^i(M) (where G acts trivially) ψ ∘ F = F ∘ ψ = q^n. (Kedlaya writes 'F ∘ ψ equals multiplication by q^n'; on M itself only ψ ∘ F = q^n holds; see sourceIssues.)
hypotheses: A of MW-type, pure dimension n, Galois Frobenius σ with group G of order q^n.
M a (σ, ∇)-module over A; F injective on M ⊗ Ω^i.
proofSteps: Σ_τ τ(v) is G-invariant, hence equals F(w) for a unique w (F is injective since σ is faithfully flat and F : σ^*M ≅ M); set ψ(v) = w.
Dwork property: τ(σ(a)v) = σ(a)τ(v) since τ fixes σ(A); so Σ_τ τ(σ(a)v) = σ(a)F(w) = F(a w), giving ψ(σ(a)v) = aψ(v).
ψ ∘ F = |G| = q^n: for v = F(u), each τ fixes F(u), so Σ_τ τ(F(u)) = q^n F(u).
Commutation with ∇ follows from horizontality of the parallel-transport isomorphisms and of F.

On cohomology each τ induces the identity (τ reduces to the identity on the special fibre, so its action on rigid cohomology is that of the identity by functoriality, RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology and RD.4/monsky-washnitzer-comparison), so Σ_τ τ = q^n there and F ∘ ψ = q^n as well.
acceptance: For A = M = K⟨x⟩†, σ(x) = x^q, G = μ_q: ψ(x^{qj}) = q x^j and ψ(x^m) = 0 for q ∤ m; F(ψ(x)) = 0 ≠ q x, while ψ(F(x)) = ψ(x^q) = q x.

we have that ψ is a Dwork operator, F ◦ ψ equals multiplication by q n if A has pure dimension n, and ψ commutes with ∇.

nodes.title: The ideal generated by σ(a) − a is the unit ideal when there are no rational points
nodes.statement: Let A be a dagger algebra of MW-type over K with special fibre X̄ and Frobenius lift σ (σ|_K = id). If X̄(F_q) = ∅, then the ideal of A generated by {σ(a) − a : a ∈ A} is A.
hypotheses: A of MW-type with reduction R = A^int / m A^int, X̄ = Spec R; σ a Frobenius lift; X̄ has no F_q-rational points.
proofSteps: In R the ideal J̄ generated by {b^q − b : b ∈ R} cuts out the closed subscheme of points where every function takes values in F_q, i.e. the F_q-rational points; since there are none, J̄ = R (van der Put, proof of 4.1.0).
Write 1 = Σ r̄_i (b̄_i^q − b̄_i) in R and lift r_i, b_i ∈ A^int; since σ(b_i) ≡ b_i^q mod m, u := Σ r_i(σ(b_i) − b_i) ≡ 1 mod m A^int.
u = 1 − πy with y ∈ A^int; the series Σ_n π^n y^n converges in a fringe algebra of A, so u is a unit and the ideal is A.
acceptance: For A = K⟨x, (x^q − x)^{−1}⟩† (special fibre A^1 minus its F_q-points) one has 1 ∈ (σ(x) − x)A because σ(x) − x ≡ x^q − x is a unit mod m.

nodes.title: The trace of a Dwork operator vanishes without rational points
nodes.statement: Let A be of MW-type with a Frobenius lift σ whose special fibre has no F_q-rational points, and M a finitely generated A-module. Then Tr(θ) = 0 for every Dwork operator θ on M. In particular, for A with Galois Frobenius and M a (σ, ∇)-module, Tr(ψ | M ⊗_A Ω^i_A) = 0 for all i.
hypotheses: A of MW-type, Frobenius lift σ, X̄(F_q) = ∅.
θ a Dwork operator on a finite A-module M (e.g. ψ on M ⊗ Ω^i).
proofSteps: For a, b ∈ A: Tr((σ(a) − a)·b·θ) = Tr(σ(a)·(bθ)) − Tr((bθ)·σ(a))... precisely Tr(σ(a) b θ) = Tr(b θ a) = Tr(a b θ) by the Dwork property θ∘σ(a) = a∘θ and Tr(fg) = Tr(gf) (RD.6/dwork-operators-are-nuclear), so Tr((σ(a) − a) b θ) = 0.
By RD.6/unit-ideal-without-rational-points write 1 = Σ b_i (σ(a_i) − a_i); then θ = Σ (σ(a_i) − a_i) b_i θ has trace 0 by linearity.

nodes.title: Frobenius is bijective on rigid cohomology of a smooth variety
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth F_q-scheme of pure dimension n and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K). The linear q-Frobenius F is bijective on H^i_rig(X/K, E) and on H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) for all i.
hypotheses: X smooth of pure dimension n over F_q; E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K).
proofSteps: Poincaré duality (RD.5/poincare-duality) gives a perfect pairing ⟨ , ⟩ : H^i_rig(X/K, E) × H^{2n−i}_{c,rig}(X/K, E^∨) → K(−n) that is Frobenius-equivariant: ⟨Fa, Fb⟩ = q^n⟨a, b⟩.
If Fa = 0 then q^n⟨a, b⟩ = ⟨Fa, Fb⟩ = 0 for all b, so a = 0 by perfectness; hence F is injective on H^i_rig, and symmetrically on H^{2n−i}_{c,rig}.
The spaces are finite-dimensional (RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology), so injective endomorphisms are bijective.
This replaces the citation of Étesse–Le Stum [ElS, Proposition 2.1] in Kedlaya's proof of Theorem 5.3.2.

nodes.title: Rigid cohomology of Spec F_{q^d}
nodes.statement: Let x = Spec F_{q^d} viewed over F_q, and E ∈ F-Isoc†(x/K), given (RD.3) by a finite-dimensional K_x-space V with a bijective σ_x-semilinear F (K_x/K unramified of degree d). Then H^0_rig(x/K, E) = H^0_{c,rig}(x/K, E) = V regarded as a K-space (dimension d·dim_{K_x} V) with the K-linear F, and H^i = 0 for i ≠ 0. For E = O_x, F on K_x is the generator σ_x of Gal(K_x/K); its eigenvalues are the d-th roots of unity, each with multiplicity one, and Tr(F^r | K_x) = d if d | r and 0 otherwise. In general det_K(1 − tF | V) = det_{K_x}(1 − t^d F^d | V).
hypotheses: x = Spec F_{q^d}; σ_K = id; E ∈ F-Isoc†(x/K).
proofSteps: A frame for x is Spf O_{K_x} (smooth over O_K, x proper); the tube is a single point of the generic fibre, so rigid cohomology is H^0 = V and higher cohomology vanishes (RD.4/rigid-cohomology; x is proper so H_c = H).

σ_x has order d and K_x/K is Galois with group generated by σ_x; by the normal basis theorem σ_x permutes a K-basis of K_x cyclically, so its characteristic polynomial is t^d − 1 and Tr(σ_x^r) = d·[d | r].
The block-cyclic computation of RD.6/frobenius-at-closed-point gives the determinant identity.

nodes.title: Alternating traces are additive along Frobenius-equivariant long exact sequences
nodes.statement: Let 0 → V^0 → V^1 → ⋯ → V^m → 0 be an exact sequence of finite-dimensional K-vector spaces with endomorphisms F^j commuting with the maps. Then Σ_j (−1)^j Tr(F^j) = 0, and hence Σ_j (−1)^j Tr((F^j)^r) = 0 for every r ≥ 1. Applied to the Frobenius-equivariant excision sequence for Z ⊂ X closed with open complement U, Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F^r | H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)) = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F^r | H^i_{c,rig}(U/K, E)) + Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F^r | H^i_{c,rig}(Z/K, E)).
hypotheses: Finite-dimensional spaces; all maps (including connecting maps) commute with the endomorphisms.
proofSteps: Split the long exact sequence into short exact sequences 0 → im_{j−1} → V^j → im_j → 0; each is F-stable.
The trace is additive on each short exact sequence (tauceti:LinearMap.trace_eq_add_of_exact); telescoping gives the alternating sum 0. Powers F^r satisfy the same hypotheses.

The compact-support excision sequence is Frobenius-equivariant in every map, including the connecting maps (RD.4/excision-sequence), and all terms are finite-dimensional (RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology).

nodes.title: The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius
nodes.statement: Let X be a separated scheme of finite type over F_q, K with residue field F_q and σ_K = id, and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K). For every r ≥ 1, S_r(X, E) = Σ_{x : deg x | r} deg(x)·Tr(F_x^{r/deg x} | E_x) = Σ_{i=0}^{2 dim X} (−1)^i Tr(F^r | H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)), where F is the linear q-Frobenius. Equivalently, in K[[t]], L(X, E, t) = ∏_i det(1 − tF | H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E))^{(−1)^{i+1}}. In particular, for E = O_X: #X(F_{q^r}) = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F^r | H^i_{c,rig}(X/K)) and Z(X, t) = ∏_i det(1 − tF | H^i_{c,rig}(X/K))^{(−1)^{i+1}}.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over F_q (no smoothness or properness).
E an overconvergent F-isocrystal; σ_K = id; F the linear q-Frobenius; Tate twists as in RD.6/tate-twist-of-f-isocrystals.
proofSteps: It suffices to prove S_1(X, E) = Σ(−1)^i Tr(F | H^i_c) for every q: the case of F_{q^r} follows by base change (RD.6/base-change-to-finite-extension-of-fq), and the product form follows from the traces of all powers by the determinant–exponential identity (WeilConjectures:WC.1).
Induction on dim X; dimension 0 is RD.6/trace-formula-dimension-zero.

Both sides are additive for a closed subscheme and its open complement (left side by the definition of S_1; right side by RD.6/alternating-trace-additivity applied to RD.4/excision-sequence); so X may be replaced by an open dense subscheme, by an irreducible component, or by the complement of its finitely many F_q-rational points (whose contribution is the dimension-zero case).

By the geometric lemma on finite étale covers (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Proposition 9.1.2; Weil II Proposition 6.6.1; supplied by the RD.5 finiteness development), a smooth dense open affine U ⊂ X is finite étale over an open dense subscheme of A^n; X may be replaced by U with no F_q-points.
U has a dagger lift with a Galois Frobenius (RD.6/galois-frobenius-exists), and RD.6/trace-formula-without-rational-points gives Σ(−1)^i Tr(F | H^i_c(U/K, E)) = 0 = S_1(U, E).
Finite dimensionality of all H^i_c (RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology) makes the traces and determinants meaningful.

nodes.statement: Fix a field embedding ι : K^alg ↪ C (one exists: K^alg ≅ Q̄_p is algebraically closed of characteristic 0 and cardinality continuum, so even an isomorphism K^alg ≅ C exists by mathlib:IsAlgClosed.ringEquiv_of_equiv_of_charZero). For w ∈ R and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) on a separated finite-type F_q-scheme X: E is ι-pure of weight w if for every closed point x (degree d) every eigenvalue α ∈ K^alg of F_x satisfies |ι(α)| = q^{wd/2}; E is (strongly) ι-mixed of weight ≤ w (resp. ≥ w) if every such α satisfies |ι(α)| = q^{(w+i)d/2} for an integer i = i(α) ≤ 0 (resp. ≥ 0); weakly ι-mixed if i is only required to be real. nodes.title: The relative Dwork trick
nodes.statement: Let A be a reduced dagger algebra over K with Frobenius lift, R_A^+ the plus-part of the Robba ring over A (series Σ_{i ≥ 0} c_i t^i with c_i ∈ A satisfying the fringe convergence condition), and M a free (σ, ∇)-module over R_A^+ relative to A (∇ is A-linear, with values in M ⊗ dt). Then M has a basis v_1, …, v_n with ∇v_i = 0; on such a basis F acts by a matrix over A.
hypotheses: A reduced dagger algebra; R_A^+ ⊂ R_A as in Kedlaya, Finiteness §2.5 (supplied with the relative pushforward theory of RD.5).
M free over R_A^+ with Frobenius and relative connection.
proofSteps: Write ∇e_j = Σ N_ij e_i ⊗ dt with N = Σ_l N_l t^l over R_A^+; the recursion l U_l + Σ_{i<l} N_i U_{l−1−i} = 0 determines a unique U = I + Σ_{l ≥ 1} U_l t^l over A[[t]] with NU + dU/dt = 0.
Choose a fringe algebra B with v_B(N_l) + s(l + 1) > 0 for all l; induction gives v_B(l!·U_l) + sl > 0, so v_B(U_l) + rl → ∞ for r > s + 1/(p − 1).

By the usual Dwork trick (Kedlaya Weil II Lemma 2.5.1, via RD.2/unipotent-differential-module over R^+) this growth suffices for U to have entries in R_A^+; the same argument for M^∨ shows U^{−T} has entries in R_A^+, so v_j = Σ_i U_ij e_i is a horizontal basis.
acceptance: A = K, M = R_K^+ with ∇ = d + a dt (a ∈ R_K^+) and a Frobenius structure: the horizontal generator is exp(−∫a dt)·e, which lies in R_K^+ by the lemma.

nodes.title: Degeneration of H^1_c in a one-parameter family
nodes.statement: Let M be a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨s, x⟩† and f : K⟨s⟩† → K⟨s, x⟩† the inclusion. Let A be a localization of K⟨s⟩† over which the generic pushforwards R^i f_* M_A, R^i f_! M_A and those of M^∨ are (σ, ∇)-modules with perfect duality pairings (the generic pushforward theorem, Kedlaya Finiteness Theorem 7.3.3 and Proposition 8.6.1, supplied by RD.5). Then there is a canonical Frobenius-equivariant injection H^1_c(M/sM) ↪ H^0_{loc, s=0}(R^1 f_! M_A).
hypotheses: M a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨s, x⟩†; A a localization of K⟨s⟩† satisfying the conclusion of the generic pushforward theorem for M_A and M_A^∨ (RD.5).
proofSteps: By Poincaré duality for the pushforwards (RD.5), it suffices to construct a Frobenius-equivariant pairing H^1_c(M/sM) × H^1_{loc,s=0}(R^1 f_* M_A^∨) → K(−2) nondegenerate on the left.
Introduce Kedlaya's auxiliary ring S of series Σ c_ij s^i t^j converging on |s| = δ, ε < |t| < 1 for δ near 1; embed R^{s,+}_{K⟨x⟩†} and R^s_{K⟨x⟩†} into S^{s+,t−} and S^{t−} with x = t^{−1}.

The relative Dwork trick (RD.6/relative-dwork-trick) gives g : M/sM → M ⊗ R^{s,+}_{K⟨x⟩†} with g(v) ≡ v mod s, ∇_s g(v) = 0, ∇_t g(v) = g(∇_t v); this yields the inclusion (3.3.3) of H^1_c(M/sM) into a quotient of horizontal S-sections.

The residue pairing on S ⊗ (ds ∧ dt) (coefficient of (ds/s) ∧ (dt/t)) is perfect onto K(−2); restricting successively to ∇_t-closed and ∇_s-horizontal classes gives the pairings (3.3.4), nondegenerate on the left.
Combine with (3.3.3).
acceptance: M = O (constant): H^1_c(A^1) = 0 and both sides vanish.

nodes.title: Integrality of relative de Rham classes under vanishing fibrewise H^0
nodes.statement: Let M be a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨s, x⟩† such that H^0(M_μ') = 0 for all finite extensions K' of K and all μ in the ring of integers of K' fixed by a power of σ_K (M_μ := M ⊗ K'/(s − μ)). Let A ⊆ B be localizations of K⟨s⟩†, and v ∈ M ⊗ B⟨x⟩† with ∇_t v ∈ M ⊗ A⟨x⟩† ⊗ dx. Then v ∈ M ⊗ A⟨x⟩†.
hypotheses: M a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨s, x⟩†; fibrewise H^0 vanishes at every μ.
proofSteps: It suffices to treat the case s not invertible in A and show v ∈ M ⊗ C⟨x⟩† with C = B ∩ R^{s,+}_K; translate s ↦ s − μ (after enlarging K) for the other points.
By RD.6/relative-dwork-trick choose a basis v_i of M ⊗ R^{s,+}_{K⟨x⟩†} with ∇_s v_i = 0; integrability gives ∇_t v_j = Σ D_ij v_i ⊗ dx with D_ij ∈ K⟨x⟩†.
Expand v = Σ a_i v_i with a_i = Σ_l b_il s^l and put w_l = Σ_i b_il v_i; then ∇_t w_l = 0 for l < 0.
The K⟨x⟩†-span of the v_i is isomorphic to M/sM, which has no horizontal sections, so w_l = 0 for l < 0, i.e. v ∈ M ⊗ (A⟨x⟩† ∩ R^{s,+}) = M ⊗ C⟨x⟩†.
acceptance: If M is constant (H^0 ≠ 0) the conclusion fails: v = s^{−1}·e for a horizontal e has ∇_t v = 0 but v ∉ M ⊗ A⟨x⟩† when s is not invertible in A.

nodes.title: Freeness of R^1 f_* and R^1 f_! when fibre cohomology has constant dimension
nodes.statement: Let M be a free (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨s, x⟩† and f : K⟨s⟩† → K⟨s, x⟩† the inclusion. Suppose there is m ≥ 0 with dim_{K'} H^0(M_μ) = dim_{K'} H^0(M_μ^∨) = 0 and dim_{K'} H^1(M_μ) = dim_{K'} H^1(M_μ^∨) = m for all K' and μ. Then R^1 f_* M, R^1 f_* M^∨, R^1 f_! M and R^1 f_! M^∨ are free of rank m over K⟨s⟩† (not merely over a localization).
hypotheses: Fibrewise dimensions constant as stated for all finite extensions K' and all μ.
proofSteps: Localize: it suffices to prove local freeness of rank m near s = 0 after finite extension of K; let A be a localization with s invertible where the generic pushforward theorem holds (RD.5).

Under the hypothesis the pairings (3.3.2) and (3.3.4) of RD.6/degeneration-injection are perfect; choose a basis v_1, …, v_m of H^1_c(M/sM) and define h : (R^1 f_* M_A^∨) ⊗ R^s_K → (R^s_K)^m by w ↦ (Σ_l s^l [g(v_i), s^{−l} w ⊗ ds])_i, an isomorphism.
Use RD.6/robba-matrix-factorisation-in-parameter to find w_1, …, w_m ∈ R^1 f_* M_B^∨ whose images generate (R^{s,+}_K)^m; representatives x_j lie in M^∨ ⊗ C⟨x⟩† ⊗ dx with C = B ∩ R^{s,+}_K.

Any class over C is a C-combination of the w_j; by RD.6/horizontal-sections-descend-in-families (using vanishing of H^0) the difference vanishes already over C, so R^1 f_* M_C^∨ is free on the w_j; similarly for M.
For R^1 f_!: take the dual basis under the residue pairing M ⊗ R^t_A / M ⊗ A⟨x⟩† × (M^∨ ⊗ dx) → A; its elements pair into K⟨s⟩†, so R^1 f_! M is free of rank m.
acceptance: The H^0 hypothesis is needed: for M = L_{sx} every fibre H^1(A^1, L_{μx}) vanishes, but H^0(M_μ) ≠ 0 for μ ≡ 0 mod π, and R^1 f_* M = coker ∇_x ≅ D^{s,†}/D^{s,†}s is nonzero, so it is not free of rank 0.

nodes.title: The commutation formula in the Weyl algebra with ∂x − x∂ = π^{−1}
nodes.statement: Assume K contains π with π^{p−1} = −p. In the K-algebra R generated by x and ∂ subject to ∂x − x∂ = π^{−1}: ∂^n x^m = Σ_i n!·m! / (π^i·i!·(n − i)!·(m − i)!) · x^{m−i} ∂^{n−i}.
hypotheses: K ∋ π, π^{p−1} = −p (equivalently K contains a primitive p-th root of unity).
proofSteps: Induction on m + n: ∂^n x^m = (x∂^n + nπ^{−1}∂^{n−1}) x^{m−1}, then combine binomial coefficients; the cases m or n ≤ 1 are direct.
acceptance: ∂x = x∂ + π^{−1}; ∂x^2 = x^2∂ + 2π^{−1}x; ∂^2 x^2 = x^2∂^2 + 4π^{−1}x∂ + 2π^{−2} (checked by machine normal-ordering, see D.md).

nodes.title: Multiplication of overconvergent differential operators converges
nodes.statement: Let a = Σ a_ij x^i ∂^j and b = Σ b_kl x^k ∂^l with liminf v_p(a_ij)/(i + j) > 0 and liminf v_p(b_kl)/(k + l) > 0. Then c_mn := Σ_{i,j,s} a_ij b_{(m+s−i)(n+s−j)} · j!(m + s − i)! / (π^s s!(j − s)!(m − i)!) converges in K for each (m, n), and c = Σ c_mn x^m ∂^n satisfies liminf v_p(c_mn)/(m + n) > 0; on polynomials c = ab in R.
hypotheses: K ∋ π with π^{p−1} = −p; a, b overconvergent in the stated sense.
proofSteps: Choose e, f with v_p(a_ij) ≥ e(i + j) − f and v_p(b_kl) ≥ e(k + l) − f.
By RD.6/factorial-valuation-bounds, the valuation of the (i, j, s) summand is ≥ e(m + s) − log_p(m + s + 1) + e(n + s) − log_p(n + s + 1) − 2f − 2, which tends to ∞ with s.
For 0 < g < e pick h with ex − log_p(x + 1) ≥ gx − h, giving v_p(c_mn) ≥ g(m + n) − 2h − 2f − 2.
On R the formula is the product by RD.6/weyl-algebra-commutation-formula.

nodes.title: The overconvergent Weyl algebra D†
nodes.statement: Assume K ∋ π with π^{p−1} = −p. D† = D^{x,†} is the set of formal series Σ_{i,j ≥ 0} a_ij x^i ∂^j with a_ij ∈ K and liminf_{i+j→∞} v_p(a_ij)/(i + j) > 0, with the multiplication of RD.6/overconvergent-weyl-multiplication-converges extending the Weyl algebra R (∂x − x∂ = π^{−1}). It is a noncommutative K-algebra containing R densely for its fringe topology; every element can also be written Σ a_ij ∂^j x^i with the same growth condition. It coincides with Huyghe's overconvergent Weyl algebra A_1(K)†.
hypotheses: K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with π ∈ K, π^{p−1} = −p.
proofSteps: The set is closed under addition; multiplication is well defined and lands in D† by RD.6/overconvergent-weyl-multiplication-converges.
Associativity and distributivity hold on the dense subring R and extend by continuity of multiplication in the fringe topology.
The reversed normal form follows by the same estimate (Kedlaya Remark 4.1.4).
acceptance: x and ∂ generate a dense subalgebra; Σ_j p^j ∂^j lies in D† (v_p(p^j)/j = 1), while Σ_j ∂^j does not.

nodes.title: A Frobenius structure makes a module with connection a D†-module
nodes.statement: Let M be a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨x⟩† and D : M → M the derivation with ∇v = Dv ⊗ dx. For every sequence (v_i) tending to 0 in the fringe topology and every ε ∈ K⟨x⟩† with |ε| < 1, the double sequence ε^j π^{−j} D^j v_i tends to 0. Consequently, for Σ a_ij ∂^j x^i ∈ D† and v ∈ M the series Σ a_ij (π^{−1}D)^j x^i v converges, and M is a left D†-module with ∂v ⊗ dx = π^{−1}∇v. This is the radius estimate: a Frobenius structure forces convergence of the Taylor-type series Σ (π^{−1}D)^j.
hypotheses: M a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨x⟩† (RD.3 local description); K ∋ π with π^{p−1} = −p.
proofSteps: Choose e with |ε/π|^{p^e}·|(p^e)!| < 1; with u = d(x^σ)/dx (|u| < 1) and N^{(m)} = u u^σ ⋯ u^{σ^{m−1}} N^{σ^m}, one has D F^m e_j = Σ N^{(m)}_ij F^m e_i; choose m with |N^{(m)}| < |(p^e)!|.

Writing v_i in the basis F^m e_l and estimating in the Gauss norm of T_{1,ρ} for ρ close to 1: |d^{p^e}/dx^{p^e}(c)|_ρ ≤ |(p^e)!|·|c|_ρ, giving the bound |ε^j π^{−j} d_ijl|_ρ ≤ max{1, |ε/π|_ρ^{p^e−1}}·|(ε/π)^{p^e}(p^e)!|_ρ^{⌊j/p^e⌋}·max_l |c_il|_ρ → 0 (uses RD.6/factorial-valuation-bounds).
Corollary: choose δ with |a_ij| < |δ|^{i+j} for almost all (i, j) and apply the lemma with ε = δ and v_i = (δx)^i v.
Compatibility with the generic radius (RD.1/generic-radius): the estimate says the generic radius of M is 1, as for any module with Frobenius structure.
acceptance: M = K⟨x⟩† trivial: ∂ acts as π^{−1} d/dx and Σ a_ij (π^{−1} d/dx)^j x^i converges on polynomials.
Without Frobenius the conclusion can fail: the module with ∇e = λ e dx for |λ| > |π| is not a D†-module in this way (exp(λx)-type solutions have radius < 1).

nodes.title: The Fourier automorphism ρ of D†
nodes.statement: The K-algebra automorphism ρ of D† with ρ(x) = ∂ and ρ(∂) = −x. Explicitly, ρ(Σ c_ij x^i ∂^j) = Σ_{a,b} (Σ_k (−1)^{a+k} (a + k)!(b + k)! / (π^k k! a! b!) · c_{(b+k)(a+k)}) x^a ∂^b. (Kedlaya prints the inner coefficient with (−1)^{j+k} and c_{(i+k)(j+k)}, which sends x to x; see sourceIssues.) ρ^2 is the automorphism x ↦ −x, ∂ ↦ −∂, so ρ^4 = id.
hypotheses: K ∋ π with π^{p−1} = −p.
proofSteps: ρ respects the relation: ρ(∂)ρ(x) − ρ(x)ρ(∂) = −x∂ + ∂x = π^{−1}.
On monomials ρ(x^i ∂^j) = ∂^i (−x)^j; normal-ordering with RD.6/weyl-algebra-commutation-formula gives the displayed coefficients (verified by machine on all x^i ∂^j with i, j < 5).
The coefficient bound of RD.6/overconvergent-weyl-multiplication-converges shows ρ preserves the growth condition, so ρ extends continuously to D†; ρ^4 = id gives bijectivity.

nodes.title: The Dwork (Artin–Schreier) isocrystal L_π
nodes.statement: Assume K ∋ π with π^{p−1} = −p. The Dwork isocrystal L = L_π on A^1_{F_q} is the rank-one (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨x⟩† (standard Frobenius σ(x) = x^q) with generator e, ∇e = π e ⊗ dx and F e = θ(x)·e where θ(x) := exp(π x^q − π x) ∈ K⟨x⟩†. (Kedlaya prints F e = exp(πx − πx^q)e, which is not horizontal for ∇e = πe ⊗ dx; see sourceIssues.) For f ∈ A^int, L_f := f^*L. Then L_{f+g} ≅ L_f ⊗ L_g, the class of L_f depends only on f mod π, L becomes trivial after adjoining u with u^p − u = x, L^{⊗p} ≅ O, and at a point x_0 ∈ F_{q^r} (Teichmüller lift t) the Frobenius F_{x_0} = ψ(Tr_{F_{q^r}/F_p}(x_0))^{−1}, where ψ is the nontrivial additive character of F_p with ψ(1) = θ_p(1), θ_p(x) = exp(π(x − x^p)) being Dwork's splitting function.
hypotheses: K ∋ π with π^{p−1} = −p.
proofSteps: Horizontality: with ∇e = πe dx and F e = θe, the condition ∇(Fe) = (F ⊗ dσ)(∇e) reads θ' + πθ = πq x^{q−1} θ, i.e. θ'/θ = π(q x^{q−1} − 1), solved by θ = exp(π(x^q − x)).
Overconvergence: θ(x)^{−1} = exp(π(x − x^q)) = ∏_{i<a} θ_p(x^{p^i}) with θ_p overconvergent (Dwork: v_p of the m-th coefficient ≥ m(p − 1)/p^2); θ is the inverse of a unit of K⟨x⟩†.
Values at Teichmüller points: ∏_{j < m} θ_p(t^{p^j}) = θ_p(1)^{Tr(x_0)} for t the Teichmüller lift of x_0 ∈ F_{p^m}; θ_p(1) is a primitive p-th root of unity ≡ 1 + π mod π^2.
Tensor and pullback identities are immediate on the generator; triviality over u^p − u = x: the element exp(−πx + ...) built from u is horizontal (Kedlaya).

The additive character ψ is the trace character of FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.1/canonical-additive-character with root θ_p(1), and its lift to F_{q^r} is FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.1/trace-lift-of-an-additive-character.
acceptance: PARI/GP, p = 3, π^2 = −3, series to degree 300: θ_3(1)^3 ≡ 1 to π-adic order 144, v_π(θ_3(1) − 1) = 1 and v_π(θ_3(1) − 1 − π) = 2, θ_3(1)θ_3(−1) ≡ 1, and θ_3(0) + θ_3(1) + θ_3(−1) ≡ 0 (character sum over F_3).
PARI/GP: with the printed F e = exp(πx − πx^q)e the horizontality defect ∇(Fe) − (F ⊗ dσ)(∇e) has constant term 2π ≠ 0; with θ = exp(πx^q − πx) it vanishes identically to order 298.

nodes.title: The naive geometric Fourier transform
nodes.statement: Let M be a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨x⟩†, f : K⟨s⟩† → K⟨s, x⟩† and g : K⟨x⟩† → K⟨s, x⟩† the inclusions, and N := g^*M ⊗ L_{sx} over K⟨s, x⟩† (L_{sx} the pullback of the Dwork isocrystal along (s, x) ↦ sx). With ∇ = ∇_s ds + ∇_x dx, the naive geometric Fourier transform is M̂_geom := coker(∇_x : N → N ⊗ dx), a D^{s,†}-module with a σ-semilinear Frobenius (not necessarily locally free). Its fibre at s = μ is H^1_rig(A^1, M ⊗ L_{μx}).
hypotheses: K ∋ π with π^{p−1} = −p; M a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨x⟩†.
proofSteps: N is a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨s, x⟩† (tensor product and pullback, RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal, RD.6/dwork-isocrystal).
∇_s commutes with ∇_x by integrability, so it acts on coker ∇_x; together with multiplication by s this gives the D^{s,†}-structure; F descends to the cokernel.
Fibres: coker ∇_x ⊗ K⟨s⟩†/(s − μ) = H^1 of the fibre (right exactness of the cokernel).

nodes.title: The Fourier transform agrees with the geometric Fourier transform
nodes.statement: For a (σ, ∇)-module M over K⟨x⟩† there is a canonical isomorphism of D†-modules M̂ ≅ M̂_geom, induced by v ↦ class of (v ⊗ e) ⊗ dx.
hypotheses: M a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨x⟩†; K ∋ π.
proofSteps: Surjectivity: given v = Σ v_i s^i ∈ N, Lemma 4.2.1 (RD.6/frobenius-structure-gives-weyl-module) applied with ε = η^{−1} makes Σ_i s^i Σ_j (−1)^j π^{−(j+1)} D^j v_{i+j+1} converge to w with ∇_x w = (v − v_0) dx + Σ_j (−1)^j π^{−j−1} D^{j+1} v_{j+1} dx, so every class is represented by some v_0 ⊗ dx.
Injectivity: if ∇_x w = v dx with w = Σ w_i s^i then Dw_0 = v and πw_i + Dw_{i+1} = 0, forcing (−π)^{−i} D^{i+1} w_i = v; the same lemma makes the left side tend to 0, so v = 0.
The D†-actions match because in coker ∇_x the relation ∇_x(v ⊗ e) = (Dv + πsv) ⊗ e dx identifies s with −π^{−1}D.

nodes.statement: Let M be a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨x⟩† and d ≥ 0 such that for all K' and μ: dim H^0(M ⊗ L_{μx}) = dim H^0(M^∨ ⊗ L_{μx}) = 0 and dim H^1(M ⊗ L_{μx}) = dim H^1(M^∨ ⊗ L_{μx}) = d. Then M̂_geom is a (σ, ∇)-module of rank d over K⟨s⟩†, and if M is (absolutely) irreducible so is M̂ ≅ M̂_geom.
hypotheses: Constant fibre dimensions as stated for all finite extensions K' and all μ.
proofSteps: Apply RD.6/pushforward-free-when-fibre-cohomology-constant to N = g^*M ⊗ L_{sx}: R^1 f_* N = M̂_geom is free of rank d; it carries the induced connection and Frobenius.

Irreducibility: a Frobenius-stable D†-submodule N̂ of M̂ with N̂ and M̂/N̂ infinite-dimensional gives, undoing ρ, a Frobenius-stable D†-submodule of M, which is a (σ, ∇)-submodule with nontrivial quotient; absolute irreducibility likewise since the construction commutes with extension of K (RD.6/fourier-transform-comparison).

nodes.title: Local monodromy representation and Swan conductor of an overconvergent F-isocrystal
nodes.statement: Let C be a smooth irreducible affine curve over k with smooth compactification C̄, E ∈ F-Isoc†(C/K), and x ∈ C̄ − C with local field E_x = Frac(Ô_{C̄,x}) ≅ κ(x)((t)). By the p-adic local monodromy theorem (RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement) there is a finite Galois extension F/E_x over which E ⊗ R_x becomes unipotent; G = Gal(F/E_x) acts on the horizontal sections (and those of the successive quotients), giving the local monodromy representation ρ_x with character χ. The Swan conductor is Swan_x(E) := (1/|G|) Σ_{g ∈ G} Swan_{F/E_x}(g) χ(g), with Swan_{F/E_x}(g) = −f·inf_{y ∈ o_F − 0} v_F(y^g/y − 1) for g ≠ e and Swan(e) = −Σ_{h ≠ e} Swan(h), f the residue degree of F/E_x. Equivalently Swan_x(E) = Σ_i i·dim V(i) over the break decomposition of the wild part. It is a nonnegative integer independent of F.
hypotheses: C smooth irreducible affine curve over a perfect k; E ∈ F-Isoc†(C/K); x a point at infinity.
proofSteps: Quasi-unipotence (RD.2) provides F and the finite-image representation of G on horizontal sections.

The Swan conductor of a finite-image representation of the Galois group of an equal-characteristic local field, its integrality (Hasse–Arf) and independence of F, and the break formula are supplied by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3.
acceptance: For E unipotent at x (e.g. E = O or a unipotent extension), Swan_x(E) = 0.
For the Dwork isocrystal L_P with P of degree d prime to p, Swan_∞(L_P) = d.

nodes.title: The p-adic Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich formula
nodes.statement: Let E be an overconvergent F-isocrystal on a smooth irreducible affine curve C over k with smooth compactification C̄, and χ(C/K, E) := dim H^0_rig(C/K, E) − dim H^1_rig(C/K, E). Then χ(C/K, E) = χ(C/K, O_C)·rank(E) − Σ_{x ∈ C̄ − C} [κ(x) : k]·Swan_x(E). For C = A^1 this reads χ(A^1/K, E) = rank(E) − Swan_∞(E), equivalently χ(G_m/K, E) = −Swan_∞(E) when E is tame at 0.
hypotheses: C smooth irreducible affine curve over k; E ∈ F-Isoc†(C/K).
proofSteps: Combine (a) the Christol–Mebkhout index formula χ = χ(O)·rank − Σ[κ(x):k] Irr_x(E) with (b) Irr_x(E) = Swan_x(E) (Crew, Matsuda, Tsuzuki); neither proof is publicly available here (recorded gap).

Kedlaya's sketch: reduce to C = A^1 (removing a rational point changes both sides by rank E; pushforward along a finite étale map; Proposition 6.6.1); extend E to a meromorphic connection on P^1_K (Christol–Mebkhout), use the snake lemma (4.4.3) with R_0 ⊕ R_∞, a unit-root isocrystal E' with the same local monodromy at ∞ and tame at 0 (Katz local-to-global, Crew–Matsuda–Tsuzuki), the formula for E' via crystalline intersection theory or Brauer induction, and Mebkhout's complex Euler–Poincaré formula via GAGA.
acceptance: E = L_π on A^1: Swan_∞ = 1, so χ = 1 − 1 = 0, matching H^0 = H^1 = 0.
E = L_{x^d}, p ∤ d: χ = 1 − d, so dim H^1(A^1, L_{x^d}) = d − 1, matching the degree d − 1 of the additive L-function (FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.2/additive-l-function-purity).

nodes.title: Twisting by L_P of large degree kills local invariants and fixes H^1
nodes.statement: Let M be a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨x⟩†. There is an integer N (the largest break of the local monodromy of M at ∞) such that for every monic P ∈ o[x] of degree d > N with p ∤ d: dim H^0_loc(M ⊗ L_P) = dim H^1_loc(M ⊗ L_P) = 0, dim H^0(M ⊗ L_P) = 0 and dim H^1(M ⊗ L_P) = (d − 1)·rank(M). In particular, for n > N prime to p and r, s integral with r a unit, the fibre dimensions of M ⊗ L_{rx^n + s} satisfy the hypotheses of RD.6/fourier-transform-rank-and-irreducibility.
hypotheses: M a (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨x⟩†; P monic of degree d > N, p ∤ d.
proofSteps: The local monodromy at ∞ of M ⊗ L_P is ρ ⊗ ψ_P, where ψ_P is the Artin–Schreier character of L = k((t))[u]/(u^p − u − P(t)); since d > N, ρ ⊗ ψ_P has all breaks equal to d (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3 upper-numbering breaks; RD.6/swan-conductor-of-isocrystal).
No break 0 means no trivial subrepresentation: H^0_loc(M ⊗ L_P) = H^0_loc(M^∨ ⊗ L_{−P}) = 0, and H^1_loc = 0 by local duality (the pairing H^0_loc × H^1_loc → K(−1) of Kedlaya §2.6, from RD.5).
Swan(ρ ⊗ ψ_P) = d·rank(M), so RD.6/grothendieck-ogg-shafarevich-formula gives χ(M ⊗ L_P) = (1 − d)·rank(M).
H^0(M ⊗ L_P) injects into H^0_loc by the exact sequence (2.6.1), hence vanishes; so dim H^1 = (d − 1)·rank(M).
acceptance: M = O, P = x^d: dim H^1(A^1, L_{x^d}) = d − 1, the number of reciprocal roots of the additive character L-function of x^d.

nodes.title: ι-real and ι-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystals
nodes.statement: E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) is ι-real if for every closed point x the coefficients of det(1 − tF_x | E_x) map under ι into R (equivalently the eigenvalues of F_x on E_x ⊗_ι C occur in complex-conjugate pairs); E is ι-realizable if it is a direct summand of an ι-real overconvergent F-isocrystal. If E is ι-pure of weight w then E ⊕ E^∨(−w) is ι-real, so E is ι-realizable.
hypotheses: ι : K^alg ↪ C fixed; E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K).
proofSteps: Purity implies realizability: at each x the eigenvalues of E^∨(−w) are q^{wd}/α = ι^{−1}(conj ι(α)) because |ι(α)|^2 = q^{wd}; so the characteristic polynomial of E ⊕ E^∨(−w) at x has ι-real coefficients (RD.6/pointwise-iota-weights, RD.6/tate-twist-of-f-isocrystals).

nodes.title: Rank-one overconvergent F-isocrystals are ι-pure
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth irreducible F_q-variety and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) of rank 1. Then (i) there is n ≥ 1 with E^{⊗n} constant on X (spanned by horizontal sections); (ii) E is ι-pure of some weight, for every ι.
hypotheses: X smooth irreducible over F_q; E of rank 1.
proofSteps: (i) By Tsuzuki's theorem (Kedlaya Proposition 6.1.2; Crew for curves), there is a proper dominant generically finite étale f : Y → X, which may be taken Galois with group G of order n, such that f^*E is constant; G acts on H^0_rig(V/K, f^*E) (V = f^{−1}(U), U the étale locus) by a character χ and on H^0 of f^*E^{⊗n} by χ^n = 1, so horizontal sections of E^{⊗n} descend to U; extend over X by Étesse's theorem, or work on U (sufficient for the applications). Tsuzuki's and Étesse's proofs are not publicly available here (recorded gap).

(ii) E^{⊗n}|_U ≅ O ⊗ (rank-one object with scalar Frobenius c ∈ K^alg on H^0); at each closed point x of degree d, F_x(E)^n = c^d, so |ι(F_x)| = |ι(c)|^{d/n} and E is ι-pure of weight (2/n)·log_q|ι(c)| (RD.6/pointwise-iota-weights).
acceptance: The Dwork isocrystal: L_π^{⊗p} ≅ O, so L_π is ι-pure of weight 0.
K(−1) ⊗ L_π is ι-pure of weight 2.

nodes.title: ι-determinantal weights
nodes.statement: For an absolutely irreducible E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) of rank d on a smooth irreducible X, the ι-determinantal weight is (1/d) times the ι-weight of the rank-one object ∧^d E (well defined by RD.6/rank-one-isocrystals-are-pure). For general E the ι-determinantal weights are those of its absolutely irreducible Jordan–Hölder constituents (after finite extension of F_q, k and K, with the normalisation by the degree of the extension); E is purely of ι-determinantal weight α if all of them equal α.
hypotheses: X smooth irreducible over F_q; ι fixed.
proofSteps: ∧^d E has rank one, hence is ι-pure of a single weight.

Jordan–Hölder constituents of (σ, ∇)-modules exist (submodules closed under F and ∇ are direct summands as A-modules, Kedlaya Finiteness Lemma 3.3.4), and absolute irreducibility is attained after finite extension.

nodes.title: The global monodromy group G_M
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth irreducible affine F_q-variety with a rational point x, A a dagger algebra of MW-type with special fibre X, and M an absolutely semisimple (σ, ∇)-module over A. Let C_M be the category of finite locally free A-modules with connection isomorphic (as modules with connection, without Frobenius) to subquotients of M^a ⊗ (M^∨)^b, and G_M ⊆ GL(M_x) the algebraic subgroup of elements commuting with all morphisms of C_M. Then N ↦ N_x is an equivalence C_M ≅ Rep_K(G_M) (Tannaka duality for the neutral Tannakian category C_M with fibre functor at x). For n ≥ 1, W_n is the semidirect product of G_M with the group generated by F^n, with deg : W_n → Z.
hypotheses: X smooth irreducible affine with x ∈ X(F_q); M absolutely semisimple.
proofSteps: C_M is a neutral Tannakian category over K with fibre functor N ↦ N_x (Hom spaces are finite-dimensional and commute with base extension).

Tannaka reconstruction: the automorphism group scheme of the fibre functor and the equivalence with its representations are supplied by MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.6 (Saavedra; Deligne–Milne), with the comodule dictionary of the Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups roadmap, Layer 1.
Irreducible N ∈ C_M give absolutely irreducible representations N_x; G_M acts trivially on constant objects.
F acts on C_M by σ-pullback, normalising G_M; this defines W_n.
acceptance: For M constant, G_M is trivial.
For M = L_π on A^1 (with a rational base point), G_M = μ_p.

sources.excerpt: The functor from CM to the category of finite dimensional representations of GM taking N ∈ CM to Nx is an equivalence of categories.
(We crucially do not assume they are stable under Frobenius.)
Taking the automorphism group of the resulting fiber functor yields a linear algebraic group G(E) over Qp , called the geometric monodromy group of E.

nodes.title: N/GZ is finite for an absolutely semisimple algebraic group
nodes.statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field K of characteristic 0 and G ⊆ GL(V) an algebraic subgroup acting absolutely semisimply on V, with normaliser N and centraliser Z in GL(V). Then N/GZ is finite.
hypotheses: char K = 0; G acts absolutely semisimply.
proofSteps: Reduce to K algebraically closed and V irreducible, so Z is the scalars by Schur; in characteristic 0 finiteness of N/GZ is equivalent to the Lie algebra equality n = g + z (Lie algebras of algebraic groups: Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups roadmap, Layers 2–3; recorded request).

g ∩ sl is nondegenerate for the trace form: the radical h is an ideal; by Cartan's criterion (mathlib:LieModule.isNilpotent_derivedSeries_of_traceForm_eq_zero) and Engel's theorem (mathlib:LieModule.isNilpotent_iff_forall), [h, h] kills a nonzero g-stable subspace, so by irreducibility h is abelian with a single joint eigenspace, i.e. h ⊆ z.
Hence gl = g ⊕ g^⊥; for n ∈ n ∩ g^⊥ and x ∈ g, [n, x] ∈ g is orthogonal to g and to g^⊥, so [n, x] = 0 and n ∈ z.
acceptance: G = SL_2 on K^2: N = GL_2 = G·Z, so N/GZ is trivial.
G = the diagonal torus in GL_2 (semisimple action): N/GZ ≅ S_2.

sources.excerpt: Then N/GZ is finite; in other words, the group of outer automorphisms of G induced by N is finite.
Then the claim is precisely that we have an equality of Lie algebras n = g + z.

nodes.title: Some power of Frobenius acts on G_M by an inner automorphism
nodes.statement: In the situation of RD.6/global-monodromy-group, there is n ≥ 1 such that conjugation by F^n on G_M is inner; consequently W_n splits as a product of G_M and Z (generated by a central element of positive degree), and some power of F respects the Jordan–Hölder decompositions of all M^a ⊗ (M^∨)^b simultaneously.
hypotheses: M absolutely semisimple; G_M as constructed.
proofSteps: Conjugation by F lies in the normaliser of G_M in GL(M_x); by RD.6/normaliser-over-centraliser-finite its image in N/(G_M·Z) has finite order n, so F^n ∈ G_M·Z and W_n ≅ G_M × Z.

nodes.title: Determinantal weights via central elements of W_1
nodes.statement: For N ∈ C_M with its Frobenius structure: N is purely of ι-determinantal weight α iff for some (equivalently any) central element z of W_1 of degree m > 0, every eigenvalue λ of z on N_x satisfies |ι(λ)| = q^{mα/2}.
hypotheses: M absolutely semisimple; N ∈ C_M.
proofSteps: Reduce to N absolutely irreducible; by Schur z acts on N_x by a scalar, so it suffices to treat the top exterior power P (rank one).

By RD.6/rank-one-isocrystals-are-pure, P^{⊗l} is constant for some l, so G_M acts trivially on P_x^{⊗l} and z, F^m agree there; on P they differ by an l-th root of unity, so |ι(λ)| = q^{mα/2} iff P is ι-pure of weight α.

nodes.title: Determinantal weights under finite pullback, tensor products and exterior powers
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth irreducible affine over F_q and E, F overconvergent F-isocrystals on X. (i) For f : Y → X finite, E is purely of ι-determinantal weight α iff f^*E is. (ii) If E, F are purely of determinantal weights β, γ then E ⊗ F is purely of weight β + γ. (iii) If n(β) is the total rank of the constituents of E of determinantal weight β, the determinantal weights of ∧^d E are the numbers Σ_β a(β)β with 0 ≤ a(β) ≤ n(β) and Σ a(β) = d.
hypotheses: X smooth irreducible affine over F_q.
proofSteps: All three follow from the characterisation by central elements of W_1 (RD.6/determinantal-weight-via-central-frobenius): the eigenvalues of z on tensor products and exterior powers are products of eigenvalues, and pullback along finite maps changes z by a power (Crew, Proposition 5.7, as reproved by Kedlaya).
acceptance: E = K(−1), F = K(−2): E ⊗ F has determinantal weight 6.

nodes.title: Rankin squaring: fibres of ι-real isocrystals on curves are weakly mixed of weight ≤ the largest determinantal weight
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over F_q, E an ι-real overconvergent F-isocrystal on X, and r the largest ι-determinantal weight of E. Then every fibre E_x is weakly ι-mixed of weight ≤ r.
hypotheses: X smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over F_q; E ι-real.
proofSteps: The trace formula (RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula) for E^{⊗2i}, i ≥ 1, gives ι det(1 − tF | H^1_c(E^{⊗2i})) / ι det(1 − tF | H^2_c(E^{⊗2i})) = ∏_x ι det(1 − t^{deg x}F_x | E_x^{⊗2i})^{−1}; H^0_c = 0 on an affine curve.

Each local factor has nonnegative real coefficients since Tr(F_x^n | E_x^{⊗2i}) = Tr(F_x^n | E_x^{⊗i})^2 ≥ 0 (ι-reality); so the radius of convergence of the left side is ≤ |ι(α)|^{−2i/deg x} for every eigenvalue α of F_x (positive-coefficient series lemma, requested from DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.2).

The radius is ≥ the smallest |ι|-norm of eigenvalues of F^{−1} on H^2_c(E^{⊗2i}); by Poincaré duality (RD.5/poincare-duality) these are eigenvalues of F on H^0_rig(E^{⊗−2i})(1), which is weakly ι-mixed of weight ≥ −2ir by RD.6/determinantal-weights-functoriality(ii) and H^0 ↪ fibre.
Hence |ι(α)| ≤ q^{deg(x)(ir+1)/(2i)}; let i → ∞.
acceptance: E = O on A^1: r = 0 and all fibres have F_x = 1 (weight 0 ≤ 0).

sources.excerpt: Let E be an ι-real overconvergent F -isocrystal on a curve X, and let r be the largest of its ι-determinantal weights. Then Ex is weakly ι-mixed of weight ≤ r.

nodes.title: Constituents of ι-real isocrystals on curves are ι-pure
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over F_q. The constituents of an ι-real overconvergent F-isocrystal on X are all ι-pure; in particular every irreducible ι-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystal on X is ι-pure of some weight.
hypotheses: X a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over F_q; E ι-real (resp. irreducible ι-realizable).
proofSteps: For β a determinantal weight, let E_β be the sum of constituents of weight β, n(γ) the rank of those of weight γ > β, and N = Σ_{γ>β} n(γ).

The highest determinantal weight of ∧^{N+1}E is β + Σ_{γ>β} n(γ)γ (RD.6/determinantal-weights-functoriality (iii)), so by RD.6/rankin-squaring-bound ∧^{N+1}E is weakly ι-mixed of weight ≤ β + Σ n(γ)γ; an eigenvalue λ of F_x on (E_β)_x times the determinants of the higher constituents is an eigenvalue of ∧^{N+1}E, giving |ι(λ)| ≤ q^{β deg(x)/2}.
The same for E^∨ gives the reverse inequality; so E_β is ι-pure of weight β.
acceptance: O is pure of weight 0; the Dwork isocrystal (irreducible, ι-realizable) is pure of weight 0.

nodes.title: The weight drop lemma
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over F_q and E ι-pure of weight w. Then H^1_{c,rig}(X/K, E) is weakly ι-mixed of weight ≤ w + 2.
hypotheses: X smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve; E ι-pure of weight w.
proofSteps: Apply ι to the trace formula (RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula): ∏_x ∏_α (1 − t^{deg x}ι(α))^{−1} = ι det(1 − tF | H^1_c) / ι det(1 − tF | H^2_c).

#X(F_{q^n}) ≤ C q^n (X contains a dense open finite étale over an open of A^1, by the geometric lemma of RD.5), so Σ_x Σ_α |ι(α)||t|^{deg x} ≤ C' Σ_n q^n q^{nw/2}|t|^n converges for |t| < q^{−(w+2)/2}; the Euler product converges absolutely and has no zeros there.

H^0_rig(X/K, E^∨) is ι-pure of weight −w (RD.6/pointwise-iota-weights), so by Poincaré duality (RD.5/poincare-duality) H^2_c(E) is ι-pure of weight w + 2 and det(1 − tF | H^2_c) has no zeros in |t| < q^{−(w+2)/2}.
Hence ι det(1 − tF | H^1_c) has no zeros there, i.e. H^1_c is weakly ι-mixed of weight ≤ w + 2.
acceptance: E = O on G_m: H^1_c(G_m) = K has weight 0 ≤ 2.

nodes.title: Local invariants of a pure isocrystal are weakly mixed of weight ≤ w
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over F_q and E ι-pure of weight w. Then H^0_loc(X/K, E) (horizontal sections at the points at infinity) is weakly ι-mixed of weight ≤ w.
hypotheses: X smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve; E ι-pure of weight w.
proofSteps: The exact sequence H^0_rig(X/K, E) → H^0_loc(X/K, E) → H^1_{c,rig}(X/K, E) (Kedlaya (2.6.1), from the curve cohomology of RD.5) with H^0_rig pure of weight w and H^1_c weakly mixed ≤ w + 2 (RD.6/weight-drop-lemma) shows H^0_loc is weakly mixed ≤ w + 2.
Applied to E^{⊗n} (pure of weight nw): H^0_loc(E^{⊗n}) ⊇ H^0_loc(E)^{⊗n} is weakly mixed ≤ nw + 2, so H^0_loc(E) is weakly mixed ≤ w + 2/n for all n.

nodes.title: Local invariants are strongly mixed: equal-characteristic local weight–monodromy
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over F_q and E ι-pure of weight w. Then H^0_loc(X/K, E) is (strongly) ι-mixed of weight ≤ w; more precisely, at each point at infinity where E is unipotent with nilpotent residue N, the space W = ker N carries the F-stable filtration W_i = W ∩ im N^i with W_i/W_{i+1} ι-pure of weight w − i.
hypotheses: X smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve; E ι-pure of weight w.
proofSteps: Pass to a finite cover and enlarge q, K so that E is unipotent at each point at infinity (p-adic local monodromy theorem, RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement) and those points are rational.
On a unipotent basis the residue operator acts by a nilpotent matrix N on V (RD.2/unipotent-differential-module), and with the Frobenius lift t ↦ t^q one has NF = qFN.
W_i ⊗ W_i(−i) injects into (ker N) ⊗ V/ker N^i ⊂ H^0_loc(E ⊗ E), which is weakly mixed ≤ 2w (RD.6/local-invariants-weakly-mixed); so W_i is weakly mixed ≤ w − i.
The dual construction gives W_i^∨ weakly mixed ≤ −w − i, and the perfect pairing W_i/W_{i+1} ⊗ W_i^∨(−i) → K shows W_i/W_{i+1} is pure of weight w − i.
acceptance: If E is unipotent at the point with N = 0, then W = V and W/W_1 = V is ι-pure of weight w.

Model degeneration: V of rank 2 with N ≠ 0 and E ι-pure of weight 1 (H^1 of a family of elliptic curves near a multiplicative fibre): W = ker N = im N is ι-pure of weight 0 = w − 1, as for the ℓ-adic Tate curve.

nodes.title: Purity of H^1 on the affine line via the Fourier transform
nodes.statement: Let M be an absolutely irreducible (σ, ∇)-module over K⟨x⟩† which is ι-pure of weight w, and suppose there is d ≥ 0 such that for every finite extension K' of K and every a in its ring of integers: dim H^0_loc(M' ⊗ L_{ax}) = dim H^1_loc(M' ⊗ L_{ax}) = 0 and dim H^1(M' ⊗ L_{ax}) = d (M' = M ⊗_K K'). Then H^1(M) and H^1_c(M) are ι-pure of weight w + 1.
hypotheses: M absolutely irreducible, ι-pure of weight w; the stated local and global dimension conditions for all twists L_{ax}.
proofSteps: Assume π ∈ K and w = 0 (twist); then M and M^∨ have complex-conjugate trace functions, and so do M' ⊗ L_{ax} and (M')^∨ ⊗ L_{−ax}.

With H^0_loc = H^1_loc = 0 the forget-supports map H^1_c → H^1 is an isomorphism (exact sequence (2.6.1)); duality gives a perfect Frobenius-equivariant pairing H^1(M' ⊗ L_{ax}) × H^1((M')^∨ ⊗ L_{−ax}) → K'(−1).

By RD.6/fourier-transform-rank-and-irreducibility, M̂ and the transform of M^∨ are absolutely irreducible (σ, ∇)-modules of rank d; M̂ and the pullback of M^∨̂ along x ↦ −x have conjugate trace functions, so their sum is ι-real.
By RD.6/iota-real-constituents-are-pure (on A^1), each is ι-pure of a weight j; the pairing into K(−1) (weight 2) forces j + j = 2, so j = 1, and the fibre at s = 0 is H^1(M) ≅ H^1_c(M).
acceptance: M = L_{x^d} with p ∤ d ≥ 2 (absolutely irreducible, ι-pure of weight 0): the twists L_{x^d + ax} have H^0_loc = H^1_loc = 0 and dim H^1 = d − 1 for all a, so H^1(A^1, L_{x^d}) is ι-pure of weight 1, the rigid form of |Σ_x ψ(x^d)| ≤ (d − 1)√q (FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.2/weil-bound-additive).
M = O fails the hypothesis at a ≡ 0 mod π (H^0_loc ≠ 0), consistent with H^1(A^1) = 0.

nodes.title: Rigid Weil II on the affine line
nodes.statement: Let E be an overconvergent F-isocrystal on A^1_{F_q} which is ι-realizable and ι-mixed of weight ≥ w. Then H^1_rig(A^1/K, E) is ι-mixed of weight ≥ w + 1.
hypotheses: E ι-realizable and (pointwise) ι-mixed of weight ≥ w on A^1.
proofSteps: Enlarge k and reduce to M absolutely irreducible; by RD.6/iota-real-constituents-are-pure M is ι-pure, of weight w after twisting.

nodes.title: Rigid Weil II over a point (Kedlaya)
nodes.statement: Let X be a separated scheme of finite type over F_q, ι : K^alg ↪ C, and E an ι-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystal on X. (a) If E is (pointwise) ι-mixed of weight ≤ w, then for each i, H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) is ι-mixed of weight ≤ w + i. (b) If X is smooth and E is ι-mixed of weight ≥ w, then for each i, H^i_rig(X/K, E) is ι-mixed of weight ≥ w + i. The hypothesis 'ι-realizable' holds whenever E is a successive extension of ι-pure objects (the global notion of the notes, Definition 10.2), in particular for constant coefficients, for every ι.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over F_q (smooth in (b)); E ι-realizable; ι arbitrary.
proofSteps: Induction on n = dim X, then on rank E, for all q simultaneously.

(b) ⇒ (a) by Poincaré duality (RD.5/poincare-duality); by excision (RD.4/excision-sequence) and induction, (a) reduces to X smooth affine of pure dimension n, and by duality again to (b) for X or any open dense subset.

Enlarge K and twist to w = 0; by the geometric lemma (RD.5) an open dense affine U is finite étale over A^n, and H^i(U, E) = H^i(A^n, f_*E) (finite étale pushforward, RD.4), so X = A^n; reduce to E irreducible by the long exact sequence.

Write A^n = A^1 × A^{n−1}, f the projection; over an open dense W ⊂ A^{n−1} the kernel F_0 and cokernel F_1 of the vertical connection are overconvergent F-isocrystals (generic pushforward theorem, RD.5); if F_0 ≠ 0 then E = f^*F_0 and induction applies; else F_0 = 0.

ι-realizability of F_1: choose E' with E ⊕ E' ι-real and semisimple; by the trace formula (RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula) the fibre traces of F_1 ⊕ F_1' minus those of F_0' are ι-real, so F_1 is ι-realizable.

By RD.6/weil-ii-on-affine-line on the fibres, F_1 is ι-mixed of weight ≥ 1; by induction H^{i−1}_rig(W, F_1) is mixed ≥ i; since F_0 = 0 the Leray sequence (Kedlaya Finiteness Proposition 7.4.1, RD.5) gives a Frobenius-equivariant injection H^i_rig(X/K, E) ↪ H^{i−1}_rig(W/K, F_1), which gives (b) on X (Kedlaya prints f_*E^∨ in place of E here; see sourceIssues).
acceptance: G_m, constant coefficients: H^1_c weight 0 ≤ 0 + 1 and H^1 weight 2 ≥ 0 + 1 (RD.6/multiplicative-group-mixed-weights).
P^1: H^0 weight 0, H^2 weight 2 = 0 + 2 (RD.6/projective-line-frobenius-eigenvalues).

nodes.statement: Let X be smooth proper of pure dimension n over F_q, P_i(t) := det(1 − tF | H^i_rig(X/K)) and b_i := deg P_i = dim H^i. Then P_{2n−i}(t) = c_i · t^{b_i} · P_i(q^{−n} t^{−1}) with c_i = (−1)^{b_i} q^{n b_i} / det(F | H^i_rig(X/K)). (Kedlaya prints P_{2n−i}(t) = c t^j P_i(t^{−1}), omitting q^{−n}; see sourceIssues.)

nodes.statement: An element α ∈ K^alg has slope s ∈ Q if |α| = |q^s|, i.e. v_q(α) := v_p(α)/v_p(q) = s. An overconvergent F-isocrystal E on an F_q-scheme X has slopes in [r, s] if for every closed point x of degree d the eigenvalues of F_x on E_x have slopes in [dr, ds]. nodes.title: The Gysin sequence of a punctured smooth proper curve
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth proper curve over F_q, D ⊂ X a nonempty reduced finite closed subscheme and Y = X − D. There is a Frobenius-equivariant exact sequence 0 → H^1_rig(X/K) → H^1_rig(Y/K) → ⊕_{x ∈ |D|} H^0_rig(x/K)^∨(−1) → H^2_rig(X/K) → H^2_rig(Y/K) → 0, whose first map is restriction. If D meets every connected component of X (equivalently Y is affine), then H^2_rig(Y/K) = 0.
hypotheses: X smooth proper curve over F_q; D reduced, finite, nonempty; Y = X − D.
proofSteps: Compact-support excision for D ⊂ X (RD.4/excision-sequence): 0 → H^0_c(Y) → H^0(X) → H^0(D) → H^1_c(Y) → H^1(X) → H^1(D) = 0 → H^2_c(Y) → H^2(X) → 0, Frobenius-equivariant (X proper: H_c = H; D has dimension 0, RD.6/rigid-cohomology-of-a-finite-field-point).

Dualise with Frobenius-equivariant Poincaré duality on the smooth curves X and Y (RD.5/poincare-duality): H^j(Y) ≅ H^{2−j}_c(Y)^∨(−1), H^j(X) ≅ H^{2−j}(X)^∨(−1); the dual of H^0(D) → H^1_c(Y) → H^1(X) → 0 twisted by (−1) gives the displayed sequence (duality is natural for restriction/excision).

If D meets every component, H^0(X) → H^0(D) is injective (a horizontal section vanishing at a point of a connected component vanishes, RD.6/pointwise-iota-weights h0 embedding), so H^0_c(Y) = 0 and H^2(Y) = 0.

nodes.title: Weights 1 and 2 of Frobenius on H^1 of a smooth affine curve
nodes.statement: Let X_k be a smooth proper curve over F_q, D_k ⊂ X_k a nonempty reduced finite closed subscheme meeting every connected component, and Y_k = X_k − D_k (a smooth affine curve). Let F be the F_q-linear (q-power) Frobenius on H^1_rig(Y_k/K). Then every eigenvalue of F is a Weil q-number: those on the image of H^1_rig(X_k/K) (a subspace of dimension 2g, g the genus when X_k is geometrically connected) have weight 1, and those on the quotient, which embeds in the residue part ⊕_{x ∈ |D_k|} H^0_rig(x/K)^∨(−1) ('K(−1)^{(D)}'), are of the form q·ζ with ζ a root of unity (weight 2). In particular no eigenvalue of F is a root of unity, and for every n, m ≥ 1 no product of n eigenvalues has a power equal to 1.
hypotheses: X_k smooth proper curve over F_q; D_k nonempty reduced finite, meeting every component; K with residue field F_q, σ_K = id.
proofSteps: RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves gives 0 → H^1(X_k) → H^1(Y_k) → ⊕_x H^0(x)^∨(−1), Frobenius-equivariant, so the eigenvalues of F on H^1(Y_k) are those on H^1(X_k) together with some of those on ⊕_x H^0(x)^∨(−1).

H^0_rig(x/K) for x of degree d is K_x with F the generator of Gal(K_x/K): eigenvalues the d-th roots of unity (RD.6/rigid-cohomology-of-a-finite-field-point); on the dual they are inverted and the twist (−1) multiplies by q (RD.6/tate-twist-of-f-isocrystals): eigenvalues qζ, Weil numbers of weight 2.
H^1(X_k) is ι-pure of weight 1 for every ι (RD.6/purity-smooth-proper), so its eigenvalues are Weil q-numbers of weight 1 (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0).
A Weil number of weight w ≥ 1 has all conjugates of absolute value q^{w/2} > 1, so no product of positive-weight Weil numbers has a power equal to 1.

nodes.title: The rational rigid–crystalline comparison for smooth proper varieties
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], and X a smooth proper k-scheme. There is a canonical isomorphism H^i_rig(X/K_0) ≅ H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗_W K_0 for every i, functorial in X, and compatible with finite extension of scalars: H^i_rig(X/K) = H^i_rig(X/K_0) ⊗_{K_0} K for K/K_0 finite. Here H^i_crys(X/W) is the crystalline cohomology of CrystallineCohomology:CR.3 (finitely generated over W; only its tensor product with K_0 is used). With coefficients: for an F-crystal M of finite locally free modules with associated convergent (= overconvergent, X proper) F-isocrystal E, H^i(X_crys, M) ⊗ Q ≅ H^i_rig(X, E) (Ogus).
hypotheses: k perfect; X smooth and proper over k; W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p].
proofSteps: X proper: the compactification is X itself, so strict neighbourhoods are trivial and rigid cohomology equals Berthelot's naive cohomology H^i(]X[_P, Ω^•) for a closed embedding X ↪ P into a formal W-scheme smooth near X (Berthelot (2.4); RD.4/rigid-cohomology; independence of P, RD.3/independence-of-frame). For non-embeddable X use a Čech covering by embeddable opens (Berthelot (1.5)).
Crystalline cohomology is computed by the p-adically completed de Rham complex of the PD envelope of X in P (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2), with independence of the embedding.

Comparison map (Berthelot Proposition 2): the rational PD envelope maps to functions on a tube of radius |p|^{1/(p−1)} contained in ]X[_P; by Berthelot's Lemma 1 and Proposition 1 (the tube is locally a fibration in open unit polydiscs and the de Rham complex of an open polydisc is acyclic, with Theorem B), the de Rham cohomology of this smaller tube agrees with that of ]X[_P; for X smooth the resulting map H^*_naïf(X/K_0) → H^*_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0 is an isomorphism. Berthelot states this 'sans difficulté'; the detailed proof (Berthelot, LNM 407 and Berthelot–Ogus) is not in the public sources read (recorded gap).
Functoriality in X and base change in K follow from functoriality of both constructions in the embedding.
acceptance: P^1: H^0 = K_0, H^1 = 0, H^2 = K_0 on both sides; H^2_crys(P^1/W) = W with Frobenius p, matching H^2_rig = K_0(−1) for q = p.
Elliptic curve E/F_p: both H^1 are 2-dimensional, with the same characteristic polynomial T^2 − a_p T + p of Frobenius (RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison).

nodes.title: The comparison matches the q-Frobenius with the f-th iterate of crystalline Frobenius
nodes.statement: Let k = F_q with q = p^f, W = W(F_q), K_0 = W[1/p], X smooth proper over F_q, and φ the σ-semilinear crystalline Frobenius on H^i_crys(X/W) induced by the absolute Frobenius of X and the Witt vector Frobenius σ (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3). Under RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison, the linear q-Frobenius F on H^i_rig(X/K_0) (RD.6/linear-q-frobenius) corresponds to φ^f ⊗ 1. Since σ^f = id on W(F_q), φ^f is W-linear, and det(1 − tF | H^i_rig(X/K_0)) = det(1 − tφ^f | H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0).

The q-Frobenius on rigid cohomology is induced by Fr_X^f over σ^f = id (independence of the Frobenius lift, RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology; RD.6/linear-q-frobenius), and φ^f is induced by the same pair on crystalline cohomology (functoriality in CR.3), so the two agree.

nodes.title: The Weil factors are integral polynomials determined by weights
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth proper over F_q. For each i, P_i(X, t) ∈ 1 + tZ[t]; its reciprocal roots are Weil q-numbers of weight i (algebraic integers all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value q^{i/2}); P_i(X, t) = ∏_α (1 − αt)^{m(α)}, where α runs over the reciprocal zeros (i odd) or reciprocal poles (i even) of Z(X, t) of weight i and m(α) is the order; distinct P_i have no common root. Integrality is justified separately from the alternating product: it uses purity for every ι and Fatou's lemma, not the equality of zeta functions alone.
hypotheses: X smooth proper over F_q.
proofSteps: Z(X, t) = ∏ P_i^{(−1)^{i+1}} (RD.7/rigid-zeta-expression) and Z ∈ Q(t) ∩ (1 + tZ[[t]]) (WeilConjectures:WC.1).
Every reciprocal root of P_i is ι-pure of weight i for every ι : K^alg ↪ C (RD.6/purity-smooth-proper); hence algebraic over Q and a Weil q-number of weight i (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0).
Weights separate degrees: for i ≠ j no root of P_i is a root of P_j, so no cancellation occurs in the alternating product.

Weight-separated factor identification (WeilConjectures:WC.3): a factorisation of Z into polynomials with pairwise distinct pure weights is unique, each factor is the weight part of Z, is fixed by Gal(Q̄/Q) (weights are conjugation invariant) and so lies in Q[t]; by Fatou's lemma the reduced numerator and denominator of Z lie in 1 + tZ[t], so the reciprocal roots are algebraic integers and each P_i ∈ Z[t].
Consistency check: p-adic slopes of the roots lie in [0, i] (RD.6/slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology), confirming p-integrality.
acceptance: E/F_7 ordinary: P_1 = 1 − 3t + 7t^2, roots of modulus 7^{−1/2}; genus-2 curve y^2 = x^5 + x + 3 over F_7: Frobenius polynomial T^4 + 3T^3 + 7T^2 + 21T + 49 (PARI/GP hyperellcharpoly), integral, all roots of modulus √7.

nodes.title: Crystalline, rigid and ℓ-adic Weil factors agree for smooth projective varieties (Katz–Messing)
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth projective over F_q, q = p^f, and ℓ ≠ p. For every i, det(1 − tF | H^i_rig(X/K)) = det(1 − tφ^f | H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0) = det(1 − t·Frob_q | H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)) as elements of 1 + tZ[t] (Frob_q the geometric Frobenius), for every finite extension F_{q^r} as well. In particular b_i^{rig} = b_i^{crys ⊗ Q} = b_i^{ℓ}.
hypotheses: X smooth projective over F_q; ℓ ≠ p.
proofSteps: ℓ-adic side: Z(X, t) = ∏_i det(1 − t Frob_q | H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ))^{(−1)^{i+1}} for every finite extension (WeilConjectures:WC.1, common trace/zeta expression), and each factor is pure of weight i for every ι (Deligne, Weil I 1.6; DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.4).
Rigid side: RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral.
Both are weight-separated factorisations of the same Z(X, t) ∈ Q(t); by uniqueness (WeilConjectures:WC.3) the i-th factors coincide in Q[t].
Crystalline equality: RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison.

Katz and Messing proved the crystalline–ℓ-adic equality from Weil I and the crystalline trace formula; their paper is not publicly available (recorded gap); this route uses Kedlaya's p-adic purity instead.

nodes.title: A de Rham comparison over a lift does not give the finite-field Frobenius statement
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth proper over F_q with a smooth proper formal lift 𝔛 over W. Berthelot's comparison H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0 ≅ H^i_dR(𝔛/W) ⊗ K_0 identifies the vector spaces but carries no Frobenius by itself: the linear q-Frobenius on H^i_dR(𝔛/W) ⊗ K_0 is only defined by transport from crystalline or rigid cohomology, because 𝔛 in general admits no endomorphism lifting Fr_X (and X in general admits no lift at all). Hence the equality of characteristic polynomials of RD.7/weil-factor-export is a statement about crystalline/rigid Frobenius and cannot be obtained from a de Rham comparison over the lift, nor from a characteristic-zero comparison on the generic fibre alone. Example: for a supersingular elliptic curve E over F_p (p ≥ 5), no lift 𝔈 over Z_p carries an endomorphism lifting Frobenius: its pullback would preserve the Hodge line H^0(𝔈, Ω^1) and act there by a root of T^2 + p in Z_p, which does not exist; for an ordinary E the canonical lift carries one (the unit root of T^2 − a_p T + p lies in Z_p by Hensel).
hypotheses: X smooth proper over F_q with a smooth proper lift 𝔛 over W (when it exists).
proofSteps: Berthelot §1.2: for X smooth with a smooth formal lift, crystalline cohomology is de Rham cohomology of the lift (integrally if e ≤ p − 1, after ⊗K in general); the identification depends only on the lift, not on any Frobenius.

Frobenius on crystalline cohomology is induced by the absolute Frobenius of X (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3), and on rigid cohomology by any lift of Frobenius on a frame or dagger algebra (RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology); lifts exist on weak completions of affine pieces, not globally on 𝔛 (Kedlaya, point counting §2).

Supersingular example: an endomorphism Π of 𝔈 lifting Fr would act on H^1_dR(𝔈) ≅ H^1_crys(E/Z_p) as φ (functoriality of the comparison, RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison), with characteristic polynomial T^2 − a_pT + p = T^2 + p, and would preserve the line H^0(Ω^1), whose eigenvalue would be a root of T^2 + p in Z_p; there is none (v_p would be 1/2).
acceptance: Supersingular y^2 = x^3 + x over F_7: T^2 + 7 has no root in Z_7 (Newton slopes 1/2, 1/2).

Ordinary y^2 = x^3 + x + 1 over F_7: T^2 − 3T + 7 has two roots in Z_7 (reduction T(T − 3) has simple roots): a unit root u and 7/u (slopes 0, 1); the canonical-lift Frobenius acts on the Hodge line by 7/u.

nodes.title: Elliptic curves and P^1: p-adic slopes versus complex weights
nodes.statement: Let E be an elliptic curve over F_q, q = p^f, and a := q + 1 − #E(F_q). Then P_1(E, t) = 1 − at + qt^2; both reciprocal roots have complex absolute value q^{1/2} (weight 1) for every embedding; their p-adic slopes (valuations normalised by v_p(q)) are {0, 1} if p ∤ a (ordinary) and {1/2, 1/2} if p | a (supersingular). For P^1 the eigenvalues 1 and q have weights 0, 2 and slopes 0, 1. Thus slope = weight/2 fails in general: slopes are not determined by weights, and both are needed to pin down eigenvalues (an eigenvalue with |ι(α)| = q^{w/2} for all ι and slope w/2 is q^{w/2} times a root of unity).
hypotheses: E an elliptic curve over F_q.
proofSteps: P_1 from RD.7/weil-factor-export (degree 2 = b_1; P_0, P_2 as for P^1 by Poincaré duality).
Weights: RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral (purity for every ι).

Slopes: Newton polygon of T^2 − aT + q (RD.1/frobenius-slopes; RD.6/slope-interval-of-isocrystal); v_p(q) = f; p ∤ a gives slopes 0 and 1; p | a with |a| ≤ 2√q gives both roots of valuation f/2 (for q = p ≥ 5, a = 0), i.e. slope 1/2.
Slope bounds [0, 1] on H^1 agree with RD.6/slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology.
acceptance: PARI/GP ellap and newtonpoly: y^2 = x^3 + x + 1 over F_7: a = 3, P = x^2 − 3x + 7, slopes (1, 0); over F_5: a = −3, slopes (1, 0); y^2 = x^3 + 2x + 3 over F_13: a = −4, slopes (1, 0); y^2 = x^3 + x over F_7 and F_11: a = 0, slopes (1/2, 1/2); all roots have modulus √p.
y^2 = x^3 + x over F_49: a = −14, P = (x + 7)^2 (brute-force count #E(F_49) = 64); α = −7 = −q^{1/2} has slope 1/2 and weight 1, and α/q^{1/2} = −1 is a root of unity (Kedlaya §1.5).

nodes.title: Certified point counting by Kedlaya's algorithm: precision and integral reconstruction
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, q = p^n, Q ∈ F_q[x] squarefree of degree 2g + 1, C the smooth projective curve y^2 = Q(x) and A the dagger algebra of C' = C − div(y) with the Frobenius lift σ of Kedlaya (x ↦ x^p, y ↦ y^σ by a binomial series). What the source proves, with corrections: (i) q^i + 1 − #C(F_{q^i}) = Tr(q^i F^{−i} | H^1(A; K)^−) (RD.6/monsky-washnitzer-fixed-point-formula); (ii) the characteristic polynomial T^{2g} + a_1T^{2g−1} + ⋯ + a_{2g} of F on H^1(A; K)^− is the Frobenius polynomial of C, with a_{2g−i} = q^{g−i} a_i (printed 'a_i = a_{2g−i}') and |a_i| ≤ C(2g, i) q^{i/2} ≤ 2^{2g} q^{g/2} (RD.7/weil-factor-export); (iii) integral reconstruction: a_1, …, a_g ∈ Z are determined by their residues modulo p^{N_1} once p^{N_1} > 2·max_i C(2g, i)q^{i/2}, which holds for N_1 ≥ (g/2)n + (2g + 1) log_p 2; (iv) Lemma 2: the reduction of A(x) dx/y^{2m+1} (deg A ≤ 2g) becomes integral after multiplying by p^{⌊log_p(2m+1)⌋}; (v) Lemma 3 as printed is incorrect; the corrected statement (Kedlaya's errata, J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 18 (2003) 417–418, as quoted by Harvey) multiplies by p^{⌊log_p((2g+1)(e+2) − 2)⌋} for F_j(x) y^{e} dx with e = −p(2k+1) + 2j; (vi) the q-Frobenius matrix is M M^σ ⋯ M^{σ^{n−1}} for the p-Frobenius matrix M. The running time is O(g^{4+ε} n^{3+ε}) with a rational Weierstrass point. The source does not prove that the Frobenius matrix is integral on the basis x^i dx/y; the working precision must absorb the denominators bounded in (iv)–(v).
hypotheses: p odd; Q squarefree of degree 2g + 1 over F_q; C with a rational Weierstrass point at infinity.
proofSteps: (i) from the Monsky–Washnitzer trace formula applied to C' and its quotient by the hyperelliptic involution (the correct count of removed points is #C'(F_{q^i}) = #C(F_{q^i}) − 1 − r_i with r_i the number of roots of Q in F_{q^i}; the printed intermediate counts are corrected in sourceIssues).

(ii) from RD.7/weil-factor-export applied to C (integrality, purity, functional equation), transported to H^1(A; K)^− ≅ H^1_rig(C/K) (RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves: removing the 2g + 2 points adds only the + part).
(iii) an integer a with |a| ≤ B is determined by a mod p^N if p^N > 2B (symmetric residue).
(iv)–(v) by local expansion at the Weierstrass points and at infinity (Kedlaya Lemma 2; the corrected Lemma 3 is proved as Lemma 4.3.5 of Edixhoven's notes, not read; recorded gap).
acceptance: PARI/GP: C: y^2 = x^5 + x + 3 over F_7 (g = 2): Frobenius polynomial T^4 + 3T^3 + 7T^2 + 21T + 49; a_3 = 21 = 7·a_1 and a_4 = 49 = 7^2 (the corrected relation), while the printed a_1 = a_3 fails; |a_i| ≤ C(4, i)·7^{i/2} for all i; N_1 = ⌈1 + 5 log_7 2⌉ = 3 and 7^3 = 343 > 84 = 2·max C(4, i)7^{i/2}, and a_1, a_2 are recovered from their residues mod 343; #C(F_7) = 11 by brute force = 8 − (−3).
PARI/GP: for the same curve #C'(F_{7^k}) = #C − 1 − r_k gives 10, 54, 370 for k = 1, 2, 3, while the printed #C − 2g gives 7, 51, 367.

gaps.title: Cyclic vector lemma: elementary proof for arbitrary constant fields not read
gaps.detail: The public proof read (Magid, arXiv:2212.04643v2) assumes algebraically closed constants and uses Picard-Vessiot theory, which no library has; the node reduces the general case to it by a descent argument written here (constants are algebraically closed in F, F ⊗_C C^alg is a field, and a nonvanishing polynomial determinant has a point in C^m). The elementary proofs cited by Kedlaya (Dwork-Gerotto-Sullivan Theorem III.4.2; Kedlaya's book Theorem 5.4.2) and Katz's explicit algorithm (Amer. J. Math. 109 (1987) 65-70) were not available. NEXT ACTION: read Katz 1987 or Churchill-Kovacic 'Cyclic vectors' (2002) and replace the Picard-Vessiot route by Katz's formula.

gaps.title: Overconvergence of Dwork's splitting function exp(π(x − x^p)): no public proof read
gaps.detail: Kedlaya (Weil II Remark 4.2.3) states it as 'an observation of Dwork'. The standard proof (integrality of the Artin-Hasse exponential by Dwork's lemma, then exp(πx − πx^p) = E(πx)·exp(−Σ_{j≥2}(πx)^{p^j}/p^j), giving radius ≥ p^{(p−1)/p^2}) was not read in a public source. PARI/GP confirms v_p(c_n) ≥ n(p−1)/p^2 for n ≤ 120 (p = 3) and n ≤ 60 (p = 5). NEXT ACTION: find a public account of Dwork's lemma for the Artin-Hasse exponential (e.g. lecture notes on p-adic analysis) and cite it.

gaps.title: Proof interiors of Kedlaya-Xiao Theorems 2.2.5-2.5.2 and of Arabia's Sections 1-2 not read

NEXT ACTION: read Kedlaya-Xiao Sections 2.2-2.5 and Arabia Sections 1-2 and split the nodes accordingly.

Math. 120 (1998) 1165-1190, Theorem 5.1.1 (= Theorem 4.2.6 as cited in SFR Theorem 7.2.5), not public.
