requests.need: For every complete nonarchimedean field K of characteristic 0 with residue field of characteristic p (discretely valued here; residue field not assumed perfect) and every interval I ⊆ (0, 1] (closed, open or half-open): the K-algebra of Laurent series Σ_{n∈Z} a_n t^n converging on the annulus {|t| ∈ I}, with its multiplicative ρ-Gauss norms |·|_ρ (ρ ∈ I), its Fréchet topology, and the injective restriction maps with dense image for I ⊆ J; the Robba ring R_K = colim_{r→1} (functions on r < |t| < 1) with its LF topology; the bounded subring R^bd (bounded coefficients) and the integral subring R^int (coefficients in O_K); the integral Amice ring O_E = {Σ a_n t^n : a_n ∈ O_K, a_n → 0 as n → −∞} with its π-adic and weak (levelwise) topologies and E = O_E[1/π]; base change along finite extensions K'/K. P7's cyclotomic Frobenius and Γ-action are not needed; RD.0 supplies arbitrary Frobenius lifts, the algebraic structure theory (henselian DVR, units, Bézout, freeness of vector bundles) and the derivation d/dt.

Monsky-Washnitzer weak completion S† of a finitely generated O_K-algebra S (elements Σ_j p_j(x_1, …, x_n) of the π-adic completion with p_j ∈ π^j O_K[X] and deg p_j ≤ λ(j + 1)), with S/π^m ≅ S†/π^m, weak completeness, noetherianity and functoriality (a map A → B extends uniquely to A† → B†); dagger algebras K⟨x_1, …, x_n⟩† = ∪_{ρ>1} K⟨x/ρ⟩ and their quotients, and the inclusion into the Tate algebra K⟨x⟩; for S smooth, the module of continuous differentials Ω^1_{S†} (finite projective) and the overconvergent de Rham complex Ω^•_{S†} ⊗ K with its cohomology; the weak completion S†⟨T⟩† of S†[T] with the evaluations T ↦ 0, 1 and the decomposition Ω^q(S†⟨T⟩†) = S†⟨T⟩† ⊗ Ω^q(S†) ⊕ S†⟨T⟩† dT ∧ Ω^{q−1}(S†).

Formal schemes locally of finite type over Spf O_K (p-adically complete, topologically of finite type), their generic fibres P_K as rigid analytic spaces (or adic spaces) with the specialisation map sp : P_K → P (continuous, anticontinuous on opens), functoriality of (−)_K and sp in morphisms of formal schemes, compatibility with fibre products (P × P')_K = P_K × P'_K, the tube ]T[ = sp^{-1}(T) of a locally closed subset of the special fibre as an admissible open, and the closed polydisc/open polydisc of radius ρ as rigid spaces. RD.3 (frames, tubes, strict neighbourhoods, j†) is built on these.

Coherent sheaves on rigid analytic spaces with Kiehl's Theorems A and B on affinoids and on quasi-Stein spaces (in particular the tube ]X[_P of an affine P, which is quasi-Stein), and admissible coverings/gluing of coherent sheaves; also the vanishing of H^i(U, F) (i > 0) for coherent F on an open polydisc. Used for j†, the exactness of j† on coherent sheaves and the global sections of overconvergent isocrystals on affine frames.

Weakly complete (dagger) algebras K⟨x_1..x_n⟩† and their quotients with the radius-indexed presentation A† ⊗ K = colim_{λ→1} (affinoid algebra of the polydisc of radius λ^{-1}), dagger differential forms and the exterior derivative, and the notion of strict neighbourhood of an affinoid inside a larger affinoid. OWNERSHIP NOTE: F1 owns dagger algebras and affinoid strict neighbourhoods; RD.3 owns strict neighbourhoods of tubes in frames (Berthelot 2.5a) and j†, and uses F1 to identify Γ(]Y[, j†O) with A† ⊗ K. Also the rigid Quillen-Suslin statement's ring K⟨t⟩† and O⟨t⟩† (RD.3/rigid-quillen-suslin).

Separated schemes of finite type over a field k, open immersions into proper k-schemes (Nagata compactification), closures of subschemes, graph closures in products (Y'' = closure of the diagonal of X in Y × Y'), smooth morphisms and smooth loci, and finite étale morphisms; beyond what Mathlib has (Mathlib has Scheme, IsOpenImmersion, IsProper, Smooth but not Nagata's theorem).

The category F-Isoc(X/K) of convergent F-isocrystals on a k-scheme X, realised (Berthelot 1986 §4.1, Ogus) as coherent O_{]X[_P}-modules on the tube of X in a smooth formal O_K-scheme P with an integrable connection whose Taylor isomorphism converges on the tube ]X[_{P×P} of the diagonal, together with a Frobenius isomorphism; independence of P; tensor structure; and the comparison with F-crystals up to isogeny on the crystalline site (Ogus). RD.3/restriction-to-convergent lands in this category and RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent is a statement about it.

For K/Q_p finite: Berger's ring B†_rig,K and its identification with a Robba ring R_{F'}(π_K) over the maximal unramified subfield F' of K_∞ in a variable π_K (Berger Proposition 2.31 / §2.6), with the Frobenius ϕ (ϕ(π) = (1+π)^p − 1, a q = p Frobenius lift in the sense of RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring) and the derivation ∂ = (1+π) d/dπ, and the ring B†_log,K = B†_rig,K[log π]. Needed to state RD.2/berger-form-of-local-monodromy in Berger's form for R06.3.

The field of norms: for finite L/K (K/Q_p finite) the corresponding finite separable extension of the residue field k_K((π̄_K)) of B†_K, and the fact that B†_rig,L is the finite étale extension of B†_rig,K attached to it (every finite separable extension of k_K((π̄_K)) arises from some finite L/K). Needed to translate the finite Robba-ring extension of RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy into Berger's 'finite extension L/K' in RD.2/berger-form-of-local-monodromy.

Weakly complete dagger algebras over K (quotients of K⟨x_1,…,x_n⟩†) with their fringe (radius-indexed) presentations and fringe topology, dagger localisations A⟨f^{-1}⟩† and completed tensor products A ⊗̂ B, noetherianity, the MW-type (smooth reduction, regular) condition; their modules of continuous differentials Ω^i_{A/K} with exterior derivative; de Rham complexes of coherent modules with integrable connection on dagger spaces and on strict neighbourhoods; compact-support variants. RD.4/RD.5 build j†, rigid cohomology and Kedlaya's relative Robba rings on these.
The Raynaud generic fibre P_K of a formal O_K-scheme P of finite type (rigid/adic space with its G-topology) and the specialisation map sp: P_K → P_k, functorial in P; for P = P̂^n, P_K = P^{n,an}_K.

Kiehl's Theorem B: coherent sheaves on affinoid and on quasi-Stein rigid spaces have vanishing higher cohomology, and coherent sheaves on an affinoid correspond to finite modules over its algebra; acyclicity for direct images along inclusions of admissible opens used in the two-term description of RΓ_{]X[}; trace for finite étale analytic maps.
Nagata's compactification theorem for separated schemes of finite type over a field k: an open immersion into a proper k-scheme (the noetherian case of the stage's compactification statement).

de Jong's alteration theorem (Smoothness, semi-stability and alterations, Theorem 4.1) over an arbitrary field k of characteristic p: for X integral separated of finite type over k, a proper surjective generically finite X' → X with X' smooth over a finite purely inseparable extension of k (regular, with normal crossings boundary); and the construction of proper hypercoverings Y_• → X whose terms are such alterations (coskeleton method), as used by Tsuzuki (Invent. Math. 151, Section 4) and Kedlaya (Finiteness, Section 9.2).

For an algebraic function field F/k (a smooth projective curve), the identification of Kähler differentials Ω^1_{F/k} with Weil differentials compatible with residues, so that regular Kähler differentials of the curve have dimension g and principal parts of differentials at the missing points of an affine curve have one-dimensional cokernel (residue theorem).

For a separated finite-type scheme X over F_q: finiteness of the set of closed points of each degree; N_r = #X(F_{q^r}) = Σ_{m | r} m·a_m; the zeta function Z(X, t) = ∏_{x}(1 − t^{deg x})^{−1} = exp(Σ N_r t^r/r) ∈ 1 + tZ[[t]]; the determinant–exponential identity det(1 − tA)^{−1} = exp(Σ_{r ≥ 1} Tr(A^r) t^r/r) in E[[t]] for an endomorphism A of a finite-dimensional vector space over a field E of characteristic 0 (and its Euler-product form over closed points with the degree normalisation); rational descent (a power series in Q[[t]] that is rational over an extension field E ⊇ Q is in Q(t)); Fatou's lemma (a rational function in 1 + tZ[[t]] is a quotient of coprime polynomials in 1 + tZ[t]); and the ℓ-adic cohomological expression Z(X_{F_{q^r}}, t) = ∏_i det(1 − t Frob_q^r | H^i_c(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ))^{(−1)^{i+1}} for every r.

The abstract weight-separation lemma, stated for an arbitrary coefficient field E of characteristic 0 with algebraic closure Ē: if Z(t) ∈ Q(t) ∩ (1 + tZ[[t]]) and Z = ∏_{i=0}^{m} P_i^{(−1)^{i+1}} in Ē[[t]] with P_i ∈ 1 + tĒ[t] whose reciprocal roots are ι-pure of weight i for every embedding ι : Ē → C, then each P_i equals the weight-i part of Z (reciprocal zeros for odd i, poles for even i, with multiplicity), lies in 1 + tZ[t], and is independent of the presentation; in particular two such presentations (rigid with E = K p-adic, ℓ-adic with E = Q_ℓ) have equal factors.

For an arbitrary field E of characteristic 0 (in particular a p-adic field K) with an embedding ι : Ē → C and q > 1: the ι-weight predicates (ι-pure of real weight w, ι-mixed ≤ w / ≥ w with integral or real excess) on nonzero elements of Ē and on endomorphisms of finite-dimensional E-spaces (via the roots of the characteristic polynomial), with the normalisation by q^a for an F_{q^a}-structure; Weil q-numbers of integral weight; and the bridge lemma: α ∈ Ē^× is ι-pure of weight w for every embedding ι : Ē → C iff α is algebraic over Q and a Weil q-number of weight w (for |Ē| ≤ continuum).

The positive-series lemmas of Weil I §3 in the form: if a power series Σ c_n t^n with c_0 = 1 is an Euler product ∏_x f_x(t^{deg x}) of series with nonnegative real coefficients, then its radius of convergence is at most |β|^{−1/deg x} for every reciprocal root β of each local factor; and the radius of convergence of a rational function is the smallest modulus of its poles.

Deligne's Weil I Theorem 1.6 for every smooth projective X over F_q and ℓ ≠ p: every eigenvalue of geometric Frobenius on H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) is an algebraic number all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value q^{i/2}.
Deligne's Weil II (3.3.9) for every smooth proper X over F_q and ℓ ≠ p: H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) is pure of weight i for every embedding (the smooth proper non-projective case).

For a smooth scheme X over a perfect field k embedded in a p-adic formal scheme P smooth over W(k): crystalline cohomology RΓ_crys(X/W) is computed by the p-adically completed de Rham complex of the PD envelope of X in P, independently of the embedding, functorially in (X, P); and for a smooth formal lift 𝔛 of X, H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0 ≅ H^i_dR(𝔛/W) ⊗ K_0.

For X smooth proper over a perfect field k: H^i_crys(X/W(k)) finitely generated over W(k), functorial in X, with the σ-semilinear Frobenius φ induced by the absolute Frobenius of X and the Witt vector Frobenius σ, and its compatibility with the de Rham comparison of a smooth lift; for k = F_{p^f}, φ^f is W-linear.

p-adic operator theory over a complete discretely valued field K of characteristic 0: completely continuous (compact) endomorphisms of K-Banach spaces of countable type are nuclear; nuclear endomorphisms of locally convex spaces obtained as increasing unions of such Banach spaces have a trace and an entire Fredholm determinant det(1 − tθ), with Tr linear, Tr(θg) = Tr(gθ) for θ nuclear and g continuous, the Riesz decomposition for each nonzero eigenvalue with finite-dimensional generalized eigenspace, and: for a nuclear endomorphism of a bounded complex with finite-dimensional cohomology, Σ(−1)^i Tr(θ | C^i) = Σ(−1)^i Tr(θ | H^i) (van der Put (1.5)).

For a neutral Tannakian category C over a field K of characteristic 0 with fibre functor ω: the affine group scheme G = Aut^⊗(ω), algebraic when C is generated by one object, and the tensor equivalence C ≅ Rep_K(G) given by ω (Saavedra II.4.1.1; Deligne–Milne 2.11).

For an equal-characteristic local field E = κ((t)) with perfect residue field κ of characteristic p: upper-numbering ramification groups of finite Galois extensions, breaks of finite-image representations, the Swan conductor Swan(ρ) = Σ_i i·dim V(i) and its expression through the Swan function, its integrality (Hasse–Arf) and independence of the finite quotient, and the Artin–Schreier computation: for P ∈ κ[t^{−1}] of degree d prime to p, the character of κ((t))[u]/(u^p − u − P) has break d, so for ρ with all breaks < d, ρ ⊗ ψ_P has all breaks d.

Weakly complete (dagger) algebras W_n = K⟨x_1, …, x_n⟩† and their quotients: W_n is noetherian and regular of dimension n, so finitely generated modules have finite projective resolutions; fringe topology via the affinoid algebras T_{n,ρ}.

Lie algebras of affine algebraic groups over a field of characteristic 0, with the dimension formula dim G = dim Lie(G), Lie algebras of normalisers and centralisers, and the criterion that a closed subgroup H ⊆ N has finite index iff Lie(H) = Lie(N) (with Layer 3 for components and quotients). A Tau Ceti layer cannot be listed as a node prerequisite; recorded here and as a gap.

restructure.title: Robba coefficient rings: P7:annulus-foundations owns the Laurent-series rings, RD.0 their structure theory
restructure.detail: RD.0's text asks to 'build bounded and full Robba rings with their radius-indexed norms and topology', and P7:annulus-foundations asks to 'construct the bounded, overconvergent and Robba coefficient rings from actual convergent Laurent series on annuli, their norms/topologies and restriction maps'. The audit (AUDIT-37) lists P7 as a duplicate of RD.0, and the atlas edge runs P7 → RD.0, so P7 owns the carrier. P7's text is written for the cyclotomic (φ,Γ) setting, but RD needs an arbitrary complete discretely valued coefficient field K (imperfect residue fields included) and arbitrary Frobenius lifts.
restructure.proposal: P7:annulus-foundations constructs the annulus rings, R_K, R^bd, R^int, O_E and E for every complete nonarchimedean K of characteristic 0 (request recorded), with Gauss norms, topologies, restriction maps and coefficient extension. RD.0 keeps: the identification with Kedlaya's analytic rings (RD.0/robba-ring), the henselian DVR / field structure of R^int / R^bd, units, the PID and Bézout properties, freeness of vector bundles, finite separable extensions and flatness, arbitrary Frobenius lifts and their Taylor comparison, the extended Robba ring, and the derivation. P7's cyclotomic Frobenius is an instance of RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring.

restructure.title: Dagger algebras: F1 owns weak completion and overconvergent de Rham complexes, RD.0 owns Frobenius lifts on them
restructure.detail: RD.0 asks to 'construct overconvergent power-series algebras as unions over strict radii, their weak completion maps and differential forms'; AdicSpacesPartII:F1 owns 'weakly complete dagger affinoid algebras, their radius-indexed presentations', 'differential forms, exterior derivative'. F1 does not mention Frobenius lifts.
restructure.proposal: RD.0 imports weak completions, dagger algebras, Ω† and de Rham complexes from F1 (request recorded) and plans only the Frobenius-lift existence and homotopy statements (RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra, RD.0/frobenius-lifts-induce-homotopic-maps), which ColemanIntegration L1 requests.

restructure.title: Dieudonné-Manin: VB0 covers E-breve (residue field F̄_q); RD.1 needs arbitrary algebraically closed residue fields and the extended Robba ring
restructure.detail: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block fixes isocrystals over W_{O_E}(F̄_q)[1/π] and uses Dieudonné-Manin there. Kedlaya's slope theory needs Dieudonné-Manin over W(κ, O)[π^{-1}] for κ the completed algebraic closure of k((t)) (generic slopes) and over the extended Robba ring R^alg (special slopes); the latter is equivalent, through Fargues-Fontaine's dictionary, to VB2's classification of bundles on X_C, but neither roadmap plans that dictionary.
restructure.proposal: Keep RD.1/dieudonne-manin-classical (any algebraically closed residue field) and RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring; VB0 cites RD.1/dieudonne-manin-classical for the general residue field, and the sign dictionary (VB0's block of slope d/h = Kedlaya's M_{−d,h}) is recorded in RD.1/standard-frobenius-modules. A comparison node 'φ-modules over the extended Robba ring ↔ bundles on X_C' belongs to VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals, Part II.

restructure.title: RD.1 σ-modules over R are the Γ-free core of PG.2's Robba (φ,Γ)-modules
restructure.detail: AUDIT-37 lists PG.2 ('Robba (φ,Γ)-modules') as overlapping RD.1. PG.2 adds a Γ-action and the étale/Galois comparison; RD.1 has no Γ.
restructure.proposal: Keep both; PG.2 imports RD.1/frobenius-module, RD.1/frobenius-slopes and RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module (and RD.2's slope filtration) instead of re-planning slopes of φ-modules over the Robba ring.

restructure.title: Extended Robba ring versus the rings B_{C^♭,I} of RF0:annuli
restructure.detail: For a perfect complete ℓ, Kedlaya's Γ^ℓ_I is, after renormalising radii, the ring of functions on the annulus Y_{Spa ℓ, I} of RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli; RD.0 needs the analytic rings also for imperfect ℓ (k((t)) and its finite separable extensions).
restructure.proposal: Keep RD.0/analytic-ring (general ℓ) and add a comparison with RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli for perfect ℓ when RF0 is implemented.

restructure.title: The slope filtration theorem belongs to RD.2, not RD.1
restructure.detail: The atlas text of RD.1 mentions slope filtrations with existence, uniqueness and descent; the reviewed decomposition and the part interface ids put the slope filtration theorem in RD.2 (id RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement kept). Its proof needs the whole analytic ring theory of SFR (Bézout property, Dieudonné-Manin over the extended Robba ring, isoclinic descent), which is RD.2 material; RD.1 needs only Newton polygons and generic slopes over Γ.
restructure.proposal: RD.1: differential modules, generic radii, Frobenius slopes and the classical Dieudonné-Manin decomposition over the complete ring Γ^alg[π^{-1}]. RD.2: the slope filtration theorem over the Robba ring with its descent (SFR Chapters 2-6), horizontality and the local monodromy theorem. Update the RD.1 stage text accordingly. For the atlas, RD.1 may also be divided into two sub-layers: RD.1a "p-adic differential modules and radii" and RD.1b "Frobenius modules and slopes".

restructure.title: Residues and primitives on annuli: a foundational owner is needed
restructure.detail: RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative (residue, primitives on the Robba ring and on R[log u]) overlaps the ColemanIntegration part-A nodes on exactness on annuli iff the residue vanishes and on logarithmic primitives (open pull request, not yet on main, so their ids cannot be cited). RD.2 must not depend on ColemanIntegration:L0, whose stage requirements pull in automorphic roadmaps, and ColemanIntegration consumes RD.
restructure.proposal: Move residues and primitives of analytic functions on annuli (and on the Robba ring, with log u adjoined) to RD.0 (or to PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations); both RD.2 and ColemanIntegration:L0 cite that node.

restructure.title: Convergent F-isocrystals (CR.3) versus overconvergent ones (RD.3)
restructure.detail: The audit lists RD.3 against CR.1/CR.3. CrystallineCohomology:CR.3 owns convergent F-isocrystals; RD.3 owns frames, tubes, strict neighbourhoods, j†, overconvergent (F-)isocrystals, independence of the frame, the restriction functor and Kedlaya's full faithfulness theorem. The tube of a frame is needed by both.
restructure.proposal: RD.3 owns RD.3/frame and RD.3/tube (Berthelot's definitions); CR.3 realises convergent F-isocrystals on tubes (Berthelot 4.1) citing RD.3/tube and proves their comparison with crystals on the crystalline site (CR.1, Ogus); RD.3/restriction-to-convergent and RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent cite CR.3's category.

restructure.title: Strict neighbourhoods: dagger affinoids (F1) versus tubes in frames (RD.3)
restructure.detail: The AdicSpacesPartII:F1 stage lists strict neighbourhoods; RD.3's stage text lists strict neighbourhoods of the tube of a frame. These are different notions: an affinoid relatively compact in another (F1) and an admissible open V with ]X[ ⊆ V ⊆ ]Y[ such that {V, ]Y−X[} is an admissible covering (Berthelot 2.5a).
restructure.proposal: F1 owns dagger algebras and affinoid strict neighbourhoods; RD.3 owns RD.3/strict-neighbourhood and j†, citing F1 to identify global overconvergent sections on affine frames with dagger algebras.

restructure.title: The p-adic local monodromy theorem is exported by RD.2; R06.3 keeps the Galois bridge
restructure.detail: The audit lists R06.3 as restating the p-adic local monodromy theorem. RD.2 plans the analytic theorem and the comparison RD.2/berger-form-of-local-monodromy (Berger's Théorème 5.20 form: solutions in B†_log,L for a differential module with Frobenius over B†_rig,K).
restructure.proposal: R06.3 cites RD.2/berger-form-of-local-monodromy and owns only V ↦ N_dR(V), Berger's Théorèmes 3.6/5.10 and the deduction that de Rham representations are potentially semistable.

restructure.title: RD.4 and AdicSpacesPartII:F1: who owns the overconvergent de Rham complex
restructure.detail: F1 owns dagger algebras, their differential forms and exterior derivative, de Rham complexes on dagger spaces and compact-support variants by boundary vanishing; RD.4 restates "the overconvergent de Rham complex on frames".
restructure.proposal: F1 keeps the analytic objects (dagger algebras, Ω^•, de Rham complexes of coherent modules with connection on dagger spaces and strict neighbourhoods). RD.4 owns j† on tubes of frames, the frame cohomology, rigid cohomology with and without supports, their independence of choices, functoriality and Frobenius, and imports F1 through requests.

restructure.title: RD.4 and AG2.4: ordinary-locus rigid cohomology
restructure.detail: AG2.4 builds the overconvergent logarithmic de Rham complex with compact-support boundary ideal and its hypercohomology for HLTT.
restructure.proposal: AG2.4 consumes RD.4/rigid-cohomology, RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology and RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology and keeps only the Shimura-variety-specific boundary and slope comparisons.

restructure.title: RD.5 and CR.3: finiteness, duality and Künneth
restructure.detail: CR.3 owns finiteness, base change, Künneth and (CR.3:duality) duality for crystalline cohomology of proper smooth schemes; RD.5 proves the rigid statements for all separated finite-type schemes with overconvergent F-isocrystal coefficients.
restructure.proposal: Keep both; RD.5 does not use crystalline cohomology (Kedlaya's proof avoids it), and RD.7 compares the two for proper smooth X. Record a link RD.5 → RD.7 only.

restructure.title: RD.2 and RD.5: absolute versus relative local monodromy
restructure.detail: The audit lists RD.2 as duplicated by RD.5.
restructure.proposal: RD.2 owns the local monodromy theorem over R_K; RD.5 owns its reformulation with a Robba-ring identification (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Theorem 5.1.2) and the relative theorem over dagger algebras (Theorem 5.1.3), which are new statements.

restructure.title: Nonarchimedean locally convex duality has no owner
restructure.detail: RD.5 needs strict maps, LF and Fréchet–Montel spaces, transposes of strict maps and Hahn–Banach over a spherically complete field (Crew Part I; Kedlaya 8.3); LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0 constructs locally convex inductive limits and continuous duals of spaces of locally analytic functions. Mathlib's locally convex spaces are over ordered fields.
restructure.proposal: Move RD.5/strict-map, RD.5/frechet-montel-transpose-strict, RD.5/nonarchimedean-hahn-banach and RD.5/finite-cokernel-strict to LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0 (or a new foundational nonarchimedean functional analysis layer), with RD.5 importing them.

restructure.title: Owner of de Jong alterations
restructure.detail: AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5 proves de Jong Theorems 4.1 and 6.5 and proper hypercovers by alterations; SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4 also lists alterations.
restructure.proposal: L5 owns alterations and alteration hypercoverings; SF.4 and RD.5 import them (RD.5 through a request).

restructure.title: Sub-layers of RD.5 for the atlas
restructure.detail: RD.5 has 67 nodes in four distinct blocks.
restructure.proposal: RD.5a Relative local monodromy and generic pushforwards (relative-robba-ring … relative-local-monodromy-theorem, unipotent/relative-local-cohomology nodes, generic-pushforward-*, leray-long-exact-sequence, pushforward-flat-base-change, pushforward-external-product, six-term-isomorphism-lemma, finitely-generated-intersection); RD.5b Curves (near-isomorphism … crew-finiteness-and-duality-on-curves, van-der-put-legendre-computation, dimension-of-h1-of-affine-curve); RD.5c Topology and duality (strict-map … relative-poincare-duality, trace-map, poincare-pairing, top-compact-support-cohomology, excision-duality-compatibility, poincare-duality); RD.5d Main theorems (etale-covers-of-affine-space, finiteness-for-smooth-varieties, smooth-proper-hypercovering, cohomological-descent-for-proper-hypercoverings, finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology, finiteness-of-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology, frobenius-bijective-on-cohomology, compact-support-vanishing-above-twice-dimension, euler-characteristic-duality, kunneth-*, no-finiteness-without-frobenius, affine-curve-duality-acceptance).

restructure.title: ι-weights of numbers and endomorphisms belong to DWP.0
restructure.detail: RD.6's text asks to 'define algebraic/iota weights using an embedding of algebraic coefficient eigenvalues into C'; DWP.0 already owns Weil q-numbers and the ι-weight predicate on coefficient-field elements and on endomorphisms. RD.6 keeps only the pointwise weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals, ι-real/ι-realizable objects and determinantal weights, and imports the number-level notions (and the 'all ι ⇒ Weil number' bridge) from DWP.0.
restructure.proposal: Narrow RD.6's weight target to overconvergent F-isocrystals; add the stage link DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0 → PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6, and ask DWP.0 to state its predicates for an arbitrary characteristic-0 coefficient field (p-adic included).

restructure.title: Weight-separated identification of the factors P_i belongs to WC.3
restructure.detail: RD.7 must 'use purity and disjoint absolute values by degree to identify each characteristic polynomial'; WC.3 owns exactly this abstract argument (Deligne Weil I (1.7) ⇒ (1.6)) for the étale realisation. The abstract lemma should be stated once for any characteristic-0 coefficient field and used by both.
restructure.proposal: Add the stage link WeilConjectures:WC.3 → PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7 (no cycle: WC.3 does not depend on RD.7, and WC.6 stays downstream); RD.7 instantiates the lemma for rigid cohomology.

restructure.title: Rigid Weil II versus ℓ-adic Weil II (DWP.5, R34.5)
restructure.detail: The audit lists RD.6 as overlapping DWP.5 and R34.5. The overlap is structural only: the ℓ-adic local weights and fundamental estimate (DWP.5) and their interface (R34.5) concern lisse ℓ-adic sheaves, while RD.6 proves Kedlaya's rigid theorem for overconvergent F-isocrystals through the p-adic Fourier transform. Only the elementary positive-series lemma is shared (requested from DWP.2).
restructure.proposal: Keep both; record that the analytic positive-series lemma is owned by DWP.2 and imported by RD.6; no mathematics moves.

restructure.title: RD.7 needs CR.2 as well as CR.3
restructure.detail: The rigid–crystalline comparison computes crystalline cohomology by the PD-envelope de Rham complex of an embedding, which CR.2 owns; RD.7's stage text lists only CR.3.
restructure.proposal: Add the stage link CrystallineCohomology:CR.2 → PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7 (CR.2 already precedes CR.3, so no cycle).

restructure.title: RD.7's ℓ-adic comparison for smooth proper (non-projective) X needs DWP.7
restructure.detail: DWP.4 gives ℓ-adic purity only for smooth projective X; RD.7's stage text says 'smooth proper'. The rigid side needs no projectivity (Kedlaya's purity).
restructure.proposal: Add the stage link DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7 → PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7 for the proper case, or narrow the ℓ-adic clause of RD.7 to projective X and let WC.6 (which already uses DWP.7) extend it.

restructure.title: Split RD.6 into three sub-layers for the atlas
restructure.detail: RD.6 has about sixty declarations in three independent strands.
restructure.proposal: RD.6a 'Trace formula and L-functions' (normalisations, L-function, Dwork operators, trace formula, P^1/G_m tests); RD.6b 'p-adic Fourier transform' (D†, ρ, Dwork isocrystal, geometric transform, GOS, conductor estimate, degeneration lemmas of Kedlaya §3); RD.6c 'Weights and rigid Weil II' (ι-weights, determinantal weights, monodromy group, Rankin squaring, local weights, Weil II, purity, functional equation, slopes, curve H^1 weights).
